scenes.synopsis: the counsel on the stairs — Augusta's terms for a night at the press; the general's blessing, priced.
scenes.prose:
> *("You are going," says Augusta on the stairs, in her dressing gown — which on Augusta looks less like a dressing gown than a uniform stripped of its braid — "into a room full of men who live by other people's shame, to ask them to show you tomorrow's shame in advance. Do not threaten them. Do not bribe them loudly. And do not let Pyke see you are afraid of what is in the type." "I am not afraid of what is in the type," says Rose. "It is the same libel, accelerated — the same fraud, the same dupes, only set faster." "Then be afraid of something else," says Augusta, descending one step, the general's gravity settling. "Be afraid of wanting it stopped so badly you would pay any price to stop it. That is the fear Pyke listens for. He has made a fortune listening for it.")*
> *(Letitia appears at the stairhead with a shawl, the household's own quartermaster. "Printing houses are damp." "It is not the damp I am dressed for," says Rose — but takes it, because Letitia's shawls have won campaigns before. At the door Augusta holds her sleeve — the grip light, the meaning heavy. "One rule, and it is the whole of the night. You may buy a man's time tonight. Not his trade. Time is honest; a shilling for an hour is a clean transaction. Trade is the man himself, and men are not for sale." "And Pyke?" "Pyke will offer to sell you the paper. Remember: a man who will sell you his press will sell you to the next buyer, and the next buyer is the purse. Good hunting, child.")*
> *(The door closes behind her with the soft finality of a chapter turning. Rose climbs into the cab — severe dress beneath, Letitia's shawl over it, the lamp in her hand: the household, entire, going to war in one hired cab. Augusta's rules ride with her like orders in a dispatch case: no threats, no loud bribes, no visible fear, no buying of trade. And underneath the rules, the deeper counsel, the one she will need most tonight: want nothing so badly that the wanting shows. The wanting is the price Pyke charges. She will not pay it.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive "do not threaten them; do not bribe them loudly." → Remembered: The rules of engagement; she carries them verbatim.
> 2. [examine]"Be afraid of *wanting* it stopped" — the fear Pyke listens for. → Remembered: Her discipline of desire; the wanting must not show.
> 3. [micro]Take the shawl — "not the damp I am dressed for." → Remembered: How she accepts Letitia's counsel; the shawl goes to war.
> 4. [social]Take "you may buy a man's *time*; not his *trade*." → Remembered: The distinction; it will govern every coin she spends tonight.
> 5. [examine]"A man who will sell you his press will sell *you*." → Remembered: The warning; it prices Pyke's offer in advance.
> 6. [stance]"Good hunting" — the blessing, priced. → Remembered: The general's send-off; she hunts with permission.
> 7. [micro]Feel the shawl over the severe dress — the household, entire. → Remembered: What she carries; the house goes with her.
> 8. [choice]Carry the counsel as armor, as script, or as weight. → Remembered: How counsel rides; it shapes the night's answers.

scenes.synopsis: the chapel of the press — the stone, the machines, the men; Pettifer the compositor as guide.
scenes.prose:
> *(The stairs up from the alley are stone, worn in the middle by two centuries of feet, and she climbs them, lamp high, while the noise resolves around her — not noise, she understands at the third landing: work. The press floor opens before her like a chapel: the great machines ranked in their stations, the men moving between them with the unhurried economy of long practice, the smell of ink and hot metal and lamp oil hanging in the air like incense. "A cathedral of honest noise," she thinks — and corrects herself at once. Honest work. The libel is printed here, yes, but so is everything else that London reads: the sermons, the shipping news, the birth notices, the advertisements for lost dogs. The press does not know what it prints. The men — the men know. She stands a moment in the doorway with her lamp, the severe dress dark against the lamplight, and lets the chapel take her measure.)*
> *(An old man detaches himself from the great central stone — white hair, ink to his elbows, a compositor's apron worn forty years into softness. He looks at her lamp, her dress, her directness, and something in his face shifts: recognition, and then a decision. "Pettifer," he says, by way of everything — name, trade, and introduction in a single word. "You are the Hartwell girl." It is not a question. "I set your name this week — and last." No apology in it. A statement of trade, the way a mason might own the wall he built. "Show me the stone," says Rose. He studies her a moment longer — the severe dress, the lamp, the absence of flinching — and nods once, the chapel's memory choosing its guide. "This way, miss. Mind the chase — it bites.")*
> *(He leads her between the machines, and the men glance up as she passes — not staring, she notes with approval: glancing, the way men glance at weather. The girl is at the far stone, no more than sixteen, checking a locked chase the way one checks a pulse, her fingers light on the metal. Pettifer stops before the forme that holds tomorrow. There it is, locked in its iron chase, the type standing shoulder to shoulder in perfect order: her name, in metal, waiting for ink. She looks at it a long moment — the libel as objects, as labor, as a man's hands set letter by letter — and understands what she has come to learn: who sets the type chooses the truth, and the truth is set by hand.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Take the stairs — "a cathedral of honest noise." → Remembered: Her arrival register; she reverences the labor before the libel.
> 2. [social]Be met by Mr. Pettifer — the chapel's memory. → Remembered: How the night acquires a guide; Pettifer's memory chooses her.
> 3. [micro]"Ink to his elbows" — the trade, worn on the body. → Remembered: What she respects; the trade is legible in flesh.
> 4. [examine]Name the trade's true work — "what the paper *does*." → Remembered: Her comprehension; she separates trade from libel.
> 5. [stance]Refuse the tour — "I have come to read, not to tour." → Remembered: Her focus; the night has one errand.
> 6. [social]"Show me the stone" — the direct ask. → Remembered: Her plainness; the chapel hears a direct question.
> 7. [examine]Read the chase — the type, locked, her name standing. → Remembered: The sight; her name in metal, waiting for ink.
> 8. [choice]Touch the type, read only, or ask Pettifer to read aloud. → Remembered: Her manner with evidence; the chase remembers the hand.

scenes.synopsis: reading tomorrow's number in the chase — the libel as labor; copying it into the campaign book.
scenes.prose:
> *(Pettifer reads it for her, his finger tracking the lines of standing type the way a priest tracks a psalter — and the libel, heard aloud in the compositor's flat workman's voice, is revealed for what it is: the same fraud, accelerated. The same dupes quoted, the same gold hinted, the same Hartwell name set crooked in the sentence like a stone in a shoe. But faster — half again more of it, the venom thickened to fill the space the impatient purse has purchased. Her eye, trained by three weeks of breakfast reading, catches what the compositor's did not: the Hartwell name mis-set, an e turned, a tiny error in the libel's own machinery. She notes it the way a proofreader notes everything — without triumph, without mercy. The error is evidence. Everything is evidence now.)*
> *(She takes out the campaign book — the general's kit, chosen at the hall mirror — and copies the libel into it in her clearest hand, line by line, while Pettifer holds the lamp. The book that has held the warehouse, the roads, the scarred knuckle, now holds tomorrow: the pre-print text, taken at the stone, before ink, before dawn, before the town. "You will want the price of this," she says, not looking up from the page. Pettifer is quiet a moment. "An hour of your company, miss. That is the price." Time, not trade — Augusta's rule, honored on both sides of the stone. She pays it gladly, and the hour stretches: the press's rhythm under their talk, the girl's soft humming at the far chase, the cold of the stone coming up through the iron into her fingertips where she steadies the forme.)*
> *(The cold surprises her — she had not expected the truth to have a temperature, but it does: the iron chase is cold, the type is cold, the whole locked forme sits in her hands' memory like a winter railing. Tomorrow this cold metal will be warm with ink and the town will read it warm at breakfast and never know it was cold first. She closes the campaign book on the copied libel and understands the night's true arithmetic: she has not stopped the number. She has witnessed it. And a witnessed lie is a different animal from an unwitnessed one — it has a reader now who was there at the setting, and readers, Pyke is about to learn, are dangerous.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Read tomorrow's libel — "the same fraud, accelerated." → Remembered: Her discipline; she reads as a clerk, not a victim.
> 2. [micro]"The Hartwell name, mis-set" — her eye, proofing. → Remembered: Her proofreader's eye; the error is evidence.
> 3. [examine]Time the acceleration — type, set faster. → Remembered: The measurement; half-again-more libel per week.
> 4. [stance]Copy the libel into the campaign book — the record. → Remembered: Her documentation; the book holds the pre-print text.
> 5. [social]Ask Pettifer the price of candor — "time, not trade." → Remembered: How she buys; Augusta's rule, honored.
> 6. [micro]Feel the stone's cold through the chase — the truth, metal. → Remembered: The physical fact; the lie has a temperature.
> 7. [choice]Confront Pyke tonight, read and withdraw, or buy the night's silence. → Remembered: Her restraint; the choice sets the chapter's strategy.

scenes.synopsis: the chapel's people — the foreman, the girl at the chase; "they set what they are told to set."
scenes.prose:
> *(The foreman comes down from the machines with the weight of the night's run on his face — not a wicked face, she reads at once: a pressed face. Wages, and the weight on them. He looks at her lamp, her book, her severe dress, and his mouth tightens the way men's mouths tighten when the gentry arrive with questions. "I am Hartwell's," says Rose, plainly, before he can ask — the name owned, not flinched from, set down between them like the lamp. "I have read tomorrow's number in the chase. I have copied it. I am not here to stop your press." The tightness eases a fraction. Behind him the girl has stopped her humming and watches — sixteen, ink on her cheek, her fingers still resting on the chase she was checking the way one checks a pulse, tenderly, as if the metal were alive.)*
> *(She talks with them in the intervals of the work — the press never stopping, the men feeding it like stokers feed a furnace — and learns the press's political economy: two hungers drive it, the paper's hunger for copy and the men's hunger for wages, and the libel feeds both at once, which is why it runs so hot. "They set what they are told to set," says the foreman at last, not defending, not apologizing — stating. And she absolves them in her heart on the spot, completely, the way Augusta absolved a regiment once: the labor is not the libel. The men are not the machine. The girl shows her the locked forme she has been tending, proud as a nurse, and Rose bends to it with genuine respect — and makes her promise, there in the chapel's honest noise: "The truth, in type, when it comes. I will bring it to this stone myself.")*
> *(They let her go up the stairs to Pyke's office with something like blessing — the foreman's nod, Pettifer's hand briefly on her sleeve, the girl's shy, ink-stained wave. She climbs with the campaign book heavy in her reticule and the cold of the chase still in her fingertips, and understands that she has done something tonight no strategy required: she has been fair to the labor. It will matter. In a war of paper, the people who set the type are the ground itself — and she has just walked the ground, lamp in hand, and learned its shape by foot.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read the foreman's face — "wages, and the weight on them." → Remembered: Her reading of men; the foreman is pressed, not wicked.
> 2. [social]"I am Hartwell's" — the plain declaration. → Remembered: How she names herself in the press; the name, owned.
> 3. [micro]Watch the girl "check the chase the way one checks a pulse." → Remembered: The detail; labor has its own tenderness.
> 4. [examine]Name the press's two hungers — paper's and men's. → Remembered: Her political economy; the press runs on both.
> 5. [stance]Promise the men "the truth, in type, when it comes." → Remembered: Her pledge; the chapel holds her to it.
> 6. [social]Let the girl show her the locked forme — trust, exchanged. → Remembered: How trust travels; the young teach the willing.
> 7. [micro]"They set what they are told to set" — the absolution. → Remembered: Her fairness; she acquits the labor of the libel.
> 8. [choice]Leave a coin for the girl, for the chapel, or for neither. → Remembered: Her generosity's direction; the purse, aimed.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — TOMORROW'S NUMBER. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Pyke's office is above the press, and the stairs' thump dulls to a murmur as Pettifer leaves her at the door — the office all green-shaded lamps and money's particular smell, lamp oil over coin, the proprietor's desk squared like a card table. Pyke does not rise. He is affable in the way of men who have already won the evening: "Miss Hartwell. To what does my press owe this — pleasure?" The pause before pleasure is the whole of him. "You have read it, I see. Pettifer talks." He taps the stack of chase proofs. Tomorrow's number. Hers. "Well — talk is cheap, and libel, as you know, is dear." No threat in it. Nothing overt. Only arithmetic, offered with a smile, in a room where the money smells faintly of ink.)*
> *(The offer comes laid like a card on the green felt of his desk. "Name your price, Miss Hartwell. The number can — disappear. A press is a machine; machines can be stopped." A beat, precisely timed. "But machines are expensive to stop." Behind him the window gives onto the press floor: the men at their stations, the girl at her chase, Pettifer's white head bent over the stone. Her war has always been against the libel. Tonight, for the first time, it is against the press itself — and the press, Pyke is telling her without ever quite saying it, can be bought, if she will pay what he asks, which is never coin. Pyke's price is always the same, and he does not need to name it: the truth, in her handwriting. Three roads lie open, and the night is spending itself while she chooses.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — Tomorrow's number:*
- **Preempt it tonight** — *Conduct+; the bold stroke.* Warn the town before dawn — letters, riders, the ton roused — that tomorrow's number is a purchased lie. *(Quill respects the nerve; Pyke will call it war.)*
- **Meet it with conduct** — *Composure+; the measured answer.* Let it print; be seen at church, at calls, at the opera — the living refutation. *(Augusta approves; the libel runs its course.)*
- **Let it print** — *Subtlety+; the long game.* Save the purse and the nerve; watch who profits from the number. *(Lavinia watches with her; the purse shows its hand.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: her nerve, her arithmetic, the hour she chose to spend them. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*
> **Turns (3):**
> 1. [examine]Hear the offer — "expensive to stop," the truth in her handwriting as the price. → Remembered: The offer; Pyke's arithmetic, heard whole.
> 2. [stance]Weigh the three roads — preempt it, meet it with conduct, or let it print. → Remembered: Her weighing; the night spending itself while she chooses.
> 3. [choice]Choose, with the press thumping below — the stairs, the stone, the chained door. → Remembered: The choosing; what she refused to buy.

scenes.synopsis: Pyke, studied — the sly proprietor; "he prints, never threatens"; the offer's arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stays long enough to study him — the enemy, at his desk, in his element — and the study is worth the staying: Pyke's slyness is never overt, she sees now, because overtness would be a confession. He prints; he never threatens. The threat is always somewhere else — in the purse behind him, in the type below him, in the arithmetic he lays out like patience. "Expensive to stop," he says again, almost gently, and she understands the sentence entire: the price is not the stopping. The price is the asking. A woman who asks a press to stop has confessed that the press can wound her — and confessions, in Pyke's office, are currency. She sits in the green lamplight doing the only arithmetic that matters: what he wants is not coin. What he wants is the truth, in her handwriting — her signature on a retraction, a confession, a surrender he can set in type.)*
> *(She refuses the way Augusta taught her: plainly, without heat, leaving no edge to grip. "I do not buy presses, Mr. Pyke. I read them." It is a creditor's sentence, and she sees it land: the affability flickers, just once, like a lamp in a draft. He recovers at once — of course he does; sly men always do — and spreads his hands in a gesture of wounded commerce. "Then we are enemies, Miss Hartwell? What a pity. I so prefer customers." "We are not enemies," says Rose, rising, the campaign book heavy in her reticule, the severe dress straight as a rule. "Enemies threaten. You print. I read. Good night, Mr. Pyke." She leaves like a creditor — back straight, lamp in hand — and does not look at the window onto the press floor until she is on the stairs.)*
> *(On the stairs she passes the stone again, and the chapel re-sees her: Pettifer's nod, the foreman's lifted chin, the girl's quick, shy smile from her chase. The men have heard nothing — the office is above the noise for a reason — but they read her face the way they read copy, and what they read seems to satisfy them. She walks out into the alley with the thump of the press under her feet and Pyke's arithmetic in her head, and does the final sum of the night: he offered to sell her the press. Augusta's warning holds — a man who will sell you his press will sell you to the next buyer. She has not bought. She has read. The alley air is cold after the press room's heat, and the book in her hand is heavier going out than it was coming in.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch Pyke's slyness — "never overt; he prints, never threatens." → Remembered: Her study of the enemy; the slyness is the threat.
> 2. [social]Answer "name your price" — the refusal, phrased. → Remembered: How she declines purchase; the refusal is the answer.
> 3. [micro]"The money smells faintly of ink" — the room, read. → Remembered: Her sense-memory; the office's smell is its truth.
> 4. [examine]Price "expensive to stop" — the arithmetic of the offer. → Remembered: Her accounting; the offer costs more than coin.
> 5. [stance]Name what Pyke wants — "the truth, in her handwriting." → Remembered: Her clarity; she prices the unspoken demand.
> 6. [social]Leave "like a creditor" — the exit, styled. → Remembered: Her departure register; the press sees her back, straight.
> 7. [micro]Take the stairs down past the stone — the chapel, re-seen. → Remembered: The return through the work; the men nod.
> 8. [choice]Carry the offer home, bury it, or spend it. → Remembered: What she does with Pyke's price; it becomes intelligence.

scenes.synopsis: the debrief — cocoa and counsel; "we do not buy presses"; the night's intelligence, filed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The cab carries her home past the ton's lit windows — the squares asleep in their dinner glow, the whole of fashionable London unconscious that its breakfast is being decided at this hour — and she holds the campaign book on her lap like a dispatch, the copied libel inside it, the pre-print text, the night's spoil. The press's thump is still in her feet. Pyke's arithmetic is still in her head. "Expensive to stop." The truth, in her handwriting. She turns the sentences over the way Pettifer's girl turns a chase, checking for the flaw — and finds none, which is itself the intelligence: a clean offer means a clean trap, and a clean trap means a deep one. She is still turning it when the cab stops, and Augusta is awake in the morning room, a single lamp lit, the general receiving the night's intelligence at half past twelve.)*
> *("Report, then," says Augusta, and Rose reports: the stone, the chase, her name in type, the mis-set e, the copied libel, the girl at the pulse of the forme. And then the office above: the green lamps, the proofs squared like a hand of cards, the offer laid like a card upon them. "Name your price. Machines are expensive to stop." Augusta listens the way she has listened to forty years of reports — without moving, without interrupting — and then delivers the doctrine in a single sentence: "We do not buy presses." It is not advice. It is law, the household's law, and Rose feels it settle over the night like a seal over a dispatch. "No," says Rose. "We read them." Letitia arrives with cocoa — the household's debrief ritual, older than the war — and the three of them sit in the lamplight with the campaign book open between them like a map of hostile country.)*
> *(They name the price aloud, together, the way one names a ghost to lay it: the truth, in her handwriting. Spoken in the morning room over cocoa, with Augusta's pen scratching a note and Letitia's shawl still around Rose's shoulders, the price loses its power — it becomes data, intelligence, a line in the campaign book. "He will try again," says Augusta. "Sly men always try again. Next time the price will be dressed differently." "Next time," says Rose, "I will know the dress." She climbs the stairs at one with the thump of the press still in her feet and the household's law in her head — we do not buy presses — and sleeps, when she sleeps, the sleep of a general after a successful reconnaissance: the ground mapped, the enemy studied, the price known.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Ride home "past the ton's lit windows" — the sleeping city. → Remembered: Her night vision; the ton sleeps through its own news.
> 2. [micro]Hold the campaign book "like a dispatch" — the record, carried. → Remembered: What she carries; the book is the night's spoil.
> 3. [social]Find Augusta awake — "report, then." → Remembered: The debrief; the general receives the night's intelligence.
> 4. [examine]Lay out Pyke's offer — "expensive to stop." → Remembered: Her intelligence work; the offer becomes data.
> 5. [stance]"We do not buy presses" — the doctrine, stated. → Remembered: The household's law; it will govern the purse.
> 6. [social]Letitia's cocoa — the household's debrief ritual. → Remembered: How the house processes war; cocoa and counsel.
> 7. [micro]"The truth, in her handwriting" — the price, named aloud. → Remembered: The naming; spoken, the price loses power.
> 8. [choice]Sleep, write, or plan — the night's remainder. → Remembered: How she spends the hours; the choice shapes dawn.

scenes.synopsis: morning — the press's thump remembered; the day's doctrine: "today we are clerks."
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes to the press's thump, remembered — not heard, but carried: the rhythm has followed her home and set itself up in her body like a second heartbeat, and for a moment, between sleep and waking, she is back on the stone with the lamp in her hand and her name standing in type. Then the morning asserts itself: the maid with chocolate, the square's ordinary noise, the day's plain light falling across the campaign book on her desk — closed now, the copied libel inside it like a pressed flower. She dresses in the armor of the ordinary: morning dress, neat, unremarkable, the camouflage of a woman with nothing to hide and everything to do. The severe dress of the night hangs in the wardrobe like a shed skin. She looks at it a moment — the law's dress, worn once — and nods to it, the way one nods to a weapon cleaned and put away.)*
> *(Breakfast is a council of war conducted over eggs: Augusta with the campaign book open beside her plate, Letitia with the household accounts, Creech expected at ten with the morning's intelligence. Rose reads the plan aloud — the day's orders, spoken plainly: today they follow the paper trail the night exposed. The purse paid half again more; the payment was not Pyke's coin; someone else's purse is deep and impatient. "Today we are clerks," she says, and the doctrine settles over the table like a tablecloth. "Not combatants. Clerks. We read, we copy, we file. The press taught me the trade's true work last night — what the paper does — and today we do it back." Augusta approves with a single nod. Letitia pours more chocolate. The household — general, quartermaster, and commander — assigns itself: Augusta to the correspondence, Letitia to the callers who will carry the day's word, Creech to the warehouse and the roads.)*
> *(There remains the question of where she places herself — the commander's oldest question — and she answers it the way she answered the knock at the press: directly. She will lead the paper trail herself this morning, with Quill at eleven; Creech's legs are better spent on the warehouse roads. The decision made, the day begins: the campaign book open, the pen ready, the thump of the remembered press settling under her work like a metronome. Today we are clerks. The clerks, she thinks, taking up her pen, are winning.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Wake "to the press's thump, remembered" — the night, carried. → Remembered: How the night persists; the thump follows her home.
> 2. [micro]Dress "in the armor of the ordinary" — morning dress. → Remembered: Her day camouflage; the ordinary, worn deliberately.
> 3. [social]Breakfast with the household — the debrief, continued. → Remembered: How war is discussed over eggs; the domestic front.
> 4. [examine]Read the plan aloud — today's campaign. → Remembered: Her command style; the day's orders, spoken.
> 5. [stance]"Today we are clerks" — the day's doctrine. → Remembered: The register; clerks, not combatants.
> 6. [social]Assign the household — Augusta, Letitia, Creech. → Remembered: Her delegation; the house becomes a staff.
> 7. [choice]Lead the paper trail herself, or send Creech. → Remembered: Where she places herself; the choice positions her.

scenes.synopsis: the proof's presentation — how truth is dressed for a solicitor; a small diegetic choice, remembered.
scenes.prose:
> *(The proof lies on her desk in the morning light — the copied libel, her clearest hand, the mis-set e marked with a clerk's neat caret — and she studies it the way a general studies ground: not for what it is, but for how it will be fought over. Quill comes at eleven, and Quill is a solicitor: he reads the form first and the content second, the way all his tribe do. A clerk's honesty, then — but what dress does a clerk's honesty wear? The evidence is clean; the presentation must be clean. But clean has registers, and she knows them all: the plain packet, unadorned, that trusts the evidence to speak; the annotated proof, her hand in the margin guiding his eye like an advocate's brief; the sealed deposition, formal and witnessed, the weapon sheathed in law. She feels the paper's tooth under her fingers — good paper, the campaign book's paper, evidence you can hold — and weighs clean against clever the way Augusta weighs ground: clever wins arguments, clean wins solicitors.)*
> *(She thinks of Pyke's office — the green lamps, the proofs squared like a winning hand — and of the stone below it, the cold chase, the girl checking the forme like a pulse. The truth has been set in type by other hands; now she sets it in her own. Whatever dress she chooses for the proof, Quill will read the dress too — solicitors always do — and the dress must say what she means: this is documented, this is witnessed, this is not hysteria and not vengeance but record. She assembles the packet slowly, each piece chosen, each piece a sentence: the copy, the note of the mis-set e, the memorandum of the hour and the stone. The form of truth, decided and owned. And the game will remember — and so will Quill.)*
> *(At eleven precisely the knocker sounds, and she looks once more at the packet on her desk — plain, annotated, or sealed — and nods. She straightens the packet's edge a fraction — the clerk's last touch — and goes down to receive him with the morning room's full composure. The truth is dressed. Let the solicitor read.)*
*Choices (no coin cost; the game remembers):*
- **The plain packet** — unadorned, numbered, clerkly; the evidence speaks. *(Quill+; the solicitor trusts the unadorned.)*
- **The annotated proof** — her hand in the margin, guiding his eye; the advocate's brief. *(Conduct+; Quill sees her mind at work.)*
- **The sealed deposition** — formal, witnessed, legal; the weapon, sheathed. *(Composure+; Quill notes the discipline.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Study the proof "the way a general studies ground." → Remembered: Her tactical eye; the proof is terrain.
> 2. [micro]Feel "the paper's tooth" — evidence, tactile. → Remembered: Her physical reading; paper has a tooth.
> 3. [stance]Choose the proof's presentation — the form of truth. → Remembered: How truth is dressed; the form carries it.
> 4. [social]Quill's eye — "he reads the form first." → Remembered: Her knowledge of her reader; Quill reads form.
> 5. [examine]Weigh "clean against clever" — the presentation's ethics. → Remembered: Her standard; clean beats clever.
> 6. [choice]Choose the proof's dress — and own the reading. → Remembered: The chosen form; Quill will read the dress too.
> 7. [micro]"A clerk's honesty" — the register, chosen. → Remembered: Her presentation doctrine; honesty, clerked.

scenes.synopsis: the solicitor — the proof read, "actionable"; the doctrine: we do not sue the press; we outlast it.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill arrives at eleven precisely, and Rose watches his face the way she watched the chase last night — for the tell. The solicitor's tell comes early: a small stillness as he lifts the first page, the professional's version of a intake of breath. He reads the packet — plain, annotated, or sealed, as she dressed it — with the slow care of a man billing by the quarter hour and thinking by the decade. "The mis-set e," he says at last, tapping the caret with one blunt finger. It is the detail that lands: the small error proving the large fraud, the libel's own machinery confessing. He reads the memorandum of the hour and the stone twice. Then he looks up, and delivers the verdict in the solicitor's flat cadence: "This is actionable, Miss Hartwell. Against the proprietor, the printer, and — with this memorandum — the purse behind them, should it ever show its face.")*
> *(The word hangs in the morning room like a drawn sword: actionable. She feels its pull — the clean, cold temptation of the law, the suit that would make the town gasp — and then she sets it down, deliberately, the way one sets down a weapon one has decided not to use. "We do not sue the press, Mr. Quill." He blinks. "We outlast it," she says, and the strategy names itself in the saying: a suit would make her the story for a season; outlasting makes the press the story. The libel feeds on attention the way the press feeds on paper; starve it of the lawsuit it wants, and it must find another hunger. Quill studies her a long moment — the severe dress of last night folded away, the morning dress neat, the campaign book closed on the desk — and she sees the solicitor's respect shift into something rarer: the advocate's admiration for a client who will not be moved.)*
> *("File it, then," says Quill, "and hold it. Ammunition keeps." They file the proof together — numbered, witnessed, the memorandum alongside — and he takes his leave with the packet's copy in his case and a new carefulness in his bow. At the door he pauses. "Miss Hartwell — most clients bring me their anger. You brought me a record." "Anger," says Rose, "does not copy well." He laughs, once, surprised, and goes. She stands in the morning room with the filed proof and the day's doctrine entire: we do not sue the press; we outlast it. The law is a shield, not a sword — and she intends to be very well shielded indeed.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Read Quill's "face, the solicitor's tell." → Remembered: Her study; the tell precedes the opinion.
> 2. [social]Lay the proof "like a hand of cards" — the presentation. → Remembered: Her dealing; the packet performs.
> 3. [micro]"The mis-set e" — the detail that lands. → Remembered: What convinces; the small error proves the large fraud.
> 4. [examine]Take his "this is actionable" — the verdict. → Remembered: The legal ground; actionability, established.
> 5. [stance]"We do not sue the press" — the doctrine, extended. → Remembered: Her restraint; law is a shield, not a sword.
> 6. [social]"We *outlast* it" — the strategy, named. → Remembered: How she frames victory; outlasting, not crushing.
> 7. [choice]File the proof, publish the proof, or hold the proof. → Remembered: What she does with ammunition; the choice arms the future.

scenes.synopsis: the paper's roads — the street's mood; the hawker tipped "for the truth of the trade."
scenes.prose:
> *(In the afternoon she walks the paper's roads with Creech — the district the libel travels, mapped now in her feet as well as her book: the print shops, the coffee houses where the numbers are read aloud, the corners where the hawkers cry. Creech counts with her, the warehouse-man's census: the Lantern's hawkers against the Gazette's, the street measured in cries. The Lantern runs hot — half again more hawkers than last week, the impatient purse's money made audible. She buys a Lantern from a hawker's boy with the exact coin, the enemy's number purchased like any intelligence, and reads her own libel standing on the pavement while the town turns pages around her. The street's mood, read closely: curiosity, mostly. A little malice, the cheap kind. And underneath, the thing she is learning to listen for — fatigue. The town is tiring of her as a subject. Fatigue is an ally.)*
> *(She lets herself be seen reading it — the living refutation, practiced: composed, unhurried, the lady reading the libel against herself the way one reads weather. Heads turn. She does not hurry. "Who buys, who lingers, who turns away" — she notes it all, the street's behavior as data, the way Pettifer's girl notes the chase. The hawker's boy watches her read, round-eyed, and she tips him — not for the paper, for the truth of the trade. "Who buys the most, lad? Mornings or evenings?" He tells her, freely, for the tip and the attention: mornings, the clerks; evenings, the idlers; and the gentlemen buy it to laugh, but they buy the Gazette to believe. Intelligence, purchased for a penny and a smile. Augusta's rule holds — time, not trade — and the boy's time was honestly bought.)*
> *(They walk home by the long way, and Creech reports the warehouse roads quiet — no new gold, no new riders, the purse's money moving only through the paper now, which means the paper is the purse's whole instrument, which means the paper is where it can be watched. She sets the street on a schedule — daily, herself, at the hour the hawkers cry loudest — and feels the campaign's geography settle: the stone below, the office above, the street between. The paper's roads are hers now, walked and counted. Tomorrow she walks them again — and the day after, and the day after, until the town tires of the subject entirely and the libel, unfed, folds like a paper left in rain.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Walk "the paper's roads" — the district, mapped. → Remembered: Her geography; the roads enter the map.
> 2. [micro]Count "the Lantern's hawkers against the Gazette's" — the street, measured. → Remembered: Her census; the street is the battlefield.
> 3. [social]Buy a Lantern from a hawker — "the enemy's number, purchased." → Remembered: Her intelligence habit; she buys what she fights.
> 4. [examine]Read the street's mood — "the town, turning pages." → Remembered: Her polling; the street reads, and is read.
> 5. [stance]Be seen reading the Lantern — "the living refutation," practiced. → Remembered: Her visibility; she is seen, composed.
> 6. [micro]Note "who buys, who lingers, who turns away." → Remembered: Her observation; the street's behavior is data.
> 7. [social]Tip the hawker "for the truth of the trade" — the coin, aimed. → Remembered: Her economy; the hawker becomes a source.
> 8. [choice]Work the street daily, weekly, or leave it to Creech. → Remembered: Her commitment; the street gets a schedule.

scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "Tonight she returns to the Lantern's press — not to read the type, but to be read by it. The severe dress: be the law, not the lady. Unadorned. Exact. Every choice a sentence the chapel will parse. The stone, the machines, the men, the girl at her chase — all will read her. Dress to be read truly."
> **Direction:** commit to one of A, B, or C — the game remembers the severity she chooses.
> **The 3 directions:**
> **A. The Statute** — the law's severity. Motif: fluted-column pleating, blind and architectural, running the full skirt like the pillars of a court. Thread: black silk / steel grey / ivory whitework. Colorway: black depth on black — three blacks, no sheen but the pleats'. Accessories: the plain band, the steel pin, the lamp carried like a mace.
> **B. The Magistrate** — the office's gravity. Motif: ledger-rule pinstripes, clerkly and exact, the bodice ruled like a page of evidence. Thread: iron grey silk / steel / silver. Colorway: iron grey on charcoal — the office, worn. Accessories: the campaign book carried openly, the steel pin, gloves buttoned to the elbow.
> **C. The Witness** — the testimony's clarity. Motif: the white rose of the clean name, worked small at the cuff and nowhere else. Thread: ivory whitework / silver / black silk. Colorway: white severity on black — the testimony, spotless. Accessories: a single white rose at the wrist, the plain band, no veil.
> *(System: commit to a direction — A, B, or C — then twenty 5-coin pins. 20 pins × 5 coins = 100 coins. Re-picks always free; the jewel shelf stays open and is never a ritual step.)*

> *(Story morsel: Augusta, on the stairs — "be seen to be the law, child. That is the whole of it.")*

ritual.occasionBrief: A night at the *Lantern's* press — the chapel, the stone, the standing type.

scenes.synopsis: the return — "the press at night, dressed"; to be read *by* the type; the inspection.
scenes.prose:
> *(She returns to the press at ten with the severe dress perfected — black depth, architectural line, the lamp in her hand like a mace — and the chapel reads her at once: Pettifer's nod deepening into something like a bow, the foreman straightening as she passes, the girl's quick curtsey, the apprentice's respect offered unasked. "You came back," says Pettifer, and it is not a question but a welcome — the trade receiving return the way a church receives a parishioner. The press at night, dressed: she walks the floor like an inspection, the law touring its ground, and the machines seem to stand a little straighter under her lamp. This is the inversion the occasion brief promised: tonight she has not come to read the type. She has come to be read by it — to offer herself to the chapel's reading, and be found, she hopes, true.)*
> *(The girl shows her the night's chase — tomorrow's number already locked, her name standing in it again, the libel unrelenting — and Rose bends to it with the composure of a woman greeting an old adversary. She touches the cold chase once, briefly: the truth, metal, re-felt, the cold confirming what the night before established. Around her the work goes on — the press never stopping, the men feeding it — and she stands at the stone in her severe dress with her lamp and understands the evening's strange honor: they have made room for her at the stone as if she belonged there. Not a lady slumming. The law, come to inspect its instruments. She takes the stairs to the back room with Pettifer, where the idle press waits under its sheet, and the night's true business begins.)*
> *(Behind her the chapel settles back to its rhythm, and she hears it as she climbs: the thump, the murmur, the girl's soft humming resumed. She has been read by the type and — the nods told her — read true. Whatever the back room holds, she carries the chapel's reading with her like a character reference: the law, recognized. It will matter in the room above, where the idle press waits and Pettifer has something to say that he would not say on the floor.)*

> 1. [examine]"The press at night, dressed" — the return, seen. → Remembered: Her second arrival; the chapel knows her now.
> 2. [social]Pettifer's "you came back" — the welcome. → Remembered: How the trade receives return; the nod deepens.
> 3. [micro]"The severe dress, perfected" — the reading. → Remembered: How the chapel reads her; the law, recognized.
> 4. [examine]Walk the floor "like an inspection" — the law, touring. → Remembered: Her circuit; the machines are mustered.
> 5. [stance]Be read by the type — "to be read *by* it." → Remembered: The inversion; she offers herself to the chapel's reading.
> 6. [social]The girl's curtsey — "the apprentice's respect." → Remembered: How the young honor her; the curtsey is remembered.
> 7. [micro]Touch the cold chase — "the truth, metal," re-felt. → Remembered: The re-touch; the cold confirms.

scenes.synopsis: the week's numbers — the acceleration confirmed in type; "orders come down"; watching the stairs.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the back room, away from the floor's noise, Pettifer shows her the week's numbers — the press's private arithmetic, kept in a compositor's careful hand: impressions per night, reams ordered, the Lantern's run climbing week by week like a fever chart. She reads it with her new data sense — the clerk's eye the campaign has trained — and there it is, graphed in ink: the acceleration. Half again more, week on week, the curve steepening exactly as Creech's note promised. "Half again," she says quietly, and Pettifer nods: the increase, confirmed in type. The impatient purse's money, made legible in impressions. She copies the figures into the campaign book beside the copied libel — numbers beside words, the war's accounts balanced — and feels the strange satisfaction of the clerk: the enemy's extravagance, documented.)*
> *("Who orders the increase?" she asks — plainly, the way she asked for the stone, the unaskable asked as if it were ordinary. Pettifer is quiet a long moment, his ink-stained fingers tracing the edge of the paper. "Orders come down, miss." The answer's shape, and its limit: orders descend, origins don't. No name. No face. Only the purse, unfaced, at the top of the stairs that no compositor climbs. She takes the shape of the answer without pressing past it — her interrogation style, learned at Augusta's table: press the question and you close the source; accept the shape and the source stays open. "Then we watch the stairs," she says, and the doctrine states itself: patience, positioned. The stairs are the watchpoint. Whatever comes down them — orders, coin, the purse's own errands — will be seen.)*
> *(She promises him, there in the paper-smelling dark with the idle press under its sheet beside them: "No names in my book, Pettifer. Not yours, not the girl's, not the foreman's. The book holds the libel and the numbers — never the men." The protection, given plainly, and she sees the weight leave his shoulders: the compositor's fear, named and answered. They stand a moment in the quiet — the press's hunger audible through the wall, fed and feeding. Hunger explains heat: the press runs hot because it is fed hot. Cool the purse, and the press cools. The stairs. Watch the stairs.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read the week's numbers — "the acceleration, graphed." → Remembered: Her data sense; the numbers become a curve.
> 2. [micro]"Half again" — the increase, confirmed in type. → Remembered: The confirmation; Creech's note, verified.
> 3. [social]Ask Pettifer "who orders the increase" — the question. → Remembered: How she asks the unaskable; plainly.
> 4. [examine]Take his "orders come down" — the answer's shape. → Remembered: The shape; orders descend, origins don't.
> 5. [stance]"Then we watch the stairs" — the doctrine. → Remembered: Her patience; the stairs are the watchpoint.
> 6. [micro]Note "the paper's hunger" — the press, fed. → Remembered: Her economics; hunger explains heat.
> 7. [social]Promise Pettifer "no names in my book" — the protection. → Remembered: How she shields sources; the book protects.
> 8. [choice]Press the question, accept the shape, or change the subject. → Remembered: Her interrogation style; the choice sets its limits.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE COUNTER-NUMBER. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The back room of the press is paper stacked to the ceiling and a single press idle under its sheet, the sheet grey with dust in the lamplight — and Pettifer, quiet, laying the temptation plain the way he lays everything: without varnish. "You could print it here, miss. Tonight. A counter-number — your truth, in type, on the Lantern's own press. No one need know till morning." The words hang in the paper-smelling dark. The press that libels her could vindicate her: her words in the same type, on the same paper, crying the truth from the same corners where the hawkers cry the lie. Her campaign book is in her hand — the truth already written, already witnessed, already copied fair. It would take an hour. The girl could set it. By morning the town would read both.)*
> *(She stands in the dark and feels the weight of it entire: to use the enemy's machine is to become the enemy's kind — to fight libel with libel's own instruments, in the night, in secret. But to leave it unused — to walk past the idle press with the truth in her book and not set it — is its own kind of surrender, the surrender of the scrupulous to the unscrupulous. The idle press waits under its sheet like a held breath. Three roads lie open in the lamplight: use it, and be vindicated by morning at the cost of her clean hands; refuse it, and keep the war clean at the cost of the weapon; or the third road, the one Augusta would see from her morning room — buy the night's silence, pay for no record of her visit, and let the press forget she ever came. The sheet, the dark, the waiting machine. Choose.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The counter-number:*
- **Print the counter-number** — *Conduct+; the bold stroke.* Her truth in the Lantern's own type, on the street by morning. *(The town reads both; Pyke will know the press was turned.)*
- **Refuse the press** — *Composure+; the clean hands.* Walk past the idle machine; the truth stays in her book, not in type. *(Augusta approves; the war stays clean.)*
- **Buy the night's silence** — *Subtlety+; the quiet coin.* Pay for no record of her visit; the press forgets she came. *(Pettifer is protected; the night becomes rumor-proof.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: her restraint or her daring, weighed in the paper-smelling dark. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*
> **Turns (3):**
> 1. [examine]Hear Pettifer's temptation — the idle press, the counter-number by morning. → Remembered: The temptation; the machine, offered in the dark.
> 2. [stance]Weigh the three roads — print it, refuse it, or buy the night's silence. → Remembered: Her weighing; clean hands against the weapon.
> 3. [choice]Choose, under the sheet's grey dust — the waiting machine, the held breath. → Remembered: The choosing; what the dark witnessed.

scenes.synopsis: the aftermath — the press under its sheet, decided; the night's two truths, carried home.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands a moment before the press under its sheet — decided, whatever she decided — and lays her hand on the sheet's dusty grey: the machine at rest, the held breath held or released. "Thank you, Pettifer," she says, and names the debt plainly: the guide, the numbers, the unaskable answered, the temptation offered without varnish. Debts named are debts honored — the household's way — and Pettifer receives it with the compositor's nod, the chapel's memory filing her among its own. On her glove, when she lifts the lamp, a smudge of ink: the night, marked. She looks at it and does not wipe it away. Let the glove carry the press home. Let the morning see it.)*
> *(She descends past the sleeping machines — the chapel at rest between runs, the great irons dreaming in the lamplight, the girl's chase covered for the night — and the floor she toured as the law releases her the way a church releases a parishioner: quietly, with the foreman's lifted chin and Pettifer's hand once more, briefly, on her sleeve. In the cab she sits with the night's two truths side by side in her lap: the libel, copied, witnessed, filed against the morning; and the choice, made in the paper-smelling dark, the idle press decided. Both truths, carried. The city, at last, asleep — the squares dark, the ton unconscious, the hawkers' corners empty till dawn. Only she is awake in it, with her lamp still lit and the ink on her glove and the campaign book heavy with the night.)*
> *(At home Augusta is asleep — the general's lamp out, the report to wait for breakfast — and Letitia has left cocoa warming, the household's faith that the commander returns. Rose sits in the morning room alone with the cooling cup and decides the counsel's timing: tonight's full report can wait for morning; the household sleeps better without the idle press in its dreams. She writes three lines in the campaign book — the date, the numbers, the decision, in her clearest hand — and closes it. The lamp gutters. The ink on her glove has dried. The night is filed. She climbs the stairs at last. Behind her the chapel settles to its idle ticking — the enemy's machines asleep, her name locked in their chases until morning.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]"The press under its sheet, decided" — the aftermath. → Remembered: How the decision sits; the sheet covers or reveals.
> 2. [social]Thank Pettifer — "the debt, named." → Remembered: How she honors guides; the debt is spoken.
> 3. [micro]"Ink on her glove" — the night, marked. → Remembered: The mark; the glove carries the press home.
> 4. [examine]Descend "past the sleeping machines" — the chapel, at rest. → Remembered: Her exit vision; the machines dream in iron.
> 5. [stance]Carry "the night's two truths" — the libel and the choice. → Remembered: What she brings home; both truths, carried.
> 6. [social]The cab home — "the city, asleep at last." → Remembered: Her night's end; the city sleeps, she doesn't.
> 7. [micro]"The lamp, still lit" — the instrument, kept. → Remembered: The lamp; it burns the whole campaign.
> 8. [choice]Report tonight, at breakfast, or never in full. → Remembered: Her counsel's timing; the choice paces the household.

scenes.synopsis: morning — the Gazette read first; the idle press reported; "today the alliance."
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes and reaches first for the Gazette, not the Lantern — the morning's discipline, chosen: read the ally before the enemy, Bell's dry steadiness before Pyke's heat. Bell's verdict on the week is characteristically precise — the proprietor's dry line falling like a paperknife: the town's appetite for the Hartwell libel noted, weighed, and found wanting in stamina. She reads it twice, the way she read Creech's note, and feels the day right itself: Bell, publicly named proprietor from the first edition, holding the paper's line while the Lantern runs hot below. The ally, in print. The morning, begun correctly.)*
> *(At breakfast the debrief is complete — the idle press, reported: the back room, the sheet, Pettifer's offer laid plain, the decision made in the paper-smelling dark. She tells it all, the counsel's completeness, the household's right: Augusta listening without moving, Letitia with the chocolate pot suspended mid-pour at the words "counter-number." And Augusta's "then" — the general, approving, the single syllable landing like a commission. Whatever she chose in the dark, the household's law holds it: the war stays hers, the hands stay clean or the stroke stays bold, each by her own choosing. The ink, washed from the glove that morning, is gone; the night is filed. What remains is the day's doctrine, and she states it over the eggs: "Today the alliance.")*
> *(The pivot, spoken: from press to ally. The press has been read, witnessed, mapped; the purse behind it remains blank and trembling at the map's center. But wars are not won on ground alone — they are won on alliance, and Lavinia Crane has been signaling since the card. She weighs the approach the way she weighed the veil: write to Lavinia, call on Lavinia, or wait for Lavinia to come to her. Each sets a different register. She chooses — the choice is the turn, and the turn is remembered — and the household assigns itself around the decision: Augusta to draft the terms, Letitia to ready the morning room. She takes up her pen and begins the day's first letter before the ink of the decision is dry. The alliance moves today. From card, toward contract.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Wake "to the Gazette, not the Lantern" — the morning's choice. → Remembered: Her morning discipline; she reads the ally first.
> 2. [micro]"Bell's verdict" — the proprietor's dry line. → Remembered: How she receives judgment; Bell's dryness steadies.
> 3. [social]Breakfast debrief — "the idle press, reported." → Remembered: Her counsel's completeness; the household hears all.
> 4. [examine]Augusta's "then" — the general, approving. → Remembered: The approval; it lands like a commission.
> 5. [stance]"Today the alliance" — the day's doctrine. → Remembered: The pivot; from press to ally.
> 6. [micro]"The ink, washed from the glove" — the night, filed. → Remembered: The washing; the mark was temporary, the record isn't.
> 7. [choice]Write Lavinia, call on Lavinia, or wait for Lavinia. → Remembered: How she approaches allies; the choice sets the register.

scenes.synopsis: the alliance — "Pyke must be broken, not bought"; from card to contract; the white rose, shared.
scenes.prose:
> *(Lavinia's card arrives with the morning post — the ally, signaling: a single line in her slanted hand, "At the morning-room hour, if it suits," and the morning-room hour is eleven, and it suits. Rose receives her in the morning room with the campaign book closed on the desk between them — neutral ground, deliberately — and studies Lavinia's dress the way Lavinia studies everyone: costumed, intentional, the ally dressed for negotiation in dove grey with a severity that answers Rose's own. They take tea. They circle. And then Lavinia sets down her cup and speaks the agenda plainly, the way she does everything: "Pyke must be broken, Miss Hartwell. Not bought." The terms, laid like a card. Broken — the press turned, the libel starved, the sly proprietor undone by his own arithmetic. Not bought — never purchased, never owned, never Pyke's creature wearing her coin.)*
> *("Then we are agreed," says Rose, and the compact speaks itself into being — no lawyers, no papers, the spoken compact, the chapter's hinge. From card to contract: what was a signal becomes an operation. They talk terms the way generals talk supply: Lavinia's knowledge of Pyke's creditors and habits, Rose's witness of the stone and the stairs, the purse's blank center between them like a map neither can yet fill. And on the table between them, in the plain vase Letitia keeps filled, the white rose — the floriography, shared: the clean name, the cause entire, blooming between the teacups. Lavinia looks at it, and something in her face — the ally with her own agenda, always — softens a fraction. "The clean name," she says. "Yes." It is the most honest thing either of them has said all morning.)*
> *(There remains the calibration — the oldest question of alliance: trust fully, trust with terms, or trust while verifying. Rose chooses with her eyes open, Augusta's counsel in her head: Lavinia wants Pyke broken, and that is true; Lavinia has her own agenda, and that is also true; both can be true at once, and the compact can hold them both. They part at noon with the contract unspoken but operational — the next move Lavinia's, the watchword the white rose. At the door Lavinia pauses. "Miss Hartwell — the press taught you its trade. Now teach it yours." She goes, dove grey into the square's light, and Rose stands in the morning room with the white rose on the table and the alliance, at last, under way.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read Lavinia's card — "the ally, signaling." → Remembered: Her reading of allies; the card is a semaphore.
> 2. [social]Receive her "at the morning-room hour" — the call. → Remembered: How she hosts alliance; the morning room is neutral ground.

> 6. [social]"From card to contract" — the chapter's hinge. → Remembered: The escalation; the alliance becomes operational.

scenes.synopsis: the square's morning round — the ton observed; the libel "quoted, and doubted"; the waverers, courted.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the square's morning round with Letitia — the ton's parade ground, observed at the fashionable hour: the carriages, the callers, the promenaders performing the morning's business of being seen. And she is seen, deliberately: the living refutation, worn lightly, the lady against whom the libel is written walking the square as if libels were weather. The greetings come with the new carefulness — the town, adjusting: nods a fraction warmer than last week, smiles a fraction less guarded, the carefulness itself a kind of progress. She counts the nods the way she counted the hawkers — the census, continued, the social accounting — and the ledger balances in her favor. The town is recalibrating. The libel's interest is compounding in reverse.)*
> *(At the bookstall she hears it — the turn, audible: her libel quoted, and doubted. Two matrons with the Lantern between them, the elder reading aloud the week's venom, the younger interrupting: "But is it true? It was true last month, was it not, and then it wasn't." Doubt, entering the quotation like light under a door. She walks on without breaking stride, lightness itself, and lets the doubt do its work unattended — the waverers, courted not by argument but by composure. At the corner she stops to speak with the doubters' set: three callers, two curates, a widow of influence — the middle of the ton, the prize ground — and is simply, radiantly ordinary with them — asking after the widow's garden, laughing at the curates' parish news. No pleading. No performance. The living refutation, worn so lightly it looks like ease.)*
> *(Home by noon, she reports the round to Augusta with the satisfaction of a scout: quoted and doubted, the nods counted, the waverers warming. "Press the advantage, hold the ground, or retreat to dignity?" Augusta asks — the general's question — and Rose answers it with the week's new tempo: hold the ground, and let the doubt compound. The libel is tiring the town faster than it is tiring her. That is the arithmetic that matters now — not the purse's half-again, but the town's half-attention, waning. She writes it in the campaign book under the date: "The town tires. Hold." And holds.)*

> 6. [social]Call on the doubters — "the waverers, courted." → Remembered: How she works the middle; the waverers are the prize.

scenes.prose:
> *(In the evening she spreads the campaign map on the morning-room table and confronts the blank center — the purse, unfaced, unnamed, the one space her clearest hand has never filled. Creech stands by with his report: the gold's roads, walked — the warehouse, the carriers, the clerks with scarred knuckles — and every road walked ends the same way: not at Pyke's office. The payment traced, confirmed, documented: not Pyke's coin. The press takes the purse's money; the press is not the purse. Someone else's purse — deep, impatient, half again more this week than last — pays for her ruin, and the face behind the purse stays offstage, unmoved, unseen. She looks at the blank a long moment, and it trembles — the paper seeming to feel what she feels: the pressure of the unfaced, the weight of the unnamed.)*
> *("Deep and impatient," she says aloud, and the characterization settles: the purse has depth — it can pay half again without blinking — and it has impatience — it pays half again because it wants the ruin now, not later. Depth and impatience together are a profile: not a miser hoarding, but a power spending. She writes it on the map's margin in her clearest hand — "deep and impatient; not Pyke's coin; half again" — and the blank, annotated, trembles a little less. The enemy, redefined: the war has two fronts now, the press below and the purse above, and she has mapped the first entirely — the stone, the stairs, the office — while the second remains a blank with a pulse. Augusta studies the margin note and nods once. "Two fronts," she says. "Good. One front is a trap. Two fronts is a campaign.")*
> *(They aim the strategy at the blank the way one aims at a target in fog: hunt the purse — spend the lean coin on riders and informants; watch the purse — post the stairs, the roads, the gold's carriers; or starve the purse — make the libel so unprofitable, so doubted, so tired, that the deep purse finds deeper water elsewhere. She chooses — the turn, remembered — and the choice aims the campaign's next week: the map's center may stay blank, but the campaign no longer orbits the press alone. It orbits the blank. And the blank, in the lamplight, is afraid of being filled — which is why it pays half again to keep her from filling it. She steadies her hand over it, and the trembling stops where her fingers rest.)*

> 2. [micro]"The trembling" — the paper, seeming to feel. → Remembered: The image; the blank has a pulse.

scenes.synopsis: the record, growing — the week's libel bound; the town tiring; the doctrine reaffirmed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's libel, bound: she binds it herself on Sunday evening, the seven numbers stitched with a clerk's neat hand — the record, growing into a volume. Beside each number, in the margin, the mis-set e's collected: the errors, filed, the libel's machinery confessing week by week. Quill comes to see the file and pronounces it with the solicitor's relish: "The file grows teeth." The law, pleased with the archive. The teeth are not for biting — the doctrine holds, we do not sue the press — but teeth show, and the showing is the point. A filed libel is a libel with a future; a bound week is a week that will be answered. She runs her hand over the stitched spine and feels the campaign book's younger sibling: the war, acquiring a body.)*
> *(And the town, tiring — the fatigue, measured across the week's patrols: the hawkers crying a fraction less eagerly, the matrons quoting a fraction less certainly, the waverers wavering toward her. She polls it the way she polls everything — nods counted, greetings weighed, the doubt at the bookstall compounding — and the measurement holds: fatigue is the ally, and the ally is winning. "We are clerks," she says to Augusta, reaffirming the doctrine over the bound volume, and the register holds: read, copy, file, outlast. No lawsuits. No counter-numbers in the night — or the counter-number, if she chose it, standing as the one bold stroke among the clerk's work. Either way, the doctrine is the spine: the stitched spine, the moral spine, the same.)*
> *(Letitia brings supper to the morning room — "the house is proud," she says, setting down the tray, the domestic front served warm — and the three of them eat among the files like a staff among its maps. The campaign book, thickening on the desk: the volume, felt in the hand, the war's body growing denser week by week. She rests her hand on it and makes the week's last decision — rest the campaign, press the campaign, or vary it — and chooses the tempo the town's fatigue suggests: vary, and watch. The week is bound. The file has teeth. The town tires. And the clerks, she thinks, closing the book, are winning.)*

scenes.synopsis: the summons — Lavinia's card, the unusual hour; "the contract calls."
scenes.prose:
> *(The invitation is unexpected — the card arriving with the afternoon post, Lavinia's slanted hand, the hour unusual: not the morning-room hour but eight in the evening, and the place unnamed, "where we met," which means the place is serious. She reads it twice, the way she reads everything now — the card weighed like evidence: the ally, writing; the timing, noted; the discretion, read. Unusual hours mean urgency. Unnamed places mean the contract is moving from speech to operation. She holds the card to the lamplight a moment, unnecessarily — the hand is recognized, the seal is Lavinia's — and feels the chapter's hinge turning under her fingers: from card to contract was the morning's work; tonight is the contract's first test.)*
> *(She answers at once — the answer's tempo is the message, and hesitation would be read: "At eight, then. Where we met." Augusta receives the report with the general's economy: "the contract calls," says Rose, and Augusta nods, already reaching for the campaign book. "Take the white rose," says Letitia, appearing with the plain vase's freshest bloom — the token, carried: the clean name goes with her, a sentence in floriography the ally will read at once. She pins it at her wrist, over the severe dress's cuff — the law's dress again tonight, though softened for the evening — and studies herself in the hall mirror: the commander, answering the ally's summons. Not eager. Not reluctant. Ready.)*
> *(The manner of answering remains — go openly, go quietly, or send word first — and she chooses the way she chose the knock at the press: directly, but not loudly. The cab, not the carriage. The side entrance, not the square's eyes. The alliance is operational now, and operational things move quietly. She rides through the evening city with the white rose at her wrist and the campaign book in her reticule, and understands what the summons means: Lavinia has something — the creditors, the lever, the first intelligence of the compact. Tonight she will learn what "broken, not bought" costs. Tonight the contract begins. The white rose at her wrist seems, in the cab's lamplight, to glow — the clean name, going with her into the evening's business.)*

> 1. [examine]"The invitation, unexpected" — the card, read. → Remembered: Her reading of surprises; the card is weighed.
> 2. [social]"Lavinia's hand" — the ally, writing. → Remembered: How the ally writes; the hand is recognized.

scenes.synopsis: the terms — Pyke's creditors laid out; "broken, not bought," reaffirmed; the compact, detailed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The room is chosen — the meeting's ground, and the ground is the message: a private parlor above a bookseller's, neutral, book-lined, the table already laid with papers. Lavinia rises as Rose enters — "you came," the welcome weighed, warmth measured exactly — and gestures to the papers on the table: the contract, material, given a body. Not legal papers. Better: intelligence. Ledgers' shadows, creditors' names, the paper's debts mapped in Lavinia's slanted hand. "Pyke's creditors are mine to know," says Lavinia, laying it out like a hand of cards. "The press's stairs are yours to watch. Between us — the paper." She looks up. "Broken, Miss Hartwell. Not bought." The agenda, reaffirmed, the terms holding like a seal.)*
> *(Rose studies the creditors' names — the intelligence, held carefully, each name a lever: the paper merchant owed three quarters, the ink supplier paid late twice, the landlord of the press building with a mortgage coming due. Pyke's sly empire, balanced on other men's patience. "He prints," says Rose slowly, "because he must. The press never stops because the debts never stop." "Now you see it," says Lavinia. "Break the credit, and the press breaks. No libel without paper. No paper without credit." The terms, spoken and detailed: Lavinia works the creditors — pressure, purchase of debt, the squeeze applied with a lady's discretion; Rose watches the stairs and the street, the witness the creditors will need. The compact, operational at last. Not friendship — compact. The overlap is the alliance: Lavinia wants Pyke broken, Rose wants the libel starved.)*
> *(And the rest — Lavinia's agenda, entire — sits between them unspoken, the price: the ally wants more than Pyke's breaking, has always wanted more, and the more is not named tonight. Rose weighs it with the campaign book open in her lap, the white rose at her wrist: sign and gain the lever, hold and keep the war clean, or write the contract herself, in her own hand, on her own terms. The room waits — book-lined, lamplit, the creditors' names on the table like pieces on a board. The compact's seal is the evening's question. And the game — and Lavinia, watching — waits for her answer.)*

> 1. [examine]"The room, chosen" — the meeting's ground. → Remembered: Her reading of ground; the room is the message.

> 4. [examine]"Pyke's creditors" — the intelligence, laid out. → Remembered: Her intelligence work; the creditors are the lever.
> 5. [stance]"Broken, not bought" — the agenda, reaffirmed. → Remembered: The reaffirmation; the terms hold.
> 6. [social]"The terms, spoken" — the compact, detailed. → Remembered: How the compact is detailed; spoken, witnessed.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE CONTRACT. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The terms lie on the table between them — Lavinia's intelligence, Rose's witness, the purse's blank center presiding over both like an empty chair. "Pyke's creditors are mine to know," says Lavinia, her finger resting on the names. "The press's stairs are yours to watch. Between us, the paper." The contract, spoken: not friendship — compact. Lavinia wants Pyke broken; Rose wants the libel starved. The overlap is the alliance, clean and operational. The rest — Lavinia's agenda, entire, the more she has always wanted and never named — is the price, sitting beside the teacups like a third guest. The white rose stands in its vase between them. The clean name. The cause entire, blooming over the creditors' names.)*
> *(She weighs it with the campaign book open in her lap, Augusta's counsel in her head and the week's whole education behind her eyes: the stone, the chase, the cold truth metal, the idle press under its sheet. Sign Lavinia's terms and gain the creditors' lever — the squeeze on Pyke's debts, the press broken by its own arithmetic — but advance Lavinia's unnamed agenda with her own. Hold to her own counsel and keep the war clean — thank the ally, keep the campaign independent — but leave the lever lying on the table. Or the third road, the boldest: write the contract herself, in her own hand, on her own paper, dictating the terms the way she dictated the knock at the press. Three roads. The white rose. The waiting ally. Choose.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The contract:*
- **Sign Lavinia's terms** — *Subtlety+; the ally's lever.* Take the creditors' intelligence; move against Pyke's debts. *(Lavinia's agenda advances with hers; the price comes later.)*
- **Hold her own counsel** — *Composure+; the clean war.* Thank Lavinia; keep the campaign independent. *(Augusta approves; the alliance cools to cordial.)*
- **Write the contract herself** — *Conduct+; the bold stroke.* Dictate the terms in her own hand; the alliance on her paper. *(Lavinia respects the nerve; the compact bears Rose's seal.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: her pen, her terms, the weight she gave the ally's agenda. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the compact, sealed — "then we begin"; the creditors' names, held; the war, widened.
scenes.prose:
> *(The contract, sealed — whatever the seal: signed, shaken, nodded, or written in her own hand. Lavinia receives it with the ally's full attention — no triumph, she notes with approval; triumph would have been vulgar, and Lavinia is never vulgar. "Then we begin," says Lavinia, and the commencement has the quiet of all real beginnings: no fanfare, only the papers gathered, the creditors' names copied into the campaign book in Rose's clearest hand, the white rose left standing in its vase on the table between them — the token, placed: the clean name stays, presiding over the compact. They part in the bookseller's lamplight with the operational details settled: Lavinia moves on the debts within the week; Rose holds the stairs and the street; the purse's blank center watched by both.)*
> *(She rides home with the creditors' names held carefully in the book — the intelligence, carried like a dispatch: the paper merchant, the ink supplier, the landlord with the mortgage. Leverage, in manuscript. The war, widened: no longer the press alone, but the credit beneath the press — the money under the ink. She understands, riding through the dark squares, what Lavinia has given her: not just names, but the press's true anatomy. Pyke prints because he must. Stop the must, and the printing stops. It is the same lesson as the stone, learned from above instead of below: who pays for the paper chooses the truth, and the paper is paid for on credit.)*
> *(Augusta receives the detailed report with the general's full attention — the contract, detailed: the terms, the seal, the creditors, the timetable — and her nod, when it comes, has the particular degree that means approved-with-reservations: the ally's agenda, entire, noted in the margin. "Watch the price," says Augusta. "Levers have handles, and handles are held." "I am watching," says Rose. And the tempo is set — move at once, prepare, or wait for Lavinia's signal — the choice pacing the alliance's first week. She writes it in the book under the date: "The compact holds. The war widens. Watch the price." Tomorrow, the work begins in earnest. The chapter's hinge, turned and oiled.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week's end — the chapter's accounts; the press cooling; the compact, tested.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's end, and she balances the chapter's accounts in the campaign book the way a clerk balances a ledger: the press — read, witnessed, mapped, its stairs watched; the purse — traced to its blank center, not Pyke's coin, deep and impatient, half again; the alliance — moved from card to contract, the creditors' names held, the compact operational. Creech reports the stairs watched — the watch posted, the eyes in place — and the quiet beyond it: no new gold on the roads, the purse holding its hand, the paper's hunger the only hunger in motion. She writes it down — "No new gold" — and reads the quiet the way Augusta reads ground: quiet means the purse is waiting. Waiting, for the libel to work, or for her to err.)*
> *(And the press, cooling — the temperature, taken across the week's patrols: the hawkers crying a fraction less eagerly, the run's heat lessening as Lavinia's squeeze begins on the creditors. Her thermometry holds: hunger explains heat, and the credit is tightening. "The alliance, working," she writes — the compact, tested in its first week, holding: Lavinia's note confirms the creditors pressed, the paper merchant paid late, the ink supplier asking questions. The white rose, fresh in its vase — the token, renewed, the clean name persisting through the week's whole campaign. She looks at it and understands the week's true balance: the press cools, the purse waits, the alliance works. The clerks are winning.)*
> *(There remains the week's summary — write it, or let the book speak — and she chooses the clerk's way: she writes it, in her clearest hand, the week's whole account on a single page. The record-keeping is the choice that closes the week: the book, complete, the chapter balanced. She closes the campaign book on the summary and feels the week's weight in her hand — thickening, the war's body — and the satisfaction, quiet and entire, of accounts kept honestly. The week is filed. Augusta reads the summary over her shoulder and nods once — the general's approval, sparingly given and therefore priceless. "A good week, child. The press read, the purse traced, the alliance sealed. Few campaigns can show so much for seven days." The compact holds. The press cools. And the blank center of the map trembles on, unfaced, in the lamplight.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week's correspondence — the forms of address weighed; the letters' dress, chosen.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's correspondence lies drafted on her desk — the letters, the campaign's other army: to Quill, the file's progress; to Lavinia, the compact's courtesies; to the waverers, the quarter's civilities. And over them all, the question of the forms of address — the etiquette, weighed like coin: a letter's direction is its first sentence, and the town reads first sentences closely. "Mr. Quill" — clerkly, exact, the law's own address, the solicitor filed correctly. "My dear Lavinia" — the alliance, honored, the compact's own warmth, the ally feeling the regard. "Madam" — distant, correct, the dignity armored for the doubtful. She weighs them the way she weighed the veil: each address a sentence, each sentence a strategy. Augusta's eye proofs the drafts — the general's final review — and finds them clean.)*
> *(She chooses the letters' dress with the care she gave the proof's presentation — the form carries, always: the plain direction for the solicitor, the warm for the ally, the formal for the town. The seal, chosen last: her own seal, the Hartwell seal, pressed firmly — the signature's weight, the name owned in wax. She thinks of the white rose at her wrist in the bookseller's parlor, of the severe dress in the chapel, of every form she has chosen this chapter: the law, not the lady; the clerk, not the combatant; the compact, not the friendship. The correspondence is the campaign in miniature — every letter a troop, every address a maneuver. And the game will remember — and so will the recipients.)*
> *(Letitia brings the sealing wax — the household's own, deep red — and watches the seal pressed on each letter with the satisfaction of a quartermaster seeing stores dispatched. "The plain for the solicitor," she murmurs, checking the direction. "The warm for the ally. The formal for the town." She knows the system already; the household learns fast. Augusta proofs the last letter with a single correction — a comma, moved — the general's final review, and nods. The correspondence, dressed and sealed, waits in a neat stack for the postboy: the campaign's other army, mustered and ready.)*
> *(The post, dispatched at dusk — the send-off: the letters going like troops into the evening, the seal flashing on each. She stands at the window and watches the postboy turn the corner, and feels the week's correspondence move out into the town like skirmishers ahead of the line. Tomorrow the solicitor files, the ally reads, the town notes the form. The letters are the campaign. The campaign, posted, is under way.)*
