scenes.synopsis: the Gazette's week — Bell holds the line; the doubt compounding; the living refutation, continued.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette's week, read whole on Sunday — the ally, in print: Bell holds the line with the proprietor's dry steadiness, the week's numbers noting the Lantern's heat without naming it, the town's fatigue with the Hartwell subject observed, weighed, and gently confirmed. Bell's dryness, savored like chocolate: the tone that steadies, the judgment that never shouts. She reads the week's verdicts twice — the reading of allies, careful — and understands what Bell is doing: not defending her, never defending her — simply declining to find her interesting as a scandal, which in the Gazette's dry arithmetic is the same as acquittal. The ally, in print. The line, held.)*
> *(She clips the week's verdicts and pastes them into the campaign book — the ally's line, preserved: Bell on the Lantern's heat, Bell on the town's fatigue, Bell on the lady's composure. The clippings accumulate week by week, the Gazette's dry arithmetic building its own case for her. "The paper," Augusta observes, reading over her shoulder, "is writing your vindication for you, and charging you nothing for the ink." "The paper," says Rose, smoothing the last clipping, "is writing the truth. I am merely giving it the material.")*
> *(And the town, reading both — the papers, compared across the week's patrols: the Lantern bought for the libel, the Gazette bought for the belief, the town comparing the two the way it compares everything, idly and constantly. The doubt, compounding: the matron at the bookstall, the younger interrupting — "But is it true?" — the interest on the doubt accumulating week by week. She polls it, the census continuing: the nods warmer, the greetings easier, the carefulness itself warming into something like regard. The living refutation, continued — worn lightly, as always: the square's morning round, the bookstall's unhurried browsing, the ordinary radiance. The visibility doctrine holds: lightness carries it.)*
> *(There remains the question of thanks — acknowledge Bell, or let the paper speak — and she chooses the way she chose everything this chapter: the clerk's way. No letter. No visit. Only, at the week's end, the Gazette's bill paid promptly with a note of the plainest courtesy — the gratitude's form, styled as business. Bell will read it correctly: the ally, acknowledged, the paper left to speak. She writes it in the book: "The doubt compounds. Bell holds. The town compares — and chooses, slowly, the cooler paper." The week's polling, filed. The living refutation, renewed for another week.)*

scenes.synopsis: the squeeze, working — Pyke's temper fraying; the press's paper thinning; "broken, not bought," advancing.
scenes.prose:
> *(The creditors, squeezed — Lavinia's work, reported midweek: the paper merchant paid late and asking for terms, the ink supplier sending the second notice, the landlord's mortgage coming due with the quarter. She reads Lavinia's note with the satisfaction of the economist: the lever, working. And Pyke's temper — the enemy, pressed — shows the strain the way sly men's strain always shows: not in anger, but in the affability's thinning. The week's Lantern carries it: the libel still hot, but the paper thinner — literally thinner, the shortage showing in the stock — and the venom, she notes with her proofreader's eye, a fraction less precise. Hunger explains heat; and now the hunger is Pyke's own. The press's paper, thinning: thin paper, thin libel.)*
> *(She walks the paper's roads and sees it: the hawkers with fewer sheets, the corners crying a shorter hour, the Lantern's heat cooling for lack of fuel. "Broken, not bought" — the agenda, advancing: no coin of hers in Pyke's pocket, no purchase, no ownership — only the creditors' patience, exhausted on schedule. The detail that tells her most: the paper merchant, paid late, telling Creech's man that the Lantern's order is cut by a third. A third. The libel, starved at the source. She writes it in the book — "the order, cut by a third" — and feels the campaign's economics turn: the purse pays half again for ruin, but the ruin's instrument is being repossessed by its own debts.)*
> *(She closes the book on the week's economics and feels the campaign's balance shift — the purse can pay half again forever, but the press it pays for is being repossessed by its own debts. That is the arithmetic that will end the war: not the purse's depth, but the press's credit. Lavinia understood it first. The stairs taught it second. The thinned paper proves it third.)*
> *(And the price, watched — Augusta's counsel, the margin note: levers have handles, and handles are held. She watches Lavinia's agenda the way she watches the stairs: the ally wants Pyke broken, and Pyke is breaking — but the breaking serves the ally's more, unnamed, entire. The calibration — press harder, hold steady, or ease off — is the week's last decision, and she chooses the general's tempo: hold steady. The squeeze works; the press thins; the libel cools. Enough. She writes it under the date: "Broken, not bought — advancing. The price, watched." And the chapter's economics, balanced: the purse deep, the press thinning, the town tiring.)*

scenes.synopsis: the season, continuing — the honorable suitor; "the war first"; the heart, managed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The suitors, waiting — the season, continuing underneath the war like a river under ice: Lord Henry Beaumont calls on Tuesday, honorable as ever, and admires the campaign with the clean admiration of an honorable man. "The campaign, admired," he says over tea — not the libel, never the libel; the work, the witness, the nerve of it. She receives the admiration the way she receives everything from him: with the warmth it deserves and the boundary it requires. The flowers he brings are white — the floriography, continued, the clean name in blooms — and she sets them with the others, the season's language accumulating in vases. He does not press. Honorable men never press; they wait, and the waiting is its own kind of speech.)*
> *(He takes his leave with the white flowers left in her hands — the floriography, entrusted: the clean name, in blooms, to be set with the others in the morning room's vases. At the door he turns. "Miss Hartwell — when the war is won, I hope the season will still be here." "The season," she says, "is very patient, my lord. It has waited for better causes than mine." He laughs, and the laugh is the honorable man's whole courtship: no pressure, only hope, offered lightly and withdrawn lightly. She watches him go down the square with the strange, quiet ache of the commander who cannot yet accept the gift — the heart, managed, but not untroubled.)*
> *(She observes the season's business with her clear eye — the marriage market, continuing: the other girls' campaigns, the mamas' maneuvers, the whole bright machinery of the ton turning while her own war runs beneath it. "The war first," she says to Augusta afterward — the priority, stated plainly: the libel starved, the press mapped, the purse still blank at the center. The heart, managed. Beaumont's patience — the suitors' patience, all of them honorable, all of them waiting — is a gift she cannot yet open, and she tells him so with the honesty honor deserves: "My lord, the war first. The season — after." He bows, and the bow says everything: understood, accepted, waiting. The honorable, waiting.)*
> *(There remains the management — encourage, deflect, or postpone — and she chooses the way she has chosen all chapter: directly, kindly, without cruelty and without promise. A letter, warm but bounded. A dance, accepted for the future. The season, paced by the war's own tempo. She writes it in the book, not as strategy but as record: "The season continues. The war first." And the white flowers, in their vases, keep the floriography current: the clean name, blooming, while the heart waits its hour.)*

scenes.synopsis: the opera — the living refutation at culture; the libel unmentioned; the interval, worked.
scenes.prose:
> *(The opera, attended — the visibility, at its most deliberate: the box, noticed, the living refutation at culture. She dresses for it with the week's new armor — the town will read the dress, and the dress must say: unbowed — and takes the box with Augusta and Letitia, the household entire, the campaign's colors flying in the most public room in London. The box performs: heads turn, glasses lift, the whispers move like weather. And the libel — unmentioned. The discipline, absolute: no one speaks of it, no one needs to; the living refutation is worn, not argued. She sits in the box's lamplight, composed, entire, and lets the town read her the way the chapel read her: truly.)*
> *(The music, heard — the evening, genuinely enjoyed, because the war has not killed the music and she will not let it: the soprano's aria, the orchestra's swell, the strange, private joy of beauty in the middle of a campaign. The composure, complete — the performance, perfected: composure is the costume, and she wears it the way she wore the severe dress, exactly. At the interval she works the room — the waverers, courted at culture: the doubters' set, the matrons, the young men of influence, all greeted with the lightness that carries the refutation. No pleading. No performance beyond the being-there. The interval, worked like the square's morning round, the campaign's social front advanced one conversation at a time. The young men of influence ask after the campaign book — they have heard of it, the town's curiosity outrunning discretion — and she smiles the living refutation's smile: "A lady's diary, gentlemen. Nothing so martial." They laugh, delighted, and she lets them — the book's true nature safe behind the smile.)*
> *(The evening's shape remains — stay for supper, leave early, or hold the box — and she chooses the commander's exit: the full evening, the supper, the unhurried departure, the town seeing her see the town. She rides home with the music still in her head and the week's armor approved by every glass in the house, and writes it in the book: "The opera. The libel unmentioned. The town, reading." The living refutation, at culture. The war, continued in evening dress.)*

scenes.synopsis: the next armor — the week's dress reviewed; the severe dress honored; the town will read it.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's dress, reviewed in the wardrobe's lamplight — the armor, assessed piece by piece: the severe dress, the law's costume, honored now and retired a hero — it walked the chapel, it faced Pyke, it was read true by the type. She touches its black depth once, gratefully, and hangs it with care: the weapon cleaned and put away, ready for the next night's work. And the next armor — the form, chosen for the week's new phase: the press thins, the town tires, the alliance works, and the campaign's dress must say it. Not the law now. The lady — the lady entire, unbowed, the season's armor over the war's foundation. Augusta's verdict, final as always: "The town reads dress, child. Give it a true text.")*
> *(The white rose, worn — the floriography, on the person: whatever she chooses, the clean name goes with her, pinned at the wrist or the shoulder, the season's signature. She stands before the mirror and considers the three armors the week has earned: the Hartwell blue, the house color, the name worn openly; the defiant jewel tone, emerald unapologetic, the spirit dressed for the town's eyes; the quiet grey, the clerk's color, the war continued in discipline. Each with its motif, its thread, its colorway, its accessories — each a sentence the town will parse. The mirror, consulted: the final survey, the town's reading anticipated. And the game will remember — and so will the ton.)*
> *(Augusta considers the three armors with the general's eye — the house color, the jewel tone, the clerk's grey — and delivers her verdict with the finality of a commander issuing orders. "The blue," she says. "The house color. The town reads the house, and the house is winning." Letitia disagrees, gently: "The emerald. The spirit, dressed. The town loves nerve." They look at Rose. The decision is hers — the turn, remembered — and she weighs it the way she has weighed everything this chapter: what will the town read, and what does she mean to say? The mirror waits. The week has earned its armor.)*
> *(She chooses — the turn, remembered — and the choice is the week's last fashion decision: the armor for the phase ahead, the text the town will read. The dress laid out, the rose pinned, the mirror confirming. Tomorrow the town reads.)*

scenes.synopsis: the week's close — the map updated; the book closed; the next chapter, opened.
scenes.prose:
> *(The map, updated — the week's intelligence, in her clearest hand: the press mapped entire, the stairs watched, the creditors squeezed, the paper thinned, the town tiring. And the blank center — the purse, still unfaced, still unnamed — trembling on in the lamplight, the one space the week could not fill. Creech's last report closes the week: the roads quiet, no new gold, the purse holding its hand. She studies the blank a long moment — the enemy, still offstage — and writes beneath it the week's final annotation: "Deep and impatient. Not Pyke's coin. Half again. Waiting." The blank, annotated, trembles a little less. The map is current. The war has a shape.)*
> *(The press, thinned — the squeeze's result, confirmed: the Lantern's order cut by a third, the hawkers' hour shortened, the libel starving at the source. The compact, holding — the alliance, tested and entire: Lavinia's lever working, the price watched, the contract operational. The household, steady — the domestic front, unbroken: Augusta's counsel, Letitia's cocoa, the campaign book thickening on the desk. Quill's filed proof. Lavinia's creditors' names. The bound libel, stitched. The map, current. The alliance, operational. She lists them in the book's margin like a general listing regiments — the week's order of battle, complete and accounted for. She surveys it all — the map, the book, the bound libel, the white rose fresh in its vase — and feels the chapter's accounts balance: the press read, the purse traced, the alliance sealed. The clerks are winning. The book, closed — the week, filed: she shuts the campaign book on the week's last page with the soft finality of a dispatch sealed.)*
> *(There remains the week's end decision — plan the next chapter, rest, or watch — and she chooses the commander's third way: watch, and plan while watching. The lamp burns low. The house sleeps. The campaign — the clerk's campaign, the law's campaign — keeps its quiet watch. The next chapter's ground is already visible: the purse, still blank; the press, still printing, though thinner; the town, still tiring. She writes the last line under the date: "The chapter closes. The campaign continues." And the book shuts, and the lamp gutters, and the blank center trembles on — waiting, like her, for the next move.)*

> 1. [examine]"The map, updated" — the week's intelligence. → Remembered: Her cartography; the map is current.

> 5. [stance]"The compact, holding" — the alliance. → Remembered: The holding; the contract endures.
> 6. [social]"The household, steady" — the domestic front. → Remembered: The steadiness; the house endures.

scenes.synopsis: the night's walk — the city at peace; the chapter's motto: "the law, not the lady."
scenes.prose:
> *(The night's walk — the city, at peace: she walks the square once before bed, the lamp unlit in her hand, the night air cool on her face. The press's thump, distant — the metronome, far now, the war receding to its proper distance: not in her feet any more, but on the horizon, where wars belong. The household, asleep behind her — the domestic peace, the house breathing evenly in the dark. She walks the square's perimeter slowly, the week's work weighed with each step: the stone, the chase, the office, the back room, the creditors, the compact. The accounts, balanced. The week, won — or, the clerk's honesty: the week, advanced. Wars are not won in weeks. But weeks are won, and this one was. The square's lamps burn steady. A cat crosses the pavement, unhurried, the night's only other pedestrian. She nods to it — the commander's courtesy to a fellow night-walker — and walks on.)*
> *("The law, not the lady" — the chapter's motto, spoken aloud to the empty square, the seal on the week's work. It has been the severe dress, the stone, the inspection, the creditors: the law, throughout. The lady attended the opera and walked the square — but the law did the work. She stands at the square's center with the distant thump under the night and understands the chapter entire: she went to the press to read the libel, and learned instead to read the press. Who sets the type chooses the truth. She has read the setters. She has bought no press. She has broken none — yet. But the credit thins, the paper thins, the libel thins. The law is patient. The law, she thinks, turning homeward, is winning.)*
> *(The lamp, guttering in her hand — the instrument, resting: she watches the flame lean and recover, lean and recover, the chapter's own rhythm. Sleep, write, or keep the vigil — the night's end choice — and she chooses the commander's mercy: sleep. The book is closed. The map is current. The blank trembles on, but the blank can wait till morning. She climbs the stairs with the guttering lamp and the week's whole weight, and the house receives her the way it receives all its soldiers: quietly, proudly, asleep.)*

> 1. [examine]"The night's walk" — the city, at peace. → Remembered: Her night vision, matured; the city rests.

> 6. [micro]"The lamp, guttering" — the instrument, resting. → Remembered: The lamp's rest; it gutters, spent.

scenes.synopsis: dawn — both papers read; the libel thinned; the fact, faced: "they have printed."
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette, at dawn — the ally's number, read first, as always: Bell's line, the verdict savored like the first chocolate — dry, precise, the week's campaign sealed in the proprietor's arch arithmetic. She reads it twice, the amusement first, then the reckoning, the morning's discipline. And then the Lantern, at dawn — the enemy's number, read second, the intelligence habit: the libel, thinned. The squeeze, in print. The paper literally thinner, the order cut by a third, the venom a fraction less precise. She holds the two papers side by side — the ally's steadiness, the enemy's starvation — and the week's economics lie visible in newsprint: the purse pays half again, but the press can barely print it.)*
> *("They have printed" — the fact, faced directly, the way she faces everything: the libel exists, the number is on the street, the hawkers are crying it at the corners. She does not flinch from the fact. Facts are the clerk's business, and the clerk's business this morning is to record: the number printed, the order cut by a third, the paper thinner, the venom less precise. The fact, documented, loses its terror — it becomes a line in the book, an entry in the accounts. They have printed. The book has recorded. The accounts balance.)*
> *(The household, waking around her — Augusta's pen already scratching, Letitia's step on the stair, the morning's ordinary music — and she greets the day with the week's earned register: clerk, commander, or lady — the morning's choice — and chooses, as she has chosen all chapter, the clerk's: read, copy, file, outlast. She takes up her pen and writes the day's first line — the date, the two papers' verdicts, the fact faced — before the household's morning properly begins. The clerk, at work. Letitia brings chocolate, unasked — the quartermaster's intelligence, reading the commander's morning. "The Lantern's thinner," she observes, glancing at the papers. "I noticed," says Rose. They smile, the household's quiet conspiracy of the competent. The two papers lie on the table. The fact is faced. And the answer — the chapter's whole answer, the campaign's whole doctrine — waits one scene more to be spoken. The morning, begun correctly — Gazette first, Lantern second, the clerk at work.)*

scenes.prose:
> *"The Lantern prints heat. The Gazette prints weather. Miss Hartwell reads both, and dresses accordingly."*
> *(The morning Gazette, read over chocolate. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, in her own dry voice — the week's verdict on the press war, arch and precise: the Lantern's acceleration noted, the town's fatigue noted, the lady's composure noted and, in Bell's dry arithmetic, found sufficient. No mystery. No hunt. Only the reward: the press read, the purse traced, the alliance sealed — and the proprietor making it all charming, which is Bell's way of making it permanent. Rose reads it twice, the amusement first, then the reckoning, and files the sting under its lesson: in London, a compliment in print is a fact in public.)*

scenes.synopsis: the chapter's seal — the press read, the purse traced, the alliance sealed; the line that is not a question.
scenes.prose:
> *(She stands at the window with the week's numbers in her hand — the Lantern, thinned; the Gazette, steady — and the chapter seals itself around her like wax around a letter. The stone. The chase. The cold truth, metal, in her fingertips' memory. The idle press under its sheet, decided — whatever she decided, decided. The creditors' names in the book, the squeeze working, the paper thinning. The white rose on the table, the compact sealed, the alliance operational. The campaign's accounts, balanced to the penny: the press read, the purse traced, the alliance sealed. The town tiring. The doubt compounding. Bell holding the line. The clerks, winning. The week's whole education stands behind her eyes: the knock in the alley, the chapel's honest noise, Pettifer's "this way, miss," the cold chase, the green lamps, the offer laid like a card, the idle press under its sheet, the creditors' names, the white rose. Every scene, filed. Every lesson, kept.)*
> *(Augusta's pen scratches in the morning room — the general, already planning. Letitia's laugh sounds in the drawing room — the quartermaster, at ease. The house, steady. The town, tiring. The press, cooling. And at the map's center, the blank — trembling still, unfaced still, waiting: the purse, deep and impatient, half again, holding its hand. She looks at it, and it looks back, and she understands the chapter's true seal: not the press, which she has read; not the alliance, which she has sealed; but the blank, which remains. The war's next front. The face offstage. The purse, waiting. It will move again — the deep purse always moves again — but the next move will find her ready: the stairs watched, the street walked, the alliance operational, the book open. Let it come.)*
> *(She turns from the map to the window, to the week's two papers on the sill, to the town beyond the glass going about its morning — and the chapter's last line writes itself, not a question, a fact, the whole campaign in six words — six words she has earned the way she has earned everything this chapter: by reading, by witnessing, by refusing to buy what cannot be bought:)*
> *(They have printed. I have read.)*

scenes.synopsis: midnight — today's number read; the hawkers' cries; the decision to buy the street's ears.
scenes.prose:
> *(Midnight, and she reads today's number by lamplight — the inversion, continued: they have printed, she has read, the seal become the campaign's habit. The Lantern's thinned pages lie on the morning-room table beside the Gazette's steady ones, and she reads both with the clerk's discipline — the enemy's number first, the ally's second, the facts faced before the comfort. The libel is thinner now, the paper literally thinner, Lavinia's squeeze showing in the stock — but the cries, she knows, are not thinner. What the press cannot print, the hawkers can cry. The street has a voice the paper does not control, and tonight, in the midnight quiet, she hears it for the first time as what it is: the war's next front.)*
> *(The hawkers' cries come up from the street even at this hour — the late criers, the last rounds, the town's voice refusing sleep: "Lantern! All about the Hartwell!" The rhyme of it, the rhythm, the way the name scans in the crier's chant. She stands at the window and listens, and understands the redefinition entire: the war has never been for the paper — the paper is only the script. The rhyme of it — the libel, versified: some ballad-monger in Pyke's pay has set the week's venom to a tune, and the cries scan now, the name fitting the meter like a stone in a shoe. She lies a moment listening — the dawn sense, the street waking her the way the press's thump once did — and understands the versification's meaning: the libel has left the paper. > *(The old crier holds the corner by the bookstall — the street's elder, sixty years crying, the senior independent of the district: she finds him at mid-morning, Creech's ledger her introduction, and the meeting has the formality of true diplomacy. He looks her over — the morning dress, the directness, the absence of flinching — and nods slowly. "You are the Hartwell girl." It is not a question. "I am the elder's," she says, surprising herself — the street's grammar, already learned: one belongs to one's corner. He laughs, a sound like paper tearing, and the ice — the street's ice — breaks.)*
> *(The first hawker, bought — the transaction, honest by Augusta's rule: not his cries — never his cries — but his time. A shilling for an hour's honest report: who buys the Lantern on his corner, who lingers, who turns away, what the town says when it thinks no lady listens. "Time, not trade," she says, and the elder repeats it slowly, tasting the distinction. "Time, not trade," he agrees. "Aye. That's honest." The elder's price — the rate, honored: the shilling paid upfront, the handshake sealing it. The street's first ear — the intelligence, begun: by noon he has told her three things worth the shilling twice over, and the street begins to report.)*
> *(the elder's round — the geography, walked with him in the afternoon: the corners, the coffee houses, the bookstall where the numbers are read aloud. He shows her the street the way the night ride showed her the press — the insider's tour, the trade's pride. And the street's honor — the code, explained as they walk: criers don't lie about the weather, don't short the change, don't cry what they haven't read. The street has honor, entire and fierce, the honor of men who live by their voice. She receives it with a commander's respect for another discipline — and understands the afternoon's lesson: the street is not the press's tool. The street is its own country, with its own laws.)*

One ear becomes a round; a round becomes a district; a district becomes the town's whole voice. Or the third road, the longest: let the cries run. Save the lean purse. Trust the town's fatigue, the doubt compounding, the rhyme tiring the way all rhymes tire. The handshake, again — but this one different: not a purchase, but a pact. The street seals simply. The cold hands — the winter, in the fingers: red-knuckled, chapped, the penny clutched in a fist that can barely close. She watches him cry the Lantern's rhyme — the libel, in a child's voice — and feels the war's cost entire: the purse's money, the press's venom, landing here, in a nine-year-old's frozen hands. Her notice; the youngest, seen. It is not intelligence. It is responsibility.)*
> *(The penny, warmed — the charity, conducted the way the household does everything: practically. She warms the penny in her glove before she gives it — the penny, warmed in her glove — and adds the shilling's honest price for the boy's hour: who buys on his corner, who listens, the small geography. The boy's round — the geography, small: the church corner, the rectory steps, the almshouses. The patch, walked with him while Letitia — summoned by a note — arrives with the quartermaster's mercy: the hot pie, wrapped in paper, pressed into the cold hands. How the household feeds: Letitia's pies, the domestic front's artillery. The hands, warmed — the result: the pie eaten, the penny warmed, the report given with a child's thoroughness.)*
> *(The street's children — the responsibility, recognized: the street has children, and the war is fought over their heads and through their hands. She understands, watching the boy eat, what the campaign owes the street: not just the shilling's honesty, but the commander's care. Help one, help the round, or help the street — the charity's scope, the choice that scales it: she starts with one — the boy, the pie, the warmed penny — but the choice is the turn, remembered. One becomes the round; the round becomes the street's young. She writes it in the book: "The street's youngest — pie, penny, report." The charity, filed like intelligence. The war, humanized.)*
> *(The boy's name is the lad — learned with the pie, kept like the others: the street's young, named. She will know them all before the chapter ends — the criers, the captains, the children. The street is not a battlefield only. It is a parish. And she — the commander of the clerks — is becoming its reluctant, responsible rector.)*

scenes.synopsis: the tally — cries counted, routes mapped; the street's arithmetic.
scenes.prose:
> *(The tally, Sunday evening — cries counted, the week's census: she sits with Creech and the elder in the morning room and counts the street the way a clerk counts coin. Cries counted, routes mapped — the arithmetic, entire: the Lantern's criers, forty-odd, crying six rounds a day; the Gazette's thirty, steady; the independents' dozen, the prize. The street's arithmetic — the totals, and what the totals tell: the Lantern out-cries the Gazette nearly two to one on the captain's corners, but the independents — the prize — cry both, and the both dilutes the venom. She sums it in the book, the totals in three inks: the street, summed. How the street sums: in cries, in corners, in ears.)*
> *(The Lantern's total — the enemy's sum, estimated from the tally: the purse's spend on cries, reckoned in pennies and shillings — half again the libel's cost, half again the cries. The purse's extravagance, made audible and now made legible. And the Gazette's total — the ally's sum: Bell's steady thirty, the steadiness counted, the truth's own tempo holding its corners. But the doubt's total — the true sum, the dividend that matters: the elder's report, the independents' reports, the lad's small geography — "they ask, miss; 'is it true?'" The doubt, spreading, compounding, the interest on the question accumulating. The true sum: not cries, but questions. The street's arithmetic pays its dividend in doubt.)*
> *(The tally, shared — the intelligence, distributed: the household tallies together — Augusta with the campaign book, Letitia with the week's pies accounted for, Creech with the ledger — the staff, at its sums. How intelligence is shared: completely, the household's way. She reads the totals aloud — the enemy's sum, the ally's sum, the doubt's dividend — and the general nods: the arithmetic holds. Count daily, weekly, or trust the trend — the census rhythm, the choice that sets it: weekly, the tally; daily, the listening. The choice sets the campaign's metronome. She writes it under the date: "The street, summed. The doubt, compounding." The tally, filed.)*
> *(The numbers stay with her after the household disperses — the cries counted, the doubt compounding. On the stairs she passes the youngest clerk coming up with tomorrow's tally sheets, and he grins at her past his armful of paper. Every "is it true?" is a crack in the libel's rhyme, and the cracks are multiplying faster than the cries.)*

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor, met — Bell in person; the street's other power; the criers, discussed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mrs. Nance Bell receives her in the Gazette's office — the proprietor, met: not the paper's voice in print, but the woman herself, dry and precise in person as on the page. The proprietor's office — the Gazette's ground, entered: book-lined, orderly, the anti-Pyke — no green lamps, no money's smell, only paper and ink and competence. Bell's dryness, in person — the tone, live: "Miss Hartwell. The street, I hear. You are buying my criers' — time." The same sentence Pyke's man used, delivered without the slyness. She laughs, surprised. "Everyone knows the street's business, it seems." "Everyone who reads," says Bell. "Which in this town is everyone who matters.")*
> *(The street's other power — the recognition, mutual: the Gazette is the street's other power, the steady thirty criers, the truth's tempo. They discuss the criers — the business, the topic: Bell's foreman's men, the independents, the captain's lads and the purse's double rate. Bell listens to the tally — the cries counted, the doubt compounding — with the proprietor's attention, and then offers the counsel, dry as ever: "Don't buy the street, Miss Hartwell. The street can't be bought — only rented, and the rent always rises. Earn it. The street remembers who earned it." Bell's advice — the counsel, weighed: the proprietor advises, and the advice has the ring of the true.)*
> *(The ally, in person — the alliance, personed: Bell, herself, the publicly named proprietor from the first edition, holding the paper's line. She understands, taking her leave, what the meeting has given her: not intelligence — she had the tally — but sanction. The Gazette's proprietor has seen her street campaign and found it sound. Accept the advice, note it, or decline it — her reception, the choice that weighs the counsel: she accepts it, the way she accepted Augusta's rules — entirely, and as law. "Earn it," she writes in the book. "The street remembers." The proprietor, met. The counsel, filed.)*
> *(At the door Bell pauses — the dryness, one last drop: "Miss Hartwell — the Lantern prints heat. We print weather. You — you are becoming the climate." She goes out into the street with the sentence in her head like a verdict, and the criers' voices around her suddenly sound different: not the war's noise, but the weather she is learning to read. The climate. She will earn it.)*

scenes.synopsis: the hawker's livery — ribbons, badges; the street's uniform, considered.
scenes.prose:
> *(The hawker's livery, studied on the week's patrols — the street's uniform: she has watched the criers' dress the way she watched the press's labor — closely, respectfully. Ribbons, badges — the insignia: the captain's lads wear the Lantern's red ribbon at the cap; Bell's men wear the Gazette's plain badge; the independents wear whatever ribbon takes their fancy, the street's own flag. The street dresses — the livery's grammar, the form as message: the ribbon says whose corner, whose cry, whose pay. She understands the grammar entire: on the street, you are read by your ribbon before you open your mouth. The elder's ribbon — his colors: plain grey, the independent's own, worn forty years. The colors, honored.)*
> *(The street's uniform — the meaning, weighed: the uniform is the street's flag, and the flag is the allegiance. She considers the livery's grammar for herself — the form, the message: the white ribbon, the clean name in the street's grammar, the floriography translated to the corner; the Gazette's badge, the ally's colors worn openly, the paper's own livery; or no livery — the lady, unbadged, the street read by presence, not ribbon. Each speaks. Each is read. She tries each in the mind's mirror — the ribbon's cleanliness, the badge's allegiance, the bare presence's nerve — and weighs what the corners will make of each: the ribbon says the name is clean and knows it; the badge says the Gazette's own walks here; the absence says the lady needs no flag. The choice — the turn, remembered — is the week's fashion decision: how the street will read her. And the game will remember — and so will the criers.)*
> *(She chooses with the elder's counsel in her head — "the street reads the ribbon, miss, but it remembers the wearer" — and the badge, pinned: the seal, the livery assumed. The mirror, consulted: the street's uniform, worn over the morning dress, the grammar correct — the ribbon at the cap, the badge at the breast, or the plain presence, whichever the choice has made. She studies the reflection the way she studied the chapel's stone: for truth, not flattery. The livery does not costume her — it translates her. Tomorrow the corners read her ribbon. Tomorrow the street knows her flag. And the flag, whatever its form, will be read truly — because the wearer, the street already knows.)*

- **The Gazette's badge** — the ally's colors, worn openly; the paper's own livery, the proprietor's sanction. *(Bell+; the proprietor notes the allegiance.)*
- **No livery** — the lady, unbadged; the street read by presence, not ribbon. *(Composure+; the elder respects the restraint.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE PRESS'S PRICE. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Pyke's office, again — the green-shaded lamps, the money's smell, the proprietor's desk squared like a card table. Pyke, affable: "Miss Hartwell. The street, I hear. You are buying my criers' — time." The pause, the smile, the slyness never overt. "Let me save you the trouble." He spreads his hands, the gesture of the generous merchant. "Name your price — for the whole street. Every corner, every crier, every cry. The captain's lads, the independents, the very cobbles. The town's ears, entire." The offer, laid like a card on the green felt: the street, wholesale. No threat in it. Nothing overt. Only the arithmetic — the whole street, for a price, the price unspoken but understood, sitting between them like a third guest.)*
> *(She stands in the green lamplight and feels the weight of it entire: buy the street entire and the war is over by morning — every corner hers, every cry hers, the town's ears entire, the libel drowned in her own purchased chorus. The bold stroke. The war, ended at a stroke. But the price — Pyke's price is never coin, and they both know it. "And your price, Mr. Pyke?" she asks, because the asking must be spoken. "The same as ever, Miss Hartwell." The smile, the pause. "The truth — in your handwriting." The whole street, for a signature: the retraction, the confession, the surrender set in type. Three roads lie open in the lamplight: buy it — pay the price, end the war by morning; refuse it — decline the wholesale, keep the street contested, the war honest; or the third road — turn it: let Pyke's offer become her intelligence, the price studied, the offer itself a weapon. The green lamps. The waiting proprietor. Choose.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The press's price:*
- **Buy the street** — *Conduct+; the bold stroke.* Pay Pyke's price for every corner; the town's ears, entire. *(The war ends by morning; the price is the signature.)*
- **Refuse the street** — *Composure+; the clean hands.* Decline the wholesale; the street stays contested. *(Augusta approves; the war stays honest.)*
- **Turn the offer** — *Subtlety+; the quiet coin.* Let the offer become intelligence; the price, studied. *(Lavinia is informed; the offer becomes a weapon.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: her nerve, her arithmetic, the price she refused to pay. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

> 2. [stance]Weigh the three roads — buy it, refuse it, or turn the offer into a weapon. → Remembered: Her weighing; the green lamps, the waiting proprietor.

scenes.synopsis: the refusal, carried — Pyke's answer; the war, declared; the street, contested.
scenes.prose:
> *(The refusal, carried — the answer, delivered in the green lamplight with the creditor's plainness: whatever she chose in the lamplight — buy, refuse, or turn — she carries it the way she carried the knock at the press: directly. "Then we are enemies, Miss Hartwell?" — Pyke's declaration, the affability thinning to show the wire beneath. The war, named: not the cold war of libels and ledgers, but the declared war, the street wholesale refused or bought or turned. She receives the declaration the way Augusta receives all declarations: as information. "We were enemies when you set my name in type, Mr. Pyke. We are merely — precise — about it now." The slyness, fraying: the pause before "precise" lands like a paperknife.)*
> *(The street, contested — the ground, whatever the choice: bought entire, the corners hers by morning; refused, the street stays contested, the war honest; turned, the offer becomes intelligence, Lavinia informed, the price studied. She carries the result to the ally — Lavinia, informed: the intelligence, shared over the bookseller's tea, the offer's anatomy dissected. "The whole street, for a signature," Lavinia repeats slowly. "He grows bold." "He grows desperate," says Rose. The distinction matters: bold men are dangerous; desperate men are readable. The offer, filed — the intelligence, in the book: Pyke's price, Pyke's boldness, the street's wholesale value, all data now.)*
> *(Tell the street, tell the town, or tell no one — her disclosure, the choice that spreads the news: she tells the street — the elder, the independents, the captains' courtesy — because the street is the ground, and the ground should know its war is declared. She tells it plainly, at the corners, in the street's own grammar: the offer, the refusal-or-bargain, the war's new precision. The captain hears it from his lads and his old captain's face does something complicated: respect, and calculation. The street, told. The war, declared. The town will hear it in time — the town always hears — but the street hears it first, the way the street hears everything first. That is the point of the street.)*
> *(She walks home with the declaration in her head like a commission — the war, declared, the street contested — and understands the afternoon's true spoil: Pyke offered her the whole street because he fears her handful of corners. The purse pays half again for ruin, but the ruin's instrument is being bought out from under it, shilling by shilling, ear by ear. The war is declared. The street is the front. And the front, she thinks, is holding.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The livery, worn — the street's reading, at dawn: she walks the full round in the perfected livery — the ribbon, the boots, the satchel — and the corners read her the way the chapel read her: truly. How the street reads: first the ribbon, then the walk, then the face. The ribbon, read correctly — the allegiance, understood. The walk, read correctly — the round, walked like one who knows it. The face, read correctly — open, the veil's absence noted. The elder's nod — the approval, deepened: the old crier falls in beside her for the first corner, the escort, the street's own honor guard. "The street reads you, miss," he says. "And the reading is good.")*
> *(The criers' respect — the reception, corner by corner: the captain's lads touch their caps — the enemy's courtesy, the captains' protocol; Bell's men nod, the ally's recognition; the independents — the prize — come up to shake the bare right hand, the street's compact offered unasked. The corners, read: every corner of the mapped rounds, the livery performing its grammar. The badge, noted — the insignia, read and reread: the white ribbon, the Gazette's badge, or the unbadged presence — whatever she chose, the street parses it. She walks with the elder and the lad trailing like a page, and understands the morning's honor: the street has accepted her livery. She is — for the dawn round — the street's own.)*
> *(The street, addressed — the presence, the commander's address to her new ground: she stops at the bookstall corner and speaks, briefly, in the street's grammar — the offer, the code, the war's precision: the ears bought honestly, the cries never bought, the doubt compounding. The independents, won — the prize, coming over: three more ears before noon, the shilling's honesty proving contagious. She walks home as the rounds end, the satchel lighter by its shillings, the pocket book heavier by its intelligence, and writes under the date: "The livery, worn. The street, reading. The prize, pursued." The round, walked.)*
> *(Walk daily, weekly, or leave the street to the elder — her patrol, the choice that sets the round: daily, herself, at dawn — the commander's patrol, the street's own hours. The choice sets the campaign's metronome. The street has a new walker. The walker has the street's reading. And the reading — the criers agree, the captains agree — is good.)*

scenes.synopsis: the coffee houses — the street's parliament; the readers, aloud.
scenes.prose:
> *(The coffee houses, entered — the street's parliament: she takes the morning's second hour in the coffee houses where the numbers are read aloud — the readers, aloud, the practice entire: a man at the long table reads the Gazette while another reads the Lantern, and the room hears both, the town hearing itself read. Her study; the coffee houses govern — the tables, divided: the factions, the street's parties in miniature — the merchants' table for the Gazette, the idlers' for the Lantern, the clerks' table (hers, increasingly) for the both. The crier at the door — the threshold: the elder's lads sell at the door, both papers, the penny's democracy. She takes her seat at the clerks' table and listens to the town listen to itself.)*
> *(The coffee house, entered — the presence, the parliament admitting her: she is known now — the lady of the street, the ribbon at the cap — and the readers make room. The reading, joined — the participation: when the Lantern's reader reaches the libel's rhyme, she does not flinch — she listens, the street's discipline — and when the Gazette's reader reaches Bell's dry answer, she nods, the ally's recognition. > *(The enemy's captain, seen plain at last: she arranges the meeting through the elder, the captains' courtesy, and meets the captain at the bookstall corner at the afternoon lull. Her study; the captain is seen plain — not the purse's creature, but the street's: forty years of corners, the history — the captain's history — in the man's weathered face. "Forty years," he says, when she asks. "Forty years of corners, miss. I've cried three kings' news." The captain's pride — the man's core: the pride is the handle, the forty years, the corners, the trade's honor. She salutes it — the captain, respected: the courtesy, the honor given where honor is due, enemy or not. "Then you know the code better than any man living," she says. "Aye," says the captain. "I wrote half of it.")*
> *(The purse's hold — the leash, examined: the double rate, the price of loyalty — the loyalty is rented, and they both know it. She names it plainly, the creditor's way: "The double rate, Captain. The purse holds you." The captain's weariness — the opening: the weariness is the door, and it opens a fraction. "The purse pays double," he says slowly, "and pays it late, and asks me to cry what my lads haven't read." The third statute, broken by the purse's own order. The captain's pride, insulted by the paymaster. She offers nothing — yet. The play for the captain is not a purchase. It is a recognition.)*
> *(Offer the honest shilling, the code's compact, or leave the captain to the purse — her play for the captain, the choice that is the pitch: she offers the code's compact — not coin for cries, never cries — but the compact: the honest shilling for honest reports, the word in the street's form, the captain's pride restored. "Cry what you've read, Captain. Report what you've seen. The shilling's honest, and the word's mine." The captain studies her — the forty years, weighing — and the old captain's face does the complicated thing again: respect, and calculation, and something like relief. "The purse pays double," he says. "Aye. But the purse," — the pause — "the purse don't give its word." The compact, offered. The leash, loosened.)*
> *(She walks away without an answer — the captain's answer will come in the street's own time — but the opening is the door, and the door is open. The enemy's captain, studied; the double rate, named; the weariness, found. The war's boldest play is not a battle. It is a recognition: the purse rents loyalty; the street gives its word. She writes it in the book: "the captain — the code, offered." The play, made.)*

She watches him make the round and understands the press from below — the view: the press seen from the errand, the libel as bundle-weight, the truth as bundle-weight, both alike to the boy's shoulders. How the street recruits: the devil, won — not bought, never bought, but befriended, the boy's loyalty given the way the street gives everything: for kindness, for honesty, for the pie. Buy the devil's ears, the devil's loyalty, or leave him — her devil's bargain, the choice that defines it: the loyalty, not the ears — the ears follow the loyalty, the street's law. The boy's name she never asks. She will know them all.)*
> *(the devil's first intelligence arrives the next morning with the bundles — the Lantern's print run, doubled; the foreman's temper, frayed; the purse's man, seen at the press at midnight. The press, from below — the view, vindicated: the devil's ears hear what the proprietor's desk conceals. scenes.prose:
> *(The street's seasons, studied as the cold deepens — the year's round: she learns the street has seasons like the estate has them — winter's street, the cold's rule: the corners empty earlier, the cries thinner, the ears fewer, the daylight itself rationed. Her study; the street has seasons. The rule; the cold governs. The criers' winter — the hardship: the cold hands, the thin cries, the lad's chapped fingers, his old bones aching on the bookstall steps. The hardship; the winter is hard, and the hard winter does not negotiate. The warm corners — the refuges: the coffee houses with their fires, the bookstall's lee, the church porch out of the wind — the street has warmth, in pockets, and the pockets are known to every crier. The refuges; the street has warmth.)*
> *(The winter, provided — the quartermaster, the household's answer: she provides the way the estate provides — completely. Her providing; the winter is answered. Letitia's winter pies — the mercy: the pies, in winter, doubled — the kitchen's output for the corners, the children, the elders. The mercy; the pies, in winter. The street, warmed — the result: the corners fed, the criers' hands warmed, the lad in a new scarf. The result; the street is warmed. She walks the round and distributes the winter the way she distributed the shillings — honestly, ear by ear, pie by pie.)*
> *(Feed the corners, clothe the criers, or warm the children — her winter's scope, the choice that scales it: all three — the quartermaster does not choose — but the children first, the elders second, the corners always, the mercy distributed the way the shillings were: honestly, ear by ear. The choice scales it. She writes it in the book: "Winter — provided." The household's winter campaign, filed alongside the street's. The war has seasons. The household keeps them all.)*
> *(The winter provision becomes the street's legend — the lady of the ribbon, feeding the corners, the baskets emptied by noon and refilled by two, the kitchen keeping pace. The lad eats with both hands, gravy to the elbows, kicking his heels against the crate. "More Thursday?" he asks, mouth full. "Thursday," she promises, "and bring your sister.")*

> *(the captain's answer, arriving at the bookstall corner at the afternoon lull — the captain's reply: the old captain comes himself, the forty years in his walk, and speaks the street's plainest grammar. Her wait; the answer arrives. The captain's terms — the compact: the captain names them — the honest shilling for honest reports, the code kept, the lads crying what they've read. The terms; the captain names them. The handshake — the seal: the bare right hand, the street's compact, sealed skin to skin. The seal; the compact is sealed. The lads, informed — the orders: the captain tells his lads himself, the captain's orders — the Lantern cried where it's read, the reports honest, the double rate's leash slipped.)*
> *(The enemy's captain, won — the victory, the war's boldest: her victory; the captain comes over — not bought, never bought, but recognized — the code's compact, the pride restored, the forty years honored at last by someone who understands their weight. The elder's verdict — his judgment: he approves, deeply — "the street's whole, miss," says the elder. "The street's whole." The judgment; the elder approves. She stands at the bookstall corner with both captains — the elder's grey and the captain's weathered face — and understands the afternoon's magnitude: the purse's own captain, won by the code, the street's factions united under the law the street wrote for itself. The street, entire, hers.)*
> *(Trust the captain fully, verify the captain, or use the captain carefully — her trust, the choice that measures it: verify — the commander's discipline — but the verification is the street's own: the reports, checked against the elder's; the lads, watched on their rounds; the code, kept or broken openly. The choice measures it. The captain's first report arrives the next dawn — honest, complete, the captain's own. The trust, verified. The compact, holding, the captain's word proving as good as the elder's. She writes it in the book: "The captain — won. The street, whole." The victory, filed.)*
> *(The street is whole — the factions united under the code, the purse's captain turned by recognition. He shakes her hand at the door like a man concluding business, and his grip is honest. "The code holds," he says. "It holds," she agrees, and means the handshake more than the words.)*

> *(The street's map, complete — the campaign book, surveyed entire: she spreads the book on the morning-room table — every corner inked, every round mapped, every name recorded: the elder, the captain, the lad, the devil, the independents, the captains, the children. Her survey; the map is complete. The record; the corners are inked, the rounds numbered, the reports dated. The book, shown — the sharing: Augusta reads it entire, the general's eye moving corner to corner, and nods — the campaign's history, the street's memory, preserved in Rose's clerkly hand. How the book is shared; Augusta reads it. The campaign's cost — the accounting: Creech reckons it aloud — the shillings, the pies, the winter's provision, the honest coin accounted to the penny — the lean purse, leaner, but the cost reckoned honestly, every expenditure justified by its intelligence. The accounting; the cost is reckoned.)*
> *(The cost, justified — the audit: she justifies it the way she justified the chapel — the street, earned, the libel exhausted, the doubt victorious, the captain won. Her justification; the audit passes. The lean purse, leaner — the economy: the purse is leaner, but the street is hers — the arithmetic holds. The household, proud — the morale: Letitia's tears, Creech's nod, the staff's pride — the household is proud, the clerks victorious. She feels the pride in the room like warmth: the campaign's dividend, shared.)*
> *(Archive the book, continue the book, or publish the book — her book's fate, the choice that decides it: continue it — the patrol continues, the record continues, the street's memory kept current, the intelligence never allowed to stale. The choice decides it. She writes the decision under the map: "The book, continued." The map, complete. The cost, justified. The household, proud. The campaign, history — and the history, ongoing, the record never closed.)*
> *(The book closes on the month with the map complete — the street, inked entire. She runs her thumb along the page edges, forty-one corners in her handwriting, and ties the tape the way Lavinia taught her: the knot that never slips, the bow crooked in exactly the approved manner. The street will remember. The book will make sure.)*

scenes.synopsis: the street, at peace — the cries, ordinary; the peace, kept; the patrol, continued.
scenes.prose:
> *(The street, at peace — the ground, surveyed on a clear morning: she walks the round and finds the street at peace — the cries, ordinary: the soundscape, the ordinary cries — the news, the notices, the weather, the lost dogs and found gloves — no libel, no rhyme, the venom gone like a fever broken. Her survey; the street is at peace. The criers, at ease — the people: the elder at his corner with his forty years, the captain's lads easy in their captain's new compact, the lad's thin cry cheerful at the church — the people, at ease. The corners, quiet — the calm: the calm, the corners quiet in the morning light, the war's noise replaced by the street's own music, the ordinary music of a town at its business.)*
> *(The peace, kept — the vigilance: she keeps it the way she kept the chapel — the patrol, continued, the discipline unbroken. Her vigilance; the peace is kept. The patrol, continued — the discipline: the dawn round, daily, the liturgy — the peace is not the campaign's end but its fruit, and the fruit is kept by walking. The street's gratitude — the reward: the caps touched, the nods deeper, the lad's wave — the reward, the street grateful. She walks and is walked with — the elder, the lad, the independents — the street's own procession.)*
> *(Rest the campaign, maintain the patrol, or plan the sky — her rest, the choice that paces it: maintain the patrol — the liturgy kept, the dawn round daily — and plan the sky: the chapter's closing turn, the next front glimpsed, the performance beginning to take shape in the book's margins. The choice paces it. She writes it in the book: "The street, at peace. The patrol, continued. The sky — next." The peace, kept. The rest, earned. The sky, awaited.)*
> *(The street at peace: the cries ordinary, the corners calm. She walks home in the clear light past the fourth corner, where the eldest crier is teaching the youngest the morning's calls — the liturgy, handed down, the boy stumbling over the long words to everyone's delight. The ordinary music of the corners, restored. The sky is next.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The ally's audit — Lavinia reads the street campaign entire: the bookseller receives her with the campaign book spread between them, and reads it the way she reads everything — for the price. Her audit; the ally audits. The purse's price, discussed: Lavinia reckons what the purse spent — the half-again, the double rate, the doubled print run — against what Rose spent — the shillings, the pies, the winter — and laughs, the bookseller's dry laugh. "You bought the street for the price of its lunch, and they couldn't buy it for the price of its ruin." The arithmetic, the ally's verdict. She feels the audit's warmth: Lavinia, who wants the purse broken not bought, reading the breakage in the book.)*
> *(The purse, broken — the assessment: not broken entire — the purse remains, the press remains, the war's larger machinery intact — but the street front, broken: the captain won, the libel exhausted, the doubt victorious, the town's ears turned. Lavinia traces the campaign's arc in the book — the knock, the code, the captain, the cry — and nods slowly. "The street was the purse's voice," she says. "You took the voice." The ally's reading; the campaign, understood. She understands, hearing it, what the chapter purchased strategically: the purse's money, made audible, then made silent — the street's voice, turned from the purse's instrument to her own.)*
> *(Accept the audit, dispute the audit, or extend the audit — her reception, the choice that receives it: accept it — the ally's eye, trusted — and extend it: the sky, next — the campaign's next front, discussed. The choice receives it. Lavinia's parting counsel, dry as ever: "The street was the rehearsal, Rose. The sky is the performance." The audit, accepted. The sky, previewed. The ally, aligned.)*
> *(She walks home with Lavinia's audit in her head — the street bought for the price of its lunch — and understands the chapter's economy entire: the purse spent half again for ruin and bought the street's contempt; she spent shillings and pies and bought the street's heart. The arithmetic of the war, entire, and the ally's laughter still in her ears. The ally approves. The street is hers — the audit's warmth staying with her all the way home.)*

scenes.synopsis: the general's verdict — Augusta on the street campaign; the household's war, reviewed.
scenes.prose:
> *(The general's verdict, delivered in the morning room — Augusta on the street campaign: the general reads the book entire, the map, the cost, the victory — the corners, the code, the captain, the cry — and delivers the verdict the way she delivers all verdicts — plainly, without ornament. "Well conducted," says Augusta. "The street, taken without a siege. No casualties, no extravagance, the ground held by its own consent." Her verdict; the general judges. The household's war, reviewed: the press front, the street front — the war's two fronts, the general's map — the press held by Bell's steadiness and the Gazette's dry truth, the street taken by the shilling's honesty and the pie's mercy. The review; the war's fronts, surveyed, the whole campaign laid out like a battle plan after the action. She receives the verdict the way she received the commission: as orders, and as honor.)*
> *(The general's counsel — the next front: Augusta turns the campaign book's last page — blank, expectant — and taps it once with a finger that has tapped a hundred such pages. "The sky," she says. "The town's ears are yours. Now — the town's eyes." The counsel; the sky, named, the visible front declared. She understands the chapter's closing movement: the street was the rehearsal — Lavinia's word, the bookseller's dry prophecy — and the performance is the sky: the town's eyes, the visible front, the next chapter's ground, the rooftops and chimneys where the town looks. The general's verdict becomes the chapter's final order: the street, held; the sky, next.)*
> *(Accept the order, question the order, or anticipate the order — her reception, the choice that receives it: anticipate it — the sky already glimpsed, the planning begun — the general's nod, the approval. The choice receives it. She writes it under the verdict: "The street, held. The sky — next." The verdict, filed. The order, received.)*
> *(Augusta rises — the audience, ending — and does what the general rarely does: she takes Rose's face in her hands, briefly, the grandmother's own gesture inside the general's. "Your mother," she says, "would have walked the street herself." The sentence lands like a commission and a blessing together. The general's verdict, complete. The household's war, reviewed. The sky, next.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The farewell round — not farewell, but the patrol's blessing: she walks the dawn round with the chapter's end in her head, and the street — knowing, the street always knows — gives her the criers' salute. The street's goodbye; the patrol, blessed. The elder at his corner, the captain's lads at theirs, the independents, the lad running ahead to announce her — the salute, corner by corner: the caps touched deeper, the nods longer, the "miss" warmer. Her walk; the street salutes its walker. The criers' salute — the honor: the street's own honor guard, the full round, walking with her.)*
> *(The patrol, blessed — the street's benediction: at the bookstall corner the criers gather — the elder, the captain, the independents, the lad, the devil with his bundles — and the elder speaks the street's grammar, the elder's voice carrying: "The street's yours, miss. Walk it when you will — the corners are yours, the ears are yours, the code is yours." The benediction; the street gives itself, entire and without reserve. She receives it the way she received the code — as law, and as love, the two the street never separates. The farewell round becomes the chapter's coronation: not the town's, never the town's — the street's. The street crowns its own, and its crown is a grey ribbon and a bare right hand.)*
> *(Walk on, rest, or return — her patrol's future, the choice that paces it: walk on — the dawn round, daily, the liturgy unbroken, the discipline kept — the chapter ends, the patrol continues, the walker remains the street's own. The choice paces it. She writes it in the book, the pen moving slowly: "The farewell round — the street, saluting. The patrol, blessed. The walk, unbroken." The round, walked. The street, hers. The blessing, kept.)*
> *(She walks home in the full light with the street's salute in her ears like music — the criers' salute, the patrol's blessing, the "miss" warmer at every corner — and understands the chapter's final truth: she came to the street to buy its ears, and the street gave her its heart. The farewell round, walked. The street, saluting. The walker, blessed — and the blessing, kept like the code.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The chapter's accounting, alone in the morning room — the street campaign, closed: she does the final sums the way Creech taught her — the shillings, the pies, the winter, the lean purse leaner — and the true sums beneath, the ones no ledger holds: the corners walked, the code learned, the captain won, the cry answered, the libel exhausted, the doubt victorious. Her accounting; the campaign, closed. The book, complete: the campaign book's street section finished — the map, the names, the story — the elder's forty years, the captain's compact, the lad's wave, the devil's ears, the grey ribbon pressed between the pages. The record; the book, complete. She closes it — not the book, never the book, but the section — and feels the chapter's weight entire: the street, earned, the earning recorded in her own hand.)*
> *(The sky, awaited — the next front, glimpsed: she stands at the window and looks up — the town's eyes, the visible front, the rooftops and chimneys where the town looks — and the chapter's closing turn arrives the way all her turns arrive: as a sentence in the head, plain and final. The street was next. The street is hers. The sky is next. She writes it — the chapter's final line in the book's margin, the ink still wet — and the sentence becomes the chapter's door: the street, closed; the sky, awaited. The accounting, complete. The walker, ready.)*
> *(Close the book, shelve the book, or carry the book — her record's fate, the choice that keeps it: carry it — the pocket book, the round's companion, the campaign's memory portable — the street's intelligence never far from her hand. The choice keeps it. The chapter's accounting, filed. The street, closed. The sky, awaited. The walker, ready.)*
> *(The evening ends with the book on the table and the street quiet beyond the window — the accounting done, the lamp low. She trims the wick, and the flame steadies, throwing her shadow tall across the campaign map. Beyond the glass a single crier calls the late edition, unhurried, at peace with his corner, and somewhere below a shutter closes for the night. The street — hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the household's celebration — the street campaign, honored; the staff, feasted.
scenes.prose:
> *(The household's celebration — the street campaign, honored: Letitia lays the supper the way the household lays all victories — the table groaning, the pies in ranks, the staff together, the kitchen's triumph as much as the street's. The campaign, honored; the staff, feasted. Augusta presides, the general at the feast — the toasts, the stories: the elder's forty years, the captain's handshake, the lad's wave, the devil's bundles, the code's statutes recited like grace. Her feast; the household celebrates. The staff, feasted — the reward: the clerks, the kitchen, the household entire — the victory's dividend, shared, the table's plenty the campaign's true monument. She watches them and feels the campaign's true spoil: not the street, but this — the household, whole, proud, together.)*
> *(The toasts — the campaign, in the household's grammar: Augusta rises — the general's toast — "The street," she says, "is ours." The toast; the street, claimed. Creech, the ledger's toast — "The shillings, honestly spent." Letitia, the kitchen's — "The pies, eaten." The toasts; the household, in its grammar, each department claiming its share of the victory. She drinks to them all — the staff, the street, the campaign — and understands the evening's truth: the war is fought for the clean name, but the clean name is kept by the household, and the household is kept by supper. The celebration, the honor. The feast, the dividend.)*
> *(Feast tonight, work tomorrow, or rest the week — her celebration's scope, the choice that paces it: feast tonight — the victory, honored, the table cleared late — work tomorrow — the patrol, continued, the dawn round unbroken. The choice paces it. She writes it in the book: "The celebration — the household, honored. The patrol — tomorrow." The feast, filed. The campaign, celebrated. The street, hers — and the household, the street's own.)*
> *(The night ends with the household at the table and the street quiet beyond — the celebration, complete — and she carries upstairs the evening's final understanding: the campaign took the street, but the feast keeps the household. Both are hers. Both are the war's true ground. The street was next. The street is home — and home is the household, and the household is the war's true ground, and the ground is held.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quiet week — the peace, surveyed; the victory, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(The quiet week — the peace, surveyed: she walks the patrol through a week of ordinary mornings — the quiet, the peace, the campaign's aftermath settling like dust. Her survey; the week is quiet. The ordinary cries — the soundscape: the news, the notices, the weather, the market prices and the lost dogs — the ordinary, restored, the libel's rhyme gone from the corners like a fever broken. The soundscape; the ordinary, restored. The patrol's ease — the discipline: the dawn round, daily, the liturgy — easy now, the street's own rhythm, the walking done the way breathing is done, the corners greeting her like old friends. The ease; the patrol, easy now. The town, calm — the verdict: the doubt victorious, the questions answered, the town calm in its decision, the breakfast tables no longer debating her name. The verdict; the town is calm.)*
> *(The victory, kept — the vigilance: she keeps it walking — the patrol, the book, the shillings, the daily earning — the victory kept by the keeping, the peace maintained by the patrol. Her vigilance; the victory, kept. The book, current — the record: the pocket book, the round's companion — current, the street's memory kept, the intelligence never staling. The record; the book, current. She walks the quiet week and feels the campaign's aftermath entire: the peace is not the war's end — the press remains, the purse remains, the larger machinery intact — but the street front, held, the ground hers by its own consent. The quiet, kept.)*
> *(Enjoy the quiet, distrust the quiet, or use the quiet — her quiet, the choice that reads it: use it — the quiet, the interval — the sky, planned in the peace. The choice reads it. She writes it in the book: "The quiet week — the victory, kept. The sky, planned." The quiet, used. The peace, surveyed. The street, held — and the holding, like the walking, is daily.)*
> *(The quiet week ends with the street's ordinary music restored — the cries, the corners, the calm. She mends the white ribbon on her walking dress where it frayed at the fourth corner, the needle moving the way Letitia taught her — small stitches, pulled snug, the knot hidden underneath. Keeping is daily work. The ribbon holds.)*

scenes.synopsis: the sky, studied — the next front; the town's eyes; the performance, prepared.
scenes.prose:
> *(The sky, studied — the next front, surveyed from the window: she stands and looks up — the town's eyes, the visible front — and studies it the way she studied the street: completely, the commander's survey before the campaign. Her study; the sky is the next front. The town's eyes — the visible: the rooftops, the chimneys, the skyline, the church spires where the town's gaze rests — the town's eyes, mapped — where the town looks, what the town sees, how the town is seen. The visible; the town's eyes, mapped. The visible front — the strategy: the street was the ears; the sky is the eyes — the performance, prepared, the rehearsal complete. The strategy; the visible front, planned. She begins the planning the way she began the street's: with the book, the map, the honest reckoning, the blank page.)*
> *(Bell's counsel, remembered — the climate: "you are becoming the climate" — the counsel, kept — the street's climate, hers; the sky's climate, next, the weather she will make visible. The counsel; the climate, kept. The performance, prepared — the readiness: Lavinia's word — "the street was the rehearsal; the sky is the performance" — the readiness, the rehearsal complete, the stage awaited. Her readiness; the performance, prepared. The livery, for the sky — the armor: the street's livery, adapted — the visible front needs its own grammar, its own ribbon, its own reading. The armor; the livery, adapted. The household, briefed — the orders: Augusta, Letitia, Creech — the next front, named, the campaign's new ground declared. The briefing; the household, briefed.)*
> *(Plan the sky, walk the street, or rest between — her interval, the choice that paces it: both — the street walked, the sky planned — the commander's interval. The choice paces it. She writes it in the book: "The sky, studied. The performance, prepared." The next front, surveyed. The chapter's door, opening — and she will walk through it the way she walked the street: earning every step.)*
> *(The planning begins with the window and the sky — the town's eyes, the visible front. She opens the casement and leans out: the rooftops, the rigging-sheds, the season's first balloon straining gently at its tether. The rehearsal is up there, in the cold air. She closes the window against the wind and reaches for her coat.)*

scenes.synopsis: the eve — the chapter's end, awaited; the watch, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(The eve — the chapter's end, awaited: she sits late in the morning room, the book closed for the night, and feels the chapter's eve the way she felt the press's eve — the expectation, the held breath before the verdict. Her survey; the eve, before the sting. The street, sleeping — the calm: beyond the window the corners sleep — the calm, the street sleeping, the criers abed, the cries silent till dawn. The household, sleeping — the peace: above, the household sleeps — the peace, the household sleeping, the day's campaign banked. The book, closed — the record: the campaign book, closed for the night — the record, the book closed, the street's memory shelved till morning. She sits in the lamplight with the chapter's whole behind her — the knock, the code, the captain, the cry, the campaign won — and the sting's eve before her, the Gazette's verdict waiting with the dawn's edition.)*
> *(The watch, kept — the vigilance: she keeps it the way she keeps everything — the eve, the watch, the lamp burning low. Her vigilance; the watch, kept. The dawn, awaited — the expectation: the Gazette's sting, the proprietor's verdict, the dawn's delivery — the expectation, the dawn awaited, the edition's arrival the chapter's final seal. She writes the eve's line in the pocket book, the pen moving slowly in the lamplight: "The eve — the street, sleeping; the household, sleeping; the watch, kept." The eve, filed, the chapter's last private entry, the watch kept faithfully.)*
> *(Sleep, watch, or write — her eve, the choice that spends it: write — the chapter's last private line — then sleep, the watch kept by the street itself, the corners guarding their walker till dawn. The choice spends it. The eve, awaited. The sting, coming. The chapter, ending.)*
> *(The night ends with the lamp low and the street silent. She sets the Gazette money — exact coin, counted twice, as always — on the hall table for the morning boy, where he will find it before she is awake, as he always does, and banks the lamp until the flame is a blue bead. The verdict waits with the dawn, and the dawn keeps its own hours. She sleeps.)*

The Lantern's purse pays half again for ruin and buys the street's contempt. The street remembers who earned it." — Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, the Gazette.)*

scenes.synopsis: the chapter's last dawn — the round, walked one last time; the sky, above; the street, behind.
scenes.prose:
> *(The dawn — the chapter's last morning, breaking over the rooftops: she walks the round one last time as the chapter's walker — the liturgy, the corners in order — the elder's corner, the church, the coffee houses, the bookstall, the captain's. Her survey; the last dawn. The round, one last time — the liturgy: the corners, in order, the criers' greeting, the caps touched, the "miss" warm at every stop — the round, walked. The criers' farewell — the parting: the elder's deep nod, the captain's salute, the independents' hands, the lad running alongside to the bookstall, the devil waving his bundles — the parting, the street saying goodbye to its walker. She walks it all and memorizes it — the corners, the cries, the faces — the chapter's ground, learned by heart, kept like the code.)*
> *(The sky, above — the next front, glimpsed: at the bookstall corner she stops and looks up — the rooftops, the chimneys, the church spires, the town's eyes — the glimpsing, the sky above, the visible front waiting. The street, behind — the ground: the corners behind her, the campaign closed, the book complete — the ground, the street behind her, held. The book, in the satchel — the record: the pocket book, the round's companion — the record, carried, the street's memory portable. The elder's last nod — the old crier at his corner, the grey ribbon at her cap — his gift, the street's colors — the nod, the farewell. She nods back, the street's grammar, and turns toward home — toward the sky's planning, the performance, the next front, the town's eyes.)*
> *(The street or the sky — the chapter's door, the choice that opens it: the street, kept — the patrol continues, the dawn round daily — and the sky, next — the performance prepared, the rehearsal complete. Her door; the choice opens it. She walks home in the full morning with the street behind her and the sky above her, and the chapter's final sentence arrives the way all her sentences arrive: as the truth, plainly spoken. The street was next. The street is hers. The street is next — was next — is kept. And the sky — the sky is next. The street is next.)*
