scenes.synopsis: The chapter opens from Ch5's S40 — the same purse paid then as pays now. Rose moves to buy the street itself.
scenes.prose:
> *(Morning, and the campaign book lies open on the morning-room table to the page where last night's hand wrote the chapter's first sentence: "The street is next." The invoices are filed — Lavinia's family file, the Lantern's old accounts, the purse proved the same then as now, witnessed, entered. Three weeks she has fought the paper — the press, the chapel, the proprietor — and the paper war is hers, fought to a standstill. But the paper does not walk to breakfast tables by itself. It is carried — by boys with stacks under their arms, by hawkers on corners, by the cry that gives the libel its voice. The Lantern's ruin travels on human feet, for human coin. Buy the feet, and the libel limps. That is the morning's arithmetic, and it is Augusta's: the purse pays for the press; the purse pays for the crying; the purse pays to suppress the other papers. Three payments. Three roads. She has traced two of them — the press's hand, the chapel's stone. The third is this morning's work, and it begins at nine o'clock, at a corner.)*
> *(She writes the orders — four lines, the campaign's shorthand, the pencil moving the way it has learned to move: "Larkin. His corner. Nine o'clock. Bring coin." Ned Larkin — the hawker who took the shilling in the second chapter, who knew the hand that writes the extra-pay notes, the street's own witness, bought and honest. If the street is to be bought, begin with the boy who knows its prices — its corners, its hours, its double rates. Downstairs the severe dress is exchanged for the public dress, the one the street knows, the blue the town first read. The ritual comes later, the full dressing; this morning is reconnaissance, and reconnaissance dresses to be seen, not armored. Augusta reads the four lines over her shoulder and nods once — the general approving the geography. The cab is called. The street, she thinks, folding the book, is waiting to be bought.)*
> *(The morning-room's particulars — the tea gone lukewarm in Augusta's cup, her spectacles low on her nose, the invoices stacked like evidence on the table: Lavinia's family file tied with tape, the Lantern's old accounts with Pyke's sly totals inked in the margins, the purse proved the same then as now. She runs a finger down the column — press, crying, suppression — and feels the campaign's weight shift under her hand. Two roads mapped, the third waiting. The street is next. The sentence sits in the book like a door standing ajar, and she is already through it.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Read the "street is next" entry — the chapter's thesis, in her own hand. → Remembered: The thesis; the street is the third road.
> 2. [social]Take Augusta's blessing — "Buy the feet, child." → Remembered: The blessing; the general approves the geography.
> 3. [micro]Write the four-line order — "Larkin. His corner. Nine o'clock. Bring coin." → Remembered: The order; the campaign's shorthand, streeted.
> 4. [choice]Choose the morning's dress — public, not severe: the street must know her. → Remembered: The dressing; reconnaissance, not armor.
> 5. [examine]Count the coin — Augusta's rule, honest, counted. → Remembered: The counting; the purse's arithmetic, answered.
> 6. [stance]Resolve the method — not outbidding, but out-presence. → Remembered: The method; the street is won by being there.
> 7. [micro]Take the cab to the corner — nine o'clock, the street waiting. → Remembered: The arrival; the third road, entered.

scenes.synopsis: Street texture — Rose's name cried, but the crowd is thinner; the gutter is tiring.
scenes.prose:
> *(The corner at nine — Larkin's corner, the one the shilling bought first, the bookstall's corner with the coffee-house opposite and the church bell counting the hour. He is there, stack under arm, voice already going, the cry pitched to carry down the street: "Lantern! The Hartwell Fraud! The Dupes!" — and Rose, from the cab window, hears her own name cried like fish, like ballad-sheets, like any morning's ware. Strange, after the chapel's ink and stone: the libel as street music, thin and commercial, her ruin rhymed for a penny. The crowd round him is thinner than the cry deserves — a knot, not a press, a dozen men where three weeks ago there were thirty. Men take the paper, glance, fold it under an arm. One laughs — at the rhyme, not the ruin. The gutter, she thinks, remembering what Lavinia said of her father's old wars with the papers: the gutter tires. Three weeks of "Fraud!" and the cry is thinning like a voice shouted hoarse, and the town's throat, she judges, is nearly sore.)*
> *(She watches a full quarter hour — the general's reconnaissance, the stillness learned at the chapel: his pitch, the practiced lift at the libel's name; his regulars, the clerks who buy without looking up; the boys on the next corners with their thinner cries, the competition audible. Larkin sees her — the stillness first, the professional's pause mid-pitch, then the grin, the touch of the cap, the whole face changing. He finishes his pitch, sells two, and crosses the street to the cab — the boy with the shilling, grown a week older in knowledge, the street's witness reporting for orders. "Miss. You come to buy the street?" The directness of him, the street's own grammar. "I come," says Rose, stepping down, "to buy its loudest voice. Walk with me, Larkin. Tell me your route — every corner, every hour, every cry.")*
> *(The cab's window frames it — the church bell counting nine, the smell of the street coming in with the air: coffee, horse, damp wool, the morning's particular perfume. The boys on the next corners cry thinner — the competition audible, the libel's price undercut by distance. A crossing-sweeper bows for a coin; a clerk buys without looking up; the whole pavement performs its morning. She watches the way she watched the chapel — the general's stillness, the quarter hour given — and the street, unaware, gives up everything: its hours, its hunger, its thinning throat.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the corner a quarter hour — pitch, regulars, the thinning crowd. → Remembered: The reconnaissance; the gutter, tiring.
> 2. [micro]Note the thin cry — her name, cried like fish, to a knot, not a press. → Remembered: The thinning; three weeks, and the town's throat is sore.
> 3. [social]Let him see her — the stillness, the grin, the cap touched. → Remembered: The recognition; the boy with the shilling, grown.
> 4. [choice]Answer his question — "to buy its loudest voice." → Remembered: The answer; the street's voice, priced.
> 5. [examine]Map his route as he walks — corners, hours, the cry's geography. → Remembered: The route; the libel's roads, walked.
> 6. [stance]Resolve the street is honest — it tires, unlike paper. → Remembered: The honesty; the street forgets, which is her ally.
> 7. [micro]Begin the walk — the lady and the hawker, the street staring. → Remembered: The walk; reconnaissance, begun.

scenes.synopsis: Fashion carries consequence — the public dress for the street campaign.
scenes.prose:
> *(Before the walk, the dress — the campaign's first decision, and the first the street will read, because the street reads everything: hems, gloves, the set of a bonnet. Not the severe dress of the chapel — that was armor for printers' ink and lamplight, and the street is not a press; armor on a corner reads as fear, and fear is the one thing the gutter never respects. Not the steel of Lavinia's dinner — that was theatre for allies, cut for candlelight and diamonds, and the street is not yet allied; theatre on a corner reads as condescension. The public dress: the one the town knows, the one the gutter can read at twenty paces without squinting. The blue she wore when the town first read her — clean-lined, unarmored, the color of a clear name, the blue of the first Gazette portrait — or the grey walking dress, quieter, the general in plain clothes, watchful rather than declared. The street must see her elevated, not defended; a lady among hawkers, not a fortress among enemies. Fashion is a courtship mechanic, and this morning she courts the crowd — the fickle, tired, honest crowd, which has read "Fraud!" for three weeks and is ready, she judges, to read something else: a person, present, unhurried.)*
> *(She stands before the glass and assembles herself the way she assembled the chapel night — each piece chosen, each piece with a purpose, nothing decorative that is not also declarative. The white rose at the waist, the clean name worn where the cry can see it, fresh from the morning's bunch. The gloves pale, the boots for walking, the bonnet's brim set for the staged reveal the ritual will perfect later. Whatever she chooses, the street will read it — hawkers are readers too, of a different text, and they read hem and bearing the way Bell reads copy. The game will remember what she wore to court the crowd — and so will the street, which forgets nothing worn in its presence.)*
*Choices (no coin cost; the game remembers):*
- **The blue habit** — the town's first image of her, reclaimed. The street remembers the blue.
- **The grey walking dress** — quieter, watchful. The general in plain clothes.
- **The severe dress again** — armor for the street. The chapel's lady, unbent.
> *(Letitia's fingers are steady with the pin — the white rose set at the waist, the clean name stationed where the gutter can see it. The glass gives her back the campaign's first decision: the blue the town first read, or the grey's quiet watch, or the severe's unbent line. Each a sentence the street will parse at twenty paces. Hawkers read hems the way Bell reads copy — the set of a bonnet, the pale glove, the boot made for walking. She turns, and the glass turns with her, and the street's text is written: a lady, present, unhurried, courted — not confronted.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [choice]Choose the public dress — blue, grey, or severe. → Remembered: The choosing; the street courted, not confronted.
> 2. [micro]Pin the white rose — the clean name, at the waist, where the gutter can see. → Remembered: The rose; floriography, streeted.
> 3. [examine]Check the glass — elevated, not armored. → Remembered: The glass; the brief forming — elevation.
> 4. [social]Take Letitia's nod — "The street will stare, Rose." → Remembered: The nod; the household, warned.
> 5. [stance]Resolve to be seen — the libel's answer is a person. → Remembered: The resolve; presence as counter-paper.
> 6. [micro]Take up the reticule — coin, the book, the pencil. → Remembered: The kit; the campaign, pocketed.
> 7. [choice]Choose the hour — nine, the cry's height. → Remembered: The hour; the street, met at its loudest.

scenes.synopsis: Rose buys Larkin — route, pay, instructions.
scenes.prose:
> *(They walk — the lady and the hawker, the street staring, the strangest pair on the pavement since the chapel night — and Rose states terms the way she stated them to Lavinia: plainly, in sentences, no purse-slyness, no clerk's hedging. "Your route. Your hours. Your pay — from me now, weekly, in coin, counted and honest. What I buy: first, your knowledge — who pays you extra, and for what, and when. Second, your route — walked my way, on my hours, the corners I name. Third — " she stops at a crossing, and the boy stops with her — "your refusal. When the extra pay comes with instructions, you tell me first. Before the cry, before the coin. That is the price of my shilling." Larkin walks, thinking — weighing the way the street weighs everything: in coin and in consequence. "And what do I cry, miss?" The question, the street's own. "Whatever the street wants to hear," says Rose. "I do not buy your cry, Larkin. I buy your eyes.")*
> *(The coin — Augusta's rule, honest, counted, the week's pay in his palm before another word. "The extra pay," says Rose. "Who pays it?" A glance — the street's caution, the look of a boy deciding how much truth costs. "A man, miss. Not the clerk — another. Pays me extra to cry the libel loudest — the Hartwell numbers, miss, yours. 'Cry it like it's news,' he says. Double, on those days." "And other days?" "Other days — " Larkin drops his voice, though the street is empty of listeners — "I'm paid not to cry. The other papers, miss. Paid to leave 'em in the stack. To cry yours instead." The suppression money — the second payment, named. The street, bought twice over: loud for the libel, silent for everything else. She writes it in the book as they walk, the pencil moving: the route, the hours, the double days, the silent days. The boy, bought — the witness, retained. The street's loudest voice, hers to hear.)*
> *(They stop at the crossing — the boy with her, the street staring. He weighs the terms the way the street weighs everything: in coin and in consequence, the shilling from the second chapter suddenly grown into a contract. She remembers him as he was — the cap touched, the grin, the boy who knew the hand that writes the extra-pay notes. A week has made him canny. The coin sits in his palm — weekly, honest, Augusta's rule — and the refusal stands between them like a third party: tell me first. Before the cry, before the coin.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]State the terms — knowledge, route, refusal; plainly, in sentences. → Remembered: The terms; the street, contracted.
> 2. [choice]Answer "what do I cry" — "whatever the street wants." → Remembered: The answer; the cry unbought, the eyes bought.
> 3. [micro]Count the coin — weekly, honest, Augusta's rule. → Remembered: The coin; the cleanest transaction, repeated.
> 4. [examine]Ask after the extra pay — who, and for what. → Remembered: The asking; the second hand, described.
> 5. [examine]Ask after the suppression — paid not to cry the others. → Remembered: The suppression; the street, bought twice.
> 6. [stance]Resolve the street is conducted — loud here, silent there. → Remembered: The conducting; the purse as choirmaster.
> 7. [micro]Write it in the book — "THE STREET," the first entries. → Remembered: The entries; the third road, mapped.
> 8. [social]Thank him — "You are decisive, Larkin." → Remembered: The thanks; the boy, allied.

scenes.synopsis: Dialogue — who pays him extra to cry the libel loudest.
scenes.prose:
> *(They stop at a coffee-house door — the smell of coffee and damp wool, the Lantern on the tables inside, the noon readers already gathering — and Rose asks the question the whole street campaign turns on, the question the book has been waiting three chapters to ask. "The man who pays you extra. Describe him." Larkin describes, the street's witness testifying: not the clerk, not the scarred knuckle of the press's errand — a different man, softer hands, a gentleman's coat gone shabby at the cuffs, the cuffs the giveaway. "Pays in coin, miss. Always coin. Says: 'Cry the Hartwell numbers loudest, boy. Like it's news.'" The phrase, the purse's own poetry. "And the suppression — who pays you not to cry the others?" "Same man, miss. 'Leave the Gazette in the stack,' he says. 'The town don't need it today.'" Rose holds very still, the general's stillness. Not the clerk — a second hand. The purse has more than one errand boy, and this one wears a gentleman's coat gone shabby, and pays in coin, always coin.)*
> *("How often?" "The extra — when the numbers are worst, miss. The big libel days, the ones with the rhymes. The suppression — " a shrug, the street's eloquence — "most days, now." Most days. The purse pays to cry the libel and pays to silence the rest — the street bought twice: loud for lies, silent for everything else, the town hearing one paper and believing one paper because one paper is all it is permitted to hear. "And the other boys?" "Some took it, miss. Some didn't." The street, divided — bought and unbought, the honest corners holding out. "Thank you, Larkin. You are decisive." The boy grins — the word his now, from the chapel night, the highest praise the campaign gives. "I try, miss." And she believes him, which is the whole of the contract: belief, priced in shillings, paid weekly, in coin.)*
> *(The coffee-house door exhales — coffee and damp wool, the noon readers bent over the Lantern's free copies, the libel's theatre in session. Larkin's voice drops the way the street's voices drop for the true things: the man's description, the softer hands, the gentleman's coat gone shabby at the cuffs. "Cry the Hartwell numbers loudest, boy. Like it's news." The phrase hangs in the doorway like smoke. The suppression's twin instruction — "Leave the Gazette in the stack" — hangs beside it. Two payments, one purse-shape, the street conducted like a choir. She holds very still, and the general's stillness does the listening.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Have him describe the man — softer hands, shabby cuffs, coin always. → Remembered: The description; the second hand, seen.
> 2. [social]Ask after the suppression's payer — the same man. → Remembered: The same man; one hand, two payments.
> 3. [examine]Ask how often — the extra on libel days, the suppression most days. → Remembered: The often; the street, conducted daily.

scenes.synopsis: The suppression money — others paid to suppress other papers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Back in the cab — the notebook open on her knee, the pencil moving — Rose maps what Larkin gave her, the morning's intelligence drawn like a battle plan: the extra pay — libel days, double, "cry it like it's news"; the suppression pay — most days, "leave the Gazette in the stack"; the second hand — soft hands, shabby cuffs, coin always, a gentleman's coat gone shabby. Two payments, one purse-shape: the purse does not merely print the libel. It conducts the street — loud here, silent there, like a choirmaster with his choir, the cries rising and falling at the purse's hand. The Lantern cried loudest; the Gazette left in the stack; the town hears one paper, believes one paper, because one paper is all the street is paid to sing. The oldest trick in the gutter's book, priced twice — and the pricing, she notes, is the purse's signature: everything bought, nothing persuaded, the town's ears rented by the day.)*
> *(She writes it in the book under a new heading — "THE STREET," underlined twice: "Extra: libel days, double, second hand — soft hands, shabby cuffs —. Suppression: most days, other papers left stacked. Boys: some bought, some not." The street, mapped like the paper's roads, the third road drawn in ink. And the counter-move forms, Augusta's arithmetic extended to geography: if the purse buys the cry, she buys the crier — his eyes, his route, his refusal. If the purse buys silence, she buys noise — her own, honest, in the open, the noise of a person present. The street is not won by outbidding; the purse will always outbid her, being deeper. It is won by out-presence — by being there, daily, visibly, undeniably. She looks out at the thinning crowd round the next corner's hawker. The gutter tires. Presence is cheap, and she has it in abundance, and the purse cannot buy it at any price.)*
> *(The cab rocks on its springs — the notebook open on her knee, the pencil moving, the morning's intelligence drawn like a battle plan. The second hand's description sits at the top of the page: softer hands, shabby cuffs, coin always, the gentleman's coat gone genteel-shabby. Below it the two payments — the extra on libel days, doubled, the instruction quoted word for word; the suppression most days, the other papers left stacked, the town permitted one paper. The choirmaster image holds: the purse conducts, the cries rise and fall, the street sings what it is paid to sing. And the counter-move holds with it — presence, daily, the one coin the purse cannot mint.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Map the payments — extra, suppression, the second hand. → Remembered: The map; the purse as choirmaster.
> 2. [micro]Write "THE STREET" — the new heading, the first entries. → Remembered: The heading; the third road, opened.

> *(The cab home — the decision waiting like a sealed order. Larkin: bought, willing, knowing — the boy who took the shilling in the second chapter and has grown canny since, the street's own witness, her eyes on the corners. Three roads for the boy, and the chapter's first key decision, the one the whole street campaign will remember. Keep him bought — the eyes, the route, the refusal standing — the street's witness retained, weekly coin, the honest contract. Turn him double — let the second hand think him bought and loyal, and feed the purse what she chooses to feed it: chosen truths, timed revelations, the double channel, the riskier game, the boy carrying her sentences into the purse's ear. Or let him go — pay him off, release him, keep the street clean of her coin — the honest road, the blind one, the campaign walking without its witness. Augusta's rule — time, not trade — counsels plainly. The purse's arithmetic counsels slyly. The boy's grin counsels warmly. Three roads. One boy. Decide.)*

scenes.synopsis: Coffee-house texture — how the paper is read in public.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Turk's Head at ten — the coffee-house where the street's morning thickens: clerks, merchants, the idle rich, all bent over papers with coffee cooling. The Lantern's copies are free — a stack by the door, "TAKE ONE," the purse's generosity made visible — and men take them, read standing, leave them on the tables folded open at the libel. "Read aloud, some of 'em," says Larkin, at her elbow, the boy navigating the coffee-house like a second home. "The funny ones. The ones with the rhymes." The libel as performance — the street's theatre, free of charge. The Grecian across the way — the keeper there took the suppression coin, Larkin reports, and the Gazette's stack sits behind the counter, uncried, unbought, the town's other paper buried like a letter never posted. The Chapter House on the corner — honest, unsubsidized, crying both papers at equal pitch, the one corner the purse hasn't bought.)*
> *(Rose watches a full half hour — the general's stillness, learned at the chapel, perfected at the corner: who reads, who laughs, who folds the paper and pockets it like evidence. A table of young men reads the latest libel aloud — the "Dupes" rhyme — and laughs, and one of them catches her eye and has the grace to look away, the paper suddenly heavy in his hands. The street is not cruel, she judges; it is entertained. And entertainment tires, like everything else. The cart mornings — the Lantern's distribution cart, free copies for the coffee-houses, the driver paid by the second hand, shabby cuffs and all — arrive at seven, Larkin says, and the stacks are gone by noon. She writes it in the book: "Coffee-houses: Turk's Head — free, read aloud; Grecian — keeper bought, Gazette stacked; Chapter — honest. Cart: 7 a.m., driver paid." The street's reading rooms, mapped. The counter-move, forming: presence against paper — herself, in these rooms, at these hours, the libel's answer with a face.)*
> *(She gives it the full half hour — the general's patience, the chapel's discipline applied to coffee and noise. The young men's table reads the "Dupes" rhyme aloud and laughs, and one catches her eye and looks away, the paper suddenly heavy. The keeper of the Turk's Head moves among the tables — the free stacks by his door, the purse's generosity — and does not meet her glance. The Grecian's keeper counts his till. The Chapter's keeper cries both papers at equal pitch, the one honest throat in the street. She reads the room the way Bell reads copy, and the room, unaware, reads back: entertained, tiring, ready.)*

> 1. [examine]Watch the Turk's Head — free Lanterns, read aloud, the laughter. → Remembered: The watching; the libel as theatre.
> 2. [micro]Note the Grecian — the keeper bought, the Gazette stacked. → Remembered: The Grecian; the suppression, shelved.

scenes.synopsis: Dialogue — who pays for the free papers, and how the Gazette sits unstacked.
scenes.prose:
> *("The free copies," says Rose, as they leave the Turk's Head — "who pays for the free?" Larkin grins — the street's economics, the boy's true subject. "The purse, miss. The cart, the copies, the driver's supper — all of it. 'Give 'em away,' the man says. 'A paper nobody pays for is a paper nobody questions.'" The wisdom of the gutter, priced: free paper, unquestioned paper, the libel at no cost and therefore at no discount. "And the Gazette — " "Sits in the stack, miss. The keeper won't cry it, the boys won't carry it — the suppression coin sees to that. A paper nobody cries is a paper nobody reads." The street's arithmetic, complete: the libel free and loud, the truth stacked and silent, the town reading what the purse permits. "And the honest corners?" "Thin on the ground, miss. The Chapter House. Two more." Three corners in the whole town where both papers cry at equal pitch. The street, mostly bought.)*
> *("What beats it, Larkin?" The boy thinks — the question beyond his trade, the street's witness asked for strategy. "Being there, miss." The simplicity of it, the gutter's own wisdom. "The paper's just paper. But you — " he gestures at her, the blue dress, the white rose, the whole of her — "you're loud without crying." She laughs — the first laugh of the morning, startled out of her by a hawker's boy. "Out-presence," she says. "Augusta will want that in the book." "Write it, miss. It's true." And it is true — the morning's thesis, confirmed by the street's own witness: the counter-move is not coin but presence, not the cry but the person, the ritual waiting for its occasion like a dress for its dinner. She writes it, the pencil moving: "Out-presence: being there, daily. The street's own counsel." The cart rattles past, seven o'clock's ghost, free copies for the noon readers. The street, she thinks, is a conversation — and she intends to join it.)*
> *(They leave the Turk's Head into the morning's glare — the cart's ghost rattling past, seven o'clock's free copies already gone to the noon readers. Larkin walks beside her, the boy's grin easier now, the street's witness grown fond of his employer. "Being there, miss." The simplicity of it follows her down the pavement: the paper is just paper, but she is loud without crying. Augusta will want it in the book — the street's own counsel, priced in shillings. The ritual waits for its occasion like a dress for its dinner. The counter-move has a name now, and the name is hers to walk.)*

scenes.synopsis: The counter-campaign — presence against paper. Lavinia's diversion is set for the Turk's Head.
scenes.prose:
> *(Noon, and the counter-campaign is written — the full plan, the week's geography, the pencil moving in the morning-room with Augusta reading over her shoulder. Presence against paper: herself in the street daily, at the hours the street reads — nine at the corners, ten at the coffee-houses, noon where the crowds thicken, the ritual's dress worn like a uniform, the white rose at the waist, the clean name streeted. Not crying, not arguing — being there, the general among the crowd, the libel's answer with a face and a walk and a nod for the honest hawkers. The street is not won by outbidding; it is won by out-presence. And the theatre — Lavinia's department, the diversion planned for Thursday, the Turk's Head at noon, the loudest table in the room, the moment the whole coffee-house looks up. "Write to her," says Augusta. "The diversion is hers to stage. You only attend.")*
> *(She writes — the letter to Lavinia, the ally with her own agenda, the partner who wants Pyke broken, not bought. "Thursday. The Turk's Head. Noon. The loudest table. Make them look up — I shall make the exit." The plan's division of labor: Lavinia the theatre, Rose the timing, the partnership's separate reins held as they have been held since the dinner. The diversion's purpose, plain in the book: when the whole coffee-house looks at Lavinia, the street learns that the town has other things to read than the libel — that the Hartwell story is not the only story, that attention is the true currency and she intends to spend it. Augusta approves the letter, the geography, the division. "Presence," says the general, "costs you nothing and the purse everything." The letter sealed. Thursday, noon, the Turk's Head. The counter-campaign, launched.)*
> *(She seals the letter with the campaign's wafer — Thursday, the Turk's Head, noon, the loudest table. Augusta reads the plan over her shoulder — the week's geography, the division of labor, the theatre's economics — and nods once, the general approving. "Presence costs you nothing," the general says, "and the purse everything." The letter goes with the noon post, the ally's commission, the diversion's design entrusted to the one who stages best. Lavinia the theatre, Rose the timing — separate reins, as always. The book's new page waits: Thursday. The room. The quarter hour. The exit, timed to the minute.)*

scenes.synopsis: Rose walks the route — the honest hawkers, the coffee-house keepers, the street learning her.
scenes.prose:
> *(Tuesday morning — the route walked, the book's geography made flesh: Larkin's corner at nine, the Grecian at ten, the Chapter House at eleven, the Turk's Head at noon, the whole of the street's reading hours in her boots. She buys a Gazette from the honest boy at the Chapter House — the paper's own small economy, the coin passed hand to hand — and reads it standing, the way the street reads: quickly, publicly, the libel's enemy consumed in the open. The keeper of the Chapter House watches her — the honest keeper, unsubsidized — and bows, the bow of a man who knows what it costs to be honest in a bought street. The free Lantern stacks sit untouched at the Turk's Head door — "TAKE ONE" — and she does not take one, the refusal visible, the street's grammar: what she will not touch, the street notices.)*
> *(The hawkers learn her — the honest three first, then the bought ones, the word traveling the corners faster than any cry: the lady walks, the lady buys the Gazette, the lady reads standing, the lady nods. A boy at the Grecian touches his cap — bought by the purse, but the cap-touch is free, the street's own courtesy, unbought. The keeper of the Turk's Head sees her seeing — the free stacks, the noon readers, the whole conducted choir — and looks away, the look of a man whose conscience has a price and knows it. She buys chestnuts from a woman at the corner — the ritual's bearing practiced early, the general among the crowd, unhurried, nodding — and the woman says, sudden, "You don't look like no fraud, my lady." The street's verdict, unprompted, unpriced. She writes it in the book that night, the pencil steady: "The street is learning me. Presence works." The first entry under the counter-move, and the truest.)*
> *(The route has a rhythm by Tuesday — nine at Larkin's corner, ten at the Grecian, eleven at the Chapter House, noon at the Turk's Head, the reading hours walked in the ritual's early dress. The honest boy's coin is warm in her palm; the Chapter keeper's bow is deeper today. At the Grecian a bought boy touches his cap — the courtesy free, the street's own coin, unbought by any purse. The Turk's Head keeper sees her seeing and looks away. She buys chestnuts at the corner, and the woman's verdict — unprompted, unpriced — follows her down the pavement like a small, clean flag: you don't look like no fraud.)*

> *(Wednesday morning — the flower girl at the corner with the morning's bunch, the white roses fresh, the dew still on them, and Rose stops the way she has stopped every morning this week: the ritual's small station, the floriography's daily renewal. "For luck, my lady?" the girl says — the street's own phrase, the one the campaign has adopted — and Rose buys the bunch, the coin passed, the honest transaction among all the bought ones. The white rose of the clean name — worn at the waist, pinned fresh each morning, the flower the whole street campaign has carried since the dinner. In the language the story speaks, the white rose says: my name is clean, and I wear the proof where the cry can see it. The street has learned to read it — the hawkers know the rose, the keepers know the rose, the chestnut woman knows the rose. Floriography, streeted: the signature thread, worn publicly, read daily.)*
> *(She pins it before the glass — the morning's small ceremony, Letitia's fingers steady, the fresh rose at the waist, yesterday's pressed in the book like a receipt. The choice, the campaign's daily fashion decision: pin it bold at the waist, the declaration — carry it in the hand, the quieter statement, the rose as companion — or give one away, the floriography as generosity, the clean name shared. Whatever she chooses, the street will read it — the flower girl watches, the hawkers watch, the whole bought street watches the unbought rose. The game remembers how she wore the clean name in the street's presence — and the street, which forgets nothing worn in its presence, remembers too.)*

> *("Thursday," says Lavinia, in the morning-room — the ally arrived with the noon post, the steel dress exchanged for the day's walking silk, the diamonds put away, the whole of her sharpened for theatre. "The Turk's Head. Noon. The loudest table — the one by the window, where the whole room sees. I shall be — " she pauses, the actress choosing the role — "memorable." Rose pours the tea, the partner's stillness. "Memorable how?" "Loud, my dear. Louder than the libel. The whole coffee-house reading the Lantern, and I shall give them something else to read — myself, at volume." The diversion's design, plain between them: when the whole room looks at Lavinia, the street learns the town has other stories — that attention is the currency, and the campaign intends to spend it where the purse cannot follow.)*
> *("And the exit?" "Timed." Rose sets down the cup. "When the room is all yours — when every eye is on the loudest table — I leave. Visibly. The white rose, the blue dress, the whole of the clean name, walking out through a room that has forgotten the libel for a quarter hour. The exit is the point, Lavinia. The theatre is yours; the timing is mine." Lavinia laughs — the ally's laugh, the one that means the plan is good. "Separate reins, as always." "Separate reins." The partnership's grammar, spoken aloud. "And the cost?" Lavinia's smile sharpens — the agenda showing, the part of her that wants Pyke broken, not bought. "The cost is mine, my dear. What the town reads about me on Friday is my choice — and my price. I have paid it before. I shall pay it again." The diversion, planned: Thursday, noon, the loudest table. The theatre, booked. The exit, timed.)*

scenes.synopsis: Dialogue — Lavinia's true-enough personal scandal; its human price.
scenes.prose:
> *("Tell me the scandal," says Rose — the question the partnership has earned, the ally's due. Lavinia is quiet a moment — the actress without a role, the woman underneath the steel. "The true-enough version," she says at last. "Not the whole — the whole is mine. But true enough: there was a man. There was a season. There was a child, lost. The town read about it — the papers, the whispers, the whole gutter's opera. And I learned what you are learning now, my dear: that the price of being read is being written, and the only choice is who holds the pen." She pours the tea herself, the hands steady. "On Thursday, the town will read about me again — the loudest table, myself at volume. And what they read will be my choice. That is the price, and I pay it gladly: I choose what the town reads about me.")*
> *(Rose holds very still — the partner's stillness, the debt of the listened-to. "The human price," she says. "Name it." Lavinia's smile — the real one, rare as the diamonds. "That my name, on Friday, will be the story. That the whispers will follow me a week. That some doors — " a pause — "will close, that were ajar. I know the cost, Rose. I counted it before you were born to campaigns." She rises, the walking silk settling, the ally with her own agenda, whole. "Wear something memorable on Thursday," she says at the door. "When the room looks at me, let them see you leaving — the clean name, the white rose, the whole of it. That is the theatre's purpose: that the town reads us both, and chooses." The door closes. Rose writes in the book: "Lavinia's price: her choosing. The partnership's debt: my witnessing." The diversion's human cost, entered — and honored.)*
> *(The quiet after the telling — Lavinia pouring her own tea, the hands steady, the actress without a role and the woman underneath it, both present. The true-enough scandal sits between them like a third guest: the man, the season, the child lost, the town's old opera. "The price of being read is being written," she says, "and the only choice is who holds the pen." Rose writes it in the book that evening — "Lavinia's price: her choosing" — the pencil steady, the debt of the witnessed entered and honored. Wear something memorable, the ally said. Thursday will be memorable. The partnership's ledger balances.)*

scenes.synopsis: Dialogue — the diversion deployed at the Turk's Head; Rose calls the exit.
scenes.prose:
> *(Noon — the Turk's Head, the loudest table, the whole coffee-house reading — and Lavinia arrives the way she arrives everywhere: like weather. The walking silk, the steel in it, the diamonds put away but the bearing wearing them anyway, the whole of her pitched, as promised, louder than the libel. She takes the window table — Thursday's stage — orders coffee for the room, and begins: the stories, the laughter, the volume, the performance of a woman entirely unbothered by being read. The room looks up — the tables turning, the papers lowering, the Lantern's theatre losing its audience to the better show. "My dear," she says, loud enough for the back tables, "you look like a woman with a secret." "I look," says Rose, "like a woman with a schedule." The room laughs — the diversion, working, the street's attention spent where the purse cannot follow.)*
> *(Rose watches the clock the way she watched the chapel's — the general's timing, the exit the point of the theatre. A quarter hour — the room all Lavinia's, every eye on the loudest table, the libel forgotten on the tables like yesterday's weather. She rises — visibly, the white rose, the blue dress, the whole of the clean name — and walks out through the room that has forgotten the libel for a quarter hour. The exit, timed: heads turning from the loudest table to the door, the town reading them both, the diversion's purpose served in a walk. Outside, the noon street — the cry thinner, the crowd thinner, the gutter's throat sore. She does not look back. In the cab she writes: "The diversion, deployed. The exit, timed. The room forgot the libel for a quarter hour — and a quarter hour, in this war, is a victory." The theatre, closed. The timing, hers.)*

Rose holds very still — the general's stillness, misplaced in the clean light. Polite émigré financiers, paying promptly in coin, come through the lady's card — asking after her. The coffee-houses first — the Turk's Head, the Grecian, the Chapter House — the keepers questioned in the street's grammar, the boy's description translated to the town's faces. The Grecian's keeper — the bought one, the suppression coin in his till — looks away. The Chapter's keeper — the honest one — shakes his head. The Turk's Head — the theatre's stage, Thursday's room — the keeper there remembers: "A gentleman, miss. Shabby cuffs. Paid the cart driver — the free copies, the seven o'clock cart. Coin, always coin." The second hand, placed: the distribution's paymaster, the cart's coin, the free paper's purse.)*
> *(And then — the street's luck, the general's reward for walking: the man himself, glimpsed, the description made flesh. Older, better-dressed than the clerk — the shabby only at the cuffs, the gentleman's coat gone genteel-shabby, the soft hands handling coin at a crossing. He walks City-ward — the financial streets, the counting-houses, the purse's own geography — and does not see her, the lady in the grey walking dress, the general in plain clothes, watchful. She follows — not far, not close, the street's own pace — to the City's edge, where he turns into a counting-house court and is gone. She writes in the book: "The second hand: placed. The cart's paymaster. City-ward." The purse, she thinks, has an address — or near enough. The face stays offstage; the hands are mapped. That is the week's intelligence, and it is enough — for now.)*
> *(The keepers get the description in the street's grammar — softer hands, shabby cuffs, coin always, the gentleman's coat gone genteel-shabby. The Grecian's bought keeper looks away, his conscience priced. The Chapter's honest keeper shakes his head, genuinely. The Turk's Head remembers: the cart's paymaster, the seven o'clock free copies, the coin always coin. And then the street's luck — the man himself at a crossing, the description made flesh, handling coin with the soft hands. He walks City-ward, toward the counting-houses, and does not see the lady in grey. She follows to the City's edge, where a counting-house court swallows him. The purse has an address. Or near enough.)*

scenes.synopsis: The balloons — the town looks up; the sky as the campaign's new front.
scenes.prose:
> *(Saturday — the cry from the next corner, thinner than ever, and then the other cry, the one that stops the street: "Balloon! Vauxhall! The ascent!" — and the whole pavement looks up, the hawkers' crowd become an audience, the libel forgotten mid-cry. The balloon rises over the rooftops — the silk vast, the colors bright, the town's whole attention hauled skyward like a sail — and Rose, in the grey walking dress, looks up with the street. The wonder of it — the age's own miracle, the sky made navigable, the crowd's gasp like a single breath. The hawkers cry the ascent — the libel abandoned, the "Fraud!" unsold, the town's ears rented to the sky for the afternoon. She watches a full half hour — the general's stillness, the new front assessed: the balloons draw the town's attention upward, and attention is the currency, and the purse — she thinks of the second hand, the shabby cuffs, the coin always — the purse understands currency.)*
> *(She files it the way she files everything — the book, the pencil, the new heading: "THE SKY." The balloons: the town's attention, hauled upward, the street's ears rented to wonder. The question, the campaign's: is the sky bought? The purse buys the press, the cry, the suppression — why not the ascent, the wonder, the afternoon's attention? She writes it as a question, not an answer — the general's discipline: "The sky: bought? The purse's reach — the balloons?" The street below, the crowd dispersing, the hawkers resuming their thinner cries. The sky above, empty, the silk gone. The new front, opened — and the counter-move already forming, Augusta's arithmetic extended upward: if the purse buys the sky, she buys presence at altitude. She looks up once more, at the empty blue. "Presence," she says, "at altitude." The book, closed. The sky, watched.)*
> *(The crowd's gasp rises like a single breath — the silk vast, the colors bright, the town's whole attention hauled skyward. The hawkers abandon the libel mid-cry — "Fraud!" unsold, the town's ears rented to wonder for the afternoon. The book gets a new heading that evening — "THE SKY" — and under it a question, not an answer: bought? The silk is gone by dusk. The question stays. The sky, watched.)*

The street campaign, scored — publicly, favorably, the Gazette's verdict on the war's third road. The libel's week: the cries thinner, the crowds thinner, the gutter's throat sore. The counter-week: the lady walking, the rose worn, the theatre staged, the exit timed. "The street," says Bell, "is losing interest in the libel — and finding it, instead, in the lady.")*

scenes.synopsis: Dialogue — the verdict read together; "we are a set"; next week smaller.
scenes.prose:
> *("We are a set," says Lavinia — the morning-room, the Gazette between them, the verdict read together like a shared letter. "The lady among the hawkers, and the theatre at the Turk's Head — Bell has made us a paragraph, my dear." She pours the tea, the ally with her own agenda, the week's cost worn like the diamonds she didn't wear. "The price," says Rose — the partner's question, the debt of the witnessed, still owed. "Paid," says Lavinia, "and priced by Bell besides. Two doors closed — but the paragraph, my dear. The town read us both, and chose to be entertained." The partnership's grammar — the separate reins, the shared paragraph, the war's advantage taken and the ally's agenda honored, both true at once.)*
> *("Next week," says Lavinia, "smaller, I think." The diversion's measure — the gutter tires of everyone, even the theatre. "The street campaign is yours now, Rose — the walking, the rose, the presence. My theatre was the week's; the weeks ahead are the corners'." Rose nods — the partner's acceptance, the division of the war's labor re-drawn. "And the sitters?" Lavinia's eyebrow — the ally's intelligence, the town's own network. "Octavia's émigrés — polite, prompt, asking after you. Watch the studio's door, my dear. The purse has many hands." The warning, the ally's gift, unasked. She rises, the walking silk settling. "We are a set," she says again at the door. "Bell said so. And Bell — " the smile, the real one — "is never wrong about the town." The door closes. Rose writes: "The set: allied. Next week: smaller. The door: watched." The verdict's week, closed.)*
> *(The Gazette lies between them like a shared letter — the morning-room, the tea, the verdict read together. "We are a set," Lavinia says. "Bell has made us a paragraph." The price re-priced in the paragraph's light: the whispers, the two doors, the week's cost — paid, and priced besides, the town having read them both and chosen to be entertained. "Next week, smaller," the ally says — the gutter tiring of everyone, even the theatre. The warning comes unasked, the ally's gift: the studio's door, the purse's many hands, Octavia's émigrés. Rose reads it twice — the general's discipline — and the question the note asks without asking: what does the purse want with Octavia's light? Polite émigré financiers, new to town, paying promptly in coin, come through the lady's card — asking after the Hartwell girl, twice now. The shape recognized, nothing proved — the campaign's arithmetic, the artist's innocence, the two held apart by the bargain.)*

The note filed in the book — "The sitters: asking, twice. The decision: pending." The romance of the route — the artist allied, the light kept clean, the question kept. scenes.synopsis: The week's accounting — the street campaign's honest books.

> *(Sunday evening — the week's accounting, the campaign's honest books, the pencil moving in the morning-room with Augusta auditing over her shoulder. The street's week, tallied: the corners walked daily — nine, ten, eleven, noon — the honest three honored, the bought ones noted, the cap-touches counted like coin. Larkin's report — the boy's weekly accounting, the witness's books: the extra pay thinner, the libel days fewer, the double days halved — "They're not paying the double so often, miss. The numbers aren't — " the street's eloquence — "landing." The suppression pay — most days still, the Gazette stacked at the Grecian, the keeper's conscience still priced. The honest corners — three still, holding. The week's arithmetic: the purse's street spending, thinning; the campaign's presence spending, daily.)*
> *("You're louder than the paper, miss." Larkin's accounting, the boy's own verdict — the witness's scoring, unasked. "Not the cry — you. The street looks at you more than it listens to me." The street campaign's books, balanced: the purse buys the cry, she buys the presence; the purse buys the silence, she buys the noise; the purse's coin thins, her presence compounds. Augusta closes the book — the general's audit, once. "The week's account," says the general. "Favorable. Bell will price it Thursday — and the price will be the town's." She writes the week's last entry: "The street: walked. The cry: thinner. The purse: thinning. The presence: compounding." The honest books, closed — the campaign's week, won on the street's own terms. Larkin touches his cap at the door — the week's pay in his palm, honest, counted. "Same time Monday, miss?" "Same time Monday, Larkin." The street's witness, retained — the third road, held.)*

scenes.synopsis: The Sabbath street — the cry thinner, the stacks fuller, the town resting.
scenes.prose:
> *(Sunday — the Sabbath street, the week's one quiet morning: the cries thinner, the corners quieter, the town resting from its own noise. She walks — the ritual's dress exchanged for the Sunday plain, the white rose still at the waist, the clean name's emblem even on the day of rest — and the street is a different text today: the hawkers' stacks fuller, the unsold papers piling, the libel's numbers sitting. A boy at the Grecian — bought by the purse, the suppression coin in his keeper's till — catches her eye and winks, the street's own courtesy, unbought. The Chapter House keeper bows — the honest one, the bow deeper on Sunday, the week's alliance honored. The free Lantern stacks at the Turk's Head — "TAKE ONE" — sit fuller than ever, the town not taking, the libel unbought even at no price.)*

"Presence at altitude," she says. "The purse buys the sky, Lavinia. The extra is certain on balloon nights — the libel flown with the wonder. I went to look up with the street." Lavinia's laugh — the ally's laugh, the one that means the plan is good and the invitation overdue. "Next time," she says, "I come. Diamonds — " the smile, the real one — "at altitude. The town has never seen it. Neither has the sky.")*
> *("The four roads," says Rose — the book open, the campaign's geography complete: the press, the chapel, the street, the sky. "The purse's whole estate — mapped. The press bought, the cry bought, the suppression bought, the wonder bought. And the counter — " she turns the page — "presence. Against paper, against silence, against wonder." Lavinia considers — the ally's arithmetic, the agenda showing. "The purse will always outbid you, my dear. Being deeper." "And I," says Rose, "will always out-presence it. Being there." The partnership's grammar — the separate reins, the shared paragraph, the war's advantage taken. "We shall keep looking up," says Lavinia at the door, the walking silk settling, the diamonds promised for the next ascent. "The town looks up on its own terms, my dear — and last night, it saw you." The door closes. Rose writes: "The partners: at altitude. The four roads: mapped. The purse: out-presenced." The sky's week, closed.)*

The book opens to the four roads — press, chapel, street, sky — the estate mapped, the counter named: presence, against everything. "The purse will always outbid you, being deeper." scenes.prose:
> *(The map-table — the evening, the book open to all four roads, the campaign's whole geography: the press — the clerk, the scarred knuckle, the chapel's stone; the street — the second hand, the shabby cuffs, the cart's coin; the suppression — most days, the keepers priced; the sky — the balloons funded, the wonder rented, since the summer. The purse, understood — not a man, not a face, but a system: hands, and a face, and a source. The hands: the clerk's, the second hand's — the errands, the coin, the always-coin. The face: offstage — London, the network's own geography, the town's best doors opened by cards like the lady's. The source: deeper still — the money's own origin, the purse behind the purse, the question the campaign has not yet earned the asking of. She writes it under a new heading — "THE PURSE," underlined three times: "Hands: mapped. Face: offstage — London. Source: unearned.")*
> *(The week's intelligence, complete — the villain's shape, the system's anatomy: everything bought, nothing persuaded; the press, the cry, the silence, the wonder — the town's ears, eyes, and upward gaze, all rented. And the counter, complete: presence — against paper, against silence, against wonder — the one thing the purse cannot buy at any price. Augusta reads the map — the general's audit, the evening's stillness. "The face stays offstage, child. The hands are enough — for now." The discipline, the campaign's: trace the coin, not the man; map the hands, not the face; earn the source's asking. She closes the book — the four roads mapped, the purse systematized, the London face offstage where the canon keeps it. "People outlast," she says — the week's last sentence, the campaign's creed. The purse buys everything but outlasting. And she — the lady among the hawkers, the theatre's partner, the clean name at altitude — intends to outlast it all.)*
