scenes.synopsis: dawn after Ch6 — Larkin's last word about balloon nights lands, and the week of facing the charges begins.
scenes.prose:
> *(She has not slept. Ned Larkin's voice has followed her upstairs: the extra pay comes on balloon nights — "they pay for the sky too." So the spectacle is bought — the paper, the hawkers, the coffee-house readers, the sky over Vauxhall, all from one purse, floated over the ton's head like a painted balloon. At the window she watches London begin its day without her permission: lamps out, carts, bells. Below, a boy shouts Thursday's number, though Thursday is three days gone. The war is not against a paper. It is against a purse that never sleeps.)*
> *(On the table: the new number, read till the paragraphs sit in her like swallowed stones. The ruin as family fraud. The suitors as dupes. The restoration as swindle. Three charges, itemized like a bill of sale. Larkin's word explains the sky; what steadies her is colder — she is not afraid. Fear would be simpler. "This week," she says to the empty room, to the cooling toast, "I am not defending myself. I am presenting myself." Not a reply, but a face. The campaign of the clean name begins here.)*
> *(She thinks about the purse that never sleeps — the extra pay on balloon nights, the double pay Larkin named, the sky itself bought and floated over Vauxhall. Pyke's press is only the purse's cheapest instrument. To answer the paper is to answer the money behind it, and money cannot be out-argued, only out-lived. The campaign, then, must be fought on ground no purse can purchase: conduct, witnessed daily, in the open, till the town itself becomes the evidence. She has rebuilt an estate this way — beam by beam, ledger by ledger — and she will rebuild a name the same way.)*
> *(Below, the house wakes — the maid's step, the kitchen's clatter, the day assembling itself without her permission. She dresses with unusual care: the white muslin, unadorned, the sash-rose fresh from yesterday's vase. The white is not mourning and not finery; it is a statement of accounts, and the town will audit it. In the green book she writes the week's first entry — fraud, dupes, swindle, each to be faced alone and answered in public. The charges will be met one by one, never in a heap. She pins the rose, squares her shoulders, and goes down. The week of the clean name begins with a face, not a reply.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Carry Larkin's sentence up the stairs — "they pay for the sky too" — and let it re-price the whole war. → Remembered: The purse behind everything; she never again treats any front as unfunded.
> 2. [stance]Refuse fear as the morning's register — take the general's clarity instead. → Remembered: Which self opens the week; the house will read the difference.
> 3. [micro]Lay the new number on the table beside the toast — the enemy's terms, kept close. → Remembered: Her habit of keeping the libel under her hand; the archive grows.
> 4. [examine]Read the three charges as a bill of sale — fraud, dupes, swindle. → Remembered: The itemizing; she will answer them one by one, never in a heap.
> 5. [stance]"I am not defending myself. I am presenting myself." — the week's doctrine, said aloud. → Remembered: The line the household will quote back to her on the hard days.
> 6. [examine]Watch London begin its day without her permission — the bells, the carts, the shouting boy. → Remembered: Her sense of the city's indifference; it steadies her more than sympathy would.
> 7. [social]Note who is absent from the morning room — no aunt, no general, no counsel yet. → Remembered: She begins the week alone; the solitude is a choice, and noted.
> 8. [choice]Mark the threshold — the campaign of the clean name, begun with a face, not a reply. → Remembered: How she marks beginnings now; the war's calendar turns.

scenes.synopsis: the charges, itemized with counsel — fraud, dupes, swindle laid on the desk like evidence.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill arrives before the toast is cleared — her lawyer does not hurry for trifles. He lays his copy of the Lantern beside hers, two identical enemies on one table, and itemizes. "Charge the first: the Hartwell ruin was not ruin but fraud — your father conspired in his own collapse, and you inherited the proceeds. Charge the second: your suitors are dupes — named by title, one by one, like a menu of fools. Charge the third: the restoration is a swindle — the Park rebuilt on money never honestly yours.")*
> *(Rose listens without moving her face, the way Augusta taught her. "Itemize them and they are smaller," she says. Quill almost smiles. "Itemized, three separate lies — lies are easier to kill one at a time. Heaped, they are an atmosphere, and atmospheres suffocate." She lets him read the fraud paragraph aloud — a general must know the enemy's exact wording. When he finishes: "Then we answer them one at a time, in the open. Tell me, Quill — which can be proved false, and which must simply be lived down?" He opens his notebook. The real work begins.)*
> *(Quill sets the fraud paragraph aside like a surgeon's first instrument. The papers exist — her father's letters, Rackham's ledgers, the Chancery filings — and Pyke printed the opposite of what they say, which is libel's cleanest ground: not interpretation but inversion. A court would take it, Quill says, when the timing is right. The dupes charge is different — no paper can certify that four honorable people are not fools. That charge will die only when the men themselves refuse it, publicly, by being themselves in rooms where the town is watching.)*
> *(The swindle charge is the cleverest — it does not deny the restoration but re-prices it, and motive is proved by conduct, not ledgers. Quill closes his notebook on that one: the town must watch her live honestly until the word sounds absurd in her company. That is not a lawsuit, he says. That is a life. She looks at the two identical enemies on the table — hers and his — and understands the week's architecture for the first time: one charge for the law, one for the men, one for the life. Three separate lies, killed one at a time.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch Quill hurry — read what his haste means about the town's reading. → Remembered: Her eye for what others' urgency tells her; counsel's tempo is intelligence.
> 2. [stance]Take the itemizing as a weapon — three lies are smaller than one atmosphere. → Remembered: Her doctrine of division; she will not fight heaps.
> 3. [social]Let him read the fraud paragraph aloud — hear the enemy's exact wording. → Remembered: Her discipline with hostile text; she knows it by heart now.
> 4. [examine]Study the dupes paragraph — the suitors named "like a menu of fools." → Remembered: Which insult lands on her and which on them; the second cuts deeper.
> 5. [micro]Touch the two identical papers on the table — hers and his. → Remembered: The doubling; she is not the only one keeping the enemy close.
> 6. [stance]Ask which lies can be proved false and which must be lived down — the real question. → Remembered: Her instinct for the right question; Quill answers it straight.
> 7. [examine]Watch him open his notebook — the real work, about to begin. → Remembered: Her recognition of work's true start; she respects the notebook.
> 8. [choice]Decide how much of the fear to show counsel — all, some, or none. → Remembered: Her candor's measure with Quill; it sets the alliance's register.

scenes.synopsis: the law's answer to each charge — what can be proved, what must be lived down.
scenes.prose:
> *("Proved," says Quill, turning the page, "is the fraud charge — or the greater part of it. The ruin's papers exist: your father's letters, Rackham's ledgers, the Chancery filings. Pyke printed the opposite of what the papers say — libel's cleanest ground. A court would take it." He taps the second paragraph. "The dupes charge — unprovable either way, therefore unkillable by law. No court can certify that Lord Julian is not a fool. That charge dies only if the men themselves refuse it.")*
> *("And the swindle?" Quill's mouth does something complicated. "The Park's books would survive any audit. But 'swindle' is about motive, and motive is proved by conduct, not ledgers. The town must watch you live honestly until the word sounds absurd in your company. That is not a lawsuit. That is a life." A long silence. Then Rose: "Then we do both. Fraud gets the law, when the law is ready. The dupes get the men themselves. And the swindle gets my life — week by week, in the open." Quill writes it down. "That is a strategy. I shall bill you for the elegance of it.")*
> *(They discuss the writ's timing — now, or after the living. Quill is for patience: a fraud action filed in the middle of a conduct campaign looks like fear wearing a wig. File it when the town has watched her for a month, he advises, and the court becomes a stage she has already rehearsed. The papers will keep — Rackham's ledgers are not going anywhere, and Pyke's paragraph is not going anywhere either, except into the record as evidence. She accepts the counsel. The law will wait its turn, like everything else this season, and take it when the living has done its work.)*
> *(Over the cold toast they settle the week's doctrine, and Quill writes it in his notebook in his small dry hand: fraud to the law, dupes to the men, swindle to the life. He reads it back, and they both hear how it sounds — not like a defense but like a campaign. A general must know the enemy's exact wording, and she does now; she could recite the fraud paragraph in her sleep. When he rises to go, he pauses at the door. “One more thing, Miss Hartwell. Pyke prints for a purse that pays on balloon nights. Remember that the paper is never the whole war.” She will remember.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear "proved" for the fraud charge — the paper trail exists, Pyke printed its opposite. → Remembered: Her grasp of libel's cleanest ground; she will not waste it.
> 2. [stance]Receive "unkillable by law" for the dupes charge — pride has no jurisdiction. → Remembered: Her understanding that the men must refuse it themselves; the law cannot.
> 3. [social]Mark Quill's complicated mouth on the swindle charge — motive is proved by conduct. → Remembered: Her reading of counsel's honesty; she trusts the hard answers.
> 4. [examine]Weigh "that is not a lawsuit. That is a life." → Remembered: The sentence that becomes the week's doctrine; she carries it into every room.
> 5. [stance]Give the strategy — law for fraud, the men for dupes, her life for swindle. → Remembered: Her tripartite answer; the household will learn it by heart.
> 6. [micro]Watch him write it down — "I shall bill you for the elegance of it." → Remembered: The first real laugh of the consultation; she needed it, and he knew.
> 7. [examine]Sit opposite him in the street's long silence — the decision, settling. → Remembered: How she lets a decision settle; the silence is part of the choosing.
> 8. [choice]Ask when the law should be ready — now, or after the living. → Remembered: Her tempo judgment; the writ's timing is half its power.

scenes.synopsis: charge the first, faced alone — the ruin as family fraud; her father's name in Pyke's type.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone, she reads the fraud paragraph once more — slowly, the way one reads a headstone. "…a ruin too convenient, a collapse too complete, a daughter too quick to inherit…" She has read Rackham's ledgers. She has read her father's letters from the last year, when the handwriting went thin. The ruin was not scenery but shipwreck; her father not a conspirator but a drowning man who taught his daughter to swim by correspondence. Pyke has re-set the worst year of her life as a confidence trick. The insult is not to her. It is to a dead man who cannot answer.)*
> *(She goes to the drawer where her father's last letter lives — the one she reads only when she needs to remember what courage looked like in a failing hand. She does not take it out. She rests her hand on the drawer, the way one rests a hand on a shoulder. "They may print what they like about me. They shall not re-write you." Quill can prove this charge false, and she will let him — but the deeper answer is older than any writ. She closes the drawer and goes down to face the day.)*
> *(She remembers the last year — the handwriting going thin, the letters shorter, the brave jokes in the margins. Her father was not a conspirator but a drowning man, and he taught her to swim by correspondence: how to read a ledger like a chart, how to face a creditor without flinching, how to keep the books honest when honesty cost the most. Pyke has taken that year — the worst year, the bravest year — and re-set it as a confidence trick. The insult is not to her. It is to a dead man who cannot answer, and she will answer for him.)*
> *(Quill can prove this charge false — the papers exist, the court would take it — but the deeper answer is older than any writ. She thinks of the audit her father faced, the calm he wore like a coat, the way he taught her that a ledger is a kind of honesty made visible. “They may print what they like about me,” she says to the drawer, to the letter inside, to the failing hand that wrote it. “They shall not re-write you.” She closes the drawer. The living-down has begun, and it begins with the dead defended.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read the fraud paragraph "like a headstone" — slowly, word by word. → Remembered: Her ritual with the worst paragraph; she reads it standing, never sitting.
> 2. [stance]Refuse the re-writing — "they shall not re-write you. I will not permit it." → Remembered: The vow to her father; it outranks every strategy.
> 3. [micro]Rest her hand on the drawer's handle — a shoulder, not an archive. → Remembered: How she touches what she will not open; the restraint is its own grief.
> 4. [examine]Recall the thin handwriting of the last year's letters — the drowning man, not the conspirator. → Remembered: What she knows that Pyke cannot print; the truth is her ballast.
> 5. [stance]Let the insult land where it belongs — on the dead man who cannot answer. → Remembered: Her anger's true address; it clarifies rather than clouds her.
> 6. [social]Say it to the drawer, the letter, the father who cannot hear and can. → Remembered: Whom she consults when alone; the dead outvote the living.
> 7. [examine]Mark that Quill can prove this one — but proof is the lesser answer. → Remembered: Her ranking of answers; remembering outranks the writ.
> 8. [choice]Close the drawer and go down to face the day — the living-down, begun. → Remembered: Her exits from grief are always toward the town; the town is the court.

scenes.synopsis: charge the second, faced alone — the suitors as dupes; the insult lands on the men she loves.
scenes.prose:
> *(The dupes paragraph is the one she cannot read twice — not because it wounds her, but because it wounds them, and they will read it. Julian: "a marquess's heir taken in like a schoolboy." Laurent: "a Frenchman fleeced in a foreign drawing-room, charm for charm." Henry: "a soldier outflanked at his own game." Even Octavia: "an artist commissioned to paint a fraud and paid in flattery." Four honorable people, set in type as fools, sold for a penny. She thinks of Julian's pride — the load-bearing wall of him — and of Henry's steadiness, never yet tested against laughter.)*
> *(Quill said no court can certify that a man is not a fool. So the answer must come from the men themselves, or from her conduct rendering the charge absurd. She walks the long gallery past the Hartwell portraits — ancestors who survived worse print, nailed to church doors. "They are not my dupes," she says to the portraits. "They are my suitors, and they chose me with their eyes open." The charge that cannot be sued must be outlived — beautifully, in white, in public, with all four at her side when she can arrange it.)*
> *(She thinks of each of them reading it — Julian's pride, the load-bearing wall of him, taking the hit the way he takes everything: standing. Laurent's charm, which will turn the insult into a joke at dinner and feel it later, alone. Henry's steadiness, never yet tested against laughter, the soldier's dignity held very still. Octavia's clarity, the artist's eye that will see the paragraph for what it is — a bad composition, badly lit — and say so. Four honorable people, set in type as fools. The charge insults her by insulting them, and that is why it is the one she cannot read twice.)*
> *(Quill said no court can certify that a man is not a fool, so the answer must come from the men themselves — or from her conduct rendering the charge absurd. She will have them at her side when she can arrange it: Julian at the assembly, Henry at the morning calls, Laurent at dinner, Octavia with her sketchbook in the corner, all of them visibly, deliberately, unfooled. The town reads who stands near a woman. “They are not my dupes,” she says to the portraits, and the portraits — who survived worse print, nailed to church doors — seem to approve. “They are my suitors, and they chose me with their eyes open.”)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Refuse to read the dupes paragraph twice — name why: it wounds them, not her. → Remembered: Where her pain actually lands; the distinction governs the week.
> 2. [stance]Picture each man reading it — Julian's pride, Henry's steadiness, Laurent's charm, Octavia's clarity. → Remembered: Her private catalog of their vulnerabilities; she guards it like funds.
> 3. [social]Hear Quill's "no court can certify that a man is not a fool" again, in the gallery's echo. → Remembered: The law's boundary, accepted; she stops asking the law for this one.
> 4. [examine]Look at the Hartwell portraits — worse print, nailed to church doors, survived. → Remembered: Her use of ancestry as ballast; the portraits are her war council.
> 5. [stance]"They are not my dupes. They are my suitors." — said to the portraits, as policy. → Remembered: The sentence she will repeat all week; it hardens with use.
> 6. [micro]Walk the long gallery's full length — the thinking walk, completed. → Remembered: Her habit of deciding on foot; the gallery measures her resolutions.
> 7. [examine]Decide the charge "must be outlived — beautifully, in white, in public." → Remembered: Her aesthetic of endurance; outliving is a performance art.
> 8. [choice]Resolve to have them at her side when she can arrange it — the visible answer. → Remembered: Her strategy of company; the town reads who stands near her.

scenes.synopsis: charge the third, faced alone — the restoration as swindle; her work, her Park, her books.
scenes.prose:
> *(The swindle paragraph is the cleverest, therefore the most dangerous: it does not deny the restoration — the Park rebuilt, the tenants housed, the debts honored — it re-prices it. "…a restoration too rapid, too complete, too convenient…" Pyke has taken the two hardest years of her life — ledgers by lamplight, timber contracts, mornings in muddy boots arguing with builders — and re-set them as a conjuring trick. From the window she looks toward the Park, miles away in Bath, and sees it anyway: the new roof, the drained field, the cottages' honest smoke. Every beam accounted for.)*
> *(Quill said motive is proved by conduct: the town must watch her live honestly until "swindle" sounds absurd in her company. Not one grand gesture but a hundred small ones, repeated till boring. The penny to the newspaper boy. The witnessed invoice. "Very well," she says to the unseen Park. "If the charge is my life, then my life is the answer, lived where everyone can watch." Every call a verdict, every appearance evidence. She rings for her maid. The white gowns come out.)*
> She knows every beam by its invoice, every field by its drainage account, every cottage by the tenant's name. Two years of ledgers by lamplight, of timber contracts argued in muddy boots, of mornings that began before the lamps were out. Pyke calls it a conjuring trick. She calls it Tuesday. The restoration was not rapid; it was relentless. It was not convenient; it was accounted for, to the penny.)*
> So be it — not one grand gesture but a hundred small ones, repeated till boring. The penny to the newspaper boy, counted out. The witnessed invoice, paid on the nail. The tenant's letter, answered in her own hand. Every call a verdict, every appearance evidence. “Very well,” she says to the unseen Park, to the smoke rising straight, to the two hardest years of her life. “If the charge is my life, then my life is the answer — lived where everyone can watch.” She rings for her maid. The white gowns come out.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Name the swindle paragraph the cleverest — it re-prices rather than denies. → Remembered: Her respect for the enemy's best shot; she never underestimates Pyke again.
> 2. [stance]Inventory the restoration's true cost — lamplight ledgers, muddy boots, timber contracts. → Remembered: Her private ledger of the hard years; it is her evidence and her armor.
> 3. [micro]Look toward the Park from a Bath window — miles away, seen anyway. → Remembered: How she holds the estate in mind; distance never loosens the grip.
> 4. [examine]Hear Quill's "motive is proved by conduct, not ledgers" as a work order. → Remembered: Her translation of counsel into conduct; the week becomes the brief.
> 5. [stance]"My life is the answer, and I shall live it where everyone can watch." → Remembered: The week's doctrine, finalized; the town is her jury now.
> 6. [social]Plan the hundred small honesties — the penny, the tip, the daily arithmetic. → Remembered: Her doctrine of boring virtue; spectacle is the enemy's tool, not hers.
> 7. [examine]Shape the unimpeachable week — every call a verdict, every appearance evidence. → Remembered: The campaign's architecture; she builds weeks the way she builds estates.
> 8. [choice]Ring for the maid — the white gowns come out. → Remembered: The moment the war became wardrobe; the town will read the color.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the resolve, set; the house adjusts to a general at war.
scenes.prose:
> *(The house can tell. By noon the servants move differently — quieter on the stairs, quicker with trays — the way households move when the mistress has stopped being busy and started being at war. Letitia, meeting the new tempo in the hall, puts a hand to her heart: "Oh, it's to be *that* kind of week" — and orders extra white gloves. Augusta, told at luncheon, nods once — a general recognizing mobilization — and asks for the carriage at three. Rose feels it physically: a settling in the shoulders, the calm her father wore before a difficult audit.)*
> *(She writes three notes before luncheon, in her business hand. To Quill: the fraud charge is his, when he judges the timing. To Élise: white, unadorned, a week's worth — the clean name, to be worn. To Mrs. Pye at the Park: hold the household ready; the town will watch the estate's mistress, and she will watch the town. She seals all three with the Hartwell crest, and the wax smells of the schoolroom where sealing was a game. "Not a game now," she says, and rings for the footman. The week of verdicts begins with the post.)*
> *(The afternoon's first call is a small test, and she passes it the way she will pass them all: white, unhurried, unflinching. The drawing-room does its half-second of assessment and finds nothing to assess — the audit, begun. Driving home, she enters the call in the green book in her business hand: date, house, witnesses, verdict. The book will be the campaign's ledger, every appearance an entry, every entry evidence. Letitia's extra white gloves arrive by the evening post, twelve pairs, and Rose laughs for the first time that day — the aunt's mobilization is always sartorial, and always exactly right.)*
> *(Augusta's carriage at three is a council of war on wheels — the general's verdict on the morning's consultation, delivered between streets: the week's architecture is sound, the three charges are the right three to face, and Rose is to hold the line. By evening the house has fully become a headquarters: the morning room is a map room, the hall table a dispatch desk, the servants a staff. She stands at the window as the lamps are lit and feels the resolve settle — not as inspiration but as schedule. Tomorrow: the calls, the flowers, the witnessed kindnesses. The war is joined.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Feel the house adjust — the servants' new tempo on the stairs. → Remembered: Her awareness of the household as an instrument; she tunes it deliberately.
> 2. [social]Take Letitia's hand-to-heart — "oh, it's to be *that* kind of week." → Remembered: The aunt's instant mobilization; extra white gloves, ordered without asking.
> 3. [examine]Read Augusta's single nod — a general recognizing mobilization. → Remembered: The nod as alliance; the two generals are now formally at war together.
> 4. [micro]Write the three notes — Quill, Élise, Mrs. Pye — in the business hand. → Remembered: Her tripartite mobilization: law, wardrobe, estate; nothing is left unposted.
> 5. [stance]Smell the schoolroom in the sealing wax — and set the memory aside. → Remembered: Her discipline with nostalgia; the past serves, never steers.
> 6. [examine]"Not a game now" — said to the seals, as oath. → Remembered: The line that ends girlhood's games; the crest is a weapon now.
> 7. [choice]Send the week out with the post — the verdicts, begun by footman. → Remembered: Her faith in beginnings by post; the town will answer in kind.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — the week's first call; white, unadorned, with the flower language begun.
scenes.prose:
> *(The white gowns are laid out, and Rose stands before them the way a general reviews troops. Élise's note came back within the hour — "white, unadorned, a week's worth" is already being cut — but today needs something now, from the wardrobe as it stands. Three candidates. The choice is diegetic and remembered: the town will read this morning's call as the first page of the week's evidence, and the Gazette's fashion eye misses nothing. Augusta's old rule governs: no white till vindication — but Augusta's note this morning said only "begin," and beginning, Rose decides, is its own kind of vindication. The clean name must be worn before it can be recognized.)*
> *(She considers. The plain white muslin — honest, severe, almost a uniform; it says* I have nothing to conceal, *and says it loudly. The white sarcenet with the grey pelisse — softer, more approachable; it says* I am still a woman, not a writ, *and invites the town closer. The white cambric with a single white rose at the sash — the flower language, begun deliberately; it says* the clean name, *in a vocabulary the ton is about to learn by heart. No jewels — the week is unadorned, and the Gazette will score any glitter as protest. She makes the choice the way she makes all choices this week: as evidence, entered into the record.)*
> *(Before the glass she holds each candidate against the morning's purpose. The muslin is the strongest statement — but strength, she knows, reads as defense, and a woman on trial in white muslin looks like a woman on trial. The sarcenet is the kindest — but kindness can be misread as concession, and this week nothing may be conceded. The cambric with the rose is the truest: it does not argue innocence, it demonstrates it, in the town's oldest vocabulary. Flowers are read before faces in London. She chooses the rose.)*
> *(The white rose at the sash is not decoration — it is the campaign's first sentence. In the flower language, the white rose says what she may not say: silence, I am worthy, the clean thing unsaid. It will be renewed daily, a fresh flower every morning, because a fresh flower is a fact and embroidery is a claim, and this week deals in facts. Bell's fashion eye will note it — verdicts have a way of mentioning a ribbon — and the town will learn the vocabulary the way it learned everything else: by seeing it, daily, until it knows it by heart. She pins it herself. The first page of the week's evidence is written in petals.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Review the three candidates "like a general reviews troops" — the morning's evidence. → Remembered: Her martial approach to the wardrobe; the town is the parade ground.
> 2. [stance]Set Augusta's "no white till vindication" against this morning's "begin" — and choose beginning. → Remembered: Her judgment on when rules bend; the general's note is read as permission.
> 3. [choice]Take the plain white muslin — the uniform of nothing-to-conceal. → Remembered: Severity chosen; the town reads armor, and armor invites attack.
> 4. [choice]Take the white sarcenet with the grey pelisse — approachability as strategy. → Remembered: Softness chosen; the town reads humanity, and humanity invites belief.
> 5. [choice]Take the white cambric with the single white rose — the flower language, begun. → Remembered: The rose chosen; floriography enters the war as a combatant.
> 6. [examine]Refuse all jewels — "the week is unadorned, and the Gazette will score any glitter as protest." → Remembered: Her jewel discipline; restraint is the week's ornament.
> 7. [social]Enter the choice "as evidence, into the record" — the town as jury, the mirror as clerk. → Remembered: Her framing of dress as testimony; every fitting is a deposition.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE CHARGES. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill returns at two with the writ papers drafted but unsigned — the fraud action, ready to file, waiting only on her word. "Three roads," he says, laying the draft beside the* Lantern *like a second weapon on the table. "One: answer each charge publicly — letters to the papers, denials, a paragraph war. Meet ink with ink, in the open. Two: answer with conduct only — the unimpeachable week, extended to a season; no denials, no letters; live so that the libel starves. Three: file this" — he taps the draft — "and sue Pyke now, in the open, and make the court our stage. Choose knowing that the choice is the season.")*
> *(The morning's consultation sits behind her — the three charges itemized, the doctrine settled — and now the charges demand an answer. She thinks of Augusta's warning: the paragraph war is Pyke's ground; of Letitia's counsel: write nothing, be everything; of her father's hand, failing, teaching her to swim by correspondence. The writ lies unsigned, the Lantern lies open, and between them the whole season waits like a held breath. She has faced mobs of creditors, rebuilt an estate from its ledgers up, buried her father and kept his books honest — and never once has a choice been so purely hers. No suitor can make it for her. No general can order it. She lays one hand on each weapon — the writ, the paper — and feels the season balance on the choice.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The charges:*
- **Answer each publicly** — *Gazette flavor set: combative.* Letters, denials, a paragraph war fought in the open — ink met with ink. *(Quill warns of the cost; Augusta respects the nerve; Lavinia will approve the aggression.)*
- **Answer with conduct only** — *Standing+; the long game.* No denials, no letters — only a life so unimpeachable the libel starves for want of a second course. *(Augusta approves the discipline; Quill holds the writ in reserve.)*
- **Sue Pyke now** — *Quill+; the law engaged.* File the fraud action at once — the writ, the court, the open stage. *(Letitia is thrilled; Augusta warns that a trial is a theatre where the audience outnumbers the jury.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the charges answered in ink, in conduct, or in court. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the aunt's counsel — comic, fierce, and unexpectedly strategic.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia arrives with the extra white gloves and an opinion, in that order. "Conduct only, darling — I heard it through the door, and before you scold me, the door was ajar and my ear was lonely." She deposits the gloves like evidence. "Letters are for people with nothing better to do. You have a week of calls, four suitors with wounded pride, and a town to convince. Write nothing. *Be* everything. Eleven years a widow in this town taught me the great secret of surviving print: the town forgets what it read the moment it sees something better to look at. Give them you — in white, unflinching — until the Lantern reads like last week's weather.")*
> *(Rose laughs — the first real laugh since the charges were itemized. "And the suitors?" "Oh, let them be angry, darling. Angry men are *useful*. Julian's temper has wanted a respectable object for years — give it Pyke. Only forbid them nothing, permit them everything, and take the credit." She rises. "They shall not have you, darling — not for a pennyworth. Not while I have gloves to lend." The door closes. The gloves remain. Rose puts them on. They fit.)*
> *(Alone with the gloves, Rose considers the counsel behind the comedy. Letitia survived eleven years of widowhood in this town — eleven years of print, of paragraphs, of the Lantern's weather — and survived them not by answering but by being better to look at than the libel. The town forgets what it read the moment it sees something better to look at. It is not frivolity; it is field-tested doctrine. Rose pulls the gloves on slowly, finger by finger, the way she would load a pistol. They fit. Of course they fit — the aunt's counsel always fits, the way her gloves always fit, because both were made for this exact hand.)*
> *(Write nothing. Be everything. She takes it as the week's marching orders — not a rejection of Quill's law but its complement. The writ will speak in court, in its season; she will speak in drawing-rooms, daily, in white. And the suitors — angry men are useful — she turns the phrase over like a coin. Julian's temper, Henry's dignity, Laurent's charm, Octavia's clarity: four wounded prides, four instruments, if she aims them and does not merely soothe them. She will forbid them nothing, permit them everything, and take the credit — the aunt's economy of war. The gloves are on. The war is joined.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the eavesdropped counsel — "my ear was lonely" — with laughter, not scolding. → Remembered: Her indulgence of the aunt's methods; the alliance deepens through comedy.
> 2. [examine]"The town forgets what it read the moment it sees something better to look at." → Remembered: Letitia's doctrine of visibility; Rose will test it all week.
> 3. [stance]Take "write nothing. *Be* everything." as the week's marching orders. → Remembered: How she receives auntly strategy; the comic source doesn't dilute the sense.
> 4. [examine]Hear "angry men are *useful*" — the suitors' temper, priced as an asset. → Remembered: Her consideration of weaponized anger; the idea will resurface at the decision.
> 5. [micro]Accept the gloves — "they fit" — the small ceremony, completed. → Remembered: The gloves as talisman; she wears them to the week's hardest call.
> 6. [social]"They shall not have you, darling — not for a pennyworth." — the vow, received. → Remembered: The aunt's fierce line; Rose will quote it when the week turns hard.
> 7. [examine]Watch Letitia rise and go — the exit, timed like a curtain. → Remembered: Her appreciation of the aunt's theatrical exits; they always land.
> 8. [choice]Decide how much of the aunt's counsel to admit she'll follow — all, or "we'll see." → Remembered: Her candor's measure with family; Letitia hears the truth or the kindness.

scenes.synopsis: the general's counsel — Augusta prices the three roads like campaigns.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta listens without moving, the way she listens to everything — as if stillness were note-taking. "The paragraph war is Pyke's ground. He prints weekly; you would write daily; the town would tire of you both. The writ" — one finger taps Quill's draft like a map's danger — "is a theatre where the audience outnumbers the jury, and the audience has read the libel. But conduct is ground Pyke cannot print on. He can print that you are a fraud. He cannot print that you flinched, if you do not flinch. A week of it, child. Then the town starts keeping score for you.")*
> *("Quill can prove the fraud charge — the papers exist." Augusta nods. "Then let him prove it when the proving does the most damage. A writ filed in anger is a pistol fired in the dark. A writ filed after a month of unimpeachable conduct is an execution." At the door she turns. "The white. I said no white till vindication — but you have begun, and beginning is a kind of vindication I had not considered. Wear it like you mean it." Two generals have told her the same thing in different words. When two generals agree, the war is half decided.)*
> *(She sits very still after the door closes — the stillness Augusta taught her, the general's habit of letting decisions settle like sediment. Two generals have told her the same thing in different words: Quill with his surgeon's patience, Augusta with her campaign maps. He cannot print that you flinched, if you do not flinch. The sentence becomes the week's drill, to be repeated before mirrors and in carriages. She will tell Quill the writ waits a month — not as Augusta's order but as her own decision, which it now is. The writ's leash is hers to hold.)*
> *(And the white — I said no white till vindication, but beginning is a kind of vindication I had not considered. The permission lands like a commission: the white is now sanctioned armor, issued by the general herself. Rose understands what has happened — Augusta has not relaxed a rule but promoted a campaign, and promotion carries obligations. The white must now be worn like she means it: daily, unadorned, unflinching, the flower language begun and sustained. She goes to the glass and practices the not-flinching. When two generals agree, the war is half decided — and the other half is conduct.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch Augusta listen "as if stillness were a form of note-taking." → Remembered: Her study of the general's stillness; she is learning to listen the same way.
> 2. [stance]Hear the paragraph war priced as "Pyke's ground" — the warning, weighed. → Remembered: Her respect for ground she cannot hold; she stops wanting the ink war.
> 3. [examine]Read the finger-tap on the writ — "a theatre where the audience outnumbers the jury." → Remembered: Augusta's image of the court; it cools any haste to file.
> 4. [social]"" — the order, received. → Remembered: The sentence that becomes the week's drill; she repeats it before mirrors.
> 5. [stance]Take "a writ filed after a month of conduct is an execution" — timing as weapon. → Remembered: Her new doctrine of the writ's timing; Quill will be told.
> 6. [examine]Receive the reversed ruling on white — "beginning is a kind of vindication I had not considered." → Remembered: The permission, granted; the white is now sanctioned armor.
> 7. [micro]Sit very still after the door closes — the agreement of two generals, absorbed. → Remembered: Her stillness after counsel; decisions settle in silence with her.
> 8. [choice]Decide whether to tell Quill the writ waits a month — now, or later. → Remembered: Her tempo with counsel; the writ's leash is hers to hold.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the week's appearances begin; morning calls under the libel's weather.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week begins in thin, respectable rain. Rose makes her first call at eleven, in the white cambric with the single white rose at the sash — the flower language, begun — and the drawing-room does what drawing-rooms do when the Lantern is still warm: a half-second of assessment, quick as a card dealt, before the smiles. She does not flinch; she practiced in the mirror, and the practice holds. Mrs. Almeria Fane — who read the libel aloud at her own table — receives her with the particular warmth of a woman deciding, in real time, which way the wind blows. The wind is blowing toward white.)*
> *(Three calls by two. At each, the same half-second, the same holding, the same thaw. At the third an older woman holds Rose's hand a fraction too long: "My dear, we are *so* glad to see you out." The emphasis does a paragraph's work: *out* means unbowed. Driving home with gloves still white and the rose unbruised, Rose understands: the town is not convinced yet, but it is *watching* — and watching is the first stage of belief. The week's first verdicts are favorable.)*
> *(Between the second and third calls she sits in the carriage with the green book open and writes the verdicts in her business hand: Fane — thaw. Almeria's emphasis — out. The third — hand held too long, meaning unbowed. Three calls, three thaws, three entries. The book is already working — the week's ledger, every appearance an entry, every entry evidence. The rain thins. She thinks of Quill's doctrine: fraud to the law, dupes to the men, swindle to the life — and adds a fourth line for herself: the town to the watching. The watching is hers to court.)*
> *(That evening Augusta hears the report and nods once — a general acknowledging a first engagement: contact made, no casualties, ground held. Watching is the first stage of belief, Rose says, trying the sentence aloud, and Augusta's nod deepens — the doctrine is sound. Tomorrow: four calls, a bookseller's, the Park agent's office, the timber invoice paid to the penny before witnesses. She lays out the white cambric for the second day and pins a fresh rose at the sash. The flower language, continued. The week's first verdicts are favorable — and the week is only beginning.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Enter the first drawing-room in rain — "a half-second of assessment, quick as a card dealt." → Remembered: Her reading of rooms; the half-second becomes her favorite instrument.
> 2. [stance]Hold the not-flinching — mirror practice, deployed in company. → Remembered: Her discipline's first field test; it holds, and she notes that it holds.
> 3. [social]Receive Mrs. Almeria Fane's real-time warmth — the wind, assessed. → Remembered: Her map of the town's weathervanes; Fane blows toward white now.
> 4. [examine]"We are *so* glad to see you out" — parse the emphasis as a paragraph. → Remembered: Her ear for coded kindness; the town speaks in italics.
> 5. [micro]Drive home with gloves still white and the rose unbruised — the small audit. → Remembered: Her end-of-day inventory; white gloves are the week's ledger.
> 6. [stance]Name watching as "the first stage of belief" — the general's read of the engagement. → Remembered: Her doctrine of the town's attention; she will court the watching.
> 7. [choice]Decide the day's verdict — favorable, and entered. → Remembered: How she scores days; the week's tally begins at three calls, three thaws.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the week's second day; the discipline of repetition.
scenes.prose:
> *(The second day is harder, as second days are: the novelty of resolve worn off, the resolve still new enough to chafe. The morning's Lantern has nothing new — its own insult: Pyke lets the charges sit, staining by stillness. She reads the three paragraphs standing, three minutes, no more — a ritual of confrontation — then eats the eggs hot, deliberately, because Augusta is watching and hot eggs read as strength.)*
> *(Four calls, a bookseller's, and the Park agent's office, where she is *seen* — by three clerks and a queue — paying a timber invoice to the penny and taking the receipt with thanks. Letitia, debriefed in the carriage, declares it "a triumph of tedium," and Rose laughs till the carriage shakes, because it is the point: a fraud does not pay timber invoices to the penny before witnesses. The town is watching her be boring, day after day, and the watching is working — she feels it the way a rider feels a horse settle. Not glamorous. Better: believed.)*
> *(That evening she totals the second day in the green book: four calls, a bookseller's, the Park agent's office, one timber invoice paid to the penny before three clerks and a queue. A triumph of tedium — Letitia's phrase, entered verbatim, because the aunt's phrases have a way of becoming the week's mottoes. Not glamorous. Better: believed. The resolve chafed this morning; tonight it fits like the gloves.)*
> *(She thinks about Pyke's insult — he lets the charges sit, staining by stillness — and understands the week's answer at last. Staining by stillness can only be answered by bleaching by conduct: the same stillness, turned inside out. He will not print a retraction; he will simply be left printing to a town that has watched her pay timber invoices to the penny. Tomorrow: the third morning, the question of detail, the white renewed. She lays out the week's accessories and considers the small decisions that carry the week's meaning. The boring is the weapon. She sharpens it.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Read the three paragraphs standing — "a ritual of confrontation, three minutes, no more." → Remembered: Her discipline with the enemy's text; the ritual hardens into habit.
> 2. [stance]Eat the eggs hot, deliberately — small normalcy as strength. → Remembered: Her performance of appetite; Augusta reads it, and approves.
> 3. [micro]Pay the timber invoice to the penny — *seen*, by clerks and a queue. → Remembered: Her doctrine of witnessed honesty; the receipt is evidence.
> 4. [social]Take Letitia's "triumph of tedium" — and laugh till the carriage shakes. → Remembered: The aunt's phrase becomes the week's motto; tedium is the weapon.
> 5. [examine]Feel the town "settle like a horse" — the watching, working. → Remembered: Her equestrian reading of public opinion; she rides the town, never drives it.
> 6. [stance]Choose boring over glamorous — "it is better than glamorous. It is believed." → Remembered: Her aesthetic of credibility; she will be boring all week on purpose.
> 7. [choice]Score the second day — harder, and won anyway. → Remembered: Her tally of hard days; the week's ledger grows by effort, not ease.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — the week's accessories; motif, colorway, thread, and the full set, with social consequence.
scenes.prose:
> *(The third morning brings a question of detail: the white is established, but *unadorned* must be renewed daily or it curdles into habit. Before the glass Rose considers the small decisions that carry the week's meaning — each diegetic, remembered, consequential, with Bell's fashion eye scoring all week. The motif: a single fresh white rose, renewed daily, never embroidered — embroidery is assertion; a fresh flower is fact. The colorway: white on white, no grey — grey is nuance, and the week has no room for nuance. The thread: ivory silk, never silver — silver catches light, and attention must be earned, not caught.)*
> *(The full set: white gloves, plain hair comb, no pendant, no bracelet — nothing that jingles or glints. The jewel case stays shut. In the glass she sees not a fashion but a statement of accounts: every item declared, nothing undeclared. The town is learning to audit her, and she intends to pass the audit.)*
> *(She wears the week's uniform through the third day's calls and feels the difference the details make. The fresh rose at the sash draws the eye first, always — the flower language, working — and the eye that finds the rose finds nothing else to find: no glitter, no jingle, no assertion. At the second call a woman asks after the rose's meaning, and Rose answers simply: the clean name, in the town's oldest vocabulary. The woman nods slowly. The vocabulary is being learned. By Friday the town will recognize the uniform — white, rose, restraint — the way it recognizes a regiment's colors.)*
> *(Bell's fashion eye is on her all week — verdicts have a way of mentioning a ribbon — and she dresses for Bell too, the way a barrister dresses for the judge. The Gazette's verdicts will score the white, the rose, the restraint; the scores will be read by the town the way the town reads everything: as permission. That evening she audits the day in the glass: every item declared, nothing undeclared, the rose fresh, the gloves white. The town is learning to audit her, and she intends to pass the audit — daily, till the passing is the story.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Face the jewel case and do not open it — the discipline, renewed. → Remembered: Her daily refusal of glitter; the unopened case is the week's ornament.
> 2. [choice]Choose the motif — a single fresh white rose, renewed daily, never embroidered. → Remembered: Fresh over embroidered; fact over assertion, and the town learns the difference.
> 3. [choice]Choose the colorway — white on white, no grey, no nuance. → Remembered: Severity of palette; the week admits no shading, and the Gazette notes it.
> 4. [choice]Choose the thread — ivory silk, never silver, never catching light. → Remembered: Her refusal of caught light; attention must be earned, not caught.
> 5. [examine]Assemble the full set — gloves, plain comb, nothing that jingles or glints. → Remembered: The week's uniform, finalized; the town will recognize it by Friday.
> 6. [stance]Read herself in the glass as "a statement of accounts" — every item declared. → Remembered: Her audit-ready self-image; she dresses to be examined.
> 7. [social]Consider Bell's fashion eye — "verdicts have a way of mentioning a ribbon." → Remembered: Her awareness of the Gazette's scoring; she dresses for Bell too.

scenes.synopsis: romance — Julian's line on being called a dupe: anger, and what the anger covers.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian comes at four, unannounced — for Julian, the equivalent of a declaration of emergency. He has read the dupes paragraph the way he reads insults: personally, thoroughly, wanting to hit someone. "A marquess's heir taken in like a schoolboy. *Taken in.* As if I were a purse left on a church pew." He stops his pacing. "Rose. Tell me you do not think me a fool — at this moment the only opinion I require is yours, and I require it stated.")*
> *(She states it: "You are not a fool. You are the least fooled man I know — you saw through Rackham's books before I did." True, and it lands like water on a burn. Underneath the anger she sees what it covers: not pride but fear — that the town believes it, that his judgment is now a public question. "They will not think it long," she says. "Boring women do not take in marquesses' heirs." He laughs — unwilling, then real. "God help Pyke when you are boring on purpose." The anger is banked. For Julian, banked is managed.)*
> *(After he goes she stands at the window and watches his carriage turn the corner, and thinks about what she saw under the anger: not pride but fear — that his judgment is now a public question. It is the fear of a man whose whole architecture is load-bearing, and she understands it the way she understands a building: the wall is sound, but the town is testing it. She will not soothe the fear away — soothing leaves the structure untested. She will give it better work to do. Angry men are useful, Letitia said, and the aunt is always right about men.)*
> *(The decision at the week's end will ask her what to do with the suitors' anger — use it, soothe it, or aim it — and she begins the aiming now, quietly. Julian's temper wants a respectable object: she will give it Pyke, the purse, the whole machinery, aimed through conduct and not through brawling. A marquess's heir, visibly unfooled, standing beside her in white — that is the dupes paragraph answered without a word printed. She writes in the green book: Julian — anger banked. For Julian, banked is managed. The first suitor is steadied. Three to go.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the unannounced arrival — "the equivalent of a declaration of emergency." → Remembered: Her reading of Julian's breaches of form; she takes them seriously.
> 2. [examine]Watch him pace "like a caged animal in a very good coat" — the anger, catalogued. → Remembered: Her private image of his temper; it will be useful to remember the coat held.
> 3. [stance]Hear "the only opinion I require is yours, and I require it stated" — and state it. → Remembered: Her directness with his pride; she never flatters it, only answers it.
> 4. [examine]See under the anger — not pride but fear, "that his judgment is now a public question." → Remembered: Her perception of what his temper covers; she will handle the fear, not the fury.
> 5. [social]"Boring women do not take in marquesses' heirs" — the line, delivered. → Remembered: Her weaponized tedium, deployed in romance; he laughs, and the laugh is the victory.
> 6. [micro]Let him take her hand — the anger banked, the contact permitted. → Remembered: The hand-holding's terms; banked anger may touch, unbanked may not.
> 7. [examine]Note "banked, which for Julian is the same as managed" — the assessment. → Remembered: Her calibration of his temper; she will measure all his moods against this one.
> 8. [choice]Decide what to do with his anger — use it, soothe it, or aim it. → Remembered: Her first instinct toward weaponized suitors; the decision foreshadows the key choice.

scenes.synopsis: romance — Laurent's line on being called a dupe: charm, and the steel under it.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent arrives at five with violets — never white roses; never on-the-nose. In the flower language violets mean modesty, and the joke is so deliberate Rose laughs before he's through the door. "A Frenchman fleeced in a foreign drawing-room. *Charm for charm.* I am wounded — not by the insult, which is beneath me, but by the *style*, which is beneath *him*. If one calls me dupe, one might at least do it with wit." He settles, all easy lines, and she watches for the steel.)*
> *(It comes when she asks what he'll do. "I shall be *seen* enjoying your company — conspicuously, expensively, often — until the town concludes that whatever I am, I am not a man who is taken in. A dupe hides. I shall not hide." At the door: "And if Pyke prints another word about my judgment, I shall call on him — socially — and explain, *charm for charm*, what I think of his." Charm as weapon, duelist's timing underneath. Rose notes: Laurent's anger is the most dangerous of the four, because it is the best dressed.)*
> *(After he goes she holds the violets to the light and considers the leash. Charm for charm — the phrase has a duelist's timing under its manners, and she does not entirely trust the word social. But to forbid the call would be to waste the weapon, and to permit it blindly would be to arm a man she cannot quite govern. The velvet leash, then: permitted, but reported — he will tell her before he goes, and after he returns, and the telling is the leash. She writes it in the green book: Laurent — the call permitted, the leash velvet, the reporting mandatory. The most dangerous of the four, because the best dressed — and the best dressed, she has learned, are always the hardest to refuse.)*
> *(The violets go into water beside the white roses — modesty beside the clean name, the joke beside the doctrine. In the flower language violets mean modesty, and the deliberate joke of them — never white roses; never on-the-nose — is the most Laurent thing about the visit. She thinks of his doctrine: a dupe hides; I shall not hide — and recognizes the rhyme with her own. He will be seen enjoying her company, conspicuously, expensively, often, until the town concludes that whatever he is, he is not a man who is taken in. It is visibility as refutation. It is also, she admits, the most enjoyable of the four refusals to watch. She will hold him to it — and to the leash.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the violets — "modesty," and the deliberate joke. → Remembered: Her delight in his coded humor; the violets join the week's floral record.
> 2. [examine]Hear "beneath *him*" — the insult's style, judged as well as its substance. → Remembered: His aesthetic of insult; she learns that for Laurent, form is content.
> 3. [stance]Watch for the steel behind the charm — and find it, in the card-room coldness. → Remembered: Her catalog of his dangerous moments; the coldness is filed.
> 4. [social]"I shall be *seen* enjoying your company, conspicuously, expensively, and often." → Remembered: His counter-strategy; visibility as refutation, and she will hold him to it.
> 5. [examine]"A dupe hides. I shall not hide." — the doctrine, weighed. → Remembered: His doctrine of exposure; it rhymes with her own, and the rhyme pleases her.
> 6. [micro]Mark the threatened social call on Pyke — "charm for charm," with a duelist's timing. → Remembered: The threat, dressed as manners; she will have to manage this one.
> 7. [stance]"The most dangerous of the four, because it is the best dressed." — the assessment. → Remembered: Her ranking of the suitors' tempers; Laurent's charm outranks Julian's fury.
> 8. [choice]Decide whether to encourage or restrain the social call — now, or never. → Remembered: Her first move toward managing him; the leash is velvet, but it is a leash.

scenes.synopsis: romance — Henry's line on being called a dupe: steadiness, and what steadiness costs.
scenes.prose:
> *(Henry comes at six, on foot, in uniform — straight from the Horse Guards. The uniform straightens the morning room. He does not pace or perform. He stands — Henry's great talent — and says, "A soldier outflanked at his own game. I have been outflanked exactly once, in Spain, and it cost forty men. This costs me nothing but vanity. I can afford vanity." A report, complete and unadorned. But under it she hears the unsaid: the paragraph has followed him into the mess, where men read the Lantern over breakfast and laugh.)*
> *("It will pass." He nods, the soldier's nod. "Things printed about soldiers pass, because soldiers are seen daily doing soldierly things, and print cannot survive daily evidence." He looks at her — the ballroom look, from when everything began. "You are doing the same. The white. The week. Then we run the same campaign on different ground." At the door: "For the record, Miss Hartwell: I was not taken in. I walked in, eyes open, and would do it again." For the first time all week, she feels entirely steady.)*
> *(After he goes the morning room seems straighter, as if the uniform left its geometry behind. She stands where he stood — Henry's great talent, standing — and practices it: feet planted, shoulders level, the ballroom look turned inward. Print cannot survive daily evidence. The sentence joins the week's doctrine, beside he cannot print that you flinched and boring is the weapon. Two campaigns, one ground: he fights his in the mess and at the Horse Guards' tables, she fights hers in drawing-rooms, and neither needs orders from the other. It is the rarest alliance — the parallel one, where each holds a line the other can see.)*
> *(For the first time all week, she feels entirely steady — and she examines the steadiness the way she examines everything now: as evidence. It was transferred, not manufactured; his gift, her acceptance. I walked in, with my eyes open, and I would do it again. The sentence outranks every libel, and she writes it in the green book verbatim, because some sentences are load-bearing and must be preserved exactly. The town will test him — the mess, the breakfast laughter — and he will stand, because standing is what he does. She will stand beside him, visibly, when the campaign permits. Two parallel lines, holding.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive him in uniform, on foot — the room, made straighter. → Remembered: The uniform's effect on the house; she notes that discipline is contagious.
> 2. [examine]"It costs me nothing but vanity. I can afford vanity." — the report, parsed. → Remembered: Her reading of his economy of self; vanity is the cheapest thing he owns.
> 3. [stance]Hear the unsaid — the mess, the breakfast laughter, the forty men in Spain. → Remembered: What she hears under his reports; the unsaid is where Henry lives.
> 4. [examine]"Print cannot survive daily evidence" — his doctrine, matching hers. → Remembered: The convergence of their campaigns; she is not alone on this ground.
> 5. [social]Take his long look — "the way he looked at her across the ballroom in S1." → Remembered: The look's history; it carries the whole courtship in a glance.
> 6. [micro]Note he does not take her hand — "restraint is its own language." → Remembered: Her fluency in his restraint; she reads it as clearly as touch.
> 7. [stance]"I walked in, with my eyes open, and I would do it again." — received as vow. → Remembered: The sentence she will keep; it outranks every libel.
> 8. [choice]Let herself feel steady — "for the first time all week, entirely steady herself." → Remembered: The moment steadiness transferred; Henry's gift, accepted.

scenes.synopsis: romance — Octavia's line on being called a dupe: clarity, and the artist's eye on the whole war.
scenes.prose:
> *(Octavia comes at seven with a sketchbook — arriving armed. She has read her paragraph and done what artists do with insults: drawn it. The sketch shows Pyke at a press, printing banknotes with Rose's face — all blank on the back. "Not finished," Octavia says. "I haven't decided what the blank side means. Either nothing behind the fraud — Pyke's accusation, and boring — or everything he can't see, which is the truth, and more interesting to draw." She looks up. "I am not a dupe, Rose. I am a witness. Witnesses choose what they record.")*
> *("Will you finish it?" "I will exhibit it — later. Now it would be a paragraph in a war; after the victory, a *record*." She closes the book. "The others are angry, I suppose. Julian's pacing, Laurent's performing, Henry's standing." "And you?" Octavia smiles — her great gift, the clear smile. "I am an artist. My line is clarity: I saw you, I painted you, I was right. The town will catch up." She leaves the sketch on the table — gift, or promise. Rose keeps it.)*
> *(She keeps the sketch on the table all evening — gift, or promise — and studies it between calls. Pyke at the press, printing banknotes with her face, all blank on the back. The blank side preoccupies her: either nothing behind the fraud — Pyke's accusation, and boring — or everything he can't see, which is the truth. It is the week's best image of the war — better than any paragraph, on either side — because it admits both readings and trusts the viewer. Octavia's great gift, the clear smile, the clearer eye. I am not a dupe, Rose. I am a witness. Witnesses choose what they record. She writes the sentence in the green book. It is the dupes charge, answered in a single line.)*
> *(Later it will be a record — the timing of art, understood. Octavia will not exhibit the sketch now, when it would be a paragraph in the war; she will exhibit it after the victory, when it becomes history. The restraint is the art's own version of Quill's writ-waiting: the weapon held till the holding does the most damage. And the cataloguing — pacing, performing, standing — the artist seeing the set whole, the three men in one line, the love in the observation. I saw you, I painted you, I was right. Clarity as a love language. The town will catch up. The sketch waits on the table, blank-backed, patient, true.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the armed arrival — the sketchbook, opened like a weapon. → Remembered: Her recognition of Octavia's armory; art is her artillery.
> 2. [examine]Study the sketch — Pyke, the press, the blank-backed banknotes. → Remembered: The image's double meaning; she will remember the blank side.
> 3. [stance]"I am not a dupe. I am a witness." — the distinction, received. → Remembered: The re-framing; witnesses choose, dupes are chosen — the power shifts.

Her part is Letitia's: forbid nothing, permit everything, take the credit. Under the strategy something simpler: gratitude, sharp as a needle. They stand in the line of fire beside her — not because she asked, but because honorable people don't leave their own insults unanswered. She writes four thank-yous, four sentences each. The suitors' answer is assembling. It is hers to conduct.)*
> *(She lays the day's four visits out like courses of a meal, and takes them in order: Julian at four, unannounced, the anger banked and aimed; Laurent at five, violets in hand, the charm weaponized and leashed; Henry at six, on foot, in uniform, the steadiness transferred like a commission; Octavia at seven, sketchbook armed, the clarity drawn and waiting. Not in court, not in print, but in conduct: the banked fury, the conspicuous enjoyment, the parallel campaign, the forthcoming record. Her part is Letitia's — forbid nothing, permit everything, take the credit — and Augusta's — aim it. She thinks of Augusta's old rule — no white till vindication — and this morning's note: "begin." Beginning is its own kind of vindication. The house is a headquarters. The mirror is the first jury.)*
> **Occasion brief (published):** "A week of appearances under the libel's charges — morning calls, the bookseller's, the Park agent's office, an evening assembly. The dress code: you will be *audited* — by drawing-rooms, by clerks, by the Gazette's fashion eye — and the audit must find nothing undeclared. White, unadorned; the brief is the clean name (white roses, worn). Mourning colors forbidden; gloves expected; jewels refused. **Editorial criterion: integrity.**"
> **The 3 Directions — commit to one; the week's appearances obey it:**
> **A. The Unimpeachable** — correct in every particular; severity as armor, the town finding nothing to question. Motif: the plain white rose, fresh at the sash — severity's only ornament, renewed daily. Thread: **ivory whitework** (severity, natural) / **silver** (severity, edged) / **steel** (severity, armed). Colorway: white + ivory + silver. Accessories: the long white kid gloves; the plain ivory shawl; the plain hair comb; no pendant — the throat, plain and unbought.
> **B. The Hartwell** — the Park's palette in white; landed, sober, the estate worn as evidence of honest money. Motif: the Hartwell oak sprig, restrained at cuff and hem — the estate, accounted for. Thread: **gold** (the landed, stated) / **copper** (the Park's autumn) / **ivory silk** (the sober, exact). Colorway: white + Hartwell blue + cream. Accessories: the Hartwell blue ribbon at the throat; pearl drop earrings; cream kid gloves; the simple gold pendant.
> **C. The Quiet Defiance** — one perfect detail; the statement, whispered, and let them find it. Motif: the single fresh rose, renewed daily — the whisper, repeated till heard. Thread: **ivory silk** (the whisper, natural) / **pale gold** (the whisper, certain) / **blush silk** (the whisper, human). Colorway: white + ivory + pale gold. Accessories: the pearl-buttoned white gloves; the silver-bordered shawl; the fresh rose at the sash; no other ornament — the whisper needs no chorus.

scenes.synopsis: B5 — the room watches Rose not flinch; the season's quietest triumph.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's fourth evening: the assembly. Rose arrives in the white sarcenet — the softer one — fresh rose at her sash, nothing that glints. The room does the half-second of assessment, but inside it something new: not curiosity but *attention*, the attention of people who realized mid-act that this is not a performance. She does not flinch — has not flinched all week — and the town has kept score in nods and half-bows and held hands.)*
> *(She dances twice — Julian, whose banked anger makes him dance dangerously well; Henry, steady on the floor as everywhere. She is *seen* laughing at Letitia's joke — genuine, unguarded. Driving home: "Did you see Fane? White muslin, darling. She is *following* you." And Augusta, from her corner: "The room watched you not flinch. That is the season's quietest triumph, and I have seen loud ones." The town is voting — with imitation, the sincerest ballot.)*
> *(She arrives early — generals arrive early — and uses the minutes to read the room the way she reads everything now: as evidence. The assembly is the week's fourth evening, and the town has had four days to practice its response. The half-second of assessment is still there — it will always be there, the ton's reflex — but inside it something new has grown: attention, the attention of people who realized mid-act that this is not a performance. She takes her place, white sarcenet, fresh rose, nothing that glints, and lets the attention do its work.)*
> *(Between the dances she keeps the green book's tally in her head: the room's thaw, Fane's muslin, the held hands, the genuine laugh at Letitia's joke — unguarded, unflinching, evidence. Julian dances dangerously well on banked anger; Henry dances the way he stands, load-bearing. She is seen, and the seeing is the campaign. Driving home, Augusta's verdict from the corner — the season's quietest triumph — sits beside her like a medal. The town is voting with imitation, the sincerest ballot. The week has four evenings behind it. The flowers are about to vote.)*
> *(She thinks of the week's first evening — the thin rain, the first half-second, the practice in the mirror — and measures the distance traveled. Four evenings. The town has gone from assessment to attention, from curiosity to investment. They have made your vindication their project, Augusta said, and people don't abandon their projects. The quietest triumph was only the beginning. She lays the white sarcenet aside and pins a fresh rose for tomorrow. The campaign continues.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Enter the assembly — the half-second, now containing *attention*, not curiosity. → Remembered: Her reading of the room's evolution; attention is the precursor to belief.
> 2. [stance]Dance with Julian's banked anger — "dangerously well" — and hold her line. → Remembered: How she dances with temper; the floor becomes a second front.
> 3. [social]Dance with Henry's steadiness — load-bearing, on the floor as everywhere. → Remembered: The steadiness, borrowed for an evening; she leans, briefly, and it holds.
> 4. [examine]Be seen laughing — genuine, unguarded, unflinching — at Letitia's joke. → Remembered: Her willingness to be seen happy; joy is evidence too.
> 5. [micro]Note Fane in white muslin — "she is *following* you." → Remembered: The imitation, logged; the town's sincerest ballot is counted.
> 6. [social]Receive Augusta's verdict — "the season's quietest triumph." → Remembered: The general's scoring; quiet triumphs outrank loud ones in her book.
> 7. [choice]Accept the week's verdict — favorable — or demand more. → Remembered: Her satisfaction's measure; she banks the win without spending it.

> *(Four tempers, four refusals, one conductor's problem. Julian's anger is banked and aimed at Pyke — he wants a fight, and he wants it to be *his* fight. Laurent's charm is weaponized and wants a *social* call on Pyke — "charm for charm," with a duelist's timing underneath, and Rose does not entirely trust the word "social." Henry's steadiness wants nothing but to stand beside her, visibly, daily — the parallel campaign, no orders needed. Octavia's clarity wants to finish the sketch and exhibit it after the victory — a record, not a weapon. Letitia's counsel rings in her ears: *forbid them nothing, permit them everything, take the credit.* Augusta's counsel rings deeper: *a general does not waste her officers' temper — she aims it.*)*
> *(The choice is not strategy — strategy was settled days ago, in the green book's columns. The choice is stewardship: four people she loves, four tempers, four prides, all placed — by them, not by her — in her hands. To conduct them is to presume; to refuse is to abandon. She thinks of her father's orchestra — he never conducted, but he knew the cost of every instrument. Julian's fury, Laurent's charm, Henry's steadiness, Octavia's clarity: each is a gift she did not ask for and cannot return. The baton is hers whether she takes it up or not. She takes it up.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The suitors' anger:*

scenes.synopsis: the aftermath — Julian hears the decision on his anger, and answers as Julian.
scenes.prose:
> *(She tells Julian first — his temper needs handling, his pride honoring. They walk the square garden: public enough for propriety, private enough for truth. She lays out the decision plainly — what she permits, forbids, asks. He listens with his whole attention, Julian's rarest courtesy. "You are conducting us," he says at last. Not an accusation — an observation, with admiration under it.)*
> *("Somebody must. Pyke wants us scattered — four angry people making four scenes. Together we are a refutation. Apart, a farce." He nods slowly. "When *you* put it any way, I find I agree. Infuriating." The banked anger shifts — she feels it — from fire seeking fuel to furnace with purpose. "One condition: if he prints about *you* — I can bear me — I reserve the right to be unconducted." "Granted," she says. "Even generals allow for the fog of war." He kisses her hand, formally, gratefully. The first officer is deployed.)*
> *(The square garden is her chosen ground — public enough for propriety, private enough for truth — and she watches him arrive with the decision already half-made in his face. He knows, she realizes; Julian has never needed telling twice, and the banked anger has been waiting for orders since Tuesday. She lays it out plainly: what she permits, what she forbids, what she asks. No flattery, no softening — Julian's pride requires the truth stated, the way it required her opinion stated on Tuesday. The only opinion I require is yours. She gives it.)*
> *(You are conducting us. Not an accusation — an observation, with admiration under it, and she owns it without apology. Somebody must. Pyke wants them scattered — four angry people making four scenes, the farce of the furious. Together they are a refutation. She feels the anger shift as he accepts: from fire seeking fuel to furnace with purpose, the banked thing becoming the managed thing. One condition, he says, if he prints about you — I reserve the right to be unconducted. Granted. Even generals allow for the fog of war.)*
> *(He kisses her hand — formally, gratefully, the ceremony of obedience — and she recognizes the gesture's language: formality is his love language, and the kiss is a commission accepted. The first officer is deployed. Walking home she plans the order of the other three tellings: Laurent next, for the velvet leash needs its terms stated soon; Henry after, though he needs no orders; Octavia last, for the artist's timing is her own. The green book receives the sequence. The conducting has begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: texture — the week's fifth day; the campaign's machinery, running smooth.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fifth day runs like a well-drilled regiment. Morning calls at eleven and twelve — both drawing-rooms warm now, the half-second of assessment shortened to a quarter-second, the thaw arriving before the tea. The bookseller's at one, where she is seen buying — *buying*, with coin, in front of witnesses — a volume of sermons, because nothing says *unimpeachable* like sermons bought in public. The Park agent's office at two, where another invoice is paid to the penny. Letitia, in the carriage between engagements, has taken to narrating the campaign like a military dispatch: "Eleven o'clock — Fane thawed completely. Twelve — the general's friend wept, actually wept, darling. One — sermons! *Sermons!*")*
> *(Rose listens, and laughs, and feels the thing she has not felt since the libels began: momentum. Not hope — hope is fragile, and she has stopped dealing in it — but momentum, which is hope with a timetable. The town is not merely watching anymore; it is *participating* — wearing white muslin, thawing on schedule, weeping at noon. The unimpeachable week has become the town's week too, a collective project, and Pyke's charges are starting to read — she can feel it in the rooms — like last week's weather: remembered, discussed, and no longer believed. She looks out at the rain, which has finally stopped, and thinks: *the sky is clearing, and nobody paid for it.* Larkin's word, answered by weather.)*
> *(The fifth day runs like a well-drilled regiment, and she takes pleasure in the smoothness — the general's pleasure in operations that no longer need commanding. The bookseller's at one: sermons, bought with coin, in front of witnesses — buying, the verb emphasized, because nothing says unimpeachable like sermons bought in public. The Park agent's office at two: another invoice, paid to the penny, the receipt taken with thanks.)*
> *(Letitia narrates from the carriage like a military dispatch — Eleven o'clock: Fane thawed completely. One: sermons! Sermons! — and Rose laughs till the carriage shakes, because the comedy is the chronicle and the chronicle is the war. Momentum, not hope — hope is fragile, and she has stopped dealing in it — but momentum, which is hope with a timetable. The town is participating now: white muslin, scheduled thaws, noon weeping. The unimpeachable week has become the town's week. The rain has stopped. The sky is clearing, and nobody paid for it.)*
