> 2. [micro]Buy the sermons — *buying*, with coin, in front of witnesses. → Remembered: Her doctrine of witnessed virtue; the sermons join the timber invoices.
> 3. [social]Take Letitia's military dispatches — "Fane thawed completely... *Sermons!*" → Remembered: The aunt's narration as morale; the dispatches become the week's chronicle.
> 4. [stance]Feel momentum — "not hope, but momentum, which is hope with a timetable." → Remembered: Her distinction between hope and momentum; she deals only in the latter now.
> 5. [examine]Sense the town *participating* — white muslin, scheduled thaws, noon weeping. → Remembered: Her recognition of the collective project; the town is now her co-belligerent.
> 6. [social]Read the charges as "last week's weather" in the rooms' new atmosphere. → Remembered: The metaphor of the libel's decay; weather is forgotten, and so is ink.
> 7. [choice]"The sky is clearing, and nobody paid for it." — Larkin's word, answered. → Remembered: Her private rebuttal to the bought sky; some things remain unbought.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — the week's evening assembly; the rose vocabulary deepens with a second flower.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's evening assembly — the last of the week's great appearances — demands something the week has not yet shown: not severity, not approachability, but *triumph*, worn quietly. The white is established; the town is following; the Gazette is scoring. Tonight Rose considers deepening the flower language — a second flower beside the white rose, speaking in the vocabulary the ton is learning. The language of flowers is precise, and the wrong second flower would say the wrong thing: rosemary is remembrance (too backward-looking), myrtle is love in marriage (too forward), ivy is fidelity (true, but common). She considers three candidates, each diegetic, each remembered, each carrying social consequence into the assembly.)*
> *(The white violet — modesty, carried further; it says *the clean name, without pride*, and it echoes Laurent's violets, which the town will notice. The white camellia — perfected loveliness, unpretentious excellence; it says *I am what I appear to be*, and dares the room to disagree. Or the rose alone, unchanged — discipline over decoration; it says *the week's statement needs no second sentence*, and trusts the town to have learned the vocabulary. No jewels — the doctrine holds to the week's end. She chooses as she has chosen all week: as evidence, entered into the record, with the Gazette's fashion eye as the sternest auditor. Tonight the audit must find triumph — quiet, white, and unadorned.)*
> *(The week's evening assembly demands something the week has not yet shown: not severity, not approachability, but triumph, worn quietly. Tonight she deepens the flower language — a second flower beside the white rose, speaking in the vocabulary the ton is learning. The language of flowers is precise, and the wrong second flower would say the wrong thing. She considers three candidates the way a general considers ground: the white violet, the white camellia, or the rose alone, unchanged.)*
> Or the rose alone — discipline over decoration; the week's statement needs no second sentence. She weighs them against the evening's need: triumph, worn quietly. The camellia, she decides — the dare, the perfected thing, the quiet triumph. The Gazette's fashion eye will score it. The town will learn the new word.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Name tonight's need — not severity but *triumph*, worn quietly. → Remembered: Her calibration of the week's arc; the final appearance must crown, not repeat.
> 2. [choice]Take the white violet — modesty further, echoing Laurent's violets. → Remembered: The echo chosen; the town will read the pairing, and so will he.
> 3. [choice]Take the white camellia — *I am what I appear to be*, dared. → Remembered: The dare chosen; perfected loveliness as a challenge to the room.
> 4. [choice]Take the rose alone — discipline over decoration, no second sentence. → Remembered: Restraint chosen; the week's statement stands unamended.
> 5. [examine]Reject rosemary, myrtle, ivy — each wrong for the week's grammar. → Remembered: Her fluency in the flower language; the rejections prove the mastery.
> 6. [stance]Hold the no-jewels doctrine "to the week's end" — unamended. → Remembered: Her consistency as evidence; the unopened case is the week's signature.
> 7. [social]Dress for the sternest auditor — Bell's fashion eye, imagined at the glass. → Remembered: Her internalization of the Gazette's scoring; she audits herself first.

scenes.synopsis: B7 — the comic aunt, fierce; "They shall not have you, darling, not for a pennyworth."
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes to pin the evening's rose herself — "flowers are a science, darling; you are a general, not a botanist" — and while she pins, she talks: the guest list dissected, Fane's muslin praised and pitied, the sermons hailed as "the single most boring masterstroke of the season." Under the comedy something builds, and when the rose sits perfect, the comedy drops like a closing fan.)*
> *("They shall not have you, darling — not for a pennyworth." Not the comic aunt's voice: the voice of a woman widowed at thirty who kept her house, her name, and her opinions in a town of penny libels. "I have watched you be boring on purpose, brave by accident, and *right* in a way that shames the town's doubt. Whatever Thursday brings, you are not alone in this house. You never were." A brisk kiss, gone before Rose's tears fall. The rose stays perfect. Some pins hold more than flowers.)*
> *(She submits to the pinning with grace — you are a general, not a botanist — and lets the comedy wash over her: the guest list dissected, Fane's muslin praised and pitied, the sermons hailed as the single most boring masterstroke of the season. It is Letitia's great art, the comedy that builds over something fiercer, and Rose has learned to hear the register shift — the fan about to close. When the rose sits perfect, the comedy drops. What follows is not the comic aunt's voice. It is the widow's.)*
> *(They shall not have you, darling — not for a pennyworth. Eleven years a widow in a town of penny libels: the woman kept her house, her name, and her opinions, and the vow is priced in that currency. The week's assessment, from family — and family, Rose has learned, scores the hardest. A brisk kiss, gone before tears fall. The rose stays perfect. Some pins hold more than flowers. She stands very still after the door closes, and lets the vow settle beside the other sentences the week has given her.)*
> *(She chooses to let the tears wait — the aunt has earned either, the tears or the delay, but the assembly needs the general, not the niece. In the glass: the white, the camellia, the perfect rose, the vow underneath like a foundation garment. You have never been alone in this house. The sentence ends the week's solitude. The house is her garrison. She goes down with the pin holding more than flowers, and the town — which has watched her all week — watches her shine, in the armor her aunt pinned on.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Submit to the pinning — "you are a general, not a botanist" — with grace. → Remembered: Her surrender of the small to the aunt; the pinning is love's logistics.
> 2. [examine]Hear the comedy build over something fiercer — the fan about to close. → Remembered: Her ear for Letitia's register shifts; the comedy always guards the steel.
> 3. [stance]Receive "not for a pennyworth" in the widow's voice, not the comic's. → Remembered: The vow's true register; she will remember who said it and how.
> 4. [social]"Be brave by accident, and be *right*" — the week's assessment, from family. → Remembered: The aunt's scoring; accidental bravery outranks performed courage.
> 5. [examine]Learn what the vow costs — eleven years a widow in a town of penny libels. → Remembered: Her new understanding of Letitia's history; the comedy has a foundation.
> 6. [micro]Feel the unnecessary adjustment of the rose — love's fidgeting, permitted. → Remembered: The small touch she will remember longest; perfection needs no adjusting.
> 7. [stance]"You have never been alone in this house." — the sentence, kept. → Remembered: The line that ends the week's solitude; the house is her garrison.
> 8. [choice]Let the tears wait till the door closes — or let them fall in front of her. → Remembered: Her permission around family; the aunt has earned the tears or the delay.

scenes.synopsis: the aunt's fierce plan — comedy as strategy; what Letitia will do while Rose is being unimpeachable.
scenes.prose:
> *(Over cold supper — nobody eats properly before a verdict — Letitia unveils her plan: ninety percent comedy, ten percent something sharp enough to cut it. "While you are unimpeachable, somebody must be *objectionable*, or the town will die of virtue. I shall be objectionable. I shall go to Fane's Thursday in colors loud enough to be heard in Bath, talk about the Lantern at the top of my voice, and say that any paper calling my niece a fraud is printed by a man who" — stage whisper — "cannot spell *subpoena*." Rose chokes on her soup.)*
> *("It is strategy, darling. You are the white rose — be it. Somebody must be the *nettle*. Nettles keep the garden honest." She is entirely serious under the performance — and entirely right. The campaign needs its contrast. "Do it," Rose says, taking her hand. "Be the nettle. But be a *careful* nettle — Pyke prints about women like us for pennies, and I need you unprinted." "My dear, I have been unprintable for eleven years. My greatest accomplishment." The week's second front opens.)*
> *(Over cold supper — nobody eats properly before a verdict — Letitia unveils the plan, and the ratio is the point: ninety percent comedy, ten percent edge. Fane's Thursday, colors loud enough to be heard in Bath, the Lantern discussed at the top of her voice. Any paper calling my niece a fraud is printed by a man who cannot spell subpoena. Rose chokes on her soup. Laughter as assent — the joke is the plan's signature.)*
> *(You are the white rose — be it. Somebody must be the nettle. Nettles keep the garden honest. The division of floral labor, stated as doctrine — and entirely serious under the performance, and entirely right. The campaign needs its contrast: the white week's severity requires the nettle's noise, the way a garden requires both flower and sting. Do it, Rose says, taking her hand. Be the nettle. But be a careful nettle — Pyke prints about women like us for pennies, and I need you unprinted. The condition on the comedy; love sets limits on strategy.)*
> *(My dear, I have been unprintable for eleven years. My greatest accomplishment. The boast, believed — and Rose believes it, because the record supports it. Eleven years of widowhood, eleven years of print, and never once a paragraph that stuck. The nettle joins the regiment. The week's second front opens. That night the green book receives: Letitia — the nettle, deployed. Careful, by order. The aunt's war, like the niece's, will be fought in the open, in colors, at the top of her voice. The town will die of virtue no longer.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Hear the plan unveiled — "ninety percent comedy and ten percent something sharp." → Remembered: Her assessment of auntly strategy; the ratio is the point.
> 2. [examine]"Somebody must be *objectionable*, or the town will die of virtue." → Remembered: The doctrine of contrast; the campaign needs its nettle.
> 3. [stance]Choke on the soup at "cannot spell *subpoena*" — laughter as assent. → Remembered: Her laughter as strategy's seal; the joke is the plan's signature.
> 4. [examine]See the seriousness under the performance — "entirely right." → Remembered: Her recognition of the steel; she stops underestimating the comedy.
> 5. [social]"You are the white rose — be the white rose. Somebody must be the *nettle*." → Remembered: The division of floral labor; the garden metaphor becomes doctrine.
> 6. [micro]Take her aunt's hand — "be a *careful* nettle." → Remembered: The condition on the comedy; love sets limits on strategy.
> 7. [stance]"I have been unprintable for eleven years." — the boast, believed. → Remembered: Her new respect for the aunt's record; unprintable is an achievement.
> 8. [choice]Seal the plan — the week's second front, opened. → Remembered: Her willingness to be defended obliquely; the nettle joins the regiment.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the week's end; a quiet evening before the last verdicts.
scenes.prose:
> *(The evening assembly went as the week has gone: the half-second shortened to nothing, the thaw arriving with the greeting, the white camellia — she chose the camellia — noted by three women and, she suspects, by Bell's fashion eye, wherever it sits. She danced with Laurent, who was *seen* enjoying her company conspicuously, as promised; she talked sermons with a bishop's wife; she came home with her gloves white and her flowers fresh. And now the house is quiet, the week nearly done, and she sits in the morning room with the* Lantern *— the whole week's numbers, stacked like evidence — and the Gazette's latest beside them, and she does what generals do after a successful engagement: she counts.)*
> *(The count: six days of appearances, twenty-one calls, four suitors deployed, one aunt weaponized, one town converted from watching to participating. The charges — fraud, dupes, swindle — answered not with ink but with conduct, day after day, in white, in public, with witnesses. Quill's writ still unsigned in its drawer, waiting for the month of conduct to make it an execution. The suitors' tempers aimed, not unleashed. The white rose at her sash, renewed daily, now the town's vocabulary as well as hers. She closes the stack of papers and looks at the quiet room, and she thinks: *this is what winning looks like before anyone calls it winning* — unglamorous, unphotogenic, unquestionably real. Tomorrow is the week's last day. Then the reckoning of the flowers.)*
> She danced with Laurent, conspicuously enjoyed, as promised; she talked sermons with a bishop's wife, the week's most boring masterstroke deployed in the field; she came home with gloves white and flowers fresh. The house is quiet. The week is nearly done.)*
> *(She does what generals do after a successful engagement: she counts. Six days of appearances, twenty-one calls, four suitors deployed, one aunt weaponized, one town converted from watching to participating. Quill's writ still unsigned in its drawer. The suitors' tempers aimed, not unleashed. This is what winning looks like before anyone calls it winning — unglamorous, unphotogenic, unquestionably real.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Count the week "like a general after a successful engagement" — the tally. → Remembered: Her habit of quantifying victory; the count is the campaign's ledger.
> 2. [stance]Name the numbers — twenty-one calls, four suitors, one aunt, one town. → Remembered: The week's arithmetic; she will quote these figures all season.
> 3. [micro]Stack the week's *Lanterns* "like evidence" beside the Gazette. → Remembered: The archive's weekly founding; the stack is the war's paperwork.
> 4. [examine]"Winning before anyone calls it winning" — unglamorous, real. → Remembered: Her definition of pre-victory; she recognizes it by its lack of glamour.
> 5. [social]Note Laurent's conspicuous enjoyment — the promise, kept. → Remembered: His compliance with the strategy; the conducted suitor performs.
> 6. [stance]Sit in the quiet room — the week's end, savored briefly. → Remembered: Her rare moments of savoring; she permits herself one evening.
> 7. [choice]Look toward tomorrow — "the reckoning of the flowers." → Remembered: Her anticipation; the week's last day is already named.

scenes.synopsis: the general's verdict on the week — scored, precisely, like a campaign.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives the week's report at breakfast — Rose gives it straight: numbers first, then assessment, then what went wrong (nothing; Augusta distrusts perfect reports). "Twenty-one calls. Four suitors deployed. One town converted." Augusta butters toast like defusing ordnance. "And the charges?" "Fraud — Quill's, when the timing is right. Dupes — the men refuse it themselves. Swindle" — a gesture at the white muslin — "being lived down, daily, in public.")*
> *("Good. Hear my verdict as a general's, not a grandmother's. You fought on ground Pyke cannot print on, and won — not loudly, which is why it's won. The town watched you not flinch and is now *invested*: they wore white muslin for you, thawed on schedule. They made your vindication their project, and people don't abandon their projects." She rises. "One more week like this, and the charges read like last year's weather. Two more, and Bell must score you — and Bell's scoring is the only verdict in London that matters." The quietest triumph was only the beginning.)*
> *(Augusta receives the week's report at breakfast, and Rose gives it straight — numbers first, then assessment, then what went wrong. Twenty-one calls. Four suitors deployed. One town converted. Nothing went wrong, which Augusta distrusts — a general distrusts perfect reports — so Rose adds the honest footnote: the second day chafed, the rose's sender is unknown, Pyke has not yet answered. Good, Augusta says, buttering toast like defusing ordnance. A report with a footnote I can believe.)*
> *(And the charges? Fraud — Quill's, when the timing is right. Dupes — the men refuse it themselves. Swindle — being lived down, daily, in public. She gestures at the white muslin. Augusta's verdict comes as a general's, not a grandmother's: You fought on ground Pyke cannot print on, and won — not loudly, which is why it's won. 
> The quietest triumph was only the beginning. Rose receives it the way she receives all Augusta's verdicts: as fuel, not rest. The second week's tempo is planned before the first ends — repeat the formula, she decides, and escalate only where the town asks for it. The general rises. The campaign continues. Thursday is coming, and with it the reckoning of the flowers.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Give the report straight — "numbers first, then assessment" — the general's format. → Remembered: Her mastery of Augusta's reporting discipline; the format becomes hers.
> 2. [examine]Watch Augusta distrust the perfect report — "a general who distrusts perfect reports." → Remembered: Her learning of command's skepticism; nothing is ever entirely won.
> 3. [stance]Answer the charges in Quill's tripartite form — fraud, dupes, swindle, each assigned. → Remembered: Her fluency in the strategy; the three answers are now reflex.
> 4. [social]"They have made your vindication their project, and people do not abandon their projects." → Remembered: Augusta's doctrine of invested towns; the insight re-prices the whole war.
> 5. [examine]"Bell's scoring is the only verdict in London that matters." → Remembered: The general's ranking of judges; the Gazette outranks the town, the court, everyone.
> 6. [micro]Watch the toast-buttering — "with the care of a woman defusing ordnance." → Remembered: Her private image of Augusta's precision; even breakfast is a campaign.
> 7. [stance]Receive "the quietest triumph was only the beginning" — the verdict, absorbed. → Remembered: How she takes praise from the general; it is fuel, not rest.
> 8. [choice]Decide the next week's tempo — repeat the formula, or escalate. → Remembered: Her campaign rhythm; the second week is planned before the first ends.

scenes.synopsis: the charges, answered — the week's tally against the three libels.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone with the week's last morning, Rose takes down the three charges one final time — not from the paper, which she has memorized, but from the week's evidence, which is better. Fraud: answered by Quill's forthcoming writ, and by the timber invoices paid to the penny in front of witnesses, and by the sermons bought in public — the paper trail and the conduct trail, running together like a double ledger. Dupes: answered by four honorable people refusing, daily, visibly, in their own manners — Julian's banked fury, Laurent's conspicuous enjoyment, Henry's parallel campaign, Octavia's forthcoming record. Swindle: answered by the white itself — twenty-one calls in unadorned white, the town auditing her daily and finding nothing undeclared.)*
> *(She writes it in the campaign book — she has started a campaign book, bound in green, the war's private ledger — in three columns, charge against answer, the way her father taught her to balance accounts. The columns balance. They more than balance: the answers exceed the charges, the way a good defense exceeds the indictment. She closes the book and looks at the morning — the week's last day, the rain long gone, the light the particular gold of a London autumn that has decided to be kind. "Itemized," she says to the book, to the week, to Pyke wherever he is setting his type, "they were always smaller than the heap. And the heap is gone." The unimpeachable week is complete. The flowers are about to vote.)*
> *(She writes it in the campaign book — bound in green, the war's private ledger — in three columns, charge against answer, the way her father taught her to balance accounts. The columns balance. Fraud, dupes, swindle — each faced alone, each answered in its own element: the law, the men, the life. The doctrine held. The week is complete.)*
> And the heap is gone. The unimpeachable week is complete. The flowers are about to vote — the white rose at her sash, the town's new vocabulary, and whatever Thursday brings. She pins a fresh rose. The reckoning begins.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Take down the charges "from the week's evidence, which is better" than the paper. → Remembered: Her preference for lived evidence over printed claims; the week outranks the *Lantern*.
> 2. [stance]Balance the three columns — charge against answer — "the way her father taught her." → Remembered: Her father's accounting as warfare; the green book is his legacy.
> 3. [micro]Open the campaign book — "bound in green, the war's private ledger." → Remembered: The book's founding; it will hold the whole season's arithmetic.
> 4. [examine]"The answers exceed the charges, the way a good defense exceeds the indictment." → Remembered: Her standard for victory; merely answering is never enough.
> 5. [social]Address Pyke "wherever he is setting his type" — the enemy, named in private. → Remembered: Her private naming of the enemy; the war stays personal.
> 6. [stance]"The heap is gone." — the atmosphere, dispersed by itemizing. → Remembered: The doctrine's proof; division defeated the heap, as predicted.
> 7. [examine]Read the morning's gold light — "a London autumn that has decided to be kind." → Remembered: Her reading of weather as omen; the gold is banked as morale.
> 8. [choice]Close the book on the week — complete — and turn toward the flowers. → Remembered: Her transitions between campaigns; the white-rose week begins where this ends.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the hawkers' corners; the Lantern's sales, softening.
scenes.prose:
> *(Rose walks the last quarter-mile to her calls — walking is seen, and being seen walking is evidence — past the hawker's corner, where Larkin's boy is having a slow morning. The Lantern's stack sits barely touched; the Gazette's is half gone. "Slow for the Lantern, then?" she asks, buying a Gazette she doesn't need. The boy shrugs, truly neutral. "Folks've read it, miss. The charges and that. They read it once. Don't buy it twice." Pyke's charges have the half-life of gossip: vivid at first telling, stale at the second.)*
> *(Across from the bookseller's, the coffee-house talk through the open door is of balloon nights, not libel — she is *seen* not going in, its own statement. The town's attention is finite, and it spends itself on spectacle. The libel war is being won not because the town loves her, but because it is *bored* of Pyke — boredom, the great leveler, doing what no writ could. She walks on through the gold morning. The Lantern sits unsold in the sun.)*
> *(The walk is deliberate — the pavement is a parade ground, and she is on parade. She buys the unneeded Gazette from Larkin's boy, and the coin is intelligence: the enemy's distributor, paid, observed, remembered. The boy's neutrality is professional — he sells both papers, believes neither — and she respects it. They read it once. Don't buy it twice. The half-life of gossip, priced by the boy who sells it: vivid at first telling, stale at the second. Pyke's charges are decaying in the sun.)*
> Absence as evidence: the negative, mastered. The town's attention is finite, and it spends itself on spectacle — the balloon, the sky, the bought weather. Letitia's doctrine, field-proven: the town forgets what it read the moment it sees something better to look at. The white week was the something better. She walks on past the unsold Lantern — in the sun, in white, unhurried — and leaves the image on the street like a photograph the town will keep.)*
> *(The economics please her: Pyke's ink has a shelf life, and the shelf is the hawker's corner. A libel that doesn't sell twice is a libel that dies — not refuted, but remaindered. She thinks of Quill's notebook, collecting prints, and of Larkin's word about the purse that never sleeps. The purse can buy the sky, the paper, the hawkers' extra pay — but it cannot buy the second purchase. The town read it once. The town will not buy it twice. The Lantern sits unsold in the sun.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Walk the last quarter-mile — "walking is seen, and being seen walking is evidence." → Remembered: Her doctrine of pedestrian visibility; the pavement is a parade ground.
> 2. [social]Buy the unneeded Gazette from Larkin's boy — the transaction, noted. → Remembered: Her habit of buying from the enemy's distributors; the coin is intelligence.
> 3. [examine]"They read it once. Don't buy it twice." — the half-life of gossip, priced. → Remembered: The hawker's economics as strategy; Pyke's ink has a shelf life.
> 4. [stance]Be seen *not* entering the coffee-house — the negative statement. → Remembered: Her mastery of absence as evidence; not-going-in is also testimony.
> 5. [examine]Hear the talk is of balloon nights, not libel — the town's finite attention. → Remembered: Her reading of the town's boredom; it is doing what no writ could.
> 6. [social]Apply Letitia's doctrine — "the town forgets what it read the moment it sees something better." → Remembered: The aunt's wisdom, field-proven; the white week was the something better.
> 7. [choice]Walk on past the unsold *Lantern* — in the sun, in white, unhurried. → Remembered: The image she leaves on the street; the town photographs her in memory.

scenes.synopsis: the week's evening — Laurent reports on the conducted charm campaign.
scenes.prose:
> *(Laurent calls at seven — the verdict-hour — in high, dangerous spirits. "I was *seen* enjoying your company at the assembly, as promised. Three conversations about your white muslin, all favorable, one actually *moved*. Fane wept again; it is her new accomplishment." He takes tea like a medal. "And Pyke? I have not called on him. The *velvet* leash holds. Though when I saw Thursday's number stacked unsold in the sun, I felt something like pity. Poor Pyke — to be defeated by *boredom*. No revenge in it, therefore no dignity.")*
> *("Pity is a luxury, Laurent. We cannot afford it yet." He sobers a fraction. "No. Not yet." A pause. "Rose — the white suits the campaign. But when it is won, I look forward to seeing you in colors again. The white is armor. I prefer you unarmored." The most honest thing he's said all week — not flirtation but a promise, held in reserve. She doesn't answer directly. The armor is working; and underneath, she checks like a pulse, she is still herself.)*
> *(Laurent calls at seven — the verdict-hour, as it has become — in high, dangerous spirits. He takes tea like a medal. The conducted charm, performing on schedule: conspicuous, expensive, often. And Pyke? I have not called on him. The velvet leash holds. The reporting, mandatory — the leash's terms, honored. She notes it in the green book: the dangerous one, compliant.)*
> Poor Pyke — to be defeated by boredom. No revenge in it, therefore no dignity. His aesthetic objection to the victory's manner — and she notes the vanity in it, the duelist's disappointment at a bloodless win. Pity is a luxury, Laurent. We cannot afford it yet. He sobers a fraction. No. Not yet. The general's answer; the war's economy admits no luxuries. The leash holds. The charm performs. The dangerous one is, for now, conducted.)*
> *(Rose — the white suits the campaign. The white is armor. I prefer you unarmored. The most honest thing he's said all week — not flirtation but a promise, held in reserve. She doesn't answer directly. The promise is banked — for after the victory, when the white can be laid aside and the colors return. The week's last evening. The war, nearly won.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the seven o'clock report — "the hour when the day's verdicts are in." → Remembered: His new punctuality as devotion; the hour becomes their ritual.
> 2. [examine]"Fane weeps at everything now; it is her new accomplishment." → Remembered: His wit on the town's conversion; the weeping is logged as victory.
> 3. [stance]Hear "the *velvet* leash holds" — the conducted charm, confirmed. → Remembered: Her management's success; the leash held without chafing.
> 4. [social]"To be defeated by *boredom* — there is no revenge in it." → Remembered: His aesthetic objection to the victory's manner; she notes the vanity in it.
> 5. [examine]"Pity is a luxury. We cannot afford it yet." — the general's answer. → Remembered: Her refusal of premature mercy; the war's economy admits no luxuries.
> 6. [stance]Receive "I prefer you unarmored" — honesty, not flirtation, held in reserve. → Remembered: The promise under the armor; she banks it for after the victory.
> 7. [micro]Check the pulse — "underneath it, she is still herself." → Remembered: Her private audit of identity; the armor has not replaced the woman.
> 8. [choice]Leave the promise unanswered — directly — and let the week end. → Remembered: Her discipline with premature tenderness; the war first, the rest after.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the white rose arrives; no card, no sender, no explanation.
scenes.prose:
> *(It comes with the evening post — handed to the footman separately by a boy he doesn't know, gone before questions. A single white rose, perfect, fresh-cut, stem wrapped in plain paper. No card, no ribbon, no seal. Rose turns it in her fingers while the house — Letitia in the doorway, Augusta on the stairs — goes very still. White roses are her flower now; half London wears the vocabulary. But this one is *sent* — deliberately, personally, silently. The silence is the message.)*
> *(Who sends a white rose with no card? Not Julian — he sends letters, everything stated. Not Laurent — he sends violets, with jokes. Not Henry — Henry sends *nothing*; a flower would be a sentence he never learned. Not Octavia — she'd have drawn it. Not the town — the town sends bouquets, wanting thanks. A single rose, no card, from a hand that never sends flowers. And she knows — cold as a general recognizing an unfamiliar flag — whose hand that is. She does not say the name aloud. Not yet.)*
> *(She lays it beside the week's Lanterns — the enemy's ink on one side, the flower on the other — and the tableau is the war's two fronts, on one table. The delivery's tradecraft preoccupies her: a boy the footman doesn't know, gone before questions, the stem wrapped in plain paper. Someone wanted no questions asked. Someone knew the house's routines — the evening post, the footman's post, the hall. The plainness is the signature: no card, no ribbon, no seal, nothing to trace, everything to read.)*
> Not Julian — he sends letters, everything stated. Not Laurent — he sends violets, with jokes. Not Octavia — she'd have drawn it. The elimination is methodical, and what remains is the cold certainty: a hand that never sends flowers. She knows — cold as a general recognizing an unfamiliar flag — whose hand that is. She does not say the name aloud. Not yet. Not in front of the house.)*
> *(The question forms, the week's last: what does a general do with an unsigned flower? Trace it — set the household's quiet machinery to work, find the boy, find the sender, know the hand. Keep it — put it in water, let it live its week beside the Lanterns, accept the message without demanding the messenger. Burn it — refuse the unsigned overture entirely; a general does not accept intelligence from unknown hands. Each choice is a doctrine. Each will be remembered. And underneath the strategy, the colder knowledge, untouched: she knows. The trilemma waits.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Receive the separate handing — "a boy the footman does not know, gone before questions." → Remembered: The delivery's tradecraft; someone wanted no questions asked.
> 2. [micro]Turn the rose in her fingers — stem wrapped in plain paper, no card, no seal. → Remembered: Her forensic reading of the flower; the plainness is the signature.
> 3. [social]Feel the house go still — Letitia in the doorway, Augusta on the stairs. → Remembered: The household's instant alert; they read her stillness as alarm.
> 4. [examine]Lay it beside the week's *Lanterns* — "the enemy's ink on one side, the flower on the other." → Remembered: The tableau she constructs; the war's two fronts, on one table.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — THE WHITE ROSE. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The rose sits on the table, perfect and silent, and the question it asks is the week's last: what does a general do with an unsigned flower? Trace it — set the household's quiet machinery to work, find the boy, find the sender, know the hand. Keep it — put it in water, let it live its week beside the* Lanterns*, accept the message without demanding the messenger. Burn it — refuse the unsigned overture entirely; a general does not accept intelligence from unknown hands. Each choice is a doctrine. Each choice will be remembered — by the house, by the town if it learns, by the sender, whoever the sender is. And underneath the strategy is the colder knowledge: she *knows* whose hand never sends flowers. The question is what she does with the knowing.)*
> *(She has made harder choices — the estate's ledgers, the father's debts, the season's opening gambit — but never one so small and so entire. A flower, a hand, a silence: the week's last question, asked in petals. The house holds its breath. Letitia in the doorway, Augusta on the stairs, the servants' edges gone quiet — all waiting on what a general does with an unsigned flower. She touches the stem once more, the plain paper, the perfect bloom. Whatever she decides, the knowing remains: the hand that never sends flowers has sent one. The decision is the week's period. She sets it.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — The white rose:*
- **Trace the sender** — *Quill+; intelligence.* Set the quiet machinery to work — the boy, the florist, the hand. Know the sender before the week ends. *(Augusta approves the thoroughness; Letitia calls it unromantic, and is ignored.)*
- **Keep it** — *Romance+; the message accepted.* Put it in water beside the *Lanterns*; let the unsigned flower live its week. The message is received without the messenger being demanded. *(The household watches it daily; the sender — whoever — sees it kept.)*
- **Burn it** — *Standing+; the refusal.* Refuse the unsigned overture — a general does not take flowers from unknown hands. *(Letitia is horrified; Augusta respects the discipline; the ash is final.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the rose traced, kept, or burned. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: after the choice — the rose's fate, and what the fate means.
scenes.prose:
> *(The decision is made, executed in daylight with the week's full care — nothing this week has been casual. The house, holding its breath since the hall, exhales. Letitia watches from the doorway, hand at heart; Augusta from the stairs, in the general's stillness. A single white rose, and a household's full attention. This is what the war has come to, and Rose does not mind. Wars are won on small ground, held deliberately.)*
> *(Alone at the window, she thinks about hands. Julian's, stating everything in letters. Laurent's, sending violets with jokes. Henry's — steady, restrained, never once picking up a flower. The cold knowledge sits like a stone in clear water: visible, undeniable, untouched. If the rose is his — *if* — it is the most un-Henry act imaginable, which is exactly why it would be his: the soldier doing what he doesn't know how to do, because the week required it. Or the Network's coin, buying a new kind of sky. The week is over. The knowing is not.)*
> *(The execution is deliberate — in daylight, with the week's full care, nothing casual. If tracing: the footman questioned, the boy described, the florists visited. If keeping: the vase, the water, the place beside the Lanterns. If burning: the grate, the ash, the finality. The house watches, holding its breath since the hall — Letitia in the doorway, hand at heart; Augusta on the stairs, in the general's stillness — and then exhales. 
> *(That evening she writes the week's epitaph in the green book: Wars are won on small ground, held deliberately. The sentence closes the campaign the way a ledger closes a year — balanced, honest, complete. The decision's doctrine is entered beside it: trace, keep, or burn, each with its reasons, each with its cost. The cold knowledge is entered too — the hand that never sends flowers — but marked unconfirmed, the stone left unlifted. Some campaigns outlast their weeks. The knowing is not over. Thursday is coming.)*
> *(She thinks of the week's arc — the dawn resolve, the itemized charges, the white week, the four suitors, the unsigned rose — and marvels at the distance: from a heap of libel to a single flower, from atmosphere to object. The war has contracted to a point, and the point is a rose. It is the campaign's strange logic: the smaller the ground, the more deliberately it must be held. She looks at the rose — traced, kept, or burned, the decision executed — and feels the week's completeness. The unimpeachable week is over. The reckoning of the flowers begins.)*

scenes.synopsis: texture — the night after the rose; the house asleep, the question awake.
scenes.prose:
> *(The house sleeps. Rose does not. In the dark morning room — no lamp, the street's lamps enough — she permits herself what the week forbade: wonder. Not strategy — wonder. About the hand. About the courage it takes for one who never sends flowers to send one — the wrongness of the gesture for the gesturer, like a soldier taking up a paintbrush. If it is who she thinks — and her cold certainty about people has never been wrong — then the week did what no one planned: it moved *him*.)*
> *(In the flower language she taught the town, the white rose means the clean name — innocence as verdict. To send *that* flower, unsigned, is to cast a ballot: the ton's floral vote, begun by a single hand. From a hand that never sends flowers, the vote weighs more. She rises, goes to the window. "Whoever you are," she says to the dark, "I received it." The dark doesn't answer. But somewhere — she is certain — someone heard.)*
> From a hand that never sends flowers, the vote weighs more — the unpracticed giver, the difficult gesture, the courage of the wrongness. She thinks of Henry's hand: steady, restrained, the hand that held a sword in Spain and holds her gaze across ballrooms and has never once picked up a flower. If it was his — if — then the war has taught a soldier a new language.)*
> *(Or it was never his at all, and the Network's coin has learned to buy flowers as well as skies. The sinister reading, kept alive — Larkin's word forbids innocence. She holds both readings the way she holds the stone in clear water: visible, undeniable, untouched. She rises, goes to the window. The dark doesn't answer. But somewhere — she is certain — someone heard. The faith, kept without evidence, sustains her more than proof would.)*
> *(She stands at the window till the street's lamps blur, and thinks about the week's strange economy: the charges answered, the town converted, the suitors deployed — and the whole campaign distilled at last to a single unsigned flower. It is the war's final reduction, and its most human. Somewhere a hand — practiced or unpracticed, loving or sinister — chose a rose and chose silence. She will know, in time. The stone will be lifted when the water is ready. Tonight, the wonder is enough.)*

scenes.synopsis: the legal front — Quill's report; the writ waits, the evidence grows.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at nine — late for Quill, so the news is worth it. "The fraud action grows stronger daily. Two of Pyke's compositors talked — to a clerk of mine, which is better. The fraud paragraph was set from copy that came *late*, in a hand not Pyke's, with instructions to print it exactly. Paid in advance. In coin." He lets it sit. "The Network's coin, Miss Hartwell. Behind the Lantern's ink. We are proving the campaign bought — not yet in court, but in my notebook, where cases are really won.")*
> *(She fits it with Larkin's word about the sky. "The purse pays for everything. The paper, the hawkers, the sky." "And the purse," Quill says carefully, "is not Pyke's. Pyke is the instrument, not the paymaster." "Can you prove whose?" He shakes his head, honestly. "Not yet. The coin travels through too many hands. But every hand leaves a print, and I am collecting prints." At the door: "The writ waits for your month of conduct, as ordered. It will be an execution. And Miss Hartwell — the white suits the war." The first wardrobe compliment of Quill's career. She files it as a legal opinion.)*
> *(She fits it with Larkin's word about the sky — the extra pay on balloon nights, the double pay, the purse that never sleeps. The purse pays for everything. The paper, the hawkers, the sky. The three facts of the bought paragraph settle into the case's foundation: late copy, a stranger's hand, coin in advance. And the purse, Quill says carefully, is not Pyke's. Pyke is the instrument, not the paymaster. The distinction re-aims the war: the instrument matters less than the hand that pays it.)*
> *(Can you prove whose? He shakes his head, honestly. Not yet. The coin travels through too many hands. But every hand leaves a print, and I am collecting prints. Quill's method, understood: the notebook is the real courtroom, and the case is being won there daily. At the door: The writ waits for your month of conduct, as ordered. It will be an execution. And then — the first wardrobe compliment of Quill's career: And Miss Hartwell — the white suits the war. She files it as a legal opinion.)*
> *(Alone, she considers the household's need to know — all of it, or the strategy only. The house gets the plan, not the prints: the writ waits, the evidence grows, the purse is not Pyke's. The prints stay in Quill's notebook, where cases are really won. She writes in the green book: Quill — the bought paragraph, three facts. The purse, not Pyke's. Prints, collecting. The legal front holds. The month of conduct continues. The execution waits its season.)*

scenes.synopsis: the day's accounting — aunt and niece close the week.
scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia comes to bed — that is, she comes to Rose's sitting room at midnight, in her dressing gown, with two cups of chocolate, which is Letitia's way of calling a council of war. "The accounting," she announces, settling. "Twenty-one calls. Four suitors. One town. One rose, unsigned, much discussed below stairs." She sips. "And one aunt, who was *magnificent* at Fane's Thursday — I wore the puce, darling, the *puce*, and I said the thing about the subpoena, and Fane laughed until she cried, which is two accomplishments in one evening." Rose laughs — tired, genuine, the week's last laugh. "You were magnificent," she says, and means it.)*
> *("And now?" Letitia asks — the real question, underneath the chocolate. "Now," Rose says, "we wait for Thursday. Pyke will answer the week — he must; the unsold stacks are an insult he cannot swallow. And Bell —" she glances at the Gazette on the table — "Bell has been scoring all week. The verdict is coming." Letitia nods, suddenly serious. "Whatever Thursday brings, darling — the white held. *You* held. And they shall not have you. Not for a pennyworth." She rises, kisses Rose's forehead, and goes — leaving the second chocolate, the way she always leaves the second chocolate, as a small proof that the house is a garrison. Rose drinks both cups. The week is closed. Thursday is coming.)*
> *(The midnight council is Letitia's own ritual — chocolate, dressing gown, war — and Rose has learned to read its liturgy: the accounting first, the boasts second, the real question last. Twenty-one calls. Four suitors. One town. One rose, unsigned, much discussed below stairs. The servants' parliament has voted, and its verdict is favorable. Below stairs, the rose is already legend — the footman's boy, the plain paper, the mistress's stillness. The house is a garrison, and the garrison talks.)*
> *(And one aunt, who was magnificent. The puce, the subpoena, Fane's tears — the nettle's first deployment, reported with full honors. Rose laughs — tired, genuine, the week's last laugh — and says it, meaning it: You were magnificent. Tired praise is the most believed. She rises, kisses Rose's forehead, and goes — leaving the second chocolate, the way she always leaves the second chocolate, as a small proof that the house is a garrison. Rose drinks both cups. The week is closed. Thursday is coming, and with it the verdict, and the reckoning of the flowers.)*

We score the flower language a triumph of the season — and remind the ton that a vocabulary learned daily is a vocabulary kept." The reward: the Gazette's formal commendation of the rose, which the ton will wear for a month. She reads it twice, cuts it out with Letitia's sewing scissors, and files it in the drawer. The week's verdicts are complete, and the last one is flowers.)*

> *(The week is over. The charges are answered — fraud to Quill's writ, dupes to the gentlemen's refusal, swindle to the white week itself. Bell has scored. The town has voted. She has traced it, or kept it, or burned it; the week's last decision is made and executed. But the *knowing* remains, untouched by the decision: she knows whose hand never sends flowers. She has known since the hall, since the turning of the stem in her fingers, since the elimination of every other hand. The knowledge sits in her like the stone in clear water — visible, undeniable, waiting.)*

scenes.synopsis: dawn after Ch7 — the white rose with no card; the flower language becomes the chapter's weapon.
scenes.prose:
> *(She wakes before the lamps are out, and the first thing she sees — she left it on the table where the gold light could find it — is the white rose. No card. No name. The week's last decision made and executed, the knowing still untouched: a hand that never sends flowers, sending one. She stands before it in her dressing gown with her tea going cold, and she understands, the way generals understand terrain at dawn, that the rose has changed the war's grammar. Last week the white was armor — worn, witnessed, audited. This week the white must become *language* — spoken, answered, voted with. The town learned the vocabulary; now the town must be given sentences to say.)*
> *(She thinks about what flowers do that paragraphs cannot. A paragraph argues; a flower *declares*. Pyke can print against an argument — he has the press, the compositors, the bought sky. He cannot print against a flower, because a flower is not an argument; it is a fact that arrives without ink. "The clean name," she says to the rose, to the dawn, to the hand that sent it and will not sign it, "in the flower language." Last week she presented herself. This week she will be *answered* — by strangers, by hostesses, by the town's own gardens. The white rose on the table is the first word. By Friday, she intends, the whole town will be speaking in flowers.)*
> *(She thinks about the week's vocabulary — about how the town has learned to read her. The white, the rose, the sash: the grammar is now fluent, and fluency is the campaign's. She will speak it all week, the way she has spoken it since the mirror. The flower language, become the chapter's weapon.)*
> *(She dresses — white, the rose at the sash, the week's opening sentence. The day's plan: the glass, the calls, the town. The knowing, untouched. The hand that never sends flowers, having sent one. The mystery, kept. The campaign, continued.)*
> *(She stands before the glass — the rose at the sash, the white holding the gold light. The week's first appearance, prepared. The town will see her today, and the town will read her. The flower, declaring. The grammar, changed. The week, begun.)*

scenes.synopsis: texture — the flower language, studied like a campaign manual.
scenes.prose:
> *(The mother's flower book lives in the morning room's lowest shelf — pressed specimens, her mother's hand, the ink brown with age. Rose takes it down before breakfast and studies it the way Quill studies a brief: for ammunition. The white rose, pressed flat, the definition in her mother's schoolroom hand: the clean name, unquestioned. She reads it twice. The older language outranks the newer — what a mother pressed in a book outweighs what a suitor implies in a ballroom. The definition is adopted, formally, like a motion carried.)*
> *(She sends for the maid and declares it, standing, the way generals issue orders: this house speaks the flower language fluently, from today. The maid — trained in this house, unflappable — nods and produces the household's rose requirements before being asked: the sash, the morning room, the carriage. Ordered before breakfast, the mobilization complete by the second cup. Single stems, Rose specifies — not bouquets. Single stems are statements. Twelve roses merely decorate; one rose argues.)*
> *(She writes the four words herself — the clean name, worn — on each card, in her own hand, the campaign's slogan issued from headquarters. The cards will go with every rose the house sends out, and the town will quote them — she knows the town; the town quotes what it is given in a good hand. The schoolroom memory comes unbidden: her mother teaching her the language at the schoolroom table, the pressed flowers, the definitions learned like catechism. This time she keeps it — the schoolroom is the point. Some memories are weapons, not distractions.)*
> *(By noon the house is a garden under orders. The roses are placed — sash, morning room, carriage — each with its card, each a sentence in the campaign's new grammar. She walks the morning room and inspects the deployment the way Augusta inspects a map: every stem a position, every card a communique. The flower language, militarized. Botany, mobilized. The town learned the vocabulary last week; this week the town will be given sentences to say — and the sentences are hers, written in her hand, on her cards, in flowers.)**
*
> *(She closes the book and returns it to the shelf — the campaign's founding document, consulted and restored. The definitions will hold. The town will learn what her mother taught: that flowers have meanings, that meanings have weight, and that the clean name, unquestioned, is the heaviest of them all.)*

> 4. [micro]Order the roses — sash, morning room, carriage — before breakfast. → Remembered: Her mobilization of flowers; the house becomes a statement.

> 6. [social]Write the four words — *the clean name, worn* — on each card. → Remembered: The campaign's slogan, in her hand; the town will quote the cards.
> 7. [choice]Keep the schoolroom memory this time — "the schoolroom is the point." → Remembered: Her reversal on nostalgia; some memories are weapons, not distractions.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — how the white roses are worn; the flower language, tailored.
scenes.prose:
> *(The week's uniform is white — established, sanctioned, followed by half the town — but *how* the roses are worn is still an open question, and open questions in wartime are opportunities. Rose stands before the glass with three white roses and considers the grammar of placement. Each option is diegetic, remembered, and consequential: the town has learned to read her flowers, the Gazette's fashion eye is scoring, and Bell's verdicts have opinions about botany. The choice must say *the clean name* in a dialect the town has not yet heard — familiar enough to recognize, new enough to notice.)*
> *(At the sash, as last week — continuity, discipline; it says *the statement stands*, and trusts the town's memory. At the breast, pinned over the heart — intimacy, courage; it says *the clean name is kept here*, and dares the room to doubt the keeping. In the hair, above the ear — softness, visibility; it says *the clean name is beautiful*, and lets the town admire what it is defending. She weighs them the way she weighs everything this season: as evidence, entered into the record. The sash is the general's choice. The breast is the lover's. The hair is the woman's. She is, this week, all three — and the town, she decides, deserves to see it.)*
> *(She weighs each option the way she weighs everything now — by consequence. The sash: continuity, the statement stands. The breast: intimacy, the clean name kept here. The hair: softness, visibility. Each is a sentence; each will be read by Bell's fashion eye and by the town's thousand eyes.)*
> *(She chooses — and the choice is a doctrine. The grammar of placement, settled for the week. The town will follow; the town always follows the placement. The roses, worn. The statement, made. The week, opened in white.)*
> *(She writes in the green book: placement, decided. The grammar, fluent. Bell's eye, anticipated. The town's eyes, a thousand. The week, uniformed.)*
> *(She stands before the glass a final time — the roses placed, the grammar settled. The week's uniform, complete. She nods to the reflection: the statement stands, the name is kept, the softness is visible. The town, about to read.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Hold the three roses before the glass — "the grammar of placement." → Remembered: Her treatment of position as syntax; where matters as much as what.
> 2. [choice]Pin it at the sash — continuity, discipline, *the statement stands*. → Remembered: The general's placement; the town reads unbroken resolve.
> 3. [choice]Pin it at the breast — intimacy, courage, *kept here*. → Remembered: The lover's placement; the room is dared to doubt the keeping.
> 4. [choice]Set it in the hair — softness, visibility, *beautiful*. → Remembered: The woman's placement; admiration becomes a form of defense.
> 5. [examine]Name herself "general, lover, woman — all three" — the week's identities. → Remembered: Her refusal to choose one self; the campaign needs all three.
> 6. [stance]Dress for Bell's botanical opinions — "verdicts have opinions about botany." → Remembered: Her awareness of the Gazette's floral scoring; she gardens for Bell.
> 7. [social]Decide the town "deserves to see it" — all three selves, in flowers. → Remembered: Her generosity with the town; the audience is given the full woman.

scenes.synopsis: B2 — white in the atelier; the gown of the clean name, commissioned; fashion as verdict.
scenes.prose:
> *(Élise's atelier is in chalk-and-white-silk rapture — half the town's order book is white, the assistants cutting like a regiment on parade. Élise herself, chalk in her hair, receives Rose like a general receiving an ally: Miss Hartwell. The campaign has come to couture. She unrolls the sketch — the gown of the clean name, the train drawn in a single sweeping line. Rose studies it. The train moves like a verdict being read. The image commissions the gown before a word is spoken.)*
> *(They weigh fresh against embroidered — fact against assertion. The fresh rose is the week's truth, living, renewed daily. The embroidered rose is permanent — the verdict, in thread, that does not wilt. The embroidered rose, Élise says, says I have been judged, and I remain. Rose nods slowly. The campaign needs both: the living flower for the days, the permanent flower for the record. Fashion as verdict — the gown will not argue; it will be the judgment.)*
> *(Make it quickly, Rose says. I have a feeling the town will need it soon. Élise's eyes narrow — the atelier's battle-focus. She claps her hands, and the atelier mobilizes: chalk flying, silk unrolling, the assistants falling into their wartime formation. Couture goes to war. Rose watches, and thinks about what the atelier has become — not a shop but a munitions factory, turning out white armor for a town at war with a libel.)*
> *(The commission is the commitment — the clean name, in thread, permanent. She signs the order book the way she signs everything that matters: in full, in ink, without hesitation. Élise takes the book, and for a moment the dressmaker's hand covers the client's. Miss Hartwell, she says quietly, this gown will outlast the libel. Thread is patient. Ink is not. Rose leaves the atelier with the sketch's image burned in her mind: the train, moving like a verdict being read, and the town — watching, waiting — about to see the judgment walk.)**
*
> *(At the door Élise presses a twist of white thread into her hand — for luck, for the record, for the war. Rose carries it home like a commission's seal. The gown is coming. The verdict is being sewn. The town will see it Thursday, and the town will have no answer.)*
> *(Driving home she thinks about permanence — about thread outlasting ink, about the embroidered rose that will not wilt when the fresh ones do. The campaign's two flowers: one living, one lasting. Both saying the same thing. Both saying: I have been judged, and I remain.)*

> 6. [micro]"Make it quickly. I have a feeling the town will need it soon." → Remembered: Her premonition of the verdict's timing; the gown is ordered against a deadline.
> 7. [stance]Watch the atelier mobilize — "couture goes to war." → Remembered: Her pleasure in professional armies; Élise's staff drills like a regiment.
> 8. [choice]Commission the masterpiece — the clean name, in thread, permanent. → Remembered: The commission as commitment; the gown binds her to victory.

scenes.synopsis: the gown's details — cut, silk, stitching; the verdict, tailored.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fitting is a jurisprudence — Élise's, exacting, delivered with chalk. Flounces, she pronounces, pinning, are doubt, made of fabric. We are not in doubt. Rose stands on the stool and submits to the chalking — the client's discipline, learned over a season of fittings. The bodice is cut on a doctrine: the clean name does not display, it declares. Display invites doubt; declaration ends it. Every seam is an argument, and every argument is being won.)*
> *(Élise demonstrates the train — an assistant walking it the length of the atelier, the white silk moving like water under judgment. Judgment, trailing, Élise says, and Rose laughs — the laugh as fitting's seal, the verdict moving correctly. The train is right. The gown is becoming what it was sketched to be: not a dress but a ruling, wearable, walkable, undeniable.)*
> *(The rings come off — surrendered without argument. The Gazette notices rings; Bell's fashion eye has opinions about jewelry, and the verdict must be unadorned. Élise tells the cautionary tale: Bell's three lines about a bracelet, the season before last, the woman still recovering. Rose listens, and leaves the rings in the atelier's small locked box. Even engaged hands go bare. The jewel discipline's final form.)*
> *(It is an acquittal, Élise says, stepping back, with sleeves. Rose receives it, and believes it — the gown's true name, spoken by its maker. She looks in the glass: the white, the train, the clean lines, the verdict made wearable. The acquittal fits. The mirror confirms the judgment. She thinks of Thursday — of the town, of Bell's eye, of the evening the gown was ordered against — and she is ready. The atelier has done its work. The war has its uniform.)**
*
> *(She pays the fitting's account in full — the atelier's war-effort, honored promptly. Élise waves off the haste — Miss Hartwell pays like a general, and generals are the atelier's favorite clients. The receipt is filed with the campaign's papers: the verdict, tailored, paid for, coming.)*
> *(At home she stands before her own glass in the half-fitted gown — pinned, chalked, unfinished — and sees what the atelier saw: the clean name, taking shape in thread. The acquittal is being sewn. Thursday will wear it. The town will read the train like a verdict, and the verdict will be hers.)*
> *(She writes in the green book: Élise — the acquittal, with sleeves. Fitting complete. The gown's doctrine entered: display invites doubt, declaration ends it. The war's uniform, nearly ready. The campaign's armor, tailored to the thread.)*

> 4. [examine]Watch the train demonstrated — "judgment, trailing" — and laugh. → Remembered: The laugh as fitting's seal; the verdict moves correctly.
> 5. [micro]Surrender the rings — "the Gazette notices rings." → Remembered: Her jewel discipline's final form; even engaged hands go bare.
> 6. [social]Hear of Bell's three lines about a bracelet — the fashion eye's precedent. → Remembered: The cautionary bracelet; she will never be its subject.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the clean name, worn; the house speaks flowers.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks through the house-turned-garden in the morning — the hall, the morning room, the stairs, all breathing roses. A beautiful secret, kept by servants: the household has converted, belief replacing performance. The roses are everywhere — not decoration, but statement. The house speaks flowers now, fluently, and the fluency is the campaign's.)*
> *(The cook sends up a breakfast-tray rose — for the week, miss. The kitchen's enlistment; the war now feeds on flowers. She takes it, and feels the campaign as construction — stem by stem, that will stand. The Park taught her how things are built: not all at once, but piece by piece, honestly, the foundations first.)*
> *(She finds Augusta arranging a vase — an act so domestic it stops conversation. The general, with flowers, her hands careful among the stems, the map-room commander become a gardener. The clean name should be seen to be kept, Augusta says. Even by vases. The doctrine of visible keeping; even porcelain participates. The general's flowers; the image outranks every strategy session.)*
> *(She puts the cook's stem in her hair — for the cook — the woman's placement, the hair above the ear, softness and visibility. The gesture's gratitude; the household's flowers are worn, not just displayed. She goes out to be seen — the garden going with her, the house's belief marching in her wake. Her daily sally, the campaign's construction, stem by stem, standing.)**
*
> *(She thinks about the house as an instrument — about how the servants' belief has become the campaign's infrastructure. The beautiful secret, kept by everyone: the house speaks flowers, and the town hears. The construction, stem by stem, stands.)*
> *(She writes in the green book: the house, garden. The cook, enlisted. The general, arranging. The name, kept visibly. The garden, going out with her. The construction, standing.)*
> *(She goes out — the cook's stem in her hair, the garden going with her. The street sees her: the white, the rose, the house's belief made visible. 
> *(She is seen — and being seen, in white, with the cook's rose in her hair, is the campaign. The house's belief, walking. The construction, standing. The garden, going out.)*

scenes.synopsis: B3 — the long game; "They can print every week, child. You need only win every day."
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta sends for her — not a summons, a sending-for. The distinction, fluent in Augusta's grammar: counsel, not command. She goes, and the general receives her in the map-room, the roses on the table between them like a campaign's markers, the week's positions laid out in flowers.)*
> *(A flower is a ballot no one can trace. The franchise, explained; the general's political theory, delivered over the roses. Untraceable ballots win in numbers; the town's voting, multiplied, becomes unanswerable. You are strategically pleased, I hope. Permission to enjoy the winning; morale is a weapon, and Augusta permits its use, even encourages it.)*
> *(They can print every week, child. You need only win every day. The sentence that becomes the season's doctrine; daily beats weekly, the annuity outlasts the lump sum. They have the bigger weapon, and you have the faster one. Her understanding of tempo as armament; speed outranks size, mornings outrank Thursdays. She looks at the general — vase-arranger yesterday, commander today — and sees whole. The woman is the strategy; the strategy is the woman.)*
> *(Daily life wins by accumulation. The war, understood in one sentence; the doctrine's final form, the sentence she will preach all season. You are already winning it. She accepts — or demands proof. The general's assurance, banked, not spent. Her faith's measure, taken. The long game, understood. Every day.)**
*
> *(She thinks about the long game — about what accumulation actually looks like, day by day. Not a single triumph, but the ledger: mornings won, conduct kept, flowers voted. The war, understood in one sentence, practiced in a thousand mornings.)*
> *(She writes in the green book: the counsel, received. The franchise, explained. The tempo, armed. The doctrine: win every day. The assurance, banked. The long game, understood.)*
> *(She leaves the map-room — the counsel banked, the doctrine settled. The long game, understood: win every day, and the weeks take care of themselves. The general's assurance, carried. The war, to be won daily.)*
> *(She thinks about the general — vase-arranger yesterday, commander today, the woman whole. The strategy is the woman; the woman is the strategy. The long game, in person.)*

scenes.synopsis: texture — "win every day"; the doctrine, absorbed.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks after the counsel — the long gallery, the thinking walk — and she turns Augusta's sentence over the way she turns a coin, feeling for the milling. *They can print every week. You need only win every day.* It is true the way her father's ledgers were true: not inspiring, but *balancing*. Weekly ink is a lump sum, spent all at once, gone by Friday. Daily conduct is an annuity — small payments, compounding, impossible to outspend. Pyke's purse can buy the sky over Vauxhall for a night. It cannot buy every dawn. It cannot buy the cook's rose on the breakfast tray. It cannot buy Augusta arranging a vase. The Network's coin is vast, but it is *lumpy* — and she is *liquid*, daily, everywhere, in white.)*
> *(She stops at the portrait of her grandmother — the one who survived the '45 by being boring on purpose, or so family legend says — and she nods to the painted woman. "Every day," she says to the portrait, to the week, to herself. The doctrine settles the way doctrines do: not as inspiration but as *schedule*. Tomorrow: the calls, the flowers, the witnessed kindnesses. The day after: the same. The press prints Thursdays; she prints *mornings*. And somewhere in Fleet Street, Pyke is setting type for a weekly weapon, and she almost — almost — pities him. Almost. Pity is a luxury. She walks on, and the gallery measures her resolution in portraits.)*
> *(She thinks about the day's arithmetic — about what winning every day actually requires. Not triumphs, but mornings. Not verdicts, but conduct. The ledger of days, balanced daily. Her father's true ledgers, applied to war.)*
> *(She thinks about the week ahead — about Thursday's number, about Pyke's silence, about the special that is certainly brewing. The doctrine holds for all of it: win the day, and the week follows. The accumulation, begun.)*
> *(She leaves the gallery — the doctrine settled, the coin's milling felt. The day's arithmetic, begun. Every day: the sentence, walked. The grandmother's portrait, nodded to. The week, to be won daily.)*
> *(She writes in the green book: the counsel, walked. The doctrine, balanced. The day, to be won. Every day. The accumulation, begun.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Turn the sentence "like a coin, feeling for the milling" — the truth, tested. → Remembered: Her habit of testing truths by touch; the sentence is genuine currency.
> 2. [stance]"Weekly ink is a lump sum. Daily conduct is an annuity." → Remembered: Her financial reading of the war; the ledgers taught her compounding.
> 3. [social]"It cannot buy the cook's rose. It cannot buy Augusta's vase." → Remembered: Her inventory of the unbought; the purse has limits, and she knows them.
> 4. [examine]Name herself *liquid* against the purse's *lumpy* — the tactical metaphor. → Remembered: The liquidity doctrine; she flows where the purse cannot.
> 5. [micro]Nod to the grandmother's portrait — "boring on purpose" since the '45. → Remembered: Her use of ancestry as precedent; tedium is a family tradition.
> 6. [stance]"She prints *mornings*" — the schedule, adopted. → Remembered: The doctrine's final form; her press runs daily, at dawn.
> 7. [choice]Almost pity Pyke — "almost. Pity is a luxury." → Remembered: Her refusal of premature mercy, renewed; Laurent's pity is overruled.

scenes.synopsis: the withholding begins — Julian knows something about the Network's London interests, and fears the telling.
scenes.prose:
> *(Julian is announced — correctly, formally, the footman's voice at its most proper — and Rose knows before he enters: managed visits from Julian mean trouble. He comes in with his serious face, the one he wears for truth, and does not sit. The correctness is his alarm bell. Something has him by the conscience, and Julian's conscience is a heavy thing to carry into a morning room.)*
> *(Rose, he says, and stops. The stopping — Julian does not stop; Julian states — is the loudest thing in the room. It's magnificent, what you've done. And it terrifies me. The two words, weighed: magnificence and terror, coexisting. She waits, the way one waits for a man defusing ordnance. The white roses watch from the morning-room table — the campaign's symbols, attending his fear like witnesses.)*
> *(I have been following the purse, he says at last. Not where it comes from — Quill has that. Where it goes. What the Network is buying here, in London, with the balloon money and the rest. Another stop, longer. Telling you puts you in danger I cannot conduct away. The fear's true object: not his danger, hers — and his helplessness before it. He came anyway — the fear of not telling outweighed the fear of telling. The visit itself is the real message.)*
> *(She names it fear — which he wears the way other men wear anger: badly, honestly. Julian's fear is rarer than his fury, and more serious. The room is quiet. She thinks about what he's guessed — the Network's London interests, the purse's true purchases, the things bought quietly while the town watched the balloons — and about what his telling would cost them both. The decision approaches: press him, permit him, or preempt him. How to meet a frightened Julian — the question the morning has been building toward, and the choice that will define the courtship's terms. The roses watch. She decides.)**
*
> *(She writes in the green book: Julian — the withholding begins. Knows the Network's London interests, fears the telling. The fear, diagnosed: not his danger, hers. The decision, approaching: press, permit, or preempt. The courtship's terms, about to be set.)*

> 1. [social]Note the correct announcement — "managed visits from Julian mean trouble." → Remembered: Her reading of his formality; correctness is his alarm bell.

scenes.synopsis: texture — what Julian fears; the Network's London interests, guessed at.
scenes.prose:
> *(Alone, she turns his fear like a loaded pistol — carefully, respectfully. Fear, in Julian, is a rare instrument; it deserves the same care as his anger. Anger can be aimed. Fear can only be carried. She carries it to the window and looks out at the street, thinking, the pistol never rushed, never mocked.)*
> *(What is the Network buying in London? She asks what a balloon buys — not attention. Altitude. The sky over Vauxhall, bought for a night: a statement of reach, of purse, of the power to command the heavens above a pleasure garden. The balloon money is the visible purchase. What are the invisible ones? She thinks of the hawkers' extra pay, the paper's bought paragraphs, the double pay on balloon nights — and wonders what else the purse has bought, quietly, while the town watched the sky.)*
> *(He came anyway — the fear of not telling outweighed the fear of telling. A man who fears for her safety comes to warn her, knowing the warning endangers her further. The logic is Julian's: honorable, impossible, complete. She looks at the flower-seller on the corner, doing the week's best trade — the town, voting with flowers — and the double vision steadies, the way it always does: the town votes with flowers. And under the flowers, the Network is buying London. The pretty surface, and the purchase beneath.)*
> *(She must decide what to do with a frightened Julian. The decision's framing, settled: he is the patient, not the problem. Press him, and she gets the intelligence but spends his peace. Permit him, and she carries the not-knowing, trusting his fear as protection. Preempt him, and she gambles on her guess, calling the fear by its name. The fear, carried, waits for her answer. The white roses watch. The town votes. The Network buys. And Julian — brave, frightened, honorable Julian — waits for her to decide what his fear is for.)**
*
> *(She writes in the green book: the Network buys London, under the flowers. Balloon money: altitude, not attention. Julian's fear, carried respectfully. The decision, framed: the patient, not the problem. Tomorrow, she will choose how to meet it.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Turn his fear "like a loaded pistol" — carefully, respectfully. → Remembered: Her handling of others' fear; it is never rushed, never mocked.
> 2. [stance]Ask what a balloon *buys* — "not attention. *Altitude*." → Remembered: Her analysis of spectacle as power; the sky is a statement of reach.
> 3. [social]"He came anyway — the fear of *not* telling outweighed the fear of telling." → Remembered: Her reading of his arrival; the visit itself is the real message.
> 4. [examine]"Anger can be aimed. Fear can only be *carried*." → Remembered: The doctrine of fear vs. anger; she will carry what she cannot aim.
> 5. [micro]Look at the flower-seller "doing the week's best trade" — the town, voting. → Remembered: The commerce of the campaign; even the street profits from the clean name.
> 6. [stance]"The town votes with flowers. And under the flowers, the Network is buying London." → Remembered: Her double vision; the pretty surface and the purchase beneath.
