scenes.synopsis: B9 — the third hand: a name; a cutout she can reach.
scenes.prose:
> *(The green door gave him up — the carrier, the eagle ring, the quarterly gold — and Rose came home with the night's work done and the folded name still in her reticule, still sealed. She sits at her desk in the small hours, the Gazette's verdict filed, the evidence file blue-bound beside her, and looks at the fold — the seal on the letter, as Lavinia called it. The third hand has a name now. Not a face — never a face; the Network's face stays offstage, those are the season's terms, honored to the end — but a name, and an hour, and a coffee-house, and debts. A cutout she can reach. She breaks the seal — slowly, deliberately, the way one opens a door — and reads the name. And smiles — the small cold smile of a general whose map has just gained its last piece. The purse is mapped. The mouth prints. The hands are three. And the third — the third is hers. The reachable, reached. She folds the name away — the intelligence secured, the hour kept — blows out the lamp, and sleeps — the sleep of a woman who has reached the reachable. Tomorrow: the cutout. Tomorrow: the purse, one hand closer. The week closes on the opened seal, the read name, the smiled smile. The third hand has a name. The name has an hour. The hour has its debts, its drink, its ring. And Rose — the purse mapped, the face unshown, the terms honored — has the one thing the season promised: a cutout she can reach. The lamp is out. The war sleeps. The reachable waits for morning. Morning comes grey and honest — the kind of morning that balances its own columns. Rose wakes with the night's shape in her head: the green door, given up; the third hand, reached; the folded name, opened. The carrier's rhythm is broken — the tide stopped, the moon found. She dresses in the grey silk — the credibility, the brief, the City's belief — and goes down to a household that knows without being told: Letitia's lamps already lit, Augusta's newspaper already folded, the chocolate already poured. "Well?" Augusta says. "Reached," Rose says. "And the name?" "Opened." Augusta nods, the general's nod, and pours the chocolate. The day's ordinary business begins — the letters, the accounts, the atelier — but beneath it the war has turned: the purse broken, the machine's heart stopped, the reachable waiting for morning. The lamp is out. The war sleeps. And morning, when it fully comes, will find the reckoning ready.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Note \"The green door gave him up.\" → Remembered:Her success; the night's work is done.
> 2. [social]Sit \"in the small hours\" — the desk. → Remembered:Her hours; the war keeps late time.
> 3. [micro]Break the seal — \"the way one opens a door.\" → Remembered:Her deliberation; the name is opened ritually.
> 4. [stance]Read it — and smile. → Remembered:Her satisfaction; the map gains its last piece.
> 5. [examine]Name it \"the third is hers.\" → Remembered:Her possession; the reachable is reached.
> 6. [social]Recall \"never a face\" — the terms, honored. → Remembered:Her discipline; the offstage stays offstage.
> 7. [micro]Blow out the lamp — the sleep. → Remembered:Her rest; the reachable reached, she sleeps.
> 8. [choice]Dream of the second hand or the purse. → Remembered:Her ambition; the map's next blank, chosen.

scenes.synopsis: the third hand — a name; a cutout she can reach. Rose follows the cutout back to the chapel floor.
scenes.prose:
> *(The name came to her at midnight, the way names come in wartime — through a cutout, a girl who sells oranges near the Strand, who repeats what a compositor's boy repeated to her, and keeps the penny for the repeating. That is the cutout's whole economy: a penny for the carrying, and no questions about the weight. A name. Not the master's name — the cutouts never carry the master's name; the master is scenery, paid to be invisible. They carry the third hand, the one close enough to touch: the hand that set the type, that carried the copy, that knows the chapel's floor by the feel of it underfoot. Mr. Pettifer's chapel sets the* Lantern. *The compositors talk, the girl says, for the price of supper — bread and cheese money, the cheapest intelligence in London, and, Rose is learning, often the truest. She stands in her bedroom with a shawl over her nightdress and the campaign book open on the desk, the candle burned low, and writes the name down in the margin beside the second charge. Three hands. One she can reach. She thinks of Augusta's rule —* never pay for what fear will give you for nothing *— and then of the corollary the general never says aloud:* pay anyway; fear's testimony is cheaper but it lies about the change. *Fear rounds down. Fear forgets the detail that matters. Coin buys the whole telling, with the blots and crossings in. She dresses before the maid wakes. Wool, dark, the boots that have walked worse streets than Fleet — the working dress of a woman going to read, not to be seen. The white rose she wore yesterday she leaves on the desk; this morning she will not be the woman with the clean name. She will be the woman who reads the type. It is a smaller claim and a larger one: no flower, no declaration, only the eye, and the stone, and the truth of what the compositors set. The house sleeps around her — the aunts, the servants, the whole of the respectable world, none of them knowing that a Hartwell is about to walk into a printer's chapel after midnight. She takes up the shawl, the book, the resolve, and goes down the stair like a general going to the ground she has chosen.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Weigh the cutout's name — third hand, close enough to touch. → Remembered: How she prices cutout intelligence; the campaign book keeps the margin note.
> 2. [micro]Write the name in the margin beside the second charge. → Remembered: The name's place in the archive; it waits its scene.
> 3. [stance]Recall Augusta's rule, and the unsaid corollary. → Remembered: Whether she trusts fear's testimony or pays for the truth; Pettifer will notice.
> 4. [examine]Choose the wool, the dark, the boots — dress for the chapel floor. → Remembered: Her working dress, noted; the compositors will read it before she speaks.
> 5. [micro]Leave the white rose on the desk — this morning, not the clean name. → Remembered: When she sets the floriography aside; the rose waits on the desk.
> 6. [stance]"The woman who reads the type" — claim it before dawn. → Remembered: The role she takes; the chapter will hold her to it.
> 7. [social]Decide who walks with her — Larkin, or no one. → Remembered: Whom she trusts on Fleet Street after dark; the escort shapes the chapel's welcome.
> 8. [choice]Go at once, or wait for the press's night shift to settle. → Remembered: Her timing; the chapel reads lateness as either fear or command.

scenes.synopsis: Fleet Street after hours — Larkin walks her to Pettifer's chapel; the press's night geography.
scenes.prose:
> *(Fleet Street after the theatres empty is a different country — the chop-houses still lit, the coffee-houses loud with the day's second sitting, the press offices dark except where the night work burns. The street belongs, after midnight, to the trades that prefer it empty: the pressmen, the link-boys, the girls with oranges and information, the watchmen calling the hour to no one. Ned Larkin knows the street the way a ferryman knows a river: which doors are watched, which alleys end, which compositors drink where, which shadows are only shadows and which are scenery with a wage. He walks half a pace ahead of her, not beside — the escort's grammar, readable to anyone who cares to read it: she is under conduct, and the conduct is armed with nothing but belonging. Belonging is the only weapon you can carry openly on Fleet Street after dark. "Pettifer's chapel," he says, at a doorway that smells of lamp-oil and damp paper, "sets the* Lantern, *the* True Briton *when it pays, and anything else with coin behind it. The chapel's the men, miss — the father of the chapel speaks for them. That's Pettifer. Mind his hands." "His hands?" "Printer's hands. They've set ten thousand lies and never told one." She considers this a recommendation — the highest the trade offers, and the most honest: a man whose hands are truer than his copy. The stair is narrow; the noise rises — the press's night voice, the thump and slide of the machine below, the compositors' talk above it like gulls over a working boat. The building breathes ink. Every surface she touches will mark her. Larkin knocks twice, then once, a rhythm that is clearly a password wearing a knock's clothes. The door opens on lamplight and type and men in paper aprons, and every head turns, and Rose Hartwell walks into the chapel the way she walks into ballrooms — as if the room had been waiting, and she had merely been late. The lamplight is the color of weak tea. The type cases rise along the walls like the pipes of an organ. The men — a dozen of them, aproned, ink-fingered — stop their work the way a congregation stops its hymn: not all at once, but in a ragged decrescendo, the last compositor setting his last sort before he looks up. She lets them look. Looking is the first tax the chapel levies, and she pays it the way she pays all taxes: in full, and without flinching.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read Larkin's escort grammar — half a pace ahead, belonging as armor. → Remembered: How she moves under conduct; Fleet Street will remember the belonging.
> 2. [social]Take "printer's hands" as recommendation — or as warning. → Remembered: Her first read of Pettifer; the chapel adjusts its price accordingly.
> 3. [micro]Climb the narrow stair — note the press's night voice. → Remembered: The geography learned; she can find the chapel again in the dark.
> 4. [examine]Enter "as if the room had been waiting" — nerve, or performance. → Remembered: The entrance the compositors will describe; the telling costs or pays.
> 5. [stance]Decide what she is here: lady, buyer, or general. → Remembered: The role declared by her bearing; Pettifer will deal with the one she shows.
> 6. [social]Let Larkin make the introduction, or make it herself. → Remembered: Whether she spends Larkin's credit or her own; the chapel prices both.
> 7. [examine]Count the men, the frames, the lamplight — the chapel's strength. → Remembered: Her estimate of Pettifer's operation; Quill will want the numbers.
> 8. [choice]Name her errand at once, or let them guess it. → Remembered: Her opening move; the chapel's talk follows the opening.

scenes.synopsis: the compositors talk — Pettifer's chapel sets what it is paid to set; the evidence is composed, not found.
scenes.prose:
> *(The chapel at night is a working church of the trade — the frames along the walls like pews, the cases of type like hymnals, the compositors standing at their stations with the devotion of men who have given their eyes to small letters. The eldest wipes his hands on his apron and gives her the measuring look of a man pricing a customer. The younger one grins — the grin of a boy who has heard that a lady is coming and decided, in advance, to enjoy it. The damp proofs hang overhead like washing on a line, the day's libels drying in the lamplight. Rose takes it all in the way Augusta taught her to take a battlefield: the strength, the temper, the price. Then she speaks, and the chapel — which respects the direct the way a press respects clean copy — answers.)*
> "The *Lantern*." — Rose (no preamble; the chapel respects the direct the way a press respects clean copy) "Who sets it?"
> "We set what's brought." — the eldest compositor, wiping his hands on his apron "The chapel doesn't ask after the copy's mother, miss. We set it."
> "And the copy's mother pays well, I collect."
> "Pays." — a younger one, grinning "Pays in coin that doesn't ask to be counted, which is the best kind, because counting's work."
> "What comes in," — Rose "besides copy? Parcels? Letters to be set as facsimile?"
> "Facsimile's dear." — the eldest "Costs the customer double. The *Lantern* pays double for one thing, these three weeks."
> "A letter." — Rose "Set to look hand-written."
> "Set to look *found*." — the younger one, and the grin goes "You didn't hear it from us, miss. The chapel sets what it's paid to set. The *finding* — that's the customer's department."
> *(Rose looks at the frames, the cases, the damp proofs hanging like washing. Evidence is composed, not found. She has suspected it since the second number; suspicion is a poor witness, but a compositor's boy is a better one — and now she has the chapel's own mouth on it.* Set to look found. *The phrase is the whole crime in four words: not the forging, which is common, but the* finding, *faked — the lie dressed as discovery. "The customer," she says. "Describe him." And the chapel — paid for its talk, or merely flattered by the asking — describes him. The eldest gives the coat. The younger gives the hands. Between them, a man takes shape in the lamplight: not the master, never the master, but the third hand, the one close enough to touch. She files it all — the double rate, the three weeks, the department of finding — in the campaign book of her memory, to be written down the moment she is alone. It is the first hard intelligence of the night, and it has the taste of true things: specific, priced, unadorned. The chapel does not deal in motives. It deals in rates. And rates, Rose is learning, are more honest than motives — a man will lie about why, but he will tell the truth about what it cost. She lets the silence after the description stretch, the way Augusta lets a silence stretch after a demand: to see what walks into it.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear "we set what's brought" — the chapel's whole ethic. → Remembered: Her grasp of the trade's amorality; it shapes her offer.
> 2. [social]"The copy's mother pays well, I collect" — buy the talk or earn it. → Remembered: Whether she pays for candor; the chapel's future talk has a price now.
> 3. [examine]Mark "set to look *found*" — the forgery's whole method. → Remembered: The phrase she'll carry to Quill; it names the crime precisely.
> 4. [micro]Note "pays double for one thing, these three weeks" — the timeline. → Remembered: The three-week window; it dates the fabrication.
> 5. [stance]"Describe him" — command, or request. → Remembered: The register she uses on working men; Pettifer hears it from the doorway.
> 6. [social]Take the description — or press for the name. → Remembered: How hard she presses the chapel; the men decide what she's worth.
> 7. [examine]Study the damp proofs "like washing" — the evidence, hanging. → Remembered: The image filed; she'll need it when she testifies to herself.
> 8. [choice]Trust the talk, verify it, or buy the boy who talked. → Remembered: Her handling of sources; the cutout's safety may depend on it.

scenes.synopsis: the chapel's economy — who pays, what a night costs; the Network's purse behind the copy.
scenes.prose:
> *(Pettifer comes down from the gallery like a judge descending to the floor — a big man, ink to the elbow, the hands Larkin warned her about, the apron of a father of the chapel worn the way a mayor wears a chain. The compositors straighten, fractionally. The talk stops being talk and becomes work. He looks at Rose the way he looks at a forme that has come in with the copy doubtful: measuring, unhurried, deciding what it will cost to set it right. She meets the look. She has been measured by better men than printers, and by worse. "Father of the chapel," she says, and gives him the title the trade gives him, because titles are the cheapest coin and she is spending carefully tonight.)*
> "Father of the chapel." — Rose (Pettifer has come down from the gallery — a big man, ink to the elbow, the hands Larkin warned her about) "I want the price of a night."
> "A night of what, miss?"
> "Of setting. Of the *Lantern's* Thursday number. The whole of it — paper, men, the facsimile letter."
> "That's the customer's business." — Pettifer "And the customer pays for it to stay his."
> "The customer pays in coin that doesn't ask to be counted." — Rose "I am asking to count it. Not the coin — the *hands* it passes through. The chapel keeps books, Mr. Pettifer. Every chapel keeps books."
> *(A silence. The press thumps below — the night's heartbeat, unhurried. Pettifer looks at her the way a man looks at a woman who has named the thing he hoped was invisible — not angry, almost respectful, the way one respects a well-set line. She has him. Not bought —* read. *There is a difference, and the chapel knows it.)* "The purse comes monthly," he says at last. "A clerk brings it. The clerk's clerk brings *him*. Three hands, miss — same as your orange girl told you. The purse is London money, and it's deep, and it's patient. The *Lantern* is the cheapest thing it buys."
> "Cheapest." — Rose "What else does it buy?"
> "Ask the clerk's clerk." — Pettifer "If you can find him. Men like that are paid to be scenery."
> *(She files it — the monthly purse, the clerk's clerk, the scenery with a wage.* The cheapest thing it buys. *The phrase lands the way Quill's phrases land: as a reframe. She has been fighting a newspaper. She is, in fact, fighting a* budget *— a line item, the cheapest line, in a London purse so deep it buys libels the way other men buy wine: regularly, and without tasting. The scale of it steadies her rather than frightens her. A purse that deep leaves tracks. A purse that patient makes mistakes. She thanks the father of the chapel — with coin, and with the word, both, the two currencies of the trade — and the chapel, which has been watching, decides, overnight, what she is worth. The coin is counted without being counted, the way the purse's coin is: weighed in the hand, accepted without ceremony. The word — the plain thank-you, given as one professional to another — lands harder. Pettifer inclines his head a fraction, the smallest possible acknowledgment, and turns back to his gallery. The interview is over. The books, she understands, are open to her now — not all the pages, but the ones that matter.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Name "the price of a night" — buy the chapel's books. → Remembered: Her opening bid; Pettifer respects the directness or resents it.
> 2. [social]"Every chapel keeps books" — the lever, applied. → Remembered: Whether she threatens or trades; the father of the chapel decides which.
> 3. [examine]Hear "three hands" — the cutout's name, confirmed. → Remembered: The confirmation filed; the third hand is real and reachable.
> 4. [micro]Mark "the cheapest thing it buys" — the purse's scale. → Remembered: Her sense of the Network's London spending; it dwarfs the *Lantern*.
> 5. [stance]"Men like that are paid to be scenery" — accept the wall, or climb it. → Remembered: Her answer to the cutout's limit; Larkin takes notes.
> 6. [examine]Study Pettifer's hands — "ink to the elbow." → Remembered: The craftsman's portrait; she'll need his trust by dawn.
> 7. [social]Offer the chapel her own coin — or her protection. → Remembered: What she trades for the books; the chapel remembers the currency.
> 8. [choice]Press for the clerk, or let Pettifer volunteer. → Remembered: Her patience with the father of the chapel; he volunteers exactly once.

scenes.synopsis: the confession of the craft — the forged letter, set in type; how the evidence was made.
scenes.prose:
> *(Pettifer takes her to the stone — the great flat bed where the type is locked for printing, the chapel's altar, the place where copy becomes evidence. On it, under a damp cloth, the forme for Thursday's number: the* Lantern's *next libel, locked and ready, the chase and quoins tight, the whole of Thursday waiting like a prisoner for the cart. He lifts the cloth the way a surgeon lifts a sheet — with the gravity of a man showing a wound he did not inflict. "There," he says. "Read it." She reads. It is the second charge against her father's name, set in blackletter, the columns justified and clean — and in the middle of the column, the sorts chosen letter by letter to fake a lady's hand, a letter. A letter from her mother. A letter her mother never wrote. Rose reads it twice, the way one reads a wound: once for the pain, once for the shape. The paper it pretends to be is old; the type is new. The crossings are marked for the compositor, the blots placed like stage directions — the forgery is in the* setting, *the whole craft of the chapel turned to making a lie look found. "Who wrote the copy?" she asks, her voice level, proud of the level the way a rider is proud of a straight line over bad ground. "A clerk brought it," Pettifer says. "Written out fair, the crossings and blots marked for the compositor. The customer pays double for facsimile, miss. Somebody wanted it* believed*." She looks at the letter — her mother's hand, faked in type — and understands the whole of the* Lantern's *method: not invention, but* composition. *The evidence is composed, not found. And composition can be uncomposed — pulled apart, sort by sort, until the lie shows its joins. It is the chapter's whole strategy in a single sentence, and she holds it the way one holds a lit match: carefully, and not for long, because it is about to be put to use. She looks once more at the faked hand — the crossings, the blots, the lady's flowing capitals rendered in sorts — and memorizes the tells the way she memorized her mother's true hand, years ago, from letters kept in a drawer: the slope, the pressure, the places where the forger's nerve failed and the type shows it. Then she steps back from the stone. Looking is free, Pettifer said. She has looked.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read the forged letter twice — "the way one reads a wound." → Remembered: Her discipline under the forgery; the chapel watches her read.
> 2. [micro]Note "the paper it pretends to be is old; the type is new." → Remembered: The forgery's tell; she'll use it when she answers.
> 3. [stance]Keep the voice level — "a straight line over bad ground." → Remembered: Her composure as witnessed; Pettifer revises his price of her.
> 4. [examine]"Crossings and blots marked for the compositor" — the craft, confessed. → Remembered: The method detailed; Quill will need every mark.
> 5. [social]Ask "who wrote the copy" — of Pettifer, or of the chapel. → Remembered: Whom she holds answerable; the father answers for his men.
> 6. [examine]Grasp "composition can be uncomposed" — the strategy, whole. → Remembered: The insight that governs the chapter; the lie has joins.
> 7. [micro]Touch the forme, or keep her hands behind her back. → Remembered: Whether she handles the evidence; the type leaves ink.
> 8. [choice]Name what she feels — or file it for later. → Remembered: Her economy with feeling; the game will ask for it at trial.

scenes.synopsis: who brought the copy — the copy-bringer described; the third hand, reachable.
scenes.prose:
> *(She asks for the copy-bringer the way Augusta asks for ground — as the thing the whole campaign depends on. Pettifer considers. The chapel does not ask after names; names are the customer's department, and the chapel is careful about departments. But faces — faces are the trade's business, and Pettifer has the eye his trade gives him. He describes the man the way a compositor describes a doubtful sort: by the particulars, without ornament.)*
> "Describe the clerk." — Rose "The one who brings the copy. Not the purse — the *copy*."
> "Different man." — Pettifer "The purse comes monthly, quiet. The copy comes weekly, and he stays to see it set. Youngish. Dark. A clerk's coat, but the coat's too good — a gentleman's cast-off, or a gentleman playing clerk. He reads French."
> "Reads French." — Rose "How do you know?"
> "Corrects the accents." — Pettifer, dry "On the facsimile. Your mother's hand —" he stops. "The *lady's* hand. He corrects the accents like a man who's been corrected himself. Émigré, I'd say. Or émigré-adjacent. The Network's —" he stops again, and looks at her. "The *purse's* London man, miss. That's what the chapel calls him. We don't know his name. The chapel doesn't ask after names; names are the customer's department."
> "But you've seen his face."
> "I've seen his hands." — Pettifer "He holds the copy like it might bite. Like he's afraid of it. A man who's afraid of the paper he carries —" the father of the chapel considers "— is a man who can be reached, miss. Fear's cheaper than coin, and it spends anywhere."
> *(Rose thinks of the orange girl's name, the third hand, the cutout she can reach. A man afraid of his own paper. The description settles over the name like type settling into a forme: youngish, dark, the too-good coat, the corrected accents, the émigré's past worn under the clerk's present. She files it the way Augusta files everything — under* leverage. *And she files Pettifer's counsel with it:* fear's cheaper than coin, and it spends anywhere. *It is the kind of sentence the trade produces the way the press produces pages: regularly, and worth reading. A man who can be reached. The third hand, with a face now, or the beginning of one. She thanks Pettifer — and the father of the chapel, who has given her the two most valuable things in his shop, watches her go with the look of a man who has just priced a customer and found her worth the trade's best. The two most valuable things: the description, and the counsel. The description — youngish, dark, the too-good coat, the corrected accents — is a face she can watch for at a door. The counsel —* fear's cheaper than coin, and it spends anywhere *— is a currency she can spend at will. She carries both down the narrow stair, past the press's night voice, past the compositors' talk like gulls over a working boat. Larkin falls in half a pace ahead. The street is colder now, the theatres long empty, the chop-houses dimming. Somewhere in London, the copy-bringer sleeps — or does not sleep — unaware that his fear has been priced, filed, and entered in a lady's campaign book under* leverage. *She walks home through the thinning dark, and the name in the margin and the face in the description settle together like type in a forme: the third hand, reachable at last.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]"A gentleman's cast-off, or a gentleman playing clerk" — the copy-bringer, pictured. → Remembered: The description fixed; she'll know him at the door.
> 2. [micro]Mark "corrects the accents" — the émigré tell. → Remembered: The detail that places him; the purse's London man has a past.
> 3. [stance]Hear "the purse's London man" — the chapel's own naming. → Remembered: How the trade names him; the name carries no face, only function.
> 4. [social]"He holds the copy like it might bite" — fear, as leverage. → Remembered: Her read of his fear; Augusta will approve the filing.
> 5. [examine]Weigh "fear's cheaper than coin" — Pettifer's counsel. → Remembered: Whether she takes the father's advice; it flavors the door-watch.
> 6. [choice]Ask for the nights he comes, or the door he uses. → Remembered: Which intelligence she buys first; the watch is built on it.
> 7. [micro]Note the stopped sentences — what Pettifer won't say. → Remembered: The chapel's limits; she won't get the master's name here.
> 8. [social]Thank the chapel — coin, or word. → Remembered: How she pays for craft confessed; the men will talk of it.

scenes.synopsis: the copy-bringer's trail — a name, a door, a cutout she can reach; the plan for the watch.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks home through the thinning dark with Larkin half a pace ahead, and builds the watch the way Augusta builds a campaign — from what the ground gives, and the ground has given generously tonight. The copy-bringer comes weekly, stays to see the facsimile set, uses the side door, fears his own paper. The orange girl's name was the third hand; Pettifer's description is the face; between them, a man she can reach — not the master, never the master, but the hand before the type, the only hand that touches the lie before it becomes print. She writes it in the campaign book while the house sleeps: the nights, the door, the too-good coat, the corrected accents, the fear. The book is filling — margins, underlinings, the second charge annotated with the chapel's own words. Then she considers the three roads, because a general does not set a watch without knowing what the watch is* for. *Take him — the law, the seizure, the type pulled as evidence, the purse knowing by morning and the depth closing like a fist. Follow him — the longer road, the master at the end of it, the purse's London depth mapped by dawn, the risk that a frightened man scents the follower. Or let him run — let him carry back what she wants the master to hear: that the* Lantern's *evidence is known, composed, and held. Three roads. The forged letter sits at the center — damp, newly set, her mother's faked hand — and the decision is not which road is righteous, but which road the* evidence *walks best. She dips the pen. She does not decide yet. Augusta taught her: decide at dawn, when the thing has kept overnight — a decision that has slept is a decision that has been interrogated by the dark, and survived it. But the naming — the naming she does now, in the book's margin, in ink: the copy-bringer. The Network's man. Hers to take, to follow, or to loose. The ink dries. The house sleeps. The watch is built, and only the choosing remains. She sits a moment longer at the desk, the candle guttering, and thinks about the three roads as Augusta would: as ground. Take him is high ground, held briefly. Follow him is the long valley. Let him run is the open field. Each has its weather. Each has its cost. She closes the book.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Build the watch from "what the ground gives" — nights, door, coat, accents. → Remembered: The watch's foundations; Larkin will build on them.
> 2. [micro]Write it in the campaign book while the house sleeps. → Remembered: The archive's night entry; the book holds the plan.
> 3. [stance]Consider the three roads — take, follow, loose. → Remembered: Her strategic temper; the key decision will test it.
> 4. [examine]Place the forged letter "at the center of all of them." → Remembered: How she centers evidence; Quill will find it already centered.
> 5. [social]Decide whom to tell at breakfast — Augusta, all; Letitia, some. → Remembered: The household's briefing level; the aunts prepare accordingly.
> 6. [micro]"Decide at dawn" — Augusta's maxim, honored. → Remembered: Her discipline with decisions; the dawn will find her ready.
> 7. [choice]Name him in the margin — "the Network's man." → Remembered: The naming, in ink; the game will hold her to it.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE FORGED LETTER. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes at dawn, summoned by a note sent with the milk — the lawyer's knock, punctual as a rent day. He reads the compositor's account: Rose's night notes, the facsimile's method, the three-week window, the chapel's own phrase,* set to look found. *Then he does what lawyers do: converts outrage into procedure. "Three roads, Miss Hartwell," he says, folding his hands. "One: expose it now — publish the forgery's method, the Gazette, the town, before Thursday's number lands. The* Lantern *bleeds in public, but the law gets nothing it can hold. Two: hold it for trial — say nothing, let Pyke print, and produce the stone and the compositor in court, when the libel action comes. The* Lantern *hangs itself, but you must endure the printing meanwhile. Three: let me seize the type — a writ, the sheriff's men at the chapel door, the forme taken as evidence tonight. The* Lantern *stops, but the chapel suffers, and Pettifer's men will not thank you." He unfolds the hands. "The letter is yours, Miss Hartwell. The law's, or the town's, or the sheriff's — choose whose." The room is quiet. The forged letter sits between them — damp, newly set, her mother's faked hand — and Rose understands that the choosing is the whole of the war: not the evidence, which is had, but the* spending *of it.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The forged letter:*
- **Expose it now** — *Gazette flavor set: combative.* Publish the forgery's method before Thursday — the town reads how the evidence was composed. *(Bell prints it; Pyke denies it; the chapel's name stays out of it.)*
- **Hold it for trial** — *Quill+; the long game.* Say nothing; let Pyke print; produce the stone and the compositor when the libel action comes. *(Quill approves the patience; Rose must endure Thursday's number unread.)*
- **Let Quill seize the type** — *Law+; the chapel pays.* A writ, the sheriff's men, the forme taken tonight — evidence in hand, the press stopped. *(Pettifer's men resent it; the Network's purse finds another chapel.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: exposure's daylight, the trial's patience, or the seizure's force. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the choice carried — Quill's counsel on the chosen road; the law's next move.
scenes.prose:
> *(The choice made, Quill does what good counsel does: stops arguing the roads and starts paving the one she chose. If she chose exposure, he drafts the paragraph for Bell — method, not accusation; the compositor unnamed, the chapel unharmed, the forgery's joins shown like a tailor's basting, the town taught to read for them. If she chose the trial, he seals her night notes in his own hand, dates them, witnesses them with Larkin — the stone will be produced when the court, not the town, is ready, and the waiting will be the weapon's tempering. If she chose seizure, he writes the writ before the ink of her decision is dry, and warns her, once, the way lawyers warn when the warning is the fee: the sheriff's men will frighten the chapel, and frightened chapels find other customers, and the purse — deep, patient — will buy another press by week's end. "One thing more," he says, folding the papers with the care of a man folding a map before a march. "The letter pretends to be your mother's hand. When this is done — however it is done — the town will remember that a forger chose* her *hand to fake. There is a compliment in it, Miss Hartwell, of the most backhanded kind: they faked the handwriting of a woman whose word the town trusts." Rose considers this. Her mother has been dead six years; the town's trust in her is one of the few Hartwell assets Rackham could not sell — the creditors took the plate, the land, the name's polish, but not the memory of a woman whose word held. "Then," she says, "we spend it." Quill bows — the small, precise bow of a man who has just been handed a weapon and told its price. It is not servitude. It is partnership — the law, joining the war, on her terms. She watches him go with the papers, and feels the choice settle: whatever road she chose, it is hers now, paved and committed, and the town, the court, or the sheriff will walk it with her. The room is very quiet after the lawyer's knock has faded. The forged letter is gone — into the law's keeping — and its absence on the table is a presence of its own: the war's first weapon, forged by the enemy, now held by her counsel. She stands at the window and watches the street wake.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Watch Quill "pave the road she chose" — counsel's discipline. → Remembered: Her trust in his execution; the law moves at her word now.
> 2. [social]Weigh the warning — "frightened chapels find other customers." → Remembered: Whether she counts the chapel's cost; Pettifer will hear of it.
> 3. [micro]Note the sealed notes, dated, witnessed — the archive hardens. → Remembered: The evidence's chain of custody; it begins at dawn.
> 4. [stance]"They faked the handwriting of a woman whose word the town trusts." → Remembered: How she takes the backhanded compliment; it becomes ammunition.
> 5. [examine]"Then we spend it" — the decision to spend her mother's trust. → Remembered: The price named aloud; the game will collect it.
> 6. [social]Read Quill's bow — "handed a weapon and told its price." → Remembered: The counsel-client register; Quill serves the general, not the girl.
> 7. [choice]Send word to Lavinia now, or hold the forgery close. → Remembered: Whether the ally is briefed; Lavinia's hand in this is older than Rose's.

scenes.synopsis: the chapel floor by daylight — ink, damp paper, the stone; the trade seen clearly.
scenes.prose:
> *(She returns to Pettifer's chapel at midday — by daylight, with Larkin, through the front door this time, like a customer and not a thief — and sees the trade as the trade sees itself. The stone stands empty, the forme gone to the press; the compositors eat bread and cheese among the cases, their aprons folded down like flags at half-mast, the dinner hour observed with the gravity of a sacrament. The damp proofs are dry now, stacked, ordinary — libels by daylight, paperwork, the night's urgencies filed into the day's routine. A boy sweeps type from the floor, and the dropped sorts tick into the pan like small change — the trade's small change, literally, the letters worth less than the sweeping. Pettifer nods from the gallery — the nod of a man who has decided, overnight, what she is worth, and decided it in her favor. On the wall, the chapel's rules, framed: the customs of the trade, the fines for smoking near the cases, the scale of prices, the whole of the craft's self-government in blackletter. Facsimile: double. She stands before the framed rules, and understands she has been fighting a* trade *— not a man, not a paper, a trade with customs and prices and men who eat bread and cheese among the evidence. Pyke is the customer. The purse is the capital. The chapel is the workshop. And a workshop can be bought, or starved, or turned — but not shamed, because shame is not in its customs. It is the most useful thing she has learned all week: you cannot shame a price list. You can only outbid it, or outlast it, or — and this is the thought she carries down the stair — make the* customer *ashamed of what the workshop sells him. She touches the framed glass once, lightly, the way one touches a map before a march. Then she goes down to the press room, to see the machine that will print Thursday — the great iron frame, the platen, the hunger of it, the way it waits, patient as the purse, for whatever copy the night brings. The press room smells of hot metal and oil. A pressman nods to her — the nod one worker gives another — and goes back to making ready. She lays her hand on the iron frame, briefly. It is cold. On Thursday it will be warm with work. She takes her hand away, and goes back up into the day.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Enter "like a customer and not a thief" — the daylight register. → Remembered: Her two entrances; the chapel compares them.
> 2. [micro]Watch the boy sweep type — "dropped sorts tick into the pan like small change." → Remembered: The trade's small change; she prices everything now.
> 3. [stance]"Fighting a trade — not a man, not a paper." → Remembered: The strategic reframe; it governs the libel war's second act.
> 4. [examine]Read the framed rules — "Facsimile: double." → Remembered: The price list memorized; the campaign book gains a page.
> 5. [social]Take Pettifer's nod — "decided, overnight, what she is worth." → Remembered: The father's valuation; the chapel's future talk follows it.
> 6. [micro]Touch the glass "like a map before a march." → Remembered: The gesture; the general's habits are forming.
> 7. [choice]Go down to the press room — or leave the machine unvisited. → Remembered: Whether she faces the press itself; Thursday needs the visit.

scenes.synopsis: the forgery, traced — the same hand that wrote her family's filth, years ago.
scenes.prose:
> *(Lavinia comes at two, unannounced, in scarlet — the drawing room goes quiet around her the way water goes quiet around a stone. She has read Rose's note, and brought, in a morocco case, the thing Rose did not know she owned: the* Lantern's *libel against the Cranes, printed four years ago, when Lavinia was new-married. The case is opened with the ceremony of a woman producing a dueling pistol. "Read the letter," Lavinia says. "The facsimile. The one they set to look found." Rose reads. It is a different hand — a different family's shame, a mother's jewels and a lover's debts — but the* crossings *are the same, the blots marked the same, the lady's flowing capitals faked with the same compositor's patience. The compositor's hand, underneath the lady's, is the same: the same shop, the same method, the same customer paying double for facsimile. Four years apart, and the trade has not changed its tune — only its victim. "Four years," Lavinia says, and the scarlet does not move — she is very still, which for Lavinia is the equivalent of shouting. "Four years ago they composed my mother's disgrace, and I paid a solicitor to call it untrue, and the town believed the solicitor because solicitors are expensive. I have waited four years for someone to* uncompose *one." She closes the morocco case — the snap of it loud in the quiet room. "You will tell me, darling, everything Pettifer's chapel told you. And then you will let me help you break him — not buy him.* Break *him." Rose looks at the closed case and understands the ally's agenda entire: Lavinia does not want the* Lantern *silenced. She wants it* unmade *— in the open, the way her family was unmade, with the town watching and the joins showing. It is a larger ambition than Rose's, and a more dangerous one: Rose wants the libel answered; Lavinia wants the manufactory dismantled, piece by piece, in daylight. The alliance holds. The agenda has teeth. And teeth, Rose thinks, are exactly what the next phase requires — her own war has been fought with ledgers and patience, and patience, while virtuous, does not break presses.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read the four-year-old facsimile — "the crossings are the same." → Remembered: The method matched across four years; the forger has a history.
> 2. [micro]Note "the compositor's hand, underneath the lady's, is the same." → Remembered: The shop identified; the same chapel set both libels.
> 3. [stance]"She is very still, which for Lavinia is shouting." → Remembered: Her read of the ally's fury; Lavinia's stillness is a weapon.
> 4. [social]"You will tell me everything" — the ally's demand, priced. → Remembered: What she shares with Lavinia; the alliance runs on information.
> 5. [examine]"Not buy him. *Break* him." — the agenda, named. → Remembered: Lavinia's terms; the general notes the teeth.
> 6. [choice]Accept "break, not buy" — or hold her own terms. → Remembered: Whether the alliance's aim is shared; the season will test it.
> 7. [micro]Close the morocco case — or leave it open. → Remembered: The gesture; Lavinia reads gestures like copy.
> 8. [social]Name the partnership aloud — "uncompose one." → Remembered: The word chosen; "uncompose" becomes the campaign's verb.

scenes.synopsis: the old libel remembered — Lavinia's four years; the agenda named aloud and priced.
scenes.prose:
> *(Lavinia tells it the way she tells everything that matters: standing, the scarlet very still, the words placed like type in a forme — each one chosen, each one locked. It is the story of the Crane libel, four years old, and it has been told rarely, and never cheaply. Rose listens the way the chapel listens to copy: completely, without interrupting the setting. The drawing room holds its breath. Even the clock seems to tick more quietly. Four years is a long time to carry a story untold. Rose watches the scarlet — the color that never apologizes — and understands that this telling is itself a kind of trust: Lavinia does not narrate her wounds to just anyone. The drawing room, with its afternoon light and its well-behaved furniture, seems an absurdly civilized place for a story about forgery and ruin. But then, Rose thinks, ruin is always absurdly civilized at the start. It arrives in good manners, and stays for the furniture.)*
> "Four years." — Lavinia "I was twenty-three, new-married, and the *Lantern* printed that my mother had sold her jewels to pay a lover's debts. The jewels were sold — to pay *my* dowry. The lover was invented. The letter was composed. I learned the word *composed* that year, darling — from a solicitor who charged by it."
> "And the town believed the solicitor."
> "The town believed the *money*." — Lavinia "Expensive solicitors are the ton's favorite novelists. But the letter, darling — the letter was *found* in no drawer on earth. It was set, letter by letter, by a compositor who was paid double. Four years I've known it. Four years I've waited for the trade to make the same mistake twice."
> "It has." — Rose "My mother's hand. Thursday's number."
> "Then we are *twice* owed." — Lavinia (rising; the scarlet moves at last, like a flag in a first wind) "You will uncompose yours, darling, and I will uncompose mine, and Pyke will learn what the gutter learns slowest: that composition has an author, and authors can be *named*."
> *(Rose watches her go — the scarlet down the stair, the morocco case under her arm — and thinks: an ally with a four-year debt is the best kind and the most dangerous. The best, because she will not sell; the debt is too old, too personal, too perfectly preserved to be bought off with anything the purse could offer. The most dangerous, because she will not stop — not at the chapel door, not at the courtroom, not at the point where a prudent general would call the ground held and go home. Lavinia's war is not Rose's war, though they march together: Rose fights to clear a name; Lavinia fights to settle a score. The distinction matters, and Rose files it where she files all distinctions about allies — under* watch, and use, and never quite trust. *The stair is empty. The scarlet is gone. The room is quiet. But the air holds the shape of what was said:* authors can be named. *It is a threat, a promise, and a program, all in four words. Rose writes it in the campaign book, in the margin, in ink. Then she goes up to dress for the evening's work — for the war, it turns out, has two fronts now: the chapel's, and the ally's.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]"The town believed the money" — Lavinia's whole philosophy. → Remembered: The ally's cynicism, priced; Rose decides what of it to use.
> 2. [social]"I learned the word *composed*" — the shared vocabulary. → Remembered: The alliance's language; "uncompose" is now a joint verb.
> 3. [micro]Mark "the scarlet moves at last" — fury's release. → Remembered: Lavinia's tells; the general files them.
> 4. [stance]"Twice owed" — accept the joint debt, or keep the books separate. → Remembered: Whether the wars merge; the alliance's depth is set here.
> 5. [examine]"Authors can be *named*" — the threat, savored. → Remembered: How far Lavinia will go; Rose measures the distance.
> 6. [choice]Offer Lavinia the chapel's name — or hold Pettifer back. → Remembered: What the ally is given; the chapel's safety is in her hands.
> 7. [social]Watch the scarlet go — "the best kind and the most dangerous." → Remembered: Her final assessment; the game will test it at the breaking.
> 8. [micro]Keep the morocco case's lesson — or return it unlearned. → Remembered: Whether the old libel teaches the new war; four years is tuition.

scenes.synopsis: the fabricated evidence, itemized — each charge, each invented source; the campaign book's ledger.
scenes.prose:
> *(They work at the Bath house's dining table — cleared, lamp-lit, the campaign book open — and itemize the* Lantern's *evidence the way Quill itemizes an estate: charge by charge, source by source, until the fabrication shows its whole skeleton. The table becomes a courtroom without a judge: the lamp the only witness, the book the only record, the three of them the whole of the prosecution. Charge the first: the ruin as family fraud — source, a "ledger" never produced, quoted but never shown, the kind of source that exists only in the quoting. Charge the second: the suitors as dupes — source, "a lady's correspondence," the facsimile letter, composed in Pettifer's chapel at double rates, her mother's hand faked in type. Charge the third: the restoration as swindle — source, "workmen's testimony," workmen who, Larkin reports, were paid a week's wages for an afternoon's remembering. Each charge, each invented source; each source, a hand that was paid. Quill writes the ledger in his clerk's hand — neat, damning, the kind of document that makes judges lean forward, the pen moving with the pleasure of a man who loves a clean case. Lavinia supplies the fourth-year parallel from the morocco case: the same chapel, the same double rate, the same customer's purse — four years of the same manufactory, the same hands, the same double. "It is not a newspaper," Quill says at last, capping his pen. "It is a* manufactory. *Evidence, made to order, at double rates." Rose looks at the ledger — three charges, four sources, every one of them bought — and feels the war change shape under her hands: she is not fighting a liar. She is fighting a* manufacturer. *And manufacturers have books, and workmen, and premises — and premises can be visited, at dawn, by a woman who reads type. It is the most clarifying sentence of the week. She copies it into the campaign book, underlines it twice, and the three of them sit a moment in the lamplight, the ledger between them like a map of ground they are about to take. Lavinia reaches for the morocco case, then stops — the parallel entered, the history filed. Quill sands the last page. The lamp burns lower. It is past midnight, and the three of them have done what the* Lantern *does, in reverse: they have taken scattered libels and composed them into evidence — true evidence, this time, with sources that can be named and hands that can be sworn.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Itemize "charge by charge, source by source" — the ledger, built. → Remembered: The fabrication's skeleton; the campaign book holds it whole.
> 2. [micro]"A ledger never produced, quoted but never shown" — the first charge's hollow. → Remembered: The missing ledger; she'll demand it in the open.
> 3. [social]"Workmen paid a week's wages for an afternoon's remembering." → Remembered: Larkin's finding; the workmen are witnesses now.
> 4. [examine]"It is a *manufactory*" — Quill's reframe. → Remembered: The war's new shape; manufacturers have premises, and premises can be visited.
> 5. [stance]Feel the war change shape — liar, or manufacturer. → Remembered: Her strategic register; the dawn visit is decided here.
> 6. [choice]Show Lavinia the chapel's name in the ledger — or keep it coded. → Remembered: How much the ally sees; Pettifer's safety is priced.
> 7. [micro]Cap the pen — the ledger, finished. → Remembered: The document's completion; Quill dates it, and it becomes evidence.
> 8. [social]Divide the night's work — who carries what to dawn. → Remembered: The division of labor; the general assigns, the household executes.

scenes.synopsis: the white rose — floriography of the clean name; motif, colorway, and wearing, chosen.
scenes.prose:
> *(The white rose is still on the desk where she left it at midnight — a little open now, the petals loosening, the clean name's flower doing what flowers do: persisting, regardless of the war. She picks it up. Tomorrow — today — she will go to the press at dawn in work dress, and be the woman who reads the type herself. But the rose goes with her, or it does not, and where it goes matters: floriography is not decoration, it is* declaration, *and the town reads flowers the way it reads faces. A white rose at the press says: the clean name, here, among the ink — worn where the lie was set, a true thing in the manufactory. A white rose half-hidden says: the name, carried privately — Pettifer will see what the chapel misses, the one reader who reads the reader. A white rose left behind says: the war first, the name after — the flower guarding the ledger, the clean name kept clean of the chapel's ink. She holds the flower to the lamplight and turns it slowly. The petals are loosening, but the color holds — white, uncompromised, the one thing in the room that has not been composed, set, or paid for. It grew. That is its whole argument, and it is unanswerable. She thinks of the faked letter — the crossings marked, the blots placed — and then of the rose, which no compositor set and no customer ordered. One true thing. She chooses — the way she chooses everything now: by what it will mean when Bell's* Gazette *describes it, because Bell will describe it, and the description will be the verdict's first draft. The rose has a post. She gives it its orders. It is a small ceremony, and she performs it with the gravity it deserves — for this is the season's whole doctrine in miniature: that true things, worn openly, are stronger than false things, set secretly. The rose cannot be forged. No compositor can set it. No customer can order it at double rates. It is the one exhibit in her whole campaign that needs no solicitor, no ledger, no chapel's confession. She pins it — or tucks it, or leaves it — and the choice, once made, feels like the first honest thing she has done all week: not strategy, not evidence, but* wearing. *The flower, the woman, the war — aligned.)*
*Choices (no coin cost; the game remembers):*
- **Pin it to the work apron's strap** — white rose at the press, the clean name among the ink. *(Motif: the rose, worn openly; the compositors will remember it.)*
- **Tuck it behind her ear, under the cap** — the rose half-hidden, the name carried privately. *(Motif: the rose, kept close; Pettifer will notice what the chapel misses.)*
- **Leave it on the campaign book** — the war first, the name after; the rose guards the ledger. *(Motif: the rose, withheld; Augusta will approve the discipline.)*
> **Turns (8):**
