scenes.synopsis: the review — the town watches her watch him; the public performance of loyalty.
scenes.prose:
> *(He answers the question she has not asked — men do that, when the unasked question has been sitting between them long enough — with an ease that surprises them both: the smile, the readiness, the sense of a man stepping forward instead of back. "Ask," he says. "Anything. I am tired of the careful phrasing." So she asks, plainly, the question the week has been circling: what do you want — not what does honor require, not what does the regiment expect, but what do you want. The question lands, and his face does something complicated — relief and alarm, the way a man looks when the saddle slips and the ground is suddenly visible.)*
> *("I want," he says slowly, "to not be asked to want. That has been the comfort of the regiment — the wanting was done for me, once, at seventeen. I signed, and the wanting stopped." The confession, plain — and she hears in it the truest thing he has said all week, the crack in the armor that is not a weakness but a window. "And now?" — Rose. "Now," he says, "I want two things that cannot both be wanted, and I am having to learn wanting the way a child learns Latin — late, and with difficulty." The image makes her laugh — the first laugh of the week that is not armor, and it breaks something open in the room, the air changing.)*
> *("Then learn it aloud," she says. "I am a patient tutor." And he does — haltingly, then faster: he wants the regiment, the agreement, the belonging; and he wants her, the un-uniformed life, the woman who asks plain questions. He wants, he discovers as he speaks, to be the man who can hold both — and the discovery is its own answer, or the beginning of one. She does not help him finish. The wanting, she has learned, is his to learn. She only holds the space for it, the way one holds a horse for a rider mounting: steady, patient, not interfering.)*
> *(He laughs — the Latin image, the child learning late — and the laugh breaks something open in the room, the air changing, the week's armor developing its first honest crack. "Then learn it aloud," she says. She holds the space the way one holds a horse for a rider mounting — steady, patient, not interfering — and the holding is its own discipline: to make room for a man's becoming without directing it. The lesson, learned aloud. The tutor, silent. The wanting, his.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Arrive in the chosen gown — the statement made physical. → Remembered: How the gown performs; the choice from S12 lands in public.
> 2. [social]Feel "every eye doing the arithmetic of loyalty." → Remembered: The town's calculation; she is being summed in public.
> 3. [stance]Watch "openly, without hiding" — the performance of unashamed watching. → Remembered: Her chosen visibility; not hiding is the statement.
> 4. [micro]The colonel's bow — "a fraction deeper than courtesy." → Remembered: The bow's depth measured; she cannot tell if she imagines it.
> 5. [examine]Henry's eye, "for one second" — the drill's only lapse. → Remembered: The second of contact; nothing changes in his face, everything in hers.
> 6. [social]Look away first — the performance becoming real. → Remembered: When watching stops being performance; the turn is involuntary.
> 7. [stance]"Your major" — the wives' currency, and its verdict. → Remembered: The town's decision for them; possession declared by grammar.
> 8. [choice]Answer the wives — accept the possessive, deflect it, or wear it. → Remembered: Her handling of "your major"; the answer is remembered by the town.

scenes.synopsis: after the review — what the public stand has cost, or earned; the second strain.
scenes.prose:
> *(Then she sets out her own terms — not as conditions, she is careful to say, but as the map of the ground she will not surrender: the boundaries drawn before the battle, the way her grandfather drew lines on maps and called them the terms of the engagement. They walk — the long gallery, the portraits watching, the late light through the high windows — and she speaks plainly, because the week has taught her that plainness is the only currency that holds. "If you stand with me," she says, "it must be your standing — not mine borrowed, not the regiment's defied, but yours, chosen. I will not be the reason a man breaks his agreement. I will not carry that." The boundary, stated — the first term, and the hardest.)*
> *("And if I step back?" — Henry. "Then you step back clean," she says. "No reproach, now or ever. I will not be the woman a man resents in the mess at midnight." The second term — and she feels it cost her, the saying of it, the giving of permission she does not want to give. "And the third term," she says, stopping at the window — the portraits, the light, the held breath of the house — "is that you decide. Not the colonel. Not me. Not the whisper in the record. You. That is the only term I will not negotiate." He is quiet a long time — the gallery's hush, the portraits' painted patience. "Those are not terms," he says at last. "Those are gifts." "Then receive them as such," she says, "and do not make me regret the giving.")*
> *(They walk on. The terms sit between them now — not as a wall, but as a foundation: the ground the decision will stand on, whoever makes it, however it falls. She has done what she can. The rest is his.)*
> *(They walk on — the long gallery, the portraits' painted patience, the late light — and the terms sit between them now, not as a wall but as a foundation: the ground the decision will stand on, however it falls. "Those are not terms," he said. "Those are gifts." And she thinks, walking, about the difference: terms are negotiated, gifts are received — and she has given him the one thing the week could not give itself: the freedom to decide without her weight on the scales. The portraits watch. The light holds. She has done what she can. The rest is his — and the his-ness of it, finally, feels like its own kind of mercy.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]The dust on his boots — the drill's residue. → Remembered: The physical trace of the afternoon; discipline made visible.
> 2. [social]"You came" vs. "I watched" — the difference, negotiated. → Remembered: Her correction; coming and watching are different statements.
> 3. [stance]Feel the publicness of the strain — "different from the garden's." → Remembered: How the review moved the strain outdoors; privacy is gone.
> 4. [examine]The colonel's remark — "the regiment's color becomes you." → Remembered: The compliment-warning decoded; the colonel reads gowns.
> 5. [micro]"The regiment's color and I understand each other." → Remembered: Her answer's poise; she meets the warning with manners.
> 6. [social]The unfinished sentence — "the crowd's noise takes it." → Remembered: What the crowd stole; the unsaid multiplies.
> 7. [stance]"A new third walker" — the unfinished sentence walks too. → Remembered: The growing company of unsaids; they accumulate.
> 8. [choice]Lavinia's "Whatever it costs" — accept the accounting. → Remembered: The aunt's final ledger; cost acknowledged in advance.

scenes.synopsis: the legal shape of the whisper — Quill on what revisiting a record actually means.
scenes.prose:
> *(She asks him what honor requires — not as a question, she realizes as she asks it, but as a gift: the one question that does not choose for him, the question that hands the choosing back, clean. The morning room, the day after the terms; he has come early, before the regiment's hour, and the earliness is its own statement — the man, not the major, asking for counsel he will not take as orders. "Tell me what you think honor requires," she says. "Not what I should do. What you think. I will not argue with it." The gift, offered — her judgment, unarmored, for him to use or set aside.)*
> *(He is quiet — the long quiet of a man turning a real question, not the parade-ground quiet of a man awaiting orders. "I think," he says at last, slowly, "that honor requires me to be the man I signed to be — and also the man I have become since. The difficulty is that they are not the same man, and the signing did not foresee the becoming." The formulation, so clean it hurts — the whole week distilled to a single sentence, the way a campaign distills to a single hill. "And if they cannot be reconciled?" — Rose. "Then honor requires me to choose which man I can live with," he says, "and to pay for the choosing. That is the part no one tells you at seventeen: the choosing is free, and the paying is forever.")*
> *(She nods — the gift received, the counsel given, the arguing forsworn. "Then choose the man you can live with," she says, "and I will live with the cost, whatever it is. That is my part." The division of the labor, stated plain: his, the choosing; hers, the living-with. He takes her hand — the second unbudgeted touch of the week — and they sit a moment in the division's quiet. Some counsel is not advice. Some counsel is only company.)*
> *(They sit a moment in the division's quiet — his, the choosing; hers, the living-with — and the quiet teaches her what counsel is when it is not advice: only company, the unarmored judgment offered and left. "Then choose the man you can live with," she said, "and I will live with the cost." The second unbudgeted touch — his hand, holding hers — and the holding says what the week has not: that the living-with is also a choosing, and she has made hers. The morning room's hush. The regiment's hour approaching. He will go to the uniform; she will go to the war. The division holds them both, clean and complete.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]The chambers — "the law's own furniture." → Remembered: The setting's authority; the law speaks from its own room.
> 2. [stance]"A judgment without a proceeding" — the legal shape of the whisper. → Remembered: Quill's definition; the revisiting has no defense.
> 3. [social]Ask the unasked question — could it end his career? → Remembered: That she asked Quill what she would not ask Henry; the asking has its own courage.
> 4. [examine]The bent tree — "the whole growth follows." → Remembered: The metaphor's botany; early bends compound.
> 5. [micro]"The tree grows elsewhere" — Quill's gentler correction. → Remembered: Half-pay, colonial posting — the regiment's forgetting named.
> 6. [stance]Sit very still — the stillness as decision. → Remembered: Her physical response to the price; stillness is also an answer.
> 7. [examine]"Your witness — and his second bending." → Remembered: The trade stated plainly; witness against bending.
> 8. [choice]Decide what to do with the knowledge — tell Henry, or carry it. → Remembered: Whether she shares Quill's arithmetic; the carrying has its own weight.

scenes.synopsis: the bent tree — does she tell him Quill's arithmetic? trust's test.
scenes.prose:
> *(She visits the regiment's chapel — alone, unannounced, the carriage left at the gate — because some questions are asked better in the presence of the regiment's dead than in its drawing rooms. The chapel is small, plain, military: the colors hung, the plaques, the names — the regiment's memory made stone, the ledger that records without summing, carved where no clerk can amend it. She walks the plaques slowly, reading: Spain, the Peninsula, the names of men who believed the ground over the despatch, or the despatch over the ground, and paid either way. The chapel does not judge. The chapel only remembers.)*
> *(She finds what she is not looking for — or what she is, though she would not admit it: the Spanish campaign's plaque, the year of the whisper, the names of the dead from the despatch that said one thing and the ground another. She stands before it a long time. The dead do not advise. That is their mercy and their limit. But standing among them, she understands something about the living: Henry's whisper is not a scandal. It is a casualty — a decision taken too fast in the dark, the kind the chapel's plaques are full of, the kind every officer carries somewhere. The regiment knows this. The regiment's memory is longer than its judgment, and kinder than its letters.)*
> *(She leaves a flower — white, from the chapel's own vase, the clean name's small offering — and walks out into the parade ground's dust and brass. The chapel has not told her what to do. It has told her what the regiment is: not the colonel's letter, but the plaques — the agreement, kept by the dead, for the living. The belonging he described. She understands it now the way one understands a foreign country after visiting its churches: from the inside, briefly, and with respect.)*
> *(She walks out into the parade ground's dust and brass — the chapel's quiet behind her, the regiment's morning music ahead — and the walk gives her what the plaques could not: the understanding, from the inside, briefly, of what the belonging is. Not the colonel's letter — the plaques. Not the warning — the agreement, kept by the dead, for the living. The white flower, left at the Spanish plaque — the clean name's small offering, the living's courtesy to the dead. She understands him now the way one understands a foreign country after visiting its churches: from the inside, briefly, and with respect. And the respect, she knows, is the only ground the choosing can stand on.)*
> **Turns (9):**
> 1. [stance]Decide to tell him — "trust's test is the telling." → Remembered: Her decision to share Quill's arithmetic; the telling is the test.
> 2. [examine]"I know the geography of it" — his prior knowledge. → Remembered: That he already knew; her errand was for herself.
> 3. [social]Feel the foolishness — "of course he knew." → Remembered: Her correction; the sums were his before hers.
> 4. [micro]"You needed to do the sums yourself." → Remembered: His generosity with her learning; he let her arrive.
> 5. [stance]"It is your war too." → Remembered: His naming of her stake; the witness-stand is shared.
> 6. [examine]"Does it change what you want?" — the test, returned. → Remembered: The question's return; she must answer what she asked.
> 7. [choice]"What I want was never the regiment's to price." → Remembered: Her answer's declaration; wanting is not the regiment's jurisdiction.
> 8. [social]His closed eyes — "relief or grief, she cannot tell." → Remembered: The unreadable reaction; some responses stay sealed.
> 9. [stance]"The price is real, and the wanting is realer." → Remembered: The agreement's terms; reality on both sides, wanting ahead.

scenes.synopsis: the wanting, examined — what she wants, priced honestly; the romance's interior.
scenes.prose:
> *(She reviews the week's intelligence — the campaign book open, the entries in plain ink — because the war does not pause for letters, and the review is Thursday, and the trial's date is coming like weather. Quill's clerk brings papers in the afternoon: the libel's trail, the money's new routes, the Network's smile at the watchers. She reads with the general's granddaughter's eye — coldly, completely — and the reading gives her the week's second front: the money has learned to move unseen, but money that moves unseen still moves, and movement is information. She marks the new routes on her private map — the streets, the hours, the hands — the cartography of evasion.)*
> *(the moneylender's man brings nothing, which is itself a report: the watchers watched, the smiled-at, the routes changed again. She does not press him — a network is not hurried, and hurrying breaks the threads. Instead she asks after his family — the boy's cough, the wife's sister — the commander's courtesy, which is also intelligence: men report better to those who remember their lives. He tells her the cough is better. She notes it in the book — not the campaign's business, but the commander's — and he stands a little straighter for the remembering.)*
> *(Then the review's preparations — the gown's fitting Thursday morning, the carriage ordered, the box arranged. The social front, which is also a front. She writes the week's summary in the book — plain ink, the hard truths: "The money evades. The letter is sent. The choice is his. The review is Thursday." Four sentences, the week's whole war. She closes the book and sits a moment in the closing's quiet. Some weeks are for advancing. This week is for holding — the holding, done well, is its own advance.)*
> *(She closes the book — the week's summary, four sentences, the whole war — and sits a moment in the closing's quiet. The money evades. The letter is sent. The choice is his. The review is Thursday. Some weeks are for advancing; this week is for holding — and the holding, done well, is its own advance. The general's granddaughter knows: the battle is not always the attack. Sometimes the battle is the line, held — the discipline of the unasked, the trust that is not the absence of questions, the waiting that is also work. The book is closed. The week is nearly done. The holding, she decides, has been well done.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Audit the wanting — "the sentence deserves an audit." → Remembered: Her self-examination; the declaration is inventoried.
> 2. [stance]Want him as witness — "the uniform's weight on the clean name's side." → Remembered: The strategic wanting; witness has legal value.
> 3. [social]Want the town to see it — "the performance has its uses." → Remembered: The public wanting; visibility is a weapon.
> 4. [micro]Want to be chosen — "the woman worth the second bending." → Remembered: The less noble wanting; vanity admitted honestly.
> 5. [examine]Want to stop wanting — the dangerous wish. → Remembered: The noble release imagined; nobility hated in advance.
> 6. [stance]The drawer of casualties — where wanting goes to be honest. → Remembered: The drawer's second use; honesty filed with casualties.
> 7. [choice]Write to Élise — the trial's first day, planned. → Remembered: The practical turn; wanting will be dressed properly.
> 8. [social]Plan for "a uniform standing beside it." → Remembered: The atelier brief; the uniform is part of the design.

scenes.synopsis: the mess dinner — Henry's world tests her; she is weighed by the regiment.
scenes.prose:
> *(The tailor's bill comes — and with it, the week's most honest arithmetic: the cost of the war in cloth, stated plainly, without the velvet glove. She reads it at her desk, the morning's post still warm: silk, fittings, the rush fee for Thursday's review — the numbers precise, the total considerable. The bill does not flinch, and neither does she. But the bill prompts the accounting she has been postponing: what has the week cost, all told — not in coin, but in the campaign's true currency. She takes out the book and does the sums, the general's granddaughter's sums, coldly and completely.)*
> *(The sitter's cancellation: a small cost, a subtraction from the campaign's manpower — the drawer of casualties, fuller by one. The money's evasion: a larger cost, the intelligence front gone dark — the watchers watched, the smiled-at, the routes redrawn. Henry's letter: the largest cost, and the least countable — the week's whole question, priced in a man's career, carried by the man himself, unshared by design. She totals nothing — the vow holds, even in accounting — but she notes the costs, each in plain ink, each without flinching. The book is honest. The book must be.)*
> *(Then she pays the tailor's bill — the coin counted, the receipt filed — and the paying steadies her: some costs are countable, and the countable ones can be met. It is the uncountable ones — the career, the whisper, the choosing — that keep her up in the small hours. But the book is closed now, the bills are paid, the review is Thursday. The week's arithmetic is done. Whatever Thursday brings, it will find the accounts in order.)*
> *(The receipt, filed — the coin counted, the tailor paid — and the paying steadies her the way the list-making steadied her: some costs are countable, and the countable ones can be met. It is the uncountable ones that keep her up — the career, the whisper, the choosing — the week's true currency, priced in a man's becoming. But the book is honest, the bills are paid, the review is Thursday, and the arithmetic is done. Whatever Thursday brings — the colonel, the regiment, the town's opera glasses — it will find the accounts in order. The general's rule, kept to the last: meet the weather with the books balanced.)*
> **Turns (9):**
> 1. [examine]The invitation — "a courtesy" that "lands as a test." → Remembered: The card's double nature; courtesy is the test's uniform.
> 2. [stance]Lavinia "dresses her like a campaign." → Remembered: The aunt's preparation; the mess is a battlefield.
> 3. [social]"Perfect manners and total attention." → Remembered: The mess's reception; manners are the examination room.
> 4. [micro]The lieutenant's question — "very alarming," three glasses in. → Remembered: The young officer's bluntness; drink loosens the careful.
> 5. [examine]Answer "with the ease of a general's granddaughter." → Remembered: Her deployment of heritage; the General's granddaughter answers.
> 6. [stance]"A regiment is an agreement" — Henry's phrase, in her mouth. → Remembered: The borrowing made public; the phrase is now theirs.
> 7. [social]The colonel's paused glass — the phrase, recognized. → Remembered: The colonel's recognition; he hears his major in her.
> 8. [micro]"To agreements" — the toast, and the table's quiet. → Remembered: The colonel's toast; agreement toasted by the agreement's keepers.
> 9. [choice]"Passed — or been passed." → Remembered: Her uncertainty about the verdict; passing and being-passed differ.

scenes.synopsis: the drive home — what the mess dinner proved, and to whom.
scenes.prose:
> *(She writes to her solicitor — not Quill, the campaign's lawyer, but the family's, the steady man who has handled the estate's dullest business for twenty years — with a question the week has raised and the campaign book cannot answer: what is the legal shape of a man's standing, when the standing is beside a woman in a controversy? The letter is careful, lawyerly, the question phrased three ways — the way one phrases a question whose answer one fears. She seals it herself. Some inquiries are not for clerks.)*
> *(While the ink dries, she thinks about the law — the war's other front, the one the regiment's letter invoked without naming. The Horse Guards' warning was not legal; it was worse, it was customary — the regiment's memory, the mess's judgment, the slow unmaking that no court orders and no appeal reverses. The law, at least, has rules. Custom has only weather. She prefers rules. Rules can be studied, navigated, turned. Weather can only be endured.)*
> *(The solicitor's reply will take days — the post, the consideration, the careful phrasing. She does not need it by Thursday; the review is social, not legal. But the trial's date is coming like weather, and she wants the legal ground surveyed before the storm. She files the copy of her letter in the campaign book — the book keeps everything now, the honest and the fearful alike — and rings for tea. The law moves slowly. So, she is learning, does honor. The week's lesson, restated: some things cannot be hurried, and hurrying breaks them.)*
> *(She files the copy — the campaign book, the honest and the fearful alike — and rings for tea. The law moves slowly. So, she is learning, does honor. The week's lesson, restated once more, the way the important lessons are restated until they hold: some things cannot be hurried, and hurrying breaks them. The solicitor will reply in days. The trial's date is coming like weather. The choosing must land before the courtroom. And she — she will wait, the way she has waited all week: plainly, patiently, the plainness the only currency that holds. The tea comes. The ink dries. The law, like honor, takes its time.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]"I quoted us" — the correction. → Remembered: The agreement's joint ownership; "us" replaces "me."
> 2. [social]"You moved it" — the examination, reversed. → Remembered: His reading of the evening; she examined the examiners.
> 3. [stance]The colonel's adoption — phrasing as position. → Remembered: How toasts become territory; language is ground.
> 4. [micro]"Both. That is what colonels do." → Remembered: His professional realism; adoption and disarmament together.
> 5. [examine]The first easy laugh "in a week." → Remembered: The laugh's rarity; ease measured in weeks.
> 6. [choice]"Not tonight" — the letter, postponed. → Remembered: Her deferral; the agreements hold the night.
> 7. [social]The lamplit streets — "the town's candles going out one by one." → Remembered: The drive's ending image; candles out, letter still unfinished.

scenes.synopsis: the chapter's dressing ritual — the courtroom's argument, made in cloth. (Turns: 21 — the direction + twenty 5-coin pins)
scenes.prose:
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The libel trial opens Thursday next, and the town will read her before the court hears her. The gown is the first witness. This is not a ball and not a rout — it is the season's most formal proceeding, and the dressing must be irreproachable, armored, and entirely her own."
> **Direction:** the courtroom's gown. The occasion is formal beyond fashion — the law's theater, the town's opera glasses, the regiment's own ground. The direction is chosen first, and the twenty pins follow the direction. Three readings of the same brief; one will be hers. The ritual is long — the gown's whole argument, decided piece by piece — and the length is the point: the trial will be read before it is heard, and the reading must be managed.
> **A. The Clean Name** — white and silver, the libel's opposite. Motif: white roses, embroidered, not appliquéd — the clean name worked into the cloth itself, the flower's language spoken in thread. Thread: silver (the name, stated) / ivory whitework (the name, lit) / pale gold (the name, gilded). Colorway: white silk, dove silk, silver tissue. Accessories: the clean name's pearls; white kid gloves; a white ribbon at the throat; silk slippers; the ivory fan.
> **B. The General's Granddaughter** — military echoes, the agreement's livery. Motif: frogging and braid, the regiment's language spoken in silk — the granddaughter's inheritance, not the major's uniform, the discipline quoted without the disobedience. Thread: silver cord (the discipline) / steel-grey silk (the record) / gold cord (the command). Colorway: dove grey, regiment blue, silver. Accessories: the gold locket, not the pearls; grey kid gloves; a sash at the waist, not a ribbon; sensible half-boots; the grey fan.
> **C. The Woman Beside the Uniform** — blue and gold, the stand made visible. Motif: oak leaves and acorns, the English strength — the woman who stands, worked in gold thread, the courage's own botany. Thread: gold (the stand, declared) / copper (the stand, warmed) / bronze silk (the stand, aged well). Colorway: deep sapphire silk, gold, ivory. Accessories: the gold locket; blue kid gloves; a gold chain at the waist; silk slippers; the painted fan.
> **Decomposed steps:** twenty pins, five coins each — the gown's whole argument, decided piece by piece. Re-picks are free, now and after — the atelier keeps every combination, and the choosing can be revisited without cost. No Crowns touch this ritual; the dressing is the player's own, bought with play.
> 1. [choice]**Direction — the commitment:** A, B, or C — the courtroom's reading, chosen first, the pins to follow. → Remembered: the direction; the town will read the gown before the court hears her.
> 2. [micro]**Pin 1 — the bodice's cut:** high and modest, the trial's line; or lower, the season's. 5 coins. → Remembered: the neckline's argument; the court reads modesty as confidence.
> 3. [micro]**Pin 2 — the sleeves:** long and plain, the working woman; or the season's lace. 5 coins. → Remembered: the arm's statement; plain sleeves say the work, not the ornament.
> 4. [micro]**Pin 3 — the neckline's finish:** a collar, a ruffle, bare. 5 coins. → Remembered: the throat's framing; the collar is armor, the ruffle is invitation.
> *(Story morsel: Élise pins the bodice and tells her — the atelier's own intelligence — that the colonel's wife ordered the same silk last week, in the same white. "I talked her into the grey," Élise says, the pins in her mouth. "The town cannot have two clean names.")*
> 5. [micro]**Pin 4 — the skirt's fullness:** the courtroom's sweep; or the ballroom's. 5 coins. → Remembered: the skirt's logic; the sweep commands the room, the ballroom concedes it.
> 6. [micro]**Pin 5 — the waist's emphasis:** sashed, corseted plain, natural. 5 coins. → Remembered: the waist's line; the sash is the direction's signature.
> 7. [micro]**Pin 6 — the fabric's weight:** the silk that holds a line; or the muslin that yields. 5 coins. → Remembered: the cloth's discipline; the trial's gown does not yield.
> 8. [micro]**Pin 7 — the hem's length:** the street's practical; or the train's drama. 5 coins. → Remembered: the hem's arithmetic; drama is for entrances, sense for exits.
> *(Story morsel: the second fitting — the silk half-made, the argument half-spoken — and Rose catches her reflection between the mirrors: the woman the review proved, cut for the courtroom. "The trial will read you before it hears you," Élise says. "Make the reading worth the ink.")*
> 9. [micro]**Pin 8 — the closure:** buttons up the back, the long line; or the side's convenience. 5 coins. → Remembered: the back's honesty; the long line of buttons is the gown's spine.
> 10. [micro]**Pin 9 — the color's depth:** the saturated; or the pale. 5 coins. → Remembered: the color's courage; saturation is a statement, pallor a question.
> 11. [micro]**Pin 10 — the trim's metal:** gold, silver, none. 5 coins. → Remembered: the trim's allegiance; metal is the direction's punctuation.
> 12. [micro]**Pin 11 — the embroidery's density:** the heavily worked; or the plainly cut. 5 coins. → Remembered: the needle's rhetoric; density persuades, plainness declares.
> *(Story morsel: Élise's girl brings the thread cards — the whole library, gold to steel to ivory whitework — and Rose holds each to the silk, watching the argument change with the metal. "The thread is the sentence," Élise says. "The silk is only the paragraph.")*
> 13. [micro]**Pin 12 — the glove's length:** the opera's; or the wrist's. 5 coins. → Remembered: the hand's formality; the opera glove is the courtroom's own.
> 14. [micro]**Pin 13 — the shoe:** the slipper's delicacy; or the boot's sense. 5 coins. → Remembered: the foot's pragmatism; the trial is long, the standing longer.
> 15. [micro]**Pin 14 — the hair:** the dressed; or the simple. 5 coins. → Remembered: the head's composure; dressed hair is the gown's roof.
> 16. [micro]**Pin 15 — the corsage:** fresh flowers at the shoulder — white rosebuds, camellias, or none. 5 coins. → Remembered: the shoulder's botany; the white rosebuds, the clean name's language.
> *(Story morsel: the locket — the gold one, the grandmother's — and Rose holds it against each silk in turn. Against the white it is the past, witnessing. Against the grey it is the inheritance, quoted. Against the blue it is the stand, declared. "The jewel," Élise says, "is the only pin that remembers you back.")*
> 17. [micro]**Pin 16 — the fan:** the carried; or the left. 5 coins. → Remembered: the hand's occupation; the fan is the courtroom's punctuation.
> 18. [micro]**Pin 17 — the shawl:** the wrap's modesty; or the bare shoulder's nerve. 5 coins. → Remembered: the shoulder's answer; modesty is armor, nerve is argument.
> 19. [micro]**Pin 18 — the scent:** the worn; or the none. 5 coins. → Remembered: the air's testimony; scent is the witness no one cross-examines.
> 20. [micro]**Pin 19 — the entrance:** the early; or the late. 5 coins. → Remembered: the arrival's timing; early is confidence, late is theater.
> 21. [micro]**Pin 20 — the first impression's weapon:** the smile; or the stillness. 5 coins. → Remembered: the face's opening statement; the smile disarms, the stillness commands.
> *(Reveal coda: the gown, complete — the twenty pins, the direction, the whole argument made cloth. Élise steps back, the mirrors' tribunal, and the woman in the silk looks back: certain, upright, unafraid. "The court will read you before it hears you," Élise says. "Let the reading be the truth." The reveal is staged — the atelier's mirrors, the silk's hush — and the gown is hers, pin by pin, choice by choice.)*
> **Jewels (owned pieces only):** the jewel shelf is open for browsing — the pieces she owns, each with its history: the gold locket, the grandmother's; the clean name's pearls; the silver brooch, the season's first. But no jewel is a ritual step; the pins decide the gown, and the jewels only attend it. Re-picks are free, and post-scene re-styling is always free — the atelier keeps every combination.

ritual.occasionBrief: A review morning beside a uniform — loyalty, decided in the open.

scenes.synopsis: the ritual's aftermath — he sees the trial gown; the uniform beside the clean name.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette comes — and with it, the week's public weather: Bell's editorial, the proprietor's own hand, the paper's judgment on the season so far. She reads it at breakfast, the coffee going cold — the editorial is not about her, not directly, which is its own statement: the Gazette does not chase the Hartwell war, it judges it, the way a magistrate judges without joining the fray. The editorial's subject is the town's appetite — for scandal, for ruin, for the spectacle of a woman fighting — and the judgment is dry, precise, faintly weary: the town, Bell writes, has mistaken the war for entertainment, and entertainment for justice.)*
> *(She reads it twice — the second reading for the subtext, the way one reads Bell: for what the proprietor does not say. What Bell does not say: who will win. What Bell does not say: whether the fighting is right. What Bell says instead: that the fighting is real, and the town would do well to remember the difference between watching and witnessing. The distinction lands — watching is the opera glass, witnessing is the chapel plaque — and she sits with it long after the coffee is cold. The Gazette is not her ally. The Gazette is her judge. The difference matters, and she respects it.)*
> *(She clips the editorial — the campaign book's press file, the war's public record — and writes beneath it, in plain ink: "The town watches. The Gazette witnesses. I must be worth witnessing." The sentence steadies her — the week's standard, stated. The editorial has not told her what to do. It has told her how she will be read. The reading, she decides, will be worth the ink.)*
> *(The sentence steadies her — "I must be worth witnessing" — the week's standard, stated in plain ink beneath the clipped editorial. The Gazette is not her ally; the Gazette is her judge — and the difference, respected, becomes its own discipline: to be worth the ink, not to court it. She thinks of Bell — the proprietor's dry hand, the faint weariness — and understands the editorial's true subject: not her war, but the town's appetite, mistaken for justice. The town watches. The Gazette witnesses. She will be witnessed — the fighting real, the distinction held, the ink earned. The coffee is cold. The standard is warm.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]His stop in the doorway — "It is not a sentence." → Remembered: The inarticulateness; the gown defeats grammar.
> 2. [social]The white roses catching the light — the turn, timed. → Remembered: How the reveal lands on him; light does the arguing.
> 3. [stance]"The uniform will look very plain beside that." → Remembered: His honest vanity; even majors measure.
> 4. [micro]"Like the agreement" — her correction. → Remembered: The uniform redefined again; agreement, not ornament.
> 5. [examine]"Thursday I stand where I can see you" — the partial answer. → Remembered: The distinction between letter and Thursday; the visible part promised.
> 6. [social]Accept the distinction — "the letter governs the war; Thursday governs the day." → Remembered: Her acceptance; days are winnable even when wars aren't.
> 7. [choice]"What loyalty looks like when it is dressed." → Remembered: The Thursday thesis; loyalty will be visible.
> 8. [stance]The week's second easy laugh — morale, measured. → Remembered: The gown's effect on morale; fashion as logistics.

scenes.synopsis: the trial's shape — Quill briefs the first day; where Henry would stand.
scenes.prose:
> *(The atelier sends word — the gown is ready for its final fitting, and the message comes with Élise's own card, the atelier's courtesy for a client the season is watching. She goes in the afternoon, the review tomorrow, the fitting's hour private — the rooms above the shop, the mirrors, the silk's hush. The gown waits on the form — and the first sight of it stops her, the way a completed argument stops a debater: the silk, the line, the whole statement made cloth. It is not a gown. It is a position.)*
> *(Élise fusses — the hem, the shoulder, the final adjustments, the pins like a constellation — and Rose stands in the mirrors' tribunal, watching herself become the woman the review requires. The fitting is long — the silk must sit, must move, must speak — and in the fitting's pauses she thinks about Thursday: the drill square, the boxes, the opera glasses, the colonel's party. The gown will be read by all of them. The reading is the point. She watches the mirrors and practices the reading — the entrance, the posture, the face that says: I am not afraid of your uniform.)*
> *(Then the accessories — the gloves, the fan, the small choices that complete the argument — and Élise steps back, the artist's appraisal, and nods: the nod of a woman who has dressed a position before and knows one when she sees it. Rose looks at herself — the mirrors' full tribunal — and the woman in the silk looks back, certain, upright, unafraid. The gown is ready. The woman, she decides, is nearly ready. Thursday will complete the fitting.)*
> *(The nod — Élise's, the artist's appraisal — and the woman in the mirrors looks back: certain, upright, unafraid. The gown is not a gown; it is a position — the week's whole argument, made cloth. She thinks of Thursday — the drill square, the boxes, the opera glasses, the colonel's party — and the thinking does not frighten her now; the rehearsal is complete, the ground surveyed, the posture practiced. The accessories — the gloves, the fan, the small completions — and the assembly is done. The gown is ready. The woman is nearly ready. Thursday will complete the fitting — and the fitting, she knows, is also the proving.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]The battle plan — "laid out like a battle plan." → Remembered: Her recognition; the trial is war by other means.
> 2. [stance]The printer testifies "to the copy — not the authorship." → Remembered: The testimony's limit; copy, not authorship, is the wedge.
> 3. [social]"If we are fortunate" — the money man's fragility. → Remembered: The Network witness's uncertainty; fortune does heavy work.
> 4. [micro]"Major Beaumont — the rank is the point." → Remembered: Quill's correction; the uniform testifies, not the man.
> 5. [examine]"The single most valuable... the single most expensive." → Remembered: The testimony's double ledger; value and expense coincide.
> 6. [stance]"Both seeings are true." → Remembered: Quill's binocular truth; court and regiment see differently, both truly.
> 7. [social]Thursday next — the date, announced. → Remembered: The trial's first day fixed; the gallery will fill.
> 8. [choice]Decide how to tell Henry — the date, the box, the cost. → Remembered: Her plan for the telling; the witness-stand described honestly.

scenes.synopsis: the witness box, described — what standing would mean, in Quill's plain terms.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks the review's ground — the drill square, the boxes, the approaches — because her grandfather walked every battlefield before the battle, and the habit is deeper than memory. The evening before, the square empty, the light going gold; she walks it alone, the carriage left at the gate, her boots on the gravel the only sound. The boxes: she notes which faces which way, which catches the light, which the colonel's party will take — the social topography, mapped like terrain. The approaches: the carriage's route, the entrance's sightlines, the first step into the crowd's view — the moment the gown will be read, choreographed in advance.)*
> *(The drill square itself: the dust, the brass polish still in the air, the regiment's morning music lingering like a scent. She stands where the watchers stood — the rail, the wives and idlers — and then where she will stand tomorrow: the box, the elevated, the seen. The difference between the two positions is the whole week: to watch, or to be watched; to witness, or to be witnessed. She stands in the box a long time, the gold light, the empty square — rehearsing, not the words (there are no words tomorrow, only presence), but the posture: the certain, the upright, the unafraid.)*
> *(She leaves as the light goes — the square empty again, the rehearsal complete. The ground has no surprises left. Whatever Thursday brings — the colonel, the regiment, the town's opera glasses — it will find her on surveyed ground. Her grandfather's rule, kept: walk it before they do.)*
> *(She leaves as the light goes — the square empty again, the rehearsal complete — and the walk home gives her the evening's clearest thought: her grandfather walked every battlefield before the battle, and the habit was not caution but courtesy — to the ground, to the men, to the decision. The boxes, mapped. The approaches, choreographed. The sightlines, known. Whatever Thursday brings — the colonel, the regiment, the town — it will find her on surveyed ground. The carriage. The dusk. The gold light fading. The ground, she thinks, has no surprises left — and the no-surprises, kept properly, is its own kind of courage.)*
> *(The survey, complete — the ground, the light, the approaches — and the completeness itself the evening’s reward: the battle, walked before it is fought.)*
> **Turns (9):**
> 1. [examine]"A witness to character" — the box's true function. → Remembered: What the testimony actually is; character, not libel.
> 2. [stance]"Both seeings are true" — Quill's truth, delivered. → Remembered: Her honesty with the double seeing; she does not soften it.
> 3. [social]The indoor middle distance — the window, the discipline. → Remembered: His retreat to the soldier's gaze; windows are for looking away.
> 4. [micro]The unfinished "his — " — the mess's word, unspoken. → Remembered: What the mess would call it; the word stays unspoken, which is worse.
> 5. [examine]"The box is only the letter, made visible." → Remembered: Her framing; the box adds no new choice, only visibility.
> 6. [stance]"I will not ask you to the box." → Remembered: The second refusal to choose for him; the dusk choice stands.
> 7. [choice]"If the letter says stand" — the Thursday promise. → Remembered: The visible stand, conditional on the letter.
> 8. [social]"Standing alone" — the alternative Thursday. → Remembered: Her readiness to stand alone; the clean name needs no uniform.
> 9. [micro]The nod, slow — his acceptance of both Thursdays. → Remembered: That he accepted both outcomes; the nod is the answer's shadow.

scenes.synopsis: the two Thursdays — she prepares for both; the general's discipline.
scenes.prose:
> *(The night before the review, she does not sleep — not from fear, she tells herself, but from the week's fullness: the letter, the terms, the gown, the ground, all of it turning in the dark like the silk on Élise's form. She gets up — the house asleep, the hour small — and goes to the morning room, the campaign book, the plain ink. The book gets the week's last entry before the review: "Tomorrow I am seen. The gown is the argument. The woman must be the proof." She underlines nothing. The plain ink is enough.)*
> *(She thinks about Henry — the letter sent, the choice made, the waiting his — and the thinking is not anxious, only attentive: the way one attends to a far-off weather, the storm on the horizon that may or may not come. She thinks about the regiment — the agreement, the belonging, the plaques — and understands, in the night's clarity, what she could not in the day's busyness: she is not fighting the regiment. She is fighting for the man inside it to be allowed to choose. The distinction matters. The distinction is the whole war.)*
> *(She goes to the window — the street empty, the lamps lit, the town asleep — and stands a long time in the night's quiet. The review is tomorrow. The trial's date is coming like weather. The letter is sent. She has done what she can. The rest — the choosing, the waiting, the Thursday — belongs to the morning. She goes back to bed and sleeps — not well, but the sleep of a general before a battle: the rest that is also readiness.)*
> The week's fullness turns in the dark — the letter, the terms, the gown, the ground — and the turning, finally, stills: the campaign book's last entry, plain ink, no underlining — "Tomorrow I am seen." The gown is the argument. The woman must be the proof. The distinction — the regiment's, the agreement's — sits with her in the dark, no longer frightening: she is not fighting the regiment. She is fighting for the man inside it to choose. The sleep comes. The readiness holds. The morning will do the rest.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Plan for the worst, dress for the best — the discipline. → Remembered: The General's doctrine applied; two Thursdays, both prepared.
> 2. [stance]Thursday the uniform — the visible agreement. → Remembered: The with-Thursday's staging; the box as theatre.
> 3. [social]Thursday alone — "the clean name, sufficient." → Remembered: The alone-Thursday's sufficiency; no uniform needed.
> 4. [micro]The side-by-side entries — "in plain ink." → Remembered: The book's two columns; plainness for hard truths.
> 5. [examine]"I will not love him less. I will love him differently." → Remembered: The drawer's hardest entry; love's revision, pre-written.
> 6. [stance]"The way one loves a soldier." → Remembered: Her definition of the different love; the agreement over the woman.
> 7. [choice]Close the book — the preparing, assigned. → Remembered: The division reaffirmed; waiting his, preparing hers.
> 8. [social]Count the days — the letter before Thursday. → Remembered: The timeline's order; the answer precedes the day.

scenes.synopsis: Pyke watches the review — the printer's sly read of the uniform's stand; no threats, only print.
scenes.prose:
> *(The review's morning: the gown, the gloves, the fan — the argument assembled, piece by piece, the way a soldier assembles his kit. her maid dresses her — the silk's hush, the pins' constellation, the mirrors' tribunal — and the woman in the mirrors is the week's whole work: certain, upright, unafraid. The carriage comes. The square waits. She goes — not to the rail, where the watchers stand, but to the box, the elevated, the seen — the position rehearsed in the gold light, the ground surveyed, the posture practiced.)*
> *(The drill begins — dust, brass, men made into a single instrument — and she watches the way she watched from the rail, but differently now: from the box, the seen, the gown speaking before she does. The opera glasses find her — she feels them, the town's reading, the Gazette's future ink — and the feeling does not unmake her. The gown holds. The posture holds. The woman holds. He is on horseback at the flank — the uniform, the man inside it, the week's whole question made flesh — and for the drill's length there is no letter, no whisper, no choosing. Only the work, and the man inside it, clean.)*
> *(After — the colonel's party, the boxes emptying, the social maneuvers — she is approached, congratulated, read. The readings vary — the gossips, the wives, the officers — but the gown's argument lands: she is not afraid of the uniform. She leaves before the maneuvering curdles — to stay too long would be a different statement, and this statement is complete. The carriage home. The gown hung. The review, survived — no, more than survived: stated.)*
> *(The carriage home — the gown hung, the gloves folded, the fan closed — and the ride gives her the day's accounting: the gown spoke, the woman held, the regiment saw. The opera glasses found her; the feeling did not unmake her. He was on horseback at the flank — the week's whole question, made flesh — and for the drill's length there was no letter, no whisper, no choosing. She leaves before the maneuvering curdles — the statement, complete — and the completeness steadies her: the review, survived; no, stated. The position, made. The town, the regiment, the colonel's party — all of them, read.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Pyke's reading — "the regiment in her pocket." → Remembered: The printer's interpretation; the stand read as capture.
> 2. [stance]"We shall see which" — the pocket's ambiguity. → Remembered: His sly even-handedness; either reading serves.
> 3. [social]The juxtaposition — "innocent as lambs." → Remembered: His method; paragraphs side by side, no accusation.
> 4. [micro]"Print suggests." → Remembered: The doctrine; suggestion outsources the threat to the reader.
> 5. [examine]"Where no lawyer can follow." → Remembered: His legal education; the mind is libel-proof.
> 6. [stance]Thursday next — the trial's first day, in his calendar. → Remembered: The printer's timeline; the town reads twice before.
> 7. [choice]"Either way, we print the picture." → Remembered: His readiness for both Thursdays; the picture prints regardless.

scenes.synopsis: the whisper, in the town — what the review's reports have started; the old story, refreshed.
scenes.prose:
> *(After the review, the reckoning — not the public kind, the private: the campaign book, the plain ink, the week's true accounting. She sits at her desk — the gown hung, the gloves folded, the fan closed — and writes the review's entry: "The gown spoke. The woman held. The regiment saw." Three sentences, the day's whole war. Then the reckoning's harder part: what did the review cost, and what did it buy — the general's granddaughter's sums, done in the evening's quiet.)*
> *(The cost: the town's reading, which is also the town's judgment — the opera glasses, the Gazette's future ink, the colonel's party's careful courtesy. She was seen, and being seen is a cost — the seen can be judged, the witnessed can be weighed. The purchase: the statement, made — I am not afraid of your uniform — delivered to the regiment's own ground, in the regiment's own sightlines. The purchase is real. The cost is real. The arithmetic, for once, balances.)*
> *(Then the week's larger reckoning — the letter, the terms, the choosing — and here the book is honest: the choosing is his, the waiting is his, the cost is his. She has done what she can — the terms, the gift, the division of the labor. The rest is the waiting, and the waiting is its own work: the discipline of the unasked, the trust that is not the absence of questions. She closes the book. The review is done. The week is nearly done. The trial's date is coming like weather — and the weather, she is learning, can be met.)*
> *(She closes the book — the review's entry, three sentences, the day's whole war — and the closing's quiet teaches her the week's hardest arithmetic: the cost is real, the purchase is real, and for once they balance. The town's reading, the Gazette's future ink, the colonel's careful courtesy — the cost of being seen. The statement, made — I am not afraid of your uniform — delivered to the regiment's own ground — the purchase. And the larger reckoning — the choosing, his; the waiting, his; the cost, his — the division of the labor, kept. The book is closed. The review is done. The weather, she is learning, can be met.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]The musicale's murmur — "much discussed," "a sad business." → Remembered: The whisper's refreshed wording; the town's euphemisms.
> 2. [social]Lavinia's fan — "snapping shut like a pistol." → Remembered: The aunt's alarm; the fan is her early warning.
> 3. [stance]"Twice-told" — the whisper's age, and its weakness. → Remembered: Lavinia's assessment; old whispers starve without feeding.
> 4. [micro]"Someone is feeding it" — the Gazette's juxtapositions. → Remembered: Her identification of the feeder; print suggests, town infers.
> 5. [examine]"Out-dress it" — Lavinia's doctrine. → Remembered: The counter-strategy; pictures beat whispers.
> 6. [social]"A whisper is only a story without a picture." → Remembered: The aunt's epigram; Thursday is the better picture.
> 7. [choice]"The picture or the frame" — Henry's role, posed. → Remembered: Lavinia's question for him; picture or frame.
> 8. [stance]The carriage's turn — the decision, carried home. → Remembered: The doctrine accepted; Thursday becomes the answer.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — THE WHISPER. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Pyke's Thursday edition lies on the table between them — folded open, the way one lays out evidence, or a weapon. The whisper is there, and not there: no accusation, nothing actionable, only a paragraph about the trial that mentions Spain the way a man mentions a loaded pistol on the mantel — in passing, for the atmosphere. Sly, never overt; that is his whole method, and the method is the menace. Beside the paper lie her own weapons, should she choose them: the General's records, Spain's despatches, the truth in her own hands — the despatch's date, the General's hand in the margin, the refutation ready, documented, printable, the pages gone soft at the corners from her reading. The paper and the papers: the town's version, and the true one.)*
> *(She thinks of the chapel — the plaques, the names, the regiment's memory made stone — and of what he told her in the amber hour: the agreement, the belonging, the once in Spain. The whisper is his record, his regiment, his fight — or it is theirs, the war's, the woman's beside him. Lavinia's doctrine arrives in Lavinia's own voice — the aunt's dry certainty, heard as clearly as if she stood in the room: "Starve it, my dear. A whisper fed with refutation becomes a conversation, and a conversation becomes the story." The champion's doctrine says fight it for him: the truth, printed where the town reads. The comrade's says stand beside, not before. Three doctrines. The trial's eve. The whisper, waiting to be answered — or not.)*
> *(He has been silent through the laying-out — the soldier's silence, which is never empty, only ordered. Now he touches the Thursday edition with one finger, the way one touches something unclean, and says: "If you fight it for me, the town will remember the lady, not the refutation. If I fight it, the mess will remember the fight, not the truth." The honesty steadies her: he has done the same sums, in his own coin. "And if we starve it?" she asks. "Then Thursday decides," he says, "and we live with Thursday." The three doctrines narrow to the room's true question — not whose fight, but what each fighting buys, and at whose expense. The refutation's pages are soft at the corners. The pistol on the mantel stays mentioned. The trial's eve holds its breath.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — the whisper:*
- **Fight it for him** — *Henry+; the champion.* Rose takes the whisper's refutation into her own hands — the General's records, Spain's despatches, the truth printed where the town reads. *(He is defended — and diminished; a major defended by his lady.)*
- **Let him fight it** — *Standing+; the comrade.* Rose refuses to fight his battle — the whisper is his record, his regiment, his fight; she stands beside, not before. *(He is respected — and alone in it; the fight is honorable and solitary.)*
- **Ignore it** — *The whisper starves.* Rose and Henry agree to starve it together — no refutation, no engagement, only Thursday's better picture. *(Lavinia's doctrine; the whisper dies unfed — if it dies.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the champion, the comrade, the starved whisper. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: after the whisper decision — the tired man's gratitude, or the comrade's pact.
scenes.prose:
> *(The trial's date is set — the news comes by Quill's clerk in the morning, the paper formal, the date like a stone dropped in still water. She reads it standing — some news one meets upright — and the standing is its own answer. The date is nearer than she hoped, farther than she feared — the law's own arithmetic, neither kind nor cruel, only scheduled. She puts the paper in the campaign book — the war's calendar, the countdown begun — and does the first thing the date requires: she breathes.)*
> *(Then the preparations — the practical, the scheduled, the safe: Quill's brief to review, the witnesses to confirm, the gown for the courtroom to commission — because the trial, like the review, will be read before it is heard, and the reading must be managed. She makes the lists — the general's granddaughter's lists, cold and complete — and the list-making steadies her: the date is a fact, and facts can be met. The fear is not a fact. The fear is weather.)*
> *(She thinks about Henry — the letter sent, the choice made, the waiting nearly over — and the date's setting changes the waiting's shape: no longer indefinite, but bounded — the choosing must land before the trial, the standing must be decided before the courtroom. The boundedness is almost a mercy. She writes in the book — plain ink, for the hard truths: "The date is set. The choosing must land. I will not hurry it, and I will not fear it." The entry steadies her. The date is coming like weather. The weather can be met.)*
> *(The entry steadies her — "I will not hurry it, and I will not fear it" — the plain ink, the hard truth, the week's discipline restated for the trial's countdown. The date is a fact; facts can be met. The fear is weather; weather can only be endured — or met, the way she has met it all week: plainly, patiently, the plainness the only currency that holds. The choosing must land before the courtroom — the boundedness, almost a mercy. No longer indefinite. Only imminent. She breathes — the first thing the date requires — and the breathing steadies her: the fact, met; the weather, watched; the choosing, awaited. The countdown, begun.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]The lifted fraction — "a carried weight shifts." → Remembered: The decision's physical relief; choosing lightens.
> 2. [social]"Thank you" — gratitude covering both. → Remembered: His thanks; it covers choosing and refusing alike.
> 3. [stance]The garden again — "the house's ears avoided." → Remembered: Their council chamber; the garden holds the war's talk.
> 4. [micro]Quill's "bleak sense of fortune." → Remembered: The lawyer's fortune; bleakness as professional habit.
> 5. [examine]"Loyalty is not the absence of cost." → Remembered: His definition; the week's tuition, summarized.
> 6. [social]"The presence of something worth the cost." → Remembered: The definition's second half; worth is the point.
> 7. [choice]The fourth walker — "the said, at last." → Remembered: The unsaid joined by the said; openness walks between them.

scenes.synopsis: the letter's answer approaches — the night before; what is said when nothing can be done.
scenes.prose:
> *(He comes at dusk — the night before, when nothing can be done and everything must be borne — and lays the truth on the table before the candles are lit: "There was ever only one letter." The revision, plain: the second draft was the road not taken, and he kept it — visible, unburned, the honesty of a man who will not pretend the other road never tempted him. She reads both, the sent and the unsent, and understands the keeping: decided does not mean untried.)*
> *("We do not wait," she says — the night's doctrine, her refusal of suspense as a posture. The night before has its own work, and they will do it: not the letter's work, for that is done, but the night's. He nods, and tells her what generals do the night before a battle. "The general walks the lines." The ritual of command: through the camp in the dark, past the sleeping men and the pickets, letting himself be seen.)*
> *("So the men see him unafraid," she says — the walk's purpose; visibility, not change. Nothing is altered by the walking, and everything is steadied by it. "Are you unafraid?" she asks Henry, plainly, because the night before deserves plain questions. "No," he says. "But I am decided." She hears it as the truest sentence of the week: decided is better than unafraid — fear is weather, and decision is ground.)*
> *(They dine — Letitia's best, the candles lit early, the deliberate normalcy of a household refusing to perform dread. The conversation keeps its boundary the way a garden keeps its wall: everything but the letter — the regiment's gossip, the cook's triumph with the joint, the absurd hat at the review, the price of white roses. The letter is not dined with. It sits in the study, both roads of it, and the night goes on around it, undefeated.)*
> *(Afterward, at the door, she does not only watch him go. "The general's granddaughter walks the lines," she says — and takes up the ritual as her own: through the house in the candlelight, past the doors kept and the staff at their posts, letting herself be seen — unafraid, or if not unafraid, decided, which is better. The house holds. The lines are walked. The night before has done its work.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]"There was ever only one letter." → Remembered: His revision; the second was the road not taken, kept visible.
> 2. [stance]"We do not wait" — the night's doctrine. → Remembered: Her refusal of waiting; the night before has its own work.
> 3. [social]"The general walks the lines." → Remembered: His metaphor; the night-before ritual of command.
> 4. [micro]"So the men see him unafraid." → Remembered: The walk's purpose; visibility, not change.
> 5. [examine]"No. But I am decided." → Remembered: The plain answer; decided is better than unafraid.
> 6. [stance]Dine — "Letitia's best, the candles lit early." → Remembered: The dinner's deliberate normalcy; candles against the unknown.
> 7. [social]Talk of everything but the letter. → Remembered: The conversation's boundary; the letter is not dined with.
> 8. [choice]"The general's granddaughter walks the lines." → Remembered: Her assumption of the ritual; she walks too.

scenes.synopsis: the answer — the colonel's reply; the letter's fate, revealed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill comes in the afternoon — the campaign's lawyer, the war's legal mind — with the trial's first papers: the brief, the witnesses, the shape of the case. They work in the morning room — the papers spread, the tea going cold — the lawyer's methodical mind against the general's granddaughter's strategic one. The case is sound — Quill says it plainly, the lawyer's plainness, which is its own comfort: the libel is documented, the money is traced, the witnesses are willing. The law, at least, has rules.)*
> *(But the papers raise the week's old question in its legal shape: Henry's standing — the man's position beside her in the courtroom, the uniform in the controversy. Quill is careful — the lawyer's care, which is not evasion but precision: "If he stands with you, the court will read it. If he steps back, the court will also read it. The court reads everything." The reading, again — the trial, like the review, will be read before it is heard. "And your advice?" — Rose. "My advice," Quill says, "is that the law cannot decide this. Only he can." The lawyer's honesty — the admission of the law's limit — and she respects it.)*
> *(They work on — the witnesses, the brief, the preparations — the practical, the scheduled, the safe. When Quill leaves, the papers stacked, the tea cold, she sits with the afternoon's residue: the case is sound, the law has rules, the choosing is his. The trial's date is coming like weather. The weather, she is learning, can be met — with papers, with witnesses, with rules. And with the man beside her, or without him — whichever the choosing lands.)*
> *(She sits with the afternoon's residue — the case is sound, the law has rules, the choosing is his — and the residue, turned over, gives her the trial's clearest thought: the law cannot decide what only he can, and the honesty of that limit is its own comfort. Quill's admission — the lawyer's limit, precisely stated — the papers stacked, the tea cold. The witnesses, mapped. The brief, studied. The gown, commissioned. The preparations, thorough — the thoroughness its own argument. The trial's date is coming like weather. The weather can be met — with papers, with witnesses, with rules. The choosing, awaited. The weather, watched.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Nine o'clock — the regimental post's punctuality. → Remembered: The hour's military precision; answers arrive on time.
> 2. [social]His face "the way one watches a horizon." → Remembered: Her reading of him; the face precedes the words.
> 3. [stance]"Consistent with the honor of the service" — the clerkship, decoded. → Remembered: The masterpiece parsed; honor, officially consistent.
> 4. [micro]"Not at this time" — the regiment's favorite tense. → Remembered: The tense's conditionality; sleep, not death.
> 5. [examine]"It sleeps until Thursday." → Remembered: Her correction; the trial may wake it.
> 6. [social]The breast pocket — "over his heart." → Remembered: Where he puts the reply; the uniform keeps it close.
> 7. [choice]"Thursday, I stand where the whole town can see." → Remembered: The Thursday promise, renewed; the agreement, visible.
> 8. [stance]The week's third easy laugh — morale, restored. → Remembered: The laugh's return; the uniform stays.

scenes.synopsis: the answer's legal meaning — Quill on "not at this time"; the trial's witness, secured.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks in the evening — the garden, the long light — because the trial's preparations have filled the day, and the evening needs emptying: the mind's parade ground, cleared for inspection. The garden is hers — the roses, the paths, the birds — the war's one demilitarized zone, where no campaign is planned and no intelligence is gathered. She walks it slowly, the gravel's hush, the roses' scent — the white roses, the clean name's flowers, blooming with the season's indifference to controversy.)*
> *(She thinks about the week — the letter, the terms, the review, the date — the whole campaign, reviewed in the garden's quiet. The week began with subtractions — the sitter, the money — and continued with the choosing, which was his. The review stated the position. The date set the countdown. The household stands. The case is sound. The sums, for once, are nearly complete — the general's granddaughter's sums, cold and clean. Nearly. The choosing remains — his, still, and the waiting nearly over.)*
> *(A bird sings — the garden's evening music, unplanned, unpaid-for — and she stops on the path, listening. The war has its music too — the drill's brass, the regiment's bugle — but the garden's is different: it asks nothing, it costs nothing, it witnesses without judging. She stands a long time in the singing's quiet. Tomorrow the choosing lands — she feels it, the way one feels weather changing. Tonight, the garden. Tonight, the roses. Tonight, the one demilitarized zone, held.)*
> *(She stands a long time in the singing's quiet — the garden's evening music, unplanned, unpaid-for — and the standing teaches her what the week has been teaching all along: the war has its music too, but the garden's asks nothing, costs nothing, witnesses without judging. Tomorrow the choosing lands — she feels it, the weather changing. Tonight, the garden. Tonight, the roses — the white roses, the clean name's flowers, blooming with the season's indifference to controversy. The week began with subtractions; it continued with the choosing, which was his. The sums are nearly complete. Nearly. The choosing remains — his, still. The garden, held. The demilitarized zone, kept.)*
> *(The choosing, awaited — his, still — and the awaiting itself the garden’s lesson: some things ripen only in the quiet, and the quiet must be kept.)*
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Quill's double reading — "the lawyer's habit with favorable documents." → Remembered: How lawyers read victories; twice, for the conditions.
> 2. [stance]"Never with better manners." → Remembered: Quill's epigram; the regiment's euphemism for never.
> 3. [social]"Officially asleep." → Remembered: The whisper's official status; sleep, certified.
> 4. [micro]The reply, set down — the document's weight, discharged. → Remembered: The paper's work done; it rests.
> 5. [examine]"The breaking has its plan. The plan has its witness." → Remembered: Quill's summary; the war's arithmetic, complete.
> 6. [stance]The alone Thursday, "folded away." → Remembered: The unused plan's quiet folding; it is kept, not discarded.
> 7. [choice]"What loyalty looks like when it is dressed." → Remembered: The Thursday thesis, repeated; it becomes the chapter's epitaph.

scenes.synopsis: the agreement, restated — what the week has made of them; the romance's new shape.
scenes.prose:
> *(The choosing lands — not with fanfare, but with the morning post: his letter, his hand, the words plain. She reads it standing — some news one meets upright — and the standing is its own answer. The letter is short — the soldier's brevity, nothing wasted — and the shortness is its own eloquence: he has decided. The decision is his — the terms kept, the vow honored, the choosing clean. She reads it twice — the second reading for the steadiness, the way one tests a floor before trusting it — and the floor holds.)*
> *(She does not weep — the general's granddaughter does not weep at letters — but her hand shakes, once, the paper's small tremor, and the tremor is its own testimony: the week's whole weight, released in a single shake. Then the steadiness returns — the commander's steadiness, the woman the review proved — and she folds the letter, squarely, the way one folds a map. The map of the ground they will fight on. The ground, now chosen.)*

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — TRIAL'S FIRST DAY. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(The trial’s first day — the courtroom, the gallery, the prosecution’s first word — and the week’s last choosing: the uniform, in the courtroom. He has chosen — the letter sent, the waiting over — but the choosing’s shape remains: does the major attend the trial’s first day in full uniform, seated where the gallery sees — the agreement, visible from the prosecution’s first word — or does the uniform stay away, unspent on spectacle, the restraint itself the statement? The town will read it either way. The regiment will read it either way. The reading, like the choosing, must be his — or hers to stage, or theirs to share.)*
> *(Quill has the brief open on the table — the campaign’s lawyer, the war’s legal mind, plain as porridge and twice as sustaining. “A uniform in the gallery,” he says, “is evidence before a word is spoken. The prosecution will call it pressure; the gallery will call it theater; the regiment —” he taps the brief’s margin, where he has written nothing, the tap itself the annotation — “the regiment will read it as the stand it is. There is no neutral reading. There is only which true reading you prefer.” The law, at least, has rules — but the gallery has appetites, and the trial’s first day will feed them whatever is set before it.)*
> *(She thinks of the parade ground — the dust, the brass, the man inside the uniform, clean — and of the review’s box, the gown’s argument, the town’s opera glasses. The trial is a different theater: the law’s rules, the court’s reading, the stakes higher and the audience colder. A uniform in the gallery is a statement no gown can make — and no gown can unmake. “The uniform is not a costume,” he says quietly — the first thing he has said about the choosing all evening, and it lands like a stone in still water. “It is the agreement, made cloth. If I wear it there, I spend the agreement where the town can see the spending.” He does not finish; the unfinished sentence finishes itself. To have him attend is to spend the stand visibly; to keep him away is to protect the major from the spectacle; to let him choose is to hand the staging back, clean. Three stagings. The trial’s first day. The gallery, waiting to read.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 3/3 — trial's first day:*
- **Have him attend** — *Henry+; the visible stand.* Rose has Henry attend the trial's first day in full uniform, seated where the gallery sees — the agreement, visible from the prosecution's first word. *(The town reads the stand; the regiment reads the defiance — both readings true.)*
- **Keep him away** — *Standing+; the protected major.* Rose keeps Henry from the trial's first day entirely — the box later, but not the gallery now; the uniform is not spent on spectacle. *(The town reads the absence; the regiment notes the restraint.)*
- **Let him choose** — *The major decides.* Rose refuses to stage him — attend or absent, his call, his uniform, his reading of the regiment's "not at this time." *(He decides; the choosing is the last of the week's choices.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the visible stand, the protected major, the major’s own call. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

The case is sound. The law has rules. The rules can be met.)*

The preparations are thorough. The thoroughness is its own argument.)*

Not the review's gown — the trial is a different theater, the reading different — but the same principle: the silk speaks before she does, and the speaking must be managed. She chooses with the week's hard-won knowledge — the certain, the upright, the unafraid — the woman the review proved, cut for the courtroom. The preparations complete — the papers, the witnesses, the gown — she sits a moment in the completion's quiet. The trial is coming. The weather can be met.)*
> *(She sits a moment in the completion's quiet — the papers, the witnesses, the gown — the trial's kit, the soldier's pack, the woman's armor. The case is sound. The law has rules. The choosing is his. The preparations, thorough — the thoroughness its own argument, the way the week's every preparation has been. The gown — Élise's rooms, the silk's hush, the choosing — the courtroom's argument, made in cloth: the certain, the upright, the unafraid, cut for the law's theater. The trial is coming. The weather can be met — with papers, with witnesses, with the gown's managed reading. The completion, held. The quiet, kept.)*

scenes.synopsis: the quiet morning — two days to Thursday; the agreement, at peace.
scenes.prose:
> *(The night before the trial's eve — the calendar's strange country, the day before the day before — she does the thing the campaign requires: she rests. Not idleness — the general's granddaughter does not idle — but the deliberate rest, the commander's discipline: the battle is prepared, the ground is surveyed, the troops are posted. The eve of the eve is for the commander's quiet. She dismisses the book — the campaign's ledger, closed for the night — and dismisses the lists, the papers, the preparations. The war, for one evening, is adjourned.)*
> *(She dines alone — the dining room's hush, the candles, the simple food — the meal's plainness its own statement: the woman, unadorned, before the trial's theater. her maid hovers — the household's care, the invisible army's concern — and Rose dismisses her gently: the commander, tonight, needs no staff. The candles burn. The food is eaten. The quiet holds.)*
> *(Then the garden — the evening walk, the demilitarized zone — the roses, the paths, the birds' last music. She walks slowly — the gravel's hush, the white roses' scent — the clean name's flowers, blooming with the season's indifference to controversy. Tomorrow the trial's eve. The day after, the trial. The countdown, nearly complete. She stands among the roses a long time — the evening's quiet, the war's adjournment. The rest, she knows, is also readiness. The general's rule, kept: before a battle, you stand still.)*
> *(The candles burn. The food is eaten. The quiet holds — the dining room's hush, the deliberate rest, the commander's discipline: the battle prepared, the ground surveyed, the troops posted. She seals each herself — some things are not for clerks — the wax, the signet, the campaign's seal.)*
> *(Then the last letter — the one the week has been writing toward, the one the choosing made possible: to him. Not long — the soldier's brevity, learned — the words plain: the trial is tomorrow, the standing is decided, the cost is shared — the division of the labor, restated for the record. She does not ask him to come — the asking would be choosing, retroactively — but she tells him the hour, the courtroom, the gown — the facts, which are also an invitation, the way a battle's hour is an invitation. The letter, sealed — the wax, the signet — the week's last correspondence.)*
> *(She sits a moment — the letters stacked, the wax cooling — in the correspondence's quiet. The trial is tomorrow. The papers are ready. The witnesses are confirmed. The gown is hung.
