> 2. [examine]See the rose going brown — the verdict, aging. → Remembered: The flowers' mortality; verdicts must be renewed.
> 3. [stance]Trace the line's travel — lamplight to daylight to Fleet Street. → Remembered: The season's arc, internalized; she is its author.
> 4. [social]Sit with the quiet house — the night before. → Remembered: The eve's stillness; she banks it against the morning.
> 5. [examine]Picture Pyke setting type — the enemy, at work. → Remembered: The parallel war; he sets while she sleeps.
> 6. [micro]Close the drawer — the inventory, concluded. → Remembered: The ritual of closing; order is also armor.
> 7. [choice]Sleep, or sit a while longer. → Remembered: The eve's discipline; rest is also strategy.

scenes.synopsis: Bell's verdict on the writ — the Gazette will report the trial, and nothing else; openly Bell's. (Turns: 1 — the reading)
scenes.prose:
> *"Hartwell v. the* Lantern. *The writ is served; the damages are large; the plaintiff will walk Fleet Street in daylight. Bell's verdict: the Gazette will report the trial — and nothing else."*
> *(The sting lands on the chapter's last beat — the verdict before the verdict, the paper's creed stated plain. "And nothing else." Three words: no paragraphs for the plaintiff, no mercy for the defendant, no verdict before the verdict — only the report, plain and complete. Augusta nods once, slowly. Letitia cuts the paragraph out with her sewing scissors before Rose can ask. The drawer gains its fourth founding. And Rose understands, with a clarity like cold water: the paper is not hers. It was never hers. That is why its verdict matters — and that is why, when the Network comes knocking, as money always does, the knock will fail. Not to her. Not to anyone.)*
> 1. [stance]Hear "and nothing else" — the independence, in three words; read it twice, once for the law and once for the warning it carries, and foresee the knock. → Remembered: The Gazette's creed; she will hold the paper to it, and she will not be surprised.
scenes.sting: Hartwell v. the* Lantern. *The writ is served; the damages are large; the plaintiff will walk Fleet Street in daylight. Bell's verdict: the Gazette will report the trial — and nothing else.

scenes.synopsis: the Network's first move — its men call on Bell; pressure, money, menaces.
scenes.prose:
> *(The news comes at dusk, by the lines — Larkin's boy, breathless, with a report that is not about the street at all: two men, well-dressed, well-spoken, have called at the Gazette's office. They asked for the proprietor. They were shown in. What was said behind the closed door, the boy does not know — but he knows the cut of their coats, and the weight of the bag one of them carried, and the way they looked at the imprint on the wall as if pricing it. Rose stands at the window with the report in her hand and understands, with the cold clarity of a general reading a dispatch: the Network has made its first move. Not at her — at the paper. Pressure, money, menaces: the three levers, applied to the one fixed point. She thinks of Bell's name on the imprint — the proprietor, publicly named, unbuyable. She thinks of "and nothing else." She thinks of the knock she foresaw at breakfast, and how foreseeing is not preventing. The lamps are lit below. Somewhere across London, behind a closed door, men are pricing the unpriceable. The chapter ends. The Network's first move — its men call on Bell — lands at dusk, and the chapter's close is the season's turn: not the writ, not the walk, but the enemy's answer. Pressure, money, menaces — the three levers Lavinia named, applied now to the Gazette's proprietor. Rose holds the report and feels the campaign's ground shift: the paper that cannot be bought is about to be tested. Bell's name on the imprint — publicly named, from the first edition — is the fixed point the Network means to move. The bag's weight, the coats' cut, the pricing look at the imprint: the boy saw what he saw. What was said behind the closed door will be known tomorrow — in the next chapter, at Bell's door, in the soft-voiced refusal. The lamps are lit. The men are inside. The chapter ends on the knock's echo, and the handoff is the Gazette's: the paper, the proprietor, the price that cannot be paid. The boy is paid and sent. Rose stands at the window, the dusk deepening. The Network's first move replays: the coats, the bag, the pricing look. Pressure, money, menaces — at Bell's door. She thinks of tomorrow, the next chapter, the soft-voiced refusal to come. The handoff is prepared. What was said will be known. The refusal will be given.)*
> 1. [micro]Take the boy's report — breathless, precise. → Remembered: The lines' gravest dividend; the boy is promoted in her trust.
> 2. [examine]Read the coats, the bag, the pricing look — the levers, identified. → Remembered: The Network's method; pressure, money, menaces.
> 3. [stance]Stand at the window — the general reading a dispatch. → Remembered: Her composure under the new threat; the house takes its cue.
> 4. [social]Think of Bell's name on the imprint — the fixed point, tested. → Remembered: The paper's trial; her faith is the question.
> 5. [examine]Weigh foreseeing against preventing — the breakfast's clarity. → Remembered: The limit of anticipation; some knocks must be answered by others.
> 6. [micro]Hold the report till the paper creases — the hand's tell. → Remembered: The one betrayal of feeling; she permits herself one.
> 7. [stance]Name it the first move — the war's new front. → Remembered: The campaign's expansion; the paper is now the battlefield.
> 8. [choice]Go to Bell tonight, or trust the morning. → Remembered: The eve's decision; the chapter's ★3 echoes into the dark.

scenes.synopsis: the set-piece — Rose walks the Lantern's street in daylight; the trade watches.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks it in white — Fleet Street, the Lantern's street, in daylight, in the clean name's color — and the trade watches. That is the whole of the set-piece, and it is enough: the plaintiff, walking, the street watching, the morning doing the rest. The white silk is severe and unadorned, the morning's ritual made cloth; the gloves are white; the shoes are silent on the flags. She passes the stationer's, the coffee-houses, the press-houses with their open courts — and at each, the work pauses, the frames are left, the devils stop mid-errand. They have read about her for months. Now they see her. The seeing is the paragraph the conduct campaign has been writing all season: the clean name, walking, in daylight, past the press that printed her ruin. A printer's devil touches his cap. A compositor lays down his stick. Nobody jeers — the street, face to face with the plaintiff, finds it has nothing to jeer at. She walks the length of it, unhurried, unbowed, and the walk is the writ's second service: not on Pyke, but on the street. By the time she turns for home, the trade has its verdict, and the verdict is walking home in white. The walk's route was planned like a campaign — Augusta's map, the streets chosen for their trade: Fleet Street first, the press-houses; then the courts, the stationers, the coffee-houses; then home by the square, the whole of it in daylight. She walks it as planned, and the plan holds, and the holding is the achievement — the set-piece, executed. A woman selling flowers offers her a white rose — "for the walk, miss" — and she takes it, and carries it, and the rose becomes the walk's standard, the floriography's seal. The trade will remember the rose longer than the silk, she thinks — the small human detail, the flower against the white. By the walk's end the rose is still fresh, and so is she: unhurried, unbowed, the morning's work done. The set-piece closes. The street has its image. The custom animation — the Fleet Street set-piece, the trade watching — holds the morning like a frame holds a portrait: the plaintiff, walking, in white, in daylight, the clean name's color. The town will describe this walk for weeks.)*
> 1. [stance]Step out at ten — the hour, chosen. → Remembered: The walk's timing; morning light favors the plaintiff.
> 2. [micro]Walk at Augusta's pace — the general's tempo. → Remembered: Her unhurried progress; haste would betray the brief.
> 3. [examine]Watch the ripples — devil, door, hawker's cry. → Remembered: The street's attention, anatomized; every trade stops differently.
> 4. [social]Pass the caricature windows — the trade's mirrors. → Remembered: The print-sellers' windows; they show her to herself.
> 5. [stance]Stop opposite the *Lantern's* court — the pause, held. → Remembered: The walk's still point; the street will describe it for years.
> 6. [examine]Let them see her looking — the seeing, seen. → Remembered: The chapter's thesis; she watches, and is watched watching.
> 7. [micro]Hear the street exhale — the long release. → Remembered: The trade's verdict, breathed; the walk is already won.
> 8. [choice]Turn at the Strand, or walk on. → Remembered: The walk's boundary; she ends it where she chooses.
scenes.animationNote: Fleet Street set-piece — Rose walks the Lantern's street in daylight; the trade watches

scenes.synopsis: the watchers — printers, devils, hawkers; the street's faces, catalogued.
scenes.prose:
> *(The watchers catalogue themselves, if she watches back: the printers at their windows, aprons inked, arms folded — the trade's jury, empaneled by curiosity. The devils, quick and bright-eyed, the street's sparrows, carrying the morning's errands and the morning's gossip in equal measure. The hawkers, who sold the libels for a penny and now sell the walk for nothing, their cries gone respectful. The paragraph-men, notebooks out, writing the plaintiff's progress court by court — the walk's first draft, in pencil. She walks through them all and lets them look; the conduct campaign's doctrine is explicit — be watchable — and the white silk is the watchable made cloth. A woman at a print-shop door stares openly, then curtsies, then stares again. A clerk on an errand stops so long his master will dock him. The street's faces, catalogued: curiosity, respect, the dawning embarrassment of men who printed what they are now watching disprove itself. Nobody throws anything. Nobody says anything, at first. Then, as she passes the Lantern's court — not stopping, never stopping — a single pair of hands applauds, once, and stops. The catalogue is complete. Among the watchers, the ones who matter: the master printers, at their upper windows — the trade's elders, the men whose opinion becomes the street's. They watch longest, arms folded, and their watching is the verdict's first draft. One of them — the Chronicle's master, she thinks — nods, once, slowly. It is the smallest gesture of the morning, and the largest: the trade's acknowledgment, given. The devils will carry the nod with the gossip; the paragraph-men will write it between the lines. She walks on, cataloguing, and the catalogue becomes the afternoon's intelligence: who watched, how long, with what face. The woman at the print-shop door — respect. The clerk — awe, and a docked wage. The master printer — the nod. It is enough. The street's faces, catalogued, become the street's verdict — and the verdict, rendered by watchers, is the walk's whole object. The white silk moves on. The watchers remain, watching — and the watching, she thinks, is the verdict's first draft, written in daylight for the whole trade to read.)*
> 1. [examine]Catalogue the master printer — ink, judgment. → Remembered: The trade's elders; their silence is the verdict.
> 2. [social]Receive the hawker's cap-touch — almost an apology. → Remembered: The libel-seller's awkwardness; the street repents in gestures.
> 3. [micro]Return the keeper's nod — a fraction. → Remembered: The fractional courtesy; it travels faster than paragraphs.
> 4. [stance]Walk through the wordless street — the silence, kept. → Remembered: Her composure under total attention; severity holds.
> 5. [examine]Read the silence as verdict — "we know the difference." → Remembered: The trade's judgment; it precedes the court's.
> 6. [social]Note the devils' open stare — youth, unguarded. → Remembered: The young trade's allegiance; the future belongs to the walking.
> 7. [choice]Acknowledge the watchers, or pass as weather. → Remembered: Her register with the trade; the fraction was enough.

scenes.synopsis: ink and morning — Fleet Street's texture; the machine's daylight face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Fleet Street in the morning is a machine waking: the presses thumping up to speed, the paper arriving in carts, the ink-men making their rounds, the whole trade shaking off the night like a dog shakes off water. The smell is the street's signature — ink and hot metal and paper-dust and the coffee from the stalls — and the sound is its voice, the thump and clatter of the morning's numbers being born. She walks through the machine's daylight face and the machine, for once, looks back: the press-houses with their open doors, the chapels at their frames, the proprietors at their windows. This is where the libels were manufactured — not in malice's dark, but here, in the morning's ordinary industry, by men eating bread at their frames. The ordinariness is the revelation she carries with her, court by court: her ruin was a product, and products are made in daylight. A press thumps. A devil runs. The morning goes on being the morning, indifferent and magnificent. She walks it, in white, and the machine's daylight face — seen at last from the inside of the walk — looks, she thinks, almost honest. The ink-men's carts are the morning's commerce — the trade's lifeblood, delivered: the black ink for the news, the colored inks for the illustrated papers, the paper in reams, the rags for the devils' aprons. She watches a cart unload at a press-house door — the reams carried in, the porters sweating — and thinks of the Lantern's paper supply, the quarter's account, the settlement demanded. The machine's daylight face has its economy, and the economy is honest: ink bought, paper printed, news sold. It is the opposite of the purchased paragraph — the honest trade, doing its work. A paper-seller's boy runs past with the morning's numbers, the headlines crying. She catches one: the Chronicle's, generous. The morning's texture — ink and metal and paper-dust and coffee — settles on her like weather. Fleet Street, awake, is magnificent: the industry, the noise, the purpose. She walks it, in white, and the machine's daylight face looks back — and what it sees, she hopes, is the clean name, walking.)*
> 1. [micro]Smell the ink rising with the damp — the street's perfume. → Remembered: The morning's sensory truth; Fleet Street has a smell like weather.
> 2. [examine]See the machine waking — presses like hearts. → Remembered: The street as organism; it can be walked, and won.
> 3. [stance]Walk it "in white, in daylight, as a plaintiff" — the brief, worn. → Remembered: The white's meaning; severity is the clean name's color.
> 4. [social]Hear the pressman singing — off-key, cheerful. → Remembered: The trade's ordinary joy; the street is not the *Lantern*.
> 5. [examine]Know "the street does not belong to Pyke" — the truth, walked. → Remembered: The gutter's ownership; whoever walks cleanly holds it.
> 6. [micro]Watch the sun slapped back from the windows — light, weaponized. → Remembered: The daylight's cooperation; the morning is her ally.
> 7. [choice]Memorize the street, or let it memorize her. → Remembered: The walk's mutual impression; both keep the morning.

scenes.synopsis: the penny's worth — the hawker who sold the first libels; the trade's repentance, priced at a penny.
scenes.prose:
> *("Penny for the walk, miss?" The hawker is the one who sold the first libels — she knows his face the way she knows the paragraphs, the cry that carried "fraud" through the streets for a penny. He knows her too; the recognition crosses his face like weather. "No penny today," she says, and stops — the walk pausing, the set-piece interrupted for a smaller, better theatre. "I owe you custom, I think. You sold a great deal of me." He flushes to the ears. "Miss — I didn't write 'em. I only cried 'em." It is the trade's repentance, priced at a penny: the distinction between the hand that writes and the voice that cries, offered as absolution. She buys a Chronicle from him — pays the penny, overpays it — and the transaction is the absolution, granted. "Cry this one," she says, tapping the headline. He grins, relieved, and cries it on the spot, loud and loyal. The walk resumes. Behind her the hawker's cry follows, changed: not "fraud" but the Chronicle's headline, whatever it is. The trade's repentance, priced at a penny, and worth — she thinks, walking on — considerably more. The hawker's repentance follows her — the changed cry, "Chronicle! Read the plaintiff's progress!" — and the walk acquires its soundtrack: the trade's loyalty, cried for a penny. Other hawkers take it up — the cry traveling the street the way weather travels — and by the walk's end the libels' old crier is leading a chorus. It is the morning's smallest victory, and the sweetest: the voice that cried "fraud" now cries the vindication. She thinks of the penny — the price of repentance, the trade's absolution — and of the overpayment, the grin, the loyalty. The transaction was small. The meaning is large: the street's voices can be changed, one hawker at a time, one penny at a time. The walk goes on, the cries following. Behind her, the hawker is selling Chronicles as if they were pardons. In a way, they are — the town's, the trade's, his own. The penny's worth, compounded — and the compounding, she thinks, is the whole of the campaign: one voice, changed, changing the street.)*
> 1. [social]Face the hawker — the libel-seller, confessing. → Remembered: The trade's repentance, personified; she receives it standing.
> 2. [examine]Recognize the Bath cry — the same cap, the same trade. → Remembered: The gutter's geography, completed; Bath to Fleet Street.
> 3. [stance]Say "you know her now" — exactly true, neither kind nor unkind. → Remembered: The line's perfect pitch; the street will quote it.
> 4. [micro]Watch his face "do something complicated" — the man's reckoning. → Remembered: The hawker's humanity; the trade is men, not machines.
> 5. [social]Feel the street hold its breath — the audience, rapt. → Remembered: The walk's theater; every corner is a stage.
> 6. [examine]Hear the devil's approving laugh — the young trade's verdict. → Remembered: The laugh's allegiance; the future laughs with her.
> 7. [choice]Forgive aloud, or let the line stand. → Remembered: Her mercy, metered; the line stands, and that is enough.

scenes.synopsis: read in the open — the trade reads her; the walk's first paragraph, written by conduct.
scenes.prose:
> *(The coffee-house reads her over its dishes — the walk's first paragraph, written by conduct, read aloud between sips. She does not go in — a lady does not take coffee in Fleet Street — but she passes the open door, and the reading pauses, and forty men perform the small choreography of respect: the half-rise, the touched hat, the cleared throat. Then the reading resumes, changed — the paragraph about the plaintiff now illustrated by the plaintiff, the text corrected by the sight. Larkin's boy brings her the phrases afterwards, verbatim: "walks like the verdict already," one man said. "White," said another, "and not a mark on it." She lays the phrases in the pocket-book, the archive's method holding. The walk's first paragraph, written by conduct and read in the open, is the conduct campaign's whole theory proved: the town does not need to be told, only shown. The coffee-house returns to its dishes. The plaintiff returns to her walk. The paragraph, illustrated, goes on being read. The coffee-house's paragraph will be the evening's — the paragraph-men's copy, filed by noon: "the plaintiff walked Fleet Street in white, and the trade watched." It is the walk's first draft, and she will not revise it — the conduct campaign's discipline is to let the town write. But she thinks, walking on, about what the paragraph leaves out: the flower-seller's rose, the hawker's changed cry, the master printer's nod. The town writes the outline; the details are hers to keep. Larkin's boy, paid and dismissed, runs back to the lines — the intelligence circuit, complete. The walk's first paragraph, written by conduct and read in the open, is also the week's: the street has its image, the papers have their copy, the plaintiff has her morning. The coffee-house returns to its dishes. The dishes are ordinary. The morning was not. The paragraph goes on being read — illustrated, now, by the plaintiff herself. And the illustration, she thinks, is the point: the town does not need to be told, only shown — and shown, in white, in daylight, the showing becomes the verdict.)*
> 1. [social]Receive the bow — apron and all, before the street. → Remembered: The trade's homage; the walk's first paragraph writes itself.
> 2. [examine]Hear the stopped applause — "not done in the morning." → Remembered: The town's decorum, even in revolution; restraint governs all.
> 3. [stance]Accept the unwitnessed witness — "she did not ask for it." → Remembered: Her grace under homage; the daylight provides.
> 4. [micro]Watch the bow become paragraph — by the Strand. → Remembered: The story's travel; conduct becomes copy by noon.
> 5. [examine]Prove the general's doctrine — "on cobblestones." → Remembered: The conduct campaign's vindication; Augusta was right.
> 6. [social]Note the customers at the windows — the audience, multiplying. → Remembered: The walk's witnesses; every window is a gallery.
> 7. [choice]Return tomorrow, or let one walk suffice. → Remembered: The walk's singularity; once, perfectly, is enough.

scenes.synopsis: the call — at Bell's door; pressure, money, menaces; the parallel action.
scenes.prose:
> *(While Rose walks Fleet Street in white, two men walk into the Gazette's office in black — well-dressed, well-spoken, with the unhurried manners of men accustomed to being shown in. They ask for the proprietor. The clerk — a sharp boy who has worked for Bell since he was twelve — shows them into the inner office, and closes the door, and stands outside it with his hands folded, because Mrs. Bell pays him to be discreet and he is. That is the whole of what the outside knows: two men, well-dressed, shown in; the door, closed. What is said behind the panel, the panel keeps. Larkin's boy brings the externals by noon — the coats, the hour, the closed door — and Rose receives them the way a general receives a scout's report: the facts, only the facts, the interpretation withheld. The Network has called on the paper. Not on her — on the paper. The war's new front is named, and it is not her door. She files the visit — date, hour, coats, door — and goes on with the morning, the white silk, the walk. The parallel holds: white walking, black calling, two daylights, one morning. The visit's meaning is the morning's undertow — beneath the walk, the white silk, the trade's verdict, the other front: the Network calls on the paper. Rose turns it over as she walks — the facts, only the facts, the interpretation withheld, but the facts are eloquent: two men, well-dressed, at eleven; the inner office; the closed door. It is the purse's impatience, showing. The cutout's tradecraft would have been quieter — a letter, a go-between, the dark. This is daylight, or near it: a call, in person, at the Gazette's office. They are done being subtle, or becoming done. She files the visit with the morning's other intelligence — the nod, the rose, the changed cry — and the filing is the discipline: facts before interpretations, externals before interiors. The walk goes on. The white silk moves through the street. Behind the morning's brightness, the other front waits — the closed door, the panel's secret. The parallel holds.)*
> 1. [examine]Watch the two men walk in — black coats, unhurried manners, the purse's tailoring. → Remembered: The Network's emissaries; money dresses quietly.
> 2. [social]Note the clerk's discretion — shown in, the door closed, the hands folded. → Remembered: Bell's household; the inner office keeps its counsel.
> 3. [micro]Mark the parallel — white walking, black calling. → Remembered: The chapter's counterpoint; two daylights, one morning.
> 4. [examine]Receive the telling's externals — the coats, the hour, the closed door. → Remembered: The lines' dividend; facts before interpretations.
> 5. [stance]Note what the telling doesn't contain — no words from behind the panel. → Remembered: The closed door; the inside stays inside.
> 6. [social]Weigh the visit's meaning — the Network calls on the paper, not on her. → Remembered: The war's new front; the paper is the ground.
> 7. [micro]Watch the men leave — the visit's length, the door's closing. → Remembered: The exit's calm; the visit's result unreadable.
> 8. [examine]File the visit — date, hour, coats, door. → Remembered: The archive's externals; the panel's secret waits.

scenes.synopsis: pressure, money, menaces — the three levers, applied; the handle thrown.
scenes.prose:
> *(The telling travels by the lines — Larkin's boy to Rose, the clerk's boy to Larkin's boy, the panel's secret kept by the panel. What the telling contains is externals: the men were shown in at eleven, stayed the better part of an hour, left unhurried; the proprietor's door closed, then opened; nothing carried in but themselves, nothing carried out but themselves. What the telling does not contain is words — no voices were raised, no phrases certain, the boy's ear, for all its sharpness, defeated by oak and discretion. One detail only, dropped like a coin: the shorter man spoke a name from Bell's past — her mother, the boy thinks, or thought he heard. Rose pays the shilling. The intelligence, such as it is, is the visit itself: the Network calls on proprietors in the morning, the way it calls on no one else. She sends the boy back to watch the door — the paper has its own sentries, but a second pair of eyes is cheap — and holds the unanswered question the way she holds the white silk's hem: lightly, for now. What was said inside waits for its scene. The boy is sent back with his instructions — watch the door, note the comings and goings, report by dusk — and the lines' circuit extends: the Gazette's office, watched. It is the morning's prudence — the paper has its own sentries, but the plaintiff's eyes are cheap, and the war's new front deserves watching. Rose turns to the day's other business — the calls, the shops, the ordinary commerce — but the unanswered question walks with her: what was said inside. She does not chase it. Augusta's doctrine is explicit: let the closed door stay closed until it opens; the intelligence will come, the lines will bring it, the telling will travel. The telling, such as it is, is filed: the externals, the hour, the dropped name. The shilling is spent. The question waits — lightly held, like the silk's hem. What was said inside waits for its scene — and the waiting, she has learned, is also intelligence: the closed door teaches patience, and patience teaches the town.)*
> 1. [examine]Hear the telling secondhand — Larkin's boy, verbatim as he gives it. → Remembered: The lines' fidelity; the boy's memory is the record.
> 2. [micro]Note the time inside — how long the door stayed closed. → Remembered: The visit's duration; long calls mean business.
> 3. [social]Catch the single detail — the short man spoke a name from Bell's past. → Remembered: The name, dropped; the past, mentioned.
> 4. [examine]Mark what the boy didn't hear — no voices raised, no words certain. → Remembered: The telling's limits; the panel kept its secret.
> 5. [stance]Pay the shilling — the intelligence, such as it is. → Remembered: The price of externals; she pays for what there is.
> 6. [choice]Send the boy back to watch the door, or let the street rest. → Remembered: The surveillance decision; the paper has its own sentries.
> 7. [micro]Hold the unanswered question — what was said inside. → Remembered: The morning's unknown; it waits for its scene.

scenes.synopsis: the handle — her mother's dismissed-housekeeper past, thrown; and why it cannot work.
scenes.prose:
> *(What is known of Bell is public — the past is not a secret, only a history: her mother was a housekeeper in a great house, dismissed under circumstances the town has long since embroidered; the daughter was twelve, and the dismissal was the making of her. Rose turns the history over in the afternoon, the way she turns the morning's intelligence over — not as leverage, but as biography. The girl of twelve, the spoon, the great house's temper, the reference withheld: the small ruin that ends a servant's career. And then the rise — the trade learned, the paper bought, the proprietor's chair, the imprint on the wall. It is the ascent the men will have studied, the past they will have priced. But Rose studies it differently: not as a handle, but as the woman. The ink on Bell's finger, never quite washed out. The plain dark dress. The soft voice. The fifty years, every one of them earned. What the past made is the proprietor — and the proprietor is the paper, and the paper is unbuyable. The history closes like a book. The woman remains. The history's public nature is its point — the town knows it, the trade knows it, the men will have known it: the dismissed housekeeper, the daughter's rise. It is not a secret to be threatened with, but a biography to be reckoned with. Rose thinks of the difference — the secret versus the history — and understands what the men misunderstood, if they studied the file: a woman who rose from this past has already survived it. The past is not her weakness. The past is her making. The ink on her finger, the plain dark dress, the soft voice — all of it the past's product, all of it the proprietor. She closes the book on the history and turns to the evening — the calls, the dinner, the ordinary round. The woman remains: fifty, plain, ink-stained, steel. Whatever the men said behind the closed door, they said it to her. The history is public. The woman is private. The distinction will hold — and the holding, she thinks, is the whole of the proprietor's strength.)*
> 1. [examine]Recall what is known — the housekeeper, the dismissal, the daughter's rise. → Remembered: Bell's history; the past is public.
> 2. [social]Picture the girl of twelve — the spoon, the great house, the withheld reference. → Remembered: The small ruin; it made the proprietor.
> 3. [stance]Honor the rise — from servant's daughter to the proprietor's chair. → Remembered: The ascent; survival as biography.
> 4. [micro]Note the ink on her finger — the trade's mark, never washed out. → Remembered: The proprietor's badge; ink is her jewelry.
> 5. [examine]Weigh what the past teaches about the woman — not the leverage, the person. → Remembered: Her read of Bell; character before tactics.
> 6. [social]Consider why the men would mention it — the past as currency. → Remembered: The Network's coin; it spends old stories.
> 7. [choice]Pity the mother, or honor the daughter. → Remembered: Where her sympathy lands; the daughter needs no pity.

scenes.synopsis: THE REFUSAL — one scene, soft-voiced, absolute. The handle doesn't work. It never works. Character, not plot.
scenes.prose:
> *(The door opens. Mrs. Nance Bell stands in it — a woman of fifty, in a plain dark dress, with ink on one finger that no amount of washing will ever quite remove — and looks at the two men, and at the bag, and she smiles. It is not a large smile. "Gentlemen," she says, and her voice is soft, "you have mistaken the shop." The tall man begins — the friends, the purses, the wisdom of restraint; the Gazette's verdicts so respected, such a pity if the paper found itself on the wrong side of a great trial — and she lets him finish, because she is courteous, and courtesy, in her, is also contempt. Then the bag: opened, briefly, the color of the notes. Then the short man, all edges: her mother, the housekeeper, dismissed — a sad story, resurfacing, when a paper makes enemies. Bell listens. She does not move. When they are done she says, still soft: "My mother was dismissed from a great house for a spoon she did not take. I was twelve. I have been threatened with that spoon for thirty-eight years, by better men than you, for better reasons." She picks up the bag — it is heavy — and holds it out. "The Gazette is not for sale. Not its verdict, not its restraint, not its silence. Take your money." The short man says something about enemies. She is still smiling. "I have them," she says. "Good day, gentlemen." The door closes. It is the whole of the scene. It is enough for a lifetime. The office, after — the inner office with the imprint on the wall, the desk, the morning light through the high windows: the room where it happened, seen afterwards only in the mind's eye, because she was not there and will not ask. But she pictures it — the proprietor cannot help picturing: the two men, the bag, the soft voice. The tall man's pitch — the friends, the purses, the wisdom of restraint — the velvet glove, the kindness as threat. The bag, opened — the color of the notes, the weight, the argument. The short man, all edges — the mother, the spoon, the resurfacing, the enemies. And Bell — still, smiling, soft. The thirty-eight years. The better men, the better reasons. The bag, held out — heavy, refused. "The Gazette is not for sale. Not its verdict, not its restraint, not its silence." The three unsellables, named. "I have them." The enemies, acknowledged. "Good day, gentlemen." The door, closed. It is the whole of the scene — pressure, money, menaces, the mother's history as leverage, the verdict not for sale — soft-voiced, absolute, character not plot. It is enough for a lifetime.)*

> 2. [examine]Hear "you have mistaken the shop" — the refusal's first line. → Remembered: The soft dismissal; shops sell, papers judge.
> 3. [social]Let him finish — courtesy, even now. → Remembered: Her manners under menace; courtesy is also contempt.
> 4. [micro]Hold the heavy bag out — the money, returned. → Remembered: The bribe's rejection, physical; weight means nothing.
> 5. [examine]Count thirty-eight years — "better men, better reasons." → Remembered: The handle's long failure; the spoon is ancient history.
> 6. [stance]Name the not-for-sale — verdict, restraint, silence. → Remembered: The paper's three unsellables; the creed is complete.

scenes.synopsis: the imprint — Bell's name, on the Gazette's wall; the paper, unbuyable.
scenes.prose:
> *(The imprint is on the wall — Bell's name, in the Gazette's office, set in type and framed: MRS. NANCE BELL, PROPRIETRESS. Rose sees it in the afternoon, when she calls — not to thank, the morning being unperformed by request, but to see the wall, the office, the paper that refused. The imprint is the whole of the argument, framed: a woman's name, on a paper's wall, in type that cannot be unsaid. The clerk — the sharp boy, discreet — shows her the presses through the inner door: the machines rolling, the paper printing, the trade's honest industry. It is the opposite of the Lantern's chapel — no purchased paragraphs here, only the day's news, set straight. She stands before the imprint a long time. The paper is unbuyable — not because the offer was small, the bag was heavy, but because the name on the wall is the woman in the office, and the woman is not for sale. The proprietor is steel. The imprint says so, in type. She leaves without seeing Bell — the morning's request honored, unperformed — and the imprint stays on the wall behind her, judging the street. The clerk — the sharp boy, discreet — shows her the frame-shop's corner, where the Gazette's own paragraphs are set: the news, straight, the compositors' honest work. It is the imprint's proof, in metal: what the paper prints is what the name stands for. She watches a compositor set a paragraph — the stick, the sorts, the deft hands — and thinks of the Lantern's chapel, the same motions, the opposite meaning. The difference was never the machine. The difference was always the wall — the name on it, the woman behind it. The boy closes the inner door — the office, the imprint, the proprietor's privacy — and she is back in the court, the afternoon's light thinning. The paper is unbuyable. The imprint says so, in type, on the wall. She walks home through the trade's evening — the presses quieting, the devils done — and the imprint stays with her: MRS. NANCE BELL, PROPRIETRESS. The steel's signature. The paper's soul, framed — and the framing, she thinks, is the whole of the argument: a woman's name, in type, unbuyable.)*
> 1. [micro]Read the plain frame — "Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor." → Remembered: The imprint's plainness; power needs no flourish.
> 2. [examine]Recall the pricing look — "pricelessness, proved." → Remembered: The men's failure, epitaphed; some things can't be priced.
> 3. [social]Take tea in the inner room — the proprietor's courtesy. → Remembered: Bell's ordinary grace; the morning is already history.
> 4. [stance]Hear "they'll try the advertisers next" — the next lever, named. → Remembered: The coming pressure; the paper's trade will be tested.
> 5. [micro]Note the ink on her finger — indelible. → Remembered: The proprietor's mark; ink is her wedding ring.
> 6. [examine]Understand "the judge cannot be owned" — the final form. → Remembered: The season's hard truth; unbuyable is the point.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — BELL'S REFUSAL. (Turns: 3 — the decision)
scenes.prose:
> *(Bell refused — softly, absolutely, the bag held out, the door closed. The morning's scene, unperformed by request, unasked-about by discipline, sits in Rose's mind like a sealed letter: the Network's money, offered; the mother's history, thrown; the verdict, not for sale. Not its verdict, not its restraint, not its silence. The three unsellables, named by a woman of fifty with ink on her finger, in a plain dark dress, smiling. She thinks of the thirty-eight years — the spoon, the better men, the better reasons — and of what the refusal cost and what it proved: the paper is the ground, the proprietor is steel, the Gazette judges and is not judged. And now the plaintiff must decide her response — for the refusal, though unperformed, demands an answer. Thank her: the warmth, the acknowledgment, the debt named openly. Say nothing: the confidence, the steel trusted, the silence as respect. Offer the paper protection: the shield, the alliance made explicit, the Gazette's flank guarded. Each honors something different. Each risks something different. The morning's closed door waits for its answer.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — BELL'S REFUSAL:*
- **Thank her** — *Warmth; the debt named.* Write tonight — the gratitude, the acknowledgment, the alliance's warmth made explicit. Bell refused for the paper; the plaintiff thanks her for the paper, openly, in daylight.
- **Say nothing** — *Confidence; the steel trusted.* Let the refusal stand unanswered — the highest compliment. To thank Bell would suggest she needed thanking; to protect her would suggest she needed protection. Silence as respect.
- **Offer the paper protection** — *The shield; the flank guarded.* Lay the Gazette's defense alongside her own — Quill's counsel, the writ's scope, the Network's impatience shared. The paper held this morning; see that it holds tomorrow.
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: whether she thanked Bell, said nothing, or offered the paper protection. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the witness — Lavinia sees the men leave Bell's door; the Network is done being subtle.
scenes.prose:
> *(Lavinia sees them leave — the scarlet shawl is in the right street at the right hour, as it always is — and the witness brings the report herself, unannounced, at dusk. "Two men," she says, "black coats, unhurried — the Network's tailoring, darling, I know it the way I know bad lace. They went into the Gazette's office at eleven and came out at twelve, and the shorter one looked like a man who had been smiled at by someone he could not afford to quarrel with." It is the gutter's reading, and it is exact: the visit's externals, the exit's manner, the conclusion. "They are done being subtle," Lavinia says, pacing. "Calling on a proprietor in daylight — that is not the cutout's tradecraft, that is the purse's impatience. The money is frightened, Rose. Frightened money makes mistakes." She is gleeful, and the glee is intelligence: the Network's first open move is also its first error. Rose hears the report through, asks the questions — the coats, the hour, the shorter man's face — and files it. The witness is dismissed with tea. The war's new front is confirmed: the paper, in daylight, unbuyable. Lavinia's report has its price — the tea, the listening, the patience for the scarlet shawl's theatre — and Rose pays it gladly, because the witness is worth the theatre: the coats, the hour, the shorter man's face, the exact reading. "Black coats," Lavinia says, "but not mourning — money's black, the kind that costs. Unhurried — men who expect to be obeyed. And the shorter one — the face of a man who went in with a bag and came out without one." It is the gutter's precision, and it confirms the telling: the visit, the manner, the outcome guessed. Rose asks the question Lavinia has been waiting for: "Did they look frightened?" The scarlet shawl snaps. "Darling, they looked like men who had been smiled at by someone they could not afford to quarrel with. That is frightened, in their language." The witness is dismissed — with tea, with thanks, with the promise of more.

> 2. [examine]See the faces — tall one's, short one's haste. → Remembered: The emissaries' demeanor; haste betrays need.
> 3. [stance]Hear "stopped being subtle" — the diagnosis. → Remembered: The Network's escalation; subtlety abandoned.
> 4. [micro]Note the bag going with them — the bribe, refused. → Remembered: The money's return; the street will know by supper.
> 5. [examine]Distinguish strategy from appetite — "the beginning of error." → Remembered: The enemy's state; appetite makes mistakes.
> 6. [social]Weigh "afraid of the trial" — the fear, priced. → Remembered: What the Network fears; the open court terrifies cutouts.
> 7. [choice]Share Bell's tea, or keep the inner room closed. → Remembered: The alliance's boundaries; Bell's privacy is hers to keep.

scenes.synopsis: done being subtle — what the call means; the ally's reading of the war.
scenes.prose:
> *("Done being subtle," Lavinia says, and the phrase becomes the evening's text. What the call means: the Network has stopped working through cutouts and chapels and started calling in person — the purse, impatient, showing its hand. "It means the writ frightened them," Lavinia says. "Not the trial — the trial they can buy witnesses for. The writ's scope. They don't know who you'll name, and not-knowing is the one thing money cannot fix." It is the ally's reading of the war, and Rose tests it the way she tests all Lavinia's readings: for the self-interest underneath. The self-interest is there — the gutter's hunger for the machine down — but the reading holds anyway. The call means the paper is the ground now; the call means the Network will try the levers in order; the call means Bell, this morning, stood where the whole war converges. "And Bell?" Lavinia asks. "Unperformed," Rose says, and Lavinia laughs — the scarlet shawl shaking — and calls it the best sentence of the war. The evening's text is closed. The subtlety is done. The evening's text gets its commentary — Augusta, told, gives the general's version: "They called on Bell because Bell is the ground. The trial will be fought on paper — the Gazette's, the Lantern's, the town's. Whoever holds the paper holds the verdict's first draft." It is the strategy, stated: the war's new front, the paper, the daylight. Letitia, listening, is bewildered and thrilled in equal measure — the chaperon's great hour, the war's map spread on the drawing-room table. Rose thinks of the morning's closed door, the soft voice, the bag — the scene she did not see, the intelligence she holds lightly. The call means the Network is done being subtle. It means the purse is impatient. It means the writ frightened them — not the trial, but the scope, the not-knowing. The evening's text is closed, the commentary filed. The subtlety is done. The daylight's war goes on — and the going-on, she thinks, is the whole of the courage: the paper held, the town knows, the war continues — the daylight's discipline, kept.)*
> 1. [examine]Take "the one reliable law" — subtle to stupid. → Remembered: Lavinia's doctrine of money; escalation is decay.
> 2. [social]Let her pace — thinking with her feet. → Remembered: The ally's method; the morning room is her war room.

> 4. [micro]Catch the pronoun — "*we* have already lost it." → Remembered: The alliance's consolidation; Lavinia says we now.
> 5. [examine]Weigh "interested, not frightened" — the wartime register. → Remembered: The ally's fearlessness; it steadies Rose.
> 6. [social]Ask if she is frightened — the honest question. → Remembered: Her care for the ally; the question is also a gift.

scenes.synopsis: the street decides — the trade's verdict, by afternoon; the walk's dividend.
scenes.prose:
> *(By afternoon the street has decided — the trade's verdict, rendered in the time it takes ink to dry: the walk was the verdict-in-progress, the white silk the clean name, the plaintiff already acquitted by the only jury that matters before the court. The paragraph-men file their copy — "walks like the verdict already" — and the evening papers will carry it. The hawkers cry the walk instead of the libels. The coffee-houses read the conduct. It is the walk's dividend, compounded hourly: every eye that saw her becomes a witness, every witness a paragraph, every paragraph a juror instructed. Rose hears the verdict in the afternoon's round — the calls, the shops, the curtsies deeper than yesterday — and receives it the way she receives all the town's verdicts: as a loan, to be repaid with a real one. Augusta, told, nods once. "The street decides quickly," the general says, "and undecides slowly. You have the first. See that you earn the second." The afternoon thins. The verdict stands — walking home, in white, the dividend compounding. And the compounding, she thinks, is the street's gift: every eye a witness, every witness a paragraph, every paragraph a juror instructed for the morning. The verdict's loan gets its terms — Augusta's doctrine, restated: "The street has lent you its verdict. The court will collect. See that you can pay." It is the evening's gravity, beneath the dividend: the town's certainty is a loan, the trial the repayment. Rose receives the terms as she receives all Augusta's terms — with the nod, the filing, the resolve. The white silk is exchanged for the evening's dress — the uniform's day done — but the verdict walks with her into the evening's calls: the congratulations warmer, the curiosity keener, the gallery's fashion already discussed. "White," the ton has decided, "for the trial. She walked in white. We shall wear —" The sentence is unfinished, the fashion undecided, but the intention is clear: the town will dress for its verdict. The afternoon's verdict, rendered by the trade, is confirmed by the ton. The loan stands. The repayment is scheduled: the morning, the court, the real one.)*
> 1. [examine]Read "the plaintiff's progress" — the phrase, sticking. → Remembered: The walk's public name; the papers will keep it.
> 2. [social]Watch the odds shorten — the trial, priced hourly. → Remembered: The street's confidence; the market moves her way.
> 3. [micro]Price the walk at sixpence — the devils' new telling. → Remembered: The story's appreciation; the look is worth sixpence.
> 4. [stance]Note Pyke's chapel, quieter — the men not meeting eyes. → Remembered: The enemy's household; the chapel is lost to him.
> 5. [examine]Distinguish men from machines — "men can be witnesses." → Remembered: The trial's human material; the chapel may testify.
> 6. [social]Receive the street's property — the walk, no longer hers. → Remembered: The legend's independence; she launched it, the street owns it.
> 7. [choice]Walk again tomorrow, or let one walk stand. → Remembered: The singularity doctrine; once, perfectly.

scenes.synopsis: rolling — the paper prints, unbuyable; the machine that cannot be bought.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Gazette's presses are rolling — the paper prints, unbuyable, the machine that cannot be bought doing its honest work in the afternoon. Rose stands in the court and listens: the thump and clatter, the paper feeding, the devils running — the same industry as the Lantern's chapel, the opposite meaning. Here the machine prints the day's news, set straight; there it printed purchased paragraphs. The difference is not the machine. The difference is the name on the wall. She thinks of the morning's closed door, the soft voice, the bag held out — the scene she did not see and will not ask about, unperformed by request — and understands what the rolling presses mean: the paper, having refused, goes on. That is the whole of the courage — not the refusal, which was a moment, but the continuation, which is a discipline. The presses roll. The paper prints. The unbuyable machine does its work in daylight, and the daylight is the point, as it has been all season. She leaves the court to the machines. The verdict is not for sale, at any price. The rolling presses get their audience — the court's idlers, the trade's apprentices, the boys who run errands and stay to watch: the machine's public, gathered. Rose watches them watch — the honest industry, admired — and thinks of the difference the name makes: the same machine, the same motions, the Gazette's paper and the Lantern's paragraphs. The audience does not know the difference. She does. The afternoon thins into evening — the presses' rhythm slowing, the day's numbers done — and the court's shadows lengthen. The paper, having refused, goes on: the continuation, the discipline, the whole of the courage. She leaves the machines to their slowing, the audience to its admiration. The presses roll. The evening comes — and the coming, she thinks, is the paper's promise: refused in the morning, rolling in the afternoon, printing in the evening, unbuyable throughout — the machine that cannot be bought, doing its honest work in daylight.)*
> 1. [micro]Hear the presses through the wall — the heart, decided. → Remembered: The evening's sound; the paper's persistence, audible.
> 2. [examine]Read the ordinary as verdict — "tonight it sounds like." → Remembered: The symbolic hearing; ordinary work becomes epic.
> 3. [stance]Stand in the lamplight, listening — the plaintiff, witness. → Remembered: Her vigil; she keeps the paper's hours.
> 4. [social]Picture Bell reading proof — ink on her finger. → Remembered: The proprietor at work; the image steadies her.
> 5. [examine]Picture the failure reported — masters who don't forgive. → Remembered: The Network's internal cost; failure has a price there.
> 6. [micro]Note "it does not know it is a symbol" — the machine's innocence. → Remembered: The press's honesty; symbols work best unknowing.
> 7. [choice]Knock, or walk on home. → Remembered: Her restraint; the paper needs no audience tonight.

scenes.synopsis: the threshold — she approaches the Lantern's court, in person; the walk's second act.
scenes.prose:
> *(The Lantern's court, in person — the walk's second act, and the threshold she has been walking toward all morning. She approaches it in white, in daylight, unhurried — the plaintiff, come to see the defendant's ground. The court's mouth is narrow, the stationer's below, the press-house above; the smell of ink and hot metal reaches her before she reaches the court. She does not go in — the walk's choreography stops at the threshold, the conduct campaign's boundary observed — but she stands in the court's mouth and looks up at the windows, and the windows, she knows, look back. Somewhere above, the chapel is at its frames; somewhere above, Pyke is at his desk. Let them see her seeing. The white silk is very white against the court's shadow. A devil on an errand stops, stares, touches his cap, runs on. The threshold holds her a full minute — the plaintiff, the court, the daylight between them. Then she walks on, the second act complete. Behind her, the press thumps. Ahead, the street. The walk goes on. The court's mouth holds her a moment longer — the threshold's discipline, the minute extended: the plaintiff, the court, the daylight between them. She thinks of what is above — the chapel, the frames, the desk — and of what will be: the trial, the courtroom, the verdict. The threshold is the season in miniature: the defendant above, the plaintiff below, the daylight between. A woman with a market basket passes, stares, curtsies. The ordinary town, going about its business, past the extraordinary court's mouth. She walks on — the second act complete, the threshold crossed in the only way the conduct campaign allows: seen, not entering. Behind her, the press thumps — the machine, manufacturing. Ahead, the street — the town, watching. The walk goes on, the white silk bright against the courts' shadows. The threshold stays behind her, holding its minute. The second act is complete — the threshold crossed in the only way the conduct campaign allows: seen, not entering, the plaintiff's discipline. And the discipline, she thinks, is the whole of the walk: the daylight, the white silk, the watching street, the verdict promised but never performed.)*
> 1. [stance]Turn back after the Strand — the second act, intended. → Remembered: The walk's design; the court was always the destination.
> 2. [examine]Find the chapel waiting, not working — the press, silent. → Remembered: The machine's first silence; the men chose it.
> 3. [micro]Hear the dropped stick clatter "like a shot." → Remembered: The morning's loudest sound; nobody picks it up.
> 4. [social]Stand in the court's mouth in white — black was the law. → Remembered: The symmetry; the chapel reads the color's promotion.
> 5. [examine]Let them see her seeing — the machinery, idle. → Remembered: The chapter's thesis, enacted; the ruin's engine, watched.
> 6. [stance]Not knock — simply stand. → Remembered: Her presence as action; knocking would diminish it.
> 7. [micro]Note the unretrieved stick — the chapel's paralysis. → Remembered: The men's awe; work itself has stopped.
> 8. [choice]Enter, or let the threshold suffice. → Remembered: The boundary's power; she enters only if he invites.

scenes.synopsis: the press interior — the press, the chapel, the proprietor's desk; she sees it all.
scenes.prose:
> *(The press-room, glimpsed through the chapel's open door — the press interior, seen because she asked to see it, and they let her, because the plaintiff in white, in daylight, is difficult to refuse. The press itself: the great machine, thumping, the paper feeding, the ink rolling — the manufacture of paragraphs, seen close. The chapel: the frames, the sticks, the sorts, the compositors at their work with ink to the elbows. The proprietor's desk: Pyke's, upstairs, not seen, but present — the showman's aerie, above the machine. She sees it all, and lets them see her seeing — the white silk among the ink, the clean name in the chapel. The men stare, then work, then stare again. It is the season's whole education in a single room: her ruin was manufactured here, by these hands, on this machine, under that desk's direction. Manufactures can be unmade. She stays a minute, no more — the threshold's discipline — and goes, leaving the chapel with the image of the plaintiff, in white, watching. The press thumps on. The image remains. The chapel's men get their minute — the compositors, the pressmen, the devils: the manufacture's hands, seen close. They stare, then work, then stare — the plaintiff, in white, among the ink. One of them — older, the chapel's father — touches his cap. It is the morning's smallest courtesy, and it stays with her: the hands that set the libels, acknowledging the plaintiff. She nods — the acknowledgment returned — and the minute is the season's whole education: her ruin was manufactured here, by these hands, on this machine. Manufactures can be unmade. The press thumps. The frames wait. The proprietor's desk is upstairs, unseen, present — the showman's aerie, above the machine. She goes — the threshold's discipline, the minute complete — leaving the chapel with the image: the plaintiff, in white, watching. The image remains. The machine goes on. The custom animation — the press interior, the chapel, the desk — holds the room like a frame holds its subject: the manufacture, seen — and the seeing, she thinks, is the plaintiff's whole education in a single room: ruin manufactured, manufactures unmade — the season's whole lesson, in metal and ink.)*
> 1. [examine]See the press "like a beast" — the machine, inside. → Remembered: The ruin's engine, anatomized; beasts can be bridled.
> 2. [micro]Smell hot metal and oil — the interior's truth. → Remembered: The press-house's honest smell; labor smells clean.
> 3. [stance]Find it magnificent — the surprise, admitted. → Remembered: Her honest awe; the machine deserves respect, the use doesn't.
> 4. [social]Climb to the proprietor's desk — the office, entered. → Remembered: The ascent; she stands where paragraphs are composed.
> 5. [examine]Read "The Plaintiff's Progress," half-set — tomorrow's headline. → Remembered: His sly tribute; he is already writing her walk.
> 6. [micro]Touch nothing — the desk, only seen. → Remembered: Her restraint in his sanctum; seeing is enough.
> 7. [stance]Let him see her seeing the headline — the double seeing. → Remembered: The mirrored watching; he knows she knows.
> 8. [choice]Comment on the headline, or leave it. → Remembered: Her silence in the office; the headline comments on itself.
