scenes.synopsis: the continental's hour — Laurent's adjacency, stated honestly; the de Varenne name. (Turns: 7)
scenes.prose:
> *(Comte Laurent de Varenne calls in the morning, before the trial's third day — a courtesy call, he says, but Rose knows better: the émigré nobleman has been turning something over all night, and the turning has brought him here. He is — as always — impossibly elegant, the continental grace that no Englishman has ever quite mastered, but underneath it this morning is something rawer: the particular anxiety of a man about to put his name to something. "Miss Hartwell," he says, and the careful French of the courtroom is gone, replaced by something more direct, "I must speak to you before I speak to them. About my — adjacency." The word hangs between them, delicate and dangerous: his adjacency to the channels, to the money, to the purse's weather across the water.)*
>
> *(What follows is the most honest quarter-hour Rose has spent with any man in this trial: Laurent, laying out his position without varnish. The de Varenne name was used — not by him, never by him, but near him, the way a great name is always used by the weather around it. Funds moved through channels he knew socially. Hands he shook in Calais drawing rooms turned out to be — handling. "I am not clean, exactly," he says, with the devastating honesty of the continent. "No émigré is, in these years. But I am not — complicit. There is a difference, and it is the only difference I have." He looks at her then, directly, the elegance set aside: "If I testify, I testify to that difference. The name, clean of the channels. Sworn. Whatever it costs me.")*
>
> *(She studies him — the raw anxiety under the elegance, the name offered up like a hostage — and understands what he is really asking: not permission, but judgment. Is the difference real? Is the name worth the swearing? She thinks of Henry's counsel — the brave tell the truth badly — and of Bell's standard — print only what the day proved — and she gives him the only answer she has: the truth as she sees it. "The difference," she says, "is real. And the court should hear it — from you, in your own voice, before Pyke's counsel makes it his." Laurent bows — the continental bow, deep and exact — and she sees the anxiety lift, fractionally, replaced by something steadier: resolve. The adjacency, stated honestly. The name, ready to be sworn. Whatever it costs.)*

scenes.synopsis: the swearing — Laurent's testimony, rehearsed; the name, clean of the channels. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *("Say it to me first," Rose says — because the courtroom will be less kind than she is, and a witness should hear his own testimony in a friendly room before he gives it in a hostile one. They are in the morning room, the lamps lit against the night's middle, and Laurent stands — he will not sit for this, the continental formality asserting itself — and begins. "My name is Laurent de Varenne." The voice is steady. "My family's name was used — not by my hand, but near it." He goes on, and Rose listens the way the court will listen: for the hesitation, the evasion, the crack. There is none. The testimony is clean the way a duelist's blade is clean: not innocent, but — exact.)*
>
> *("The channels," Laurent says, "I knew socially. The hands, I shook — in drawing rooms, in Calais. I did not know what they carried." He pauses, and the pause is the testimony's hinge: "I should have known. That is my — shame. Not my crime." Rose watches him, and the romance thread — the continental's grace, the honest quarter-hour — braids itself into the trial's rope: this is what an honorable suitor does, when the honorable thing is also the costly thing. He does not ask her to spare him. He does not ask her to use him gently. He asks only — the look says it, the formality cannot quite hide it — that she believe the difference. The name, clean of the channels. Sworn.)*
>
> *("Again," she says — the director, the general — "but slower. The court reporter must catch every word." He says it again, slower, and the second telling is better: the shame, owned; the crime, denied; the difference, held. When he finishes, the morning room is very quiet — the lamps' hiss, the night's middle, the two of them standing in the testimony's aftermath like survivors of a small, precise storm. "It will cost you," Rose says — because honesty is owed, even now, especially now. Laurent smiles, the continental smile, tired and exact: "Everything costs, Miss Hartwell. The question is only what one buys." He bows, and goes — to sleep, to the third day, to the stand. The swearing, rehearsed. The name, ready.)*

scenes.synopsis: the vanity, cracking — Rose reads Pyke's face; the sly man's limit. (Turns: 8)
scenes.prose:
> *(She replays the day's Pyke — the morning's market-stall, the colonnade's philosopher, the street door's tired man, the night's final terms — and sees, laid end to end, the thing she missed while living it: the vanity, cracking. It was there in the colonnade, under the calculation: the flicker when she refused, the instant's revision. It was there at the street door, under the tiredness: the philosopher, performing weariness because the performance of honesty was the only move left. And it was there at night, under the final terms: the doubt, weaponized — the sly man's whisper, which was also his confession. A man who is winning does not weaponize doubt. A man who is winning does not need to. The vanity is cracking, and the cracks are where the light — Bell's light, the *Gazette's* light, the court's light — gets in.)*
>
> *(She thinks of what vanity is, in a man like Pyke — not the dandy's vanity, the mirror's, but the proprietor's: the belief that the paper is the man, that the *Lantern's* survival is his survival, that to be unmade in print is to be unmade in fact. It is why he offered the retraction: not generosity, but self-preservation — the paper drawing its own poison before the court draws it. It is why he warned her about the Ledger's teeth: the paper, defending its own. And it is why the cracks matter: vanity, in a proprietor, is structural. Crack it, and the whole edition — the whole man — comes apart in your hands. Lavinia understood this first: broken, not bought. You do not buy a vain man. You break the thing he cannot live without, and let him watch.)*
>
> *(The night's middle deepens, and Rose sits with the cracked vanity the way she sat with the whisper's arithmetic: itemized, examined, filed. The cracks: the colonnade's flicker, the street door's performance, the night's weaponized doubt. The structure: the paper-is-the-man. The breaking: the witnesses, unmade; the ink, thinning; the town, decided. It is — she realizes, with the particular clarity of the small hours — the oldest story in the world: the man who believed his own edition. Pyke printed the libels. The libels are being unprinted — not retracted, unmade — by the evidence, the witnesses, the town. And the vanity, which was the engine, is becoming the wreckage. She banks the thought with the lamps, and goes — at last — toward sleep, with the cracks mapped and the morning coming: the Ledger's day, the last card, the counsel's mouth, opening.)*

> *(Henry comes late — the major's hour, the round before sleep — and finds her in the morning room's dark with the lamps banked and the two documents on the table. He does not comment on the hour. Soldiers do not comment on hours; they keep them. "Tomorrow's ground," he says, standing at the window where Pyke stood that morning, where Rose stood at noon, where the day's weathers have all passed through — "I have walked it." The quartermaster's report, the night's edition: the courtroom's layout, the counsel's table, the witness box's sight lines, the gallery's mood at day's end. "The Ledger," he says, "will be examined where everyone can see it. Creech's book, open on the clerk's desk. The ledger — in full — faced in daylight. As you decided.")*
>
> *(She tells him about Lavinia's intelligence — the last card, the old filth, the ally offered up as the play — and Henry takes it the way he takes everything: as terrain. "Then the third day," he says, "has two battlefields. The Ledger's, and Lavinia's." He turns from the window, and the banked lamps' red catches the uniform — he is still in it, the major's day unended — and does the thing he does when the professional counsel is finished: he looks at her directly. "You will be —" the pause, the man's pause under the major's — "outnumbered, at moments. Remember the corridor." The corridor: the hundred yards, the sea parted, the walk that was only pleasant. Remember the discipline. Remember the waiting, well.)*
>
> *(Before he goes — the round, resuming — he puts his hand on the two documents: the edition, the account sheet. The public, the private. "The Park," he says, "is in good order. The trial" — the hand lifts, the quartermaster's arithmetic done — "is in your hands." It is the most complete trust he has ever stated, and he states it the way he states everything: exactly, and without decoration. Then the major's hour ends, and he is gone — the stairs, the door, the night — leaving Rose in the banked red with the night watch kept and tomorrow's ground walked. The Ledger's day. Lavinia's battlefield. The last card, unplayed. The counsel's mouth — still closed. But morning is coming, and the ground has been walked, and the watch — kept.)*

Not tonight. The last card is unplayed. The counsel's mouth is closed. scenes.synopsis: the cliffhanger's answer — the card, checked; the ledger is Rose's answer.
scenes.prose:
> *(The counsel opens his mouth — and the judge raises one hand, the way a man stops a carriage. The courtroom, which has been holding its breath since yesterday's adjournment, lets it out in a sound like a sail losing wind. "Mr. —" the judge says, with the particular mildness of the judiciary about to be immovable, "— you will not read that paper as evidence. What the *Lantern* printed about Lady Lavinia's family, years ago, is not evidence in this action. It is —" he seeks the word precisely, the way a man seeks the right weight "— atmosphere. This court does not try atmosphere." Counsel stands with the paper in his hand and the whole courtroom watching the card go back into the sleeve — unplayed, again, held through another morning of losing. "The defense," counsel says, through something very like teeth, "reserves." He sits. The last card, unplayed. Still. The gallery exhales. Rose does not.)**
> *(Quill rises before the echo fades — the timing exact, the way he does everything. "The plaintiff calls Mr. Creech." Into the well walks a small, grey, precise man with a ledger under his arm — the paper supplier — and Rose feels the whole courtroom lean forward: the town, come to see the purse. Creech takes the oath with the care of a man who weighs paper for a living and therefore weighs everything, each word placed like a weight on a scale. Pyke, two rows behind his counsel, has gone very still — the folded-hands stillness — because he knows, the way a proprietor knows his own accounts, what is in that ledger. The card is back in the sleeve. The ledger is on the table. The ledger is Rose's answer — paper answering paper, in the open, where the town can watch.)*
> *(She settles in her seat and feels the day arrange itself around the ledger the way iron arranges itself around a magnet. The card checked, the witness called, the town leaning forward — this is the shape of the third day, and she knows its weight before a single column has been read. Creech opens the book. The courtroom leans further. Somewhere behind her, Fane's lorgnette comes up. The ledger's day has begun, and Rose — who has spent two days watching witnesses be unmade — understands, with a small cold clarity, that today the unmaking runs the other direction: not the witnesses, but the paper. Not the men, but the money. The account, stated.)**

> 3. [examine]See the card go back — unplayed, again. → Remembered: The reserve's second reprieve; held through another morning of losing, it grows heavier.
> 4. [micro]Note counsel's teeth — "the defense reserves." → Remembered: The cost of the holding; the sleeve is wearing thin.
> 5. [social]Feel the courtroom lean — the town, come for the purse. → Remembered: Fane's prediction, fulfilled; the audience is here for Creech, not the card.
> 6. [examine]Study Creech's oath — the weigher, weighing. → Remembered: The supplier's precision; a man who weighs paper weighs everything.
> 7. [examine]Read Pyke's stillness — the folded hands. → Remembered: The proprietor's knowledge; he knows his own accounts, and what the ledger holds.
> 8. [choice]"The ledger is Rose's answer" — receive the turn. → Remembered: Her chosen weapon for the day; paper answers paper, in the open.

scenes.synopsis: the morning conference — the ledger's plan; Creech's courage, priced and protected.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill's chambers, dawn, and the plan is laid out like the ledger itself — in columns. The candles are still lit against the grey morning, and the papers on the desk are arranged with the surveyor's precision Quill brings to everything: Creech's statement, the account summary, the list of questions in the order they will be asked. "Creech," Quill says, "has supplied the *Lantern* for six years. His book shows quantities no penny sheet affords — reams beyond honest circulation, paid in coin, never through Pyke's office. He will testify to the quantities, the payments, and the hand." "The hand?" Rose asks. "A cutout's," Quill says. "The same hand that paid our forty-pound witness and Larkin's stack. One hand — one purse behind it — and Creech's book is where the purse touches paper.")**
> "Is he afraid?" Rose asks.
> "He is a paper supplier," Quill says, "testifying against the purse that buys his paper. Of course he is afraid. I have told him the court will protect him, which is true, and that you will remember him, which is also true." He looks at her. "Will you?"
> *("Is he afraid?" Rose asks — and the question surprises her by how much it matters. Quill looks up from the columns. "He is a paper supplier," he says, "testifying against the purse that buys his paper. Of course he is afraid. "Will you?" Rose thinks of the gutter's geography and adds the station the trial has been walking toward since the first day: the supplier, behind the press. The purse, behind the supplier. "Tell him," she says, "that the Hartwell account will buy its paper from Creech for as long as he sells it. The clean name remembers its friends." Quill writes it down — the promise, entered like a column. The almost-smile crosses his face and is gone: the profession's permit, granted.)*
> *(They walk through the plan once more — the quantities first, then the payments, then the hand — and Rose feels the day's architecture settle: columns, like the ledger. "And Miss Hartwell —" Quill says as she rises to go, "when the chain is traced, the question of the purse will be yours. Name it, hold it, or let the cutout name it. The first decision of the day." She nods. The corridor is filling with the trial's morning traffic — clerks, counsel, the ton arriving early for the ledger's day. She walks into it with the plan in columns behind her eyes and the promise to Creech like a weight in her pocket: paper, for as long as sold. The clean name remembers. Today it will prove it.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Study the columns — the plan, ledgered. → Remembered: Quill's columnar thinking; the day is ordered like the book itself.
> 2. [stance]Ask "is he afraid" — the witness's due. → Remembered: Her care for the courage she is spending; witnesses are not exhibits.
> 3. [examine]Weigh the two truths — the court's protection, her memory. → Remembered: The promises made to Creech; both must be kept.
> 4. [social]Give the Hartwell account — paper, for as long as sold. → Remembered: Her patronage as protection; the clean name remembers its friends.
> 5. [micro]Note the almost-smile — the profession's permit. → Remembered: Quill's approval; the promise was the right one.
> 6. [examine]Add the station — the supplier, behind the press. → Remembered: The geography's completion; the map now reaches the money.
> 7. [stance]Receive "the question of the purse will be yours" — the first decision. → Remembered: The day's coming choice; name it, hold it, or let the cutout.
> 8. [choice]Promise loudly or quietly — the patronage's register. → Remembered: How the promise travels; quiet patronage is the more durable kind.

scenes.synopsis: the paper supplier takes the stand — the ledger, entered as exhibit.
scenes.prose:
> *(Mr. Creech climbs into the witness box with his ledger held the way other men hold a child — carefully, as if it might be taken from him — and the courtroom regards him with the attention it reserves for men about to be brave. He is small, grey, precise: thirty years weighing paper, able to tell you to the ream what a penny sheet should consume, the kind of man whose hands have learned honesty the way other men's learn trades. Quill leads him gently — the business, the years, the *Lantern's* account, each question a step — and then, the voice dropping to the register that means the point has arrived: "Mr. Creech, will you tell the court what the *Lantern* bought?" Creech opens the ledger. The courtroom leans. The reading begins — dates, quantities, prices, the columns marching in the precise unlovely hand, and the numbers doing what numbers do: testifying where words merely claim.)**
> *(The quantities unspool like a confession: reams, and reams — paper bought far beyond the *Lantern's* honest circulation, beyond what its advertised sales could consume, beyond what any penny sheet could honestly use. Rose watches the jury's foreman do the arithmetic in the air — the pencil moving, stopping, moving again — and watches Pyke's counsel sit very still, the way men sit when the numbers are doing the testifying and there is no cross-examination for arithmetic. "And these quantities," Quill says, "were they — usual?" "No," Creech says, with the quiet finality of a man who weighs things for a living. "They were — campaign quantities." The phrase lands like a stone in the pond. The paper for a war, bought by the ream, and the *Lantern* is a penny sheet. The ledger is entered. The courtroom has been shown the size of the lie, measured in paper.)*
> *(She watches the phrase travel — *campaign quantities* — from the witness box to the jury's notes to the gallery's murmur, and understands that the trial has just been given its defining measure. Not lies, but quantities. Not malice, but reams. The *Lantern* did not hate; it was funded — and funding has a size, a weight, a paper trail. Creech closes the ledger with the care of a man putting a child down to sleep, and the courtroom's attention follows his hands. The brave man, having been brave, sits very straight. Rose thinks of the Hartwell account's promise — paper, for as long as sold — and knows it was the right promise, made at the right time, to the right man. The ledger has spoken. The town will never unread it.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the ledger held — like a child. → Remembered: The supplier's care; the book is brave before the man is.
> 2. [stance]Regard the brave — the court's attention. → Remembered: How the room honors courage; attention is the courtroom's applause.
> 3. [examine]Hear the quantities unspool — the confession. → Remembered: The reams beyond honesty; the lie has a size, and it is measured in paper.
> 4. [micro]Note the foreman's pencil — moving, stopping, moving. → Remembered: The jury's arithmetic; the numbers testify where words merely claim.
> 5. [social]Watch counsel's stillness — the numbers, testifying. → Remembered: The defense's silence; there is no cross-examination for arithmetic.
> 6. [examine]Take "campaign quantities" — the phrase, landed. → Remembered: The supplier's own words; a penny sheet does not buy for a war.
> 7. [stance]Receive the exhibit number — read aloud. → Remembered: The ledger's formal entry; it is evidence now, not merely a book.
> 8. [choice]Watch Pyke or the jury — the proprietor or the box. → Remembered: Where her attention goes; the box is today's work, the proprietor tomorrow's.

scenes.synopsis: the payments — coin, never notes; the hand that never touched Pyke's office.
scenes.prose:
> "The quantities are established," Quill says. "Now the payments, Mr. Creech. How was this paper paid for?"
> "In coin," Creech says. "Always in coin. Never in notes, never by draft, never through the usual channels."
> "Coin," Quill repeats, for the jury, the gallery, the record. "And from whose hand?"
> *(Creech hesitates — a brave man naming the thing he fears — and then, the words placed like weights: "Not from Mr. Pyke's office. A cutout came with a purse. The purse paid. The office never saw the coin." The courtroom is very quiet now, the way courtrooms get when the money is discussed — money being the one subject the ton pretends not to understand and understands perfectly. "Describe the purse," Quill says. And Creech describes it: not Pyke's, not the *Lantern's* — a purse from further off, paying for campaign quantities in coin through a cutout's hand, the money arriving like weather from a direction no one in the office ever looked. The purse behind the ink. The hand that never touched Pyke's office, carrying coin that never saw a draft or a note.)**
> "One more question," Quill says. "In thirty years of weighing paper, have you ever seen a penny sheet supplied like this?"
> "No," Creech says. "A penny sheet buys what it sells. This —" he touches the ledger "— this was a paper being *funded*. There is a difference, and the difference is in the columns."
> *("Always in coin," Creech says, when Quill asks about the payments. "Never notes. Never drafts." The sentence sits in the courtroom like a stone in a shoe — coin being the purse's handwriting, the signature of money that does not want to be traced. Rose watches the ton receive it: the Directresses very still, Fane's lorgnette steady, the cipher-clerk writing faster. They understand coin. They have always understood coin. And Quill, mild as milk, lays the doctrine beside it: funded, not sold; supplied, not earned. The *Lantern* was not a business that took a bribe. It was a campaign that took funding. The difference is in the columns — and the columns are now the court's.)*
> *(She writes the sentence in her notebook in capital letters, the way she has written every sentence that matters this season: FUNDED, NOT SOLD. The purse from further off. The office clean, the campaign dirty, the deniability intact right up to the moment the ledger opened. She looks at Pyke — two rows back, the folded-hands stillness — and sees him doing his own arithmetic: the office never saw the coin, which was the whole design, and the design has just been described, under oath, by the man who weighed the paper. The divide, stated. The proprietor's deniability, and its limit. The trial has found the purse's edge.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear "always in coin" — never notes, never drafts. → Remembered: The payment's signature; coin is the purse's handwriting.
> 2. [social]Mark the brave man's hesitation — naming the fear. → Remembered: Creech's courage, priced; the hesitation is the measure of it.
> 3. [examine]Take "the office never saw the coin" — the divide. → Remembered: The proprietor's deniability, and its limit; the office is clean, the campaign is not.
> 4. [micro]Note the ton's quiet — money, discussed. → Remembered: The room's true attention; the ton understands coin perfectly.
> 5. [stance]Receive "funded, not sold" — the difference, in the columns. → Remembered: The supplier's doctrine; the ledger distinguishes what the eye cannot.
> 6. [examine]File the second sentence — next to the chapel's. → Remembered: The two sentences, paired; the gutter's whole economy in twelve words.
> 7. [social]Watch the purse described — from further off. → Remembered: The distance, stated; further off than the office, closer than the face.
> 8. [choice]Honor Creech now or later — the brave man's due. → Remembered: When the patronage is spoken; the Hartwell account's promise wants airing.

scenes.synopsis: texture — ink, columns, the truth: in a supplier's hand.
scenes.prose:
> *(In the recess Rose asks to see it — the ledger, the exhibit — and the clerk brings it to her in the corridor with the ceremony of a man handling a relic. It is a plain book, bound in calf worn smooth by thirty years of hands, and the columns march across its pages in Creech's precise, unlovely hand: dates, quantities, prices, the little tick-marks of a man who trusts nothing to memory. She turns the pages slowly — the *Lantern's* account, year by year, the honest years and then the campaign year, when the quantities triple and the payments change from notes to coin. There it is, in ink: the exact month the penny sheet became a weapon. The turn, dated. The corruption, columned. She holds the book the way Creech held it — carefully, as if it might be taken — and feels the weight of thirty years of honest weighing behind the one dishonest account.)**
> *(She thinks of all the paper she has kept this season — the *Lantern* and the *Gazette* side by side in the drawer, Lavinia's father's file, Quill's three papers — and understands this is the purest of them: no rhetoric, no performance, just columns. Ink doesn't lie the way men do; it only records, and the recording is the lie's undoing. A clerk's hand. A cutout's purse. A coin from further off than the courtroom can see. She closes the book and hands it back, her fingers leaving no mark on the calf — thirty years of hands, and hers among them now, briefly, the latest in the ledger's long line of handlers. The ledger has been read aloud. The town will never unread it. The exhibit goes back to the clerk, and she goes back to the courtroom, and the afternoon's work waits: the coin, traced backward, to the purse.)*
> *(The corridor is full of the recess's noise — counsel conferring, the ton murmuring, the clerks hurrying — but the ledger's silence follows her: the plain book, the worn calf, the columns. She thinks of the archive's drawer at home, and where this exhibit would rank among the season's papers: above the rhetoric, below nothing. The purest. She has asked the clerk for a copy for the archive — the auditor's habit — and he has promised it. The court's book, and hers. The truth, in a supplier's hand, in duplicate.)**
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Handle the relic — calf, worn smooth. → Remembered: The book's physical truth; thirty years of hands have earned its authority.
> 2. [micro]Find the exact month — the turn, in ink. → Remembered: When the penny sheet became a weapon; the columns date the corruption precisely.
> 3. [examine]Weigh "ink doesn't lie the way men do" — the doctrine. → Remembered: Her faith in the recorded; the recording is the lie's undoing.
> 4. [stance]Place it among the archive — the purest. → Remembered: The season's papers, ranked; columns outrank rhetoric.
> 5. [social]Leave no mark — hers among the hands. → Remembered: Her brief touch of the evidence; thirty years, and her fingers, briefly.
> 6. [examine]Hear "the town will never unread it" — the permanence. → Remembered: The reading's irreversibility; aloud is forever, in this town.
> 7. [choice]Ask for a copy or trust the exhibit — the auditor's habit. → Remembered: Whether the archive wants its own; the drawer grows, or the court keeps it.

scenes.synopsis: the coin, traced — from Creech's counter to the cutout's hand; the rope, tightening.
scenes.prose:
> *(The afternoon session opens with Quill tracing the coin — not the paper now, but the money: from Creech's counter, backward, through the cutout's hand, toward the purse. It is the trial's most delicate work, done with the same terrible mildness he has brought to every unmaking — the surgeon's work, near the heart. The cutout's payments to Creech: dates, amounts, always coin — and then the turn, the question the whole courtroom has been waiting for: the cutout's *own* payments, the money that filled the cutout's purse, coming from further off. "And where," Quill asks, "did the cutout's coin come from?" Creech looks at the judge; the judge nods; and Creech says, with the quiet finality of the brave: "From the purse. The same purse. One purse, through the whole of it.")**
> *(One purse, through the whole of it. The courtroom receives the sentence the way it received *campaign quantities* — as a stone in the pond, the ripples reaching every bench. Rose watches the foreman write it down — *one purse* — and watches Pyke's counsel rise to object, then sit again without objecting, the way men sit when the objection would only underline the sentence. The rope tightens: the forty-pound witness, Larkin's stack, Creech's reams — all one hand, one purse, one coin that never touched Pyke's office. The bought campaign, proved not as a scatter of bribes but as a single funded operation, with a single source. The proprietor has stopped calculating and started enduring. The vanity's exit; what remains is sly and cornered.)*
> *(She counts the rope's strands the way Quill taught her to count everything: forty pounds, the stack, the reams — three payments, one purse. The trial's turn, accomplished in an afternoon: the coin walked backward from the counter to the hand to the purse, each step testified, each step columned. Tomorrow the purse will be described to its edge. Tonight the town will do its sums. She watches Pyke's lamp — the brightness he has carried all trial — turn down to calculation, and understands that the cornered slyness is more dangerous than the vain, the way a cornered animal is. But the rope is tight. The chain is traced. The purse is next.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the surgeon's work — near the heart. → Remembered: Quill's delicacy with the money; the mildness is the scalpel.
> 2. [stance]Hear "one purse, through the whole of it" — the sentence. → Remembered: The operation's unity; not bribes, but a single funded campaign.
> 3. [micro]Note counsel rising, sitting — the unmade objection. → Remembered: The defense's paralysis; objecting would only underline it.
> 4. [examine]Study Pyke's lamp, turned down — calculation, remaining. → Remembered: The vanity's exit; what remains is sly and cornered, which is more dangerous.
> 5. [social]Feel the ripples — every bench, reached. → Remembered: The sentence's travel; one purse lands everywhere at once.
> 6. [examine]Count the rope's strands — forty pounds, the stack, the reams. → Remembered: The single operation, itemized; the hand is one, the purse is one.
> 7. [stance]Receive the tightening — the trial's turn. → Remembered: The afternoon's momentum; the coin is being walked backward to its source.
> 8. [choice]Watch Pyke or the foreman — the cornered or the convinced. → Remembered: Where her attention goes; the box writes, the proprietor calculates.

scenes.synopsis: the purse behind the ink — described, under oath; the face, pointedly not described.
scenes.prose:
> "Mr. Creech," Quill says, "you have described the purse. Now describe — if you can — what lies behind it."
> *(Creech looks at the judge. The judge looks at Quill. The courtroom holds the stillness of a room about to be told what it has waited all trial to hear — the question Quill has been walking toward since the first column was read. "Mr. Creech," Quill says, gently, "the purse that paid you — the one purse, through the whole of it. Did you ever see — further than the purse?" The pause is the longest of the trial. Creech's hands rest flat on the ledger, the brave man's hands, the weigher's hands. "No," he says. "I never saw further than the purse.")**
> "I cannot," Creech says. "The purse paid. The purse kept its own counsel. I never saw —" he hesitates "— further than the purse."
> "Further than the purse," Quill repeats. "You are certain there *is* further?"
> "A purse like that," Creech says, with the quiet authority of a man who has weighed money for thirty years, "does not fill itself. Coin in those quantities, paid through a cutout's hand — that is not a proprietor's strongbox. That is — an operation's purse. Someone fills it. I never saw who."
> *(And there it is — the line the trial cannot cross, stated by its bravest witness: the purse is proved, the face behind it is not. Rose feels the whole courtroom understand at once that the coin has a master, and the master is not in this courtroom — the ton's quick arithmetic, done in silence, the foreman's pencil still. Quill lets the sentence stand the way he lets all his best sentences stand: unadorned, unargued, the letting-stand itself the technique. "No further questions," he says. And the purse — one purse, through the whole of it, filled by someone Creech never saw, deep, never running dry — sits in the well of the court like a thing with weight, while the face behind it stays offstage, unnamed, unshown, exactly where it has been all season.)*
> *(She accepts the boundary the way she has accepted every honest limit this trial: with discipline. The coin is enough for this courtroom. The purse, proved; the face, unproved and unmentioned — the trial's honest horizon. She watches counsel for the defense and sees the disappointment: the reach never came, and the mockery starves. There will be no demanded-and-missing face to turn into doubt. There will be only the purse, sitting in the well like a stone, and the town doing its sums around it. The chain ends at the purse's edge. Beyond the edge — the offstage, the season beyond the trial, the meeting that is coming. Not here. Not now. The discipline holds — the way a fence holds, because it was built to hold, and Quill built this one.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear "I never saw further than the purse" — the line. → Remembered: The trial's boundary, stated; the purse is proved, the face is not.
> 2. [stance]Receive the court's understanding — at once. → Remembered: The ton's quick arithmetic; the master is not in this courtroom, and all know it.
> 3. [examine]Weigh "an operation's purse" — the supplier's authority. → Remembered: Creech's thirty years, distilled; strongboxes and operations are different animals.
> 4. [micro]Note Quill's letting-stand — unadorned, unargued. → Remembered: Counsel's best technique; the sentence needs no help.
> 5. [social]Feel the weight in the well — the thing, sitting. → Remembered: The purse's presence; proved things have gravity, even unnamed.
> 6. [examine]Study the offstage — unnamed, unshown, all season. → Remembered: The face's consistent absence; it has never been here, and will not be.
> 7. [stance]Accept the boundary — the coin is enough. → Remembered: Her discipline of appetite; this courtroom needs the purse, not the face.
> 8. [choice]Press Creech further or let him rest — the brave man's limit. → Remembered: Whether the witness is spent gently; he has given the trial its line.

scenes.synopsis: three hands — the cutout, the purse, the Network's coin; traced, in the open.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill traces it for the jury slowly, the way a drawing master traces a hand for pupils: three hands, one chain. The first hand: the cutout, who carried the coin to Creech's counter, to Larkin's corner, to the forty-pound witness's door — the carrier, the middle link, the man who never asked. The second hand: the purse, that filled the cutout's hand — one purse, through the whole of it, deep, never running dry, that never touched Pyke's office. The third hand: further off than the courtroom can see — the Network's coin, the operation's purse, filled by someone Creech never saw. Three hands. One chain. Traced, in the open, with the ledger as its spine. The bought campaign, proved as a single funded operation.)**
> *(Rose watches the jury follow — the foreman's pencil moving with Quill's hand, the box learning the chain the way pupils learn a hand — and the gallery too: Fane's lorgnette retrained on the tracing, the Directresses leaning, the cipher-clerk in the back row writing faster than he has all trial, someone else mapping the limits too. The ton is doing its sums, and the sums say: the *Lantern* did not merely print lies; it was *paid* to print them, by a purse, from further off, through three hands. Pyke's slyness — he prints, never threatens — is intact and irrelevant: the printing was the weapon, and the weapon was bought. His counsel sits with his case in pieces and his last card still in his sleeve, and Rose understands why it was held so long: it is the only furniture left in an empty room.)*
> *(She savors the tracing the way Quill savored the letting-stand — but stays hungry, the way he taught her. The chain is complete to the purse. The purse's edge is the trial's horizon. Beyond it, the face — unnamed, unshown, all season — waits its own season. She knows this the way she knows her own handwriting, and the knowing is a discipline: the purse is enough. The coin is enough. The verdict does not need the master. The chain, complete, in the open. The town, summing. The card, still sleeved — the only thing left, and everyone in the courtroom knows it.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Follow the drawing — the pupils, learning. → Remembered: The jury's slow rhythm; the chain is taught like a hand, and learned.
> 2. [stance]Count the three hands — cutout, purse, coin. → Remembered: The chain's anatomy; each hand is a station, each station testified.
> 3. [examine]Watch the cipher-clerk write faster — the back row. → Remembered: The unfamiliar piece, excited; someone else is tracing too.
> 4. [micro]Note Fane's lorgnette, retrieved — retrained. → Remembered: The artillery, back in action; the chain deserves the full lens.
> 5. [social]Feel the ton's sums — the printing was bought. → Remembered: The town's verdict on the mechanism; paid-to-print is worse than merely printing.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the intact slyness — irrelevant. → Remembered: The villain's remaining virtue; printing-never-threatening no longer matters.
> 7. [stance]Understand the held card — the only thing left. → Remembered: The sleeve's emptiness; everything else traced, the card is the last furniture.
> 8. [choice]Savor the tracing or stay hungry — the chain, complete. → Remembered: Her appetite's discipline; the purse is traced, the face is not, and she knows it.

scenes.synopsis: ★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — THE PURSE (Turns: 3 — the decision).
scenes.prose:
> *(The recess finds them in the corridor, and Quill lays it out with the gravity of a man handling something with weight. The purse is proved — the chain complete, the coin traced, the ledger admitted. The question is how — and whether — the trial names its workings in open court. Quill counts the choices on his fingers, the way he counts everything: name it, and put the operation's purse on the record, its workings described, the Network's coin named as coin, the jury and the Gazette carrying the name out of this building. Hold it, and keep the purse's workings back — for the reckoning beyond the trial, for the meeting that is coming, for the season beyond the trial's walls. Or let the cutout name it — put the carrier on the stand, and let the purse be described in his voice, not ours, the gutter naming the purse. Rose weighs the gravity: the decision's heft, the trial's heaviest exhibit. The record, named, carried everywhere — the Gazette's amplification. The later meeting, priced — S4's door, the purse kept back as a weapon for the masquerade. The fragile vessel — the cutout's voice, authentic and breakable. And the boundary, noted: the face stays offstage regardless. No choice names the face. Only the purse.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 1/3 — The purse:*
- **Name it in court** — *Openness+; the record complete.* Put the operation's purse on the record — its workings described, the Network's coin named as coin. *(Quill approves the boldness; the Gazette will carry it everywhere; the face stays offstage regardless.)*
- **Hold the name** — *Patience+; the later meeting.* Keep the purse's workings back — for the reckoning beyond the trial, for S4's door. *(Quill calls it the general's choice; the jury convicts on the chain without the name.)*
- **Let the cutout name it** — *Distance+; his voice, not hers.* The carrier testifies — the purse described by the hand that carried it. *(Quill warns the cutout is a fragile vessel; Lavinia calls it elegant — let the gutter name the purse.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the naming, the holding, the carrier's voice. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the purse's keeper, on the stand — the chain, complete to the purse.
scenes.prose:
> *(He is brought in the afternoon — the cutout, the man who carried the purse — and he is the least impressive villain the courtroom has seen all trial: a clerk's coat, a clerk's hands, a clerk's careful blankness, the kind of man who has made a career of being unmemorable. Quill leads him the way one leads a mule — patiently, expecting obstinacy — and the cutout answers the way mules walk: slowly, and only where led. Yes, he carried coin. Yes, to Creech's counter, to the hawker's corner, to the witness's door. Yes, from one purse. The purse's keeper, describing his keeping: the purse filled his hand, his hand filled the gutter, and he never asked whose purse it was. Asking, it turns out, is above his station.)**
> *(It is the least theatrical testimony of the trial and, Rose thinks, the most complete — the chain, complete to the purse, in the voice of the man who *was* the chain's middle link. No embroidery. Just the clerk's blankness, stating under oath that the coin came from one purse, that the purse never touched Pyke's office, that he never saw further than the purse. The foreman does not even write — he simply nods once, the way men nod when the last piece of a puzzle is placed by someone else's hand. The chain is complete: cutout, purse, coin — traced, in the open, to the purse's edge. Beyond the edge, the face — unasked, unanswered, offstage.)*
> *(She studies the keeper as he steps down — the unmemorable man, the career of blankness — and feels something between pity and indictment: carriers are not masters, but hands are hands, and his hands carried the coin that bought the *Lantern's* war. Quill thanks him with the courtesy he extends to all witnesses, used but not abused. The courtroom's attention follows the cutout out, and then returns to the well, where the purse sits — proved, described, complete to its edge. The middle link, having testified, dissolves back into blankness. The chain remains. The purse remains. The face stays offstage, where it has been all season, where it will stay until its own season comes.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Study the unmemorable — the career of blankness. → Remembered: The cutout's professional invisibility; unmemorable is the job's requirement.
> 2. [stance]Watch the mule, led — patiently. → Remembered: Quill's handling; obstinacy is led, not driven.
> 3. [examine]Hear the keeping described — purse to hand to gutter. → Remembered: The chain's middle link, testifying; the keeping is the testimony.
> 4. [micro]Note the foreman's nod — the puzzle, placed. → Remembered: The jury's completion; no notes needed when the last piece fits.
> 5. [social]Receive the least theatrical — the most complete. → Remembered: The paradox of the plain witness; blankness convinces where theater merely moves.
> 6. [examine]Weigh "never saw further than the purse" — the edge. → Remembered: The chain's terminus; the purse's edge is the trial's horizon.
> 7. [stance]Accept the enough — the purse, for this courtroom. → Remembered: Her discipline of sufficiency; the face is not needed for the verdict.
> 8. [choice]Pity the clerk or indict him — the keeper's due. → Remembered: Her judgment of the middle link; carriers are not masters, but hands are hands.

scenes.synopsis: the keeper, questioned — what the hand knew, and what it never asked.
scenes.prose:
> "You carried coin," Quill says. "For how long?"
> "Two years," the cutout says. "Thereabouts."
> "And in those two years, did you ever ask —" Quill pauses the way he pauses before the important ones "— whose coin it was?"
> "No."
> "Never?"
> "The purse paid," the cutout says, with the clerk's blank finality. "The purse was sufficient. A man in my position does not ask whose. Asking is — above my station."
> *(Quill's examination is a surgeon's work — each question placed with terrible mildness, each answer drawn like a tooth. "You carried coin," Quill says. "For how long?" "Two years," the cutout says. "Thereabouts." "And in those two years, did you ever ask —" Quill pauses the way he pauses before the important ones "— whose coin it was?" "No." "Never?" "The purse paid," the cutout says, with the clerk's blank finality. "The purse was sufficient. Asking is — above my station." Rose listens, and the sentence settles over the courtroom like dust: *asking is above my station*. The gutter's whole philosophy in five words. The chain's design, stated by the chain itself.)**
> "One more question," Quill says. "The purse — did it ever run dry?"
> "No."
> "In two years — of campaign quantities, of forty-pound witnesses, of hawkers paid by the stack — the purse never ran dry?"
> "No," the cutout says. "It was —" and here the blankness cracks, just slightly, the way ice cracks "— it was a deep purse."
> *("One more question," Quill says. "The purse — did it ever run dry?" "No." "In two years — of campaign quantities, of forty-pound witnesses, of hawkers paid by the stack — the purse never ran dry?" "No," the cutout says. The courtroom hears it — the foreman writes *deep* in his notes and underlines it, the jury's emphasis on the purse's defining fact. A purse that never ran dry through two years of buying a paper's war: not a proprietor's strongbox, not a grudge's savings — an operation's purse, deep, filled from further off than the courtroom can see. The keeper's one poetry, and it lands like a stone.)*
> *(Quill sits. The keeper has kept his last secret — whose, unasked — and given everything else: the two years, the depth, the sufficiency of the purse. The chain is complete to the purse. The face behind it stays offstage, where it has been all season. Rose watches the ton do its sums — deep purses are not grudges, they are operations, and the town understands operations the way it understands coin: perfectly. The dust settles. Five words explain two years. The keeper, having testified, is led out the way mules are led — patiently — and the courtroom sits with what he left: the depth, the blankness, the unasked question hanging in the air like smoke.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear "asking is above my station" — the philosophy. → Remembered: The gutter's creed, stated; unasking is the chain's design.
> 2. [stance]Receive the dust-settling — the courtroom's intake. → Remembered: How the room takes the creed; five words explain two years.
> 3. [examine]Watch the blankness crack — "a deep purse." → Remembered: The keeper's one poetry; the ice cracks on the purse's depth.
> 4. [micro]Note the foreman's underline — *deep*. → Remembered: The jury's emphasis; depth is the purse's defining fact.
> 5. [social]Feel the ton's sums — the operation's scale. → Remembered: The town's arithmetic; deep purses are not grudges, they are operations.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the kept secret — whose, unasked. → Remembered: The keeper's last withholding; the face stays his, and offstage.
> 7. [stance]Accept the completeness — to the purse, no further. → Remembered: The chain's honest end; complete does not mean total.
> 8. [choice]Thank the keeper or dismiss him — the witness's due. → Remembered: How the trial treats its middle links; used, not honored, but not abused.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the ton does its sums; the deep purse, digesting.
scenes.prose:
> *(The murmur has changed its pitch — Rose, connoisseur of the ton's murmur the way other women are connoisseurs of tea, notes the new note underneath: not excitement now, but calculation. A deep purse. Campaign quantities. One purse, through the whole of it. The arithmetic is simple and devastating: the *Lantern* was not a paper that printed lies; it was a weapon that was *funded* — and funded from further off than Fleet Street, by a purse that never ran dry. She catches fragments as she moves through the corridor — "two years," "never ran dry," "whose, do you think" — and the last fragment dies unanswered everywhere, because the answer is offstage, and all know it, and the town has learned not to ask what the courtroom cannot hear.)**
> *(Mrs. Almeria Fane has her lorgnette trained on Pyke now — not the witnesses, the proprietor — and the shift is the ton's verdict in miniature: the paper is done being interesting, the man is what's left to watch. The Lady Directresses are passing notes hand to hand, Almack's conducting its own trial in the gallery — and Rose sees the social verdict forming: the *Lantern* is not merely disgraced, it is *explained* — bought, funded, operated — and explained things are manageable. The town fears mysteries; it merely bankrupts explanations. The deep purse sits in the well of the court like a thing with gravity, and the town orbits what it cannot lift, doing its sums in the murmur's new pitch.)*
> *(She walks the corridor with the sums ringing in her ears and understands the town's fear for what it is: mysteries terrify, explanations merely bankrupt, and the *Lantern* has just become an explanation. The water rounds the stone. The sums move. She could stop listening — the sums will be reported anyway, by Bell, by Fane, by every table in London — but she is a connoisseur, and connoisseurs keep tasting. The murmur follows her out into the street: calculation, not excitement. The town has moved from hearing to summing. The ledger's day, digested. The purse, proved. The face — unasked, unanswered, offstage — and the town, having summed, moves on to the spending of its sums.)**
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Note the pitch change — calculation, not excitement. → Remembered: The murmur's new note; the town has moved from hearing to summing.
> 2. [micro]Catch the dying fragment — "whose," unanswered. → Remembered: The question that dies everywhere; the answer is offstage, and all know it.
> 3. [examine]Watch Fane's retraining — the proprietor, now. → Remembered: The ton's verdict in miniature; the paper is done, the man remains.
> 4. [social]Read the passed notes — Almack's own trial. → Remembered: The social court's proceedings; the gallery judges while the jury deliberates.
> 5. [stance]Distinguish explained from disgraced — manageable. → Remembered: Her understanding of the town's fears; mysteries terrify, explanations merely bankrupt.
> 6. [examine]Feel the water round the stone — the sums, moving. → Remembered: The purse's gravity; the town orbits what it cannot lift.
> 7. [choice]Listen or stop listening — the murmur's uses. → Remembered: Whether the connoisseur keeps tasting; the sums will be reported anyway.

scenes.synopsis: the proprietor, cornered — the bought campaign, proved; fabrication, funded; the vanity's last stand.
scenes.prose:
> *(Pyke sits through the cutout's testimony with the stillness of a man watching his own house burn from the street — unable to intervene, unable to look away. The slyness is still there — he has not threatened, has not blustered, has printed and only printed, the gutter weapon's whole doctrine — but it has become a museum piece, intact and irrelevant, the way a sword is irrelevant at a trial about poison. His counsel leans in, murmurs; Pyke shakes his head — not the sharp shake of the card withheld, but something slower, heavier: the shake of a man whose reserves are gone. The bought campaign, proved. The purse, opened to the edge. There is nothing left in the sleeve but the card — and the card is not a defense.)**
> *(And the card — Lavinia's old filth, read back at her — is not a defense. Rose sees him understand this in real time, the calculation moving behind the stillness: the vanity's last stand is not a stand at all, but a flailing. He catches her eye across the courtroom — the first time all trial, the direct look, terrible in its recognition — and she sees not hatred but the terrible recognition of a man beaten the way he tried to beat her: in the open, with witnesses, the *Gazette* watching, unbuyable, writing it down. He looks away first. The proprietor, cornered: the gutter weapon, spending its last shot not at the case but at the alliance. It will not save the paper. He knows it. The calculation now is only: wound, if not save.)*
> *(She grants him the slyness to the end — her final measure, the general's courtesy to a beaten opponent — and chooses her posture: pity or prosecute, the cornered watched. The girl might forgive; the general finishes. She watches him sit in the wreckage of the funded campaign — the quantities proved, the coin traced, the purse opened — and feels the trial's center of gravity shift: the paper is done, the man remains, and what remains is sly and cornered, which is more dangerous than vain. But the sleeve is empty now except the card. The card, aimed at the alliance. Tomorrow, or the day after — the recall, the reading. She holds the formation in her mind: *next to, always*. Let him play it.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the house burn — from the street. → Remembered: The proprietor's paralysis; unable to intervene, unable to look away.
> 2. [stance]Grant the slyness — to the end. → Remembered: Her final measure; intact and irrelevant, like a sword at a poison trial.
> 3. [examine]Read the slower shake — the reserves, gone. → Remembered: The new head-shake; not the card withheld, but the sleeve, empty.
> 4. [micro]Catch the direct look — the first, all trial. → Remembered: The terrible recognition; beaten in the open, with witnesses, the way he fought.
> 5. [social]Receive him looking away first — the concession. → Remembered: The small victory; the proprietor yields the gaze before the verdict.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the flailing — not a stand. → Remembered: The card's true nature; aimed at the alliance because the case is lost.
> 7. [stance]Read the calculation — wound, if not save. → Remembered: The slyness's last arithmetic; the paper is gone, the wound is the consolation.
> 8. [choice]Pity or prosecute — the cornered, watched. → Remembered: Her final posture toward him; the general finishes, the girl might forgive.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — the ledger's day, continued; black-and-white, the account's grammar, for the afternoon.
scenes.prose:
> *(The midday recess, and the ledger's day is half done — the quantities read, the payments traced, the purse described to its edge. The afternoon will bring the chain's completion and the question of the purse's naming, and the dress must hold its black-and-white through the harder half: the account's grammar, continued. In the robing corridor Letitia performs the afternoon's adjustments with the gravity of a woman tuning an instrument — a sash retied, a brooch moved a quarter-inch, the whitework at the hem shaken out like a sail. The corridor's gravity, witnessed: the robing corridor is also a gallery, and the tuning is also testimony.)**
> *(Three afternoon faces for the black-and-white, and the choice is the second half's testimony. **The Column, Continued** — the morning's black silk, severe, the ledger-lines at the hem now the afternoon's emblem: consistency is also testimony; the jury trusts a woman who does not change her story, or her dress. **The Purse's Edge** — charcoal wool with the three-link chain embroidered in silver thread at the waist, the diamond brooch moved to the shoulder like a star: the chain, complete to the purse; the edge, worn as ornament; Pyke will read the diamond and understand. **The Witness's White** — pearl-grey silk with a single white rosebud at the shoulder, swelling, anyone can see: the clean name, quietly stated; the rose argues without speaking. Each choice testifies. Each choice is remembered.)*
> *(She weighs the tuning — the quarter-inch brooch, the shaken hem — and dresses for the harder half: the naming, coming. The question of the purse will be hers, Quill said — name it, hold it, or let the cutout name it — and the dress must hold through the decision the way the morning's held through the quantities. Letitia steps back, examines, nods: the instrument, tuned. Rose reads the afternoon's need — chain, edge, or rose — and chooses. The black-and-white, continued. The account, stated. The harder half waits, and she will meet it dressed like the ledger: precise, severe, unmisreadable — the columns at the hem, the account stated in every seam, the jury reading steadiness in the unchanged dress.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [choice]Choose the Column, Continued — consistency, testified. → Remembered: Her testimony of steadiness; the unchanged dress is the unchanged story.
> 2. [choice]Choose the Purse's Edge — the chain, worn. → Remembered: Her testimony of the tracing; three links at the waist, the edge as ornament.
> 3. [choice]Choose the Witness's White — the bud, quiet. → Remembered: Her testimony of the clean name; the rose argues without speaking.
> 4. [examine]Weigh the tuning — the quarter-inch brooch. → Remembered: Letitia's instrumental care; afternoons are won in quarter-inches.
> 5. [micro]Consider the shaken hem — like a sail. → Remembered: The whitework's second wind; the ledger-lines must read at distance.
> 6. [stance]Dress for the harder half — the naming, coming. → Remembered: Her preparation for the purse's question; the dress must hold through it.
> 7. [social]Take the corridor's gravity — the tuning, witnessed. → Remembered: Who sees the adjustments; the robing corridor is also a gallery.
> 8. [examine]Read the afternoon's need — chain, edge, or rose. → Remembered: Her diagnosis of the second half; the testimony continues, the dress with it.

scenes.synopsis: the ledger, admitted — the court's weight; the exhibit, sealed into the record.
scenes.prose:
> *(The judge admits the ledger with the ceremony the judiciary reserves for exhibits that have already convicted — the formal words, the exhibit number entered, the book sealed into the record with a ribbon the color of old decisions. "The court," he says, "marks the exhibit." And the courtroom understands: the quantities, the payments, the one purse through the whole of it — these are no longer testimony, to be weighed and doubted; they are *record*, to be reckoned with. Rose watches the clerk tie the ribbon and thinks of all the ribbons she has tied this season — the archive's, the drawer's, the season's papers ranked and sealed — and understands the judiciary has its own floriography: tied means proved, in law's language. The transformation, accomplished: testimony become record.)**
> *(Pyke's counsel rises — to object to the admission, a beat too late, the way he has done everything today a beat too late — and the judge regards him over the spectacles with the expression of a man watching someone knock on a door that has already been bricked up. "Mr. —," the judge says, "the exhibit is marked." Counsel sits. The ribbon is tied. The ledger — calf-bound, thirty years of hands, the exact month the penny sheet became a weapon — is now the court's own book. Quill catches Rose's eye and gives the smallest nod: the auditor, confirming the accounts are now beyond dispute, the jury's memory sealed with the ribbon. What the box retains: ceremonies outlast arguments, and the ribbon is longer than speeches.)*
> *(She holds the proved the way she has held everything this trial: with the grip of a woman who knows how hard proved was to earn. The purse is proved, and it stays proved — sealed, ribboned, numbered, beyond dispute. She watches the clerk carry the book to its place and thinks of her own archive's drawer, and the copy the clerk has promised her: the court's book, and hers. The record, holding. The day's achievement, sealed. The ledger's day has its monument now — calf-bound, ribboned, the color of old decisions — and the town will reckon with it long after the trial ends.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the ceremony — the ribbon, the color of old decisions. → Remembered: The judiciary's floriography; tied means proved, in law's language.
> 2. [stance]Hear "the court marks the exhibit" — the transformation. → Remembered: Testimony become record; weighed things become reckoned things.
> 3. [micro]Note the late objection — the bricked-up door. → Remembered: The defense's chronic lateness; knocking after bricking is the day's emblem.
> 4. [examine]Think of her own ribbons — the archive's. → Remembered: Her parallel ceremonies; the drawer and the court tie the same knots.
> 5. [social]Receive Quill's smallest nod — beyond dispute. → Remembered: The auditor's confirmation; the accounts are now the court's own.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the jury's memory — the ribbon, longer than speeches. → Remembered: What the box retains; ceremonies outlast arguments.
> 7. [stance]Hold the proved — the record, holding. → Remembered: Her grip on the day's achievement; the purse is proved, and it stays proved.
> 8. [choice]Watch the clerk or the judge — the tier or the sealer. → Remembered: Where her attention rests; both are the law, in its two hands.

scenes.synopsis: the recess conference — Quill lays out the boundary; the purse is proved, the face beyond the courtroom's reach.
scenes.prose:
> *(They confer in the corridor with the ledger's ribbon still fresh, and Quill lays out the boundary like a surveyor's fence: "The purse is proved. Behind the purse —" he glances at the empty air where a face would be, twice, the glance itself a kind of testimony "— is further than this courtroom can go. Creech never saw; the cutout never asked. The coin came from further off, and further off is not in evidence." He looks at her. "The question is whether we chase it. Demand the face — subpoenas, inquiries, the trial reaching past its grasp. Or let it stay offstage — the coin is enough, the verdict does not need the master." The fence, laid. The trial's honest limit, stated plainly.)**
> "If we demand it and cannot produce it," Rose says, "the jury hears an absence. Absences acquit, in the wrong ears."
> "Precisely," Quill says. "A face demanded and not delivered becomes a doubt. A face unmentioned remains — a shadow. Shadows do not acquit. They merely wait."
> *(Rose thinks of the season's architecture — the libel war won in the open, the face reserved for the masquerade, rooms with walls and the face outside the walls by design — and understands the choice the way she understands all of Quill's choices: as a surveyor understands a fence. "The coin is enough for this courtroom," she says. "The face will have its season. Not this one." Quill nods — the fence agreed — and makes a note. The decision shaped, not taken: the offstage stays offstage. The purse is the trial's horizon. Beyond it — the masquerade, the black-and-gold, the meeting that is coming. She weighs the risk he named — absences acquit, in the wrong ears — and the alternative — shadows merely wait — and chooses the waiting shadow. That is its office.)*
> *(They stand a moment in the corridor's noise — the trial's traffic flowing around the fence they have just built — and she feels the decision settle: shaped, not taken, but settled enough. The second decision will take its shape here too, tonight or at dawn. She thinks of S4's door — spoken or unspoken — and leaves it unmentioned, by design. Some doors are better unmentioned. The ledger's ribbon is fresh. The boundary is laid. The face waits, in its season. The trial goes on — the purse, the chain, the card still sleeved — and she goes back in with the fence in her mind like a map.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]See the surveyor's fence — the boundary, laid. → Remembered: The trial's honest limit; further off is not in evidence.
> 2. [stance]Weigh "absences acquit, in the wrong ears" — the risk. → Remembered: Her grasp of the chase's danger; demanded-and-missing becomes doubt.
> 3. [examine]Take "shadows merely wait" — the alternative. → Remembered: Quill's doctrine of the unmentioned; waiting shadows do not acquit.
> 4. [micro]Note the empty air — glanced at, twice. → Remembered: The face's absence, acknowledged; even glances are testimony, of a kind.
> 5. [social]Think of the architecture — rooms, walls, seasons. → Remembered: Her sense of the design; the face has its season, and it is not this one.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the horizon — the purse, the trial's. → Remembered: The sufficient boundary; the coin is enough for this courtroom.
> 7. [stance]Shape the decision — offstage stays offstage. → Remembered: Her leaning, formed; the second decision takes its shape in the corridor.
> 8. [choice]Name the masquerade or leave it unnamed — the future's register. → Remembered: Whether S4's door is spoken aloud; some doors are better unmentioned.

scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, Quill's chambers, and the day's account is closed — the ledger admitted, the chain complete to the purse, the face still offstage. Quill lays it out with the bluntness of a man too tired for euphemism. The face. They can demand it — subpoenas, inquiries, the trial reaching past its grasp, and risk the absence acquitting in the wrong ears, the face not delivered becoming a doubt. They can let it stay offstage — the coin is enough, the verdict does not need the master, the shadow merely waits, and waiting shadows do not acquit. Or they can follow the coin later — the trial ends, the tracing continues, and the meeting comes in its own season, the masquerade needing its invitation. Rose weighs the reach against the discipline: subpoenas and grasp against the trial's honest boundary. The absent acquittal, priced. The shadow, waiting. S4's door, considered — the future's architecture, the meeting's season. She chooses as the general: rooms have walls, and she respects them. Tonight or dawn — the tempo; the face has waited all season, it can wait till morning.)*

> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the demand, the discipline, the later following. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.synopsis: the purse, not the face — the court hears what it cannot see; the London face, unnamed, unshown.
scenes.prose:
> *(The next morning Quill states it for the record — plainly, the way he states everything: "The plaintiff's case reaches the purse. The purse is proved — one purse, through the whole of it, deep, filled from further off. What lies further off is not in evidence, and the plaintiff does not ask the court to imagine it." The courtroom hears the sentence for what it is: the trial, drawing its honest boundary. The coin has a master. The master is not in this courtroom. The London face — unnamed, unshown, never promoted — stays offstage, exactly where it has been all season, while the purse takes the stand in its place. The boundary, stated for the record. The discipline, spoken aloud.)**
> *(Rose watches the jury receive the boundary — the foreman nods, the box settles, the honest limit honored — and watches the gallery receive it too: Fane's lorgnette dips in what might be respect, the Directresses stop passing notes, the cipher-clerk in the back row writes *boundary* in his cipher and underlines it twice, someone else mapping the limits too. The ton understands: the trial is not the war, only the battle; the purse is proved, the face is reserved, and the reservation is itself a statement — that the coin's master exists, that he is not here, that he will be met elsewhere, in another season. Discipline is also a spectacle, and Fane applauds it the way the ton applauds everything: with the lorgnette.)*
> *(Pyke's counsel, who has been waiting for the reach — the demand, the subpoena, the overgrasp he could mock — finds nothing to mock. The reach never came. The mockery starves. Rose holds the discipline the way she has held everything: the offstage, offstage; the face, not needed and not wanted here. She considers naming the elsewhere — the masquerade, the meeting — and leaves it, by design. The reservation's register is silence. The battle, not the war. The purse, proved. The face, in its season. The courtroom moves on, and the boundary holds like a fence — plain, honest, and exactly where Quill laid it: the trial's honest limit, respected by the woman it was built to protect.)**

> 1. [examine]Hear the boundary stated — plainly, for the record. → Remembered: Quill's honest limit; not asking the court to imagine is itself the argument.
> 2. [stance]Receive the foreman's nod — the box, settled. → Remembered: The jury's honor of the limit; honest boundaries convince.
> 3. [examine]Watch the cipher-clerk — *boundary*, underlined twice. → Remembered: The unfamiliar piece's interest; someone else is mapping the limits too.
> 4. [micro]Note Fane's dip — respect, perhaps. → Remembered: The ton's acknowledgment; discipline is also a spectacle, and Fane applauds it.
> 5. [social]Feel the gallery's understanding — battle, not war. → Remembered: The town's grasp of the architecture; the purse now, the face in its season.
> 6. [examine]Weigh counsel's unmocked wait — nothing to mock. → Remembered: The defense's disappointment; the reach never came, and the mockery starves.
> 7. [stance]Hold the discipline — the offstage, offstage. → Remembered: Her maintenance of the boundary; the face is not needed, and not wanted, here.
> 8. [choice]Name the elsewhere or leave it — the reservation's register. → Remembered: Whether the future is spoken; the masquerade goes unmentioned, by design.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the empty chair; the face that never comes; the offstage, kept.
scenes.prose:
> *(There is a chair in the courtroom — not in the well, not in the gallery, but in the corridor outside, where witnesses wait — that has been empty all trial. Rose passes it every morning, and this morning she stops. It is an ordinary chair, cane-bottomed, unremarkable, and it has held no one for three days: not the forty-pound witness's paymaster, not Larkin's purse-man, not Creech's further-off. The chair is the trial's truest exhibit of the offstage — the face that never comes, the master not in this courtroom, the absence around which the whole case is built. She stands before it a moment, the unportrait contemplated: some presences are best contemplated empty. The offstage has furniture, and it is cane-bottomed.)**
> *(A clerk passes, sees her looking, and says — helpful, misunderstanding completely — "Shall I have it removed, miss? It's in the way." "No," Rose says. "Leave it." And the chair stays: empty, in the way, exactly where it belongs. The offstage, kept. She thinks of the season's architecture — the masquerade, the black-and-gold, the meeting that is coming — and understands that the empty chair is also a promise: that the face will come, in its season, to a room where she is waiting. Not this room. Not this season. But the chair is ready — the second shadow, waiting, merely, at her back like company. She leaves it empty, in the way, and goes in to the ledger's day.)*
> *(She does not tell Quill about the chair — some exhibits are for one viewer only, the private archive. But she carries it with her into the courtroom: the truest exhibit, the face that never comes, the absence kept like a pressed flower. The trial will end. The chair will stay empty. And in another season, in another room, the face will come — to the masquerade, to the meeting, to the ground she chooses. The promise, kept in cane and air. She takes her seat. The ledger's day resumes. The chair waits, in the way, exactly where it belongs — empty, cane-bottomed, keeping its counsel until the season turns and it is wanted.)**

> 4. [stance]Receive the clerk's misunderstanding — helpful, complete. → Remembered: The world's literalness; not everyone reads furniture.
> 5. [social]Think of the promise — the face, in its season. → Remembered: The chair's other meaning; it is ready, for the masquerade's room.
> 6. [examine]Feel the second shadow — waiting, merely. → Remembered: The absence at her back; the shadow that waits is also company.
> 7. [choice]Tell Quill about the chair or keep it — the private exhibit. → Remembered: Whether the symbol is shared; some exhibits are for one viewer only.
