scenes.synopsis: the credibility, broken open — the town's verdict on the ledger's day.
scenes.prose:
> *(The murmur has become a verdict — Rose hears it in the corridor after the adjournment, in the street, in the coffee-house she passes: the *Lantern* is done. Not cracking, not thinning — done. The ledger did what the witnesses began: the quantities, the coin, the one purse, the deep purse that never ran dry. "Campaign quantities," the town says, trying the phrase like a new gown — and the phrase fits, and the town wears it, and London walks around in it. Fane's table has voted. Almack's has voted. The booksellers have voted with their shelves — Thursday's number, unstoked, uncried, lying in stacks the way unsold things lie. The town's verdict, more final than the court's: the credibility, broken open.)**
> *(She walks home through the London dusk with the town's verdict ringing in her ears — more final than the court's, the way the town's verdicts always are — and thinks of Pyke's dark office, the idle press, the unswept corners, the creditor's notice on the door. The gutter weapon, spending its last: the proprietor cornered, the only thing left in the sleeve the card aimed at the alliance. Tomorrow the card will be played — she knows it the way she knows her own handwriting — and the alliance will receive it standing up. Next to. Always. But tonight: the ledger's day, won. The purse, proved. The face, offstage, waiting its season. The strongbox, opened — everyone can see inside now.)*
> *(She touches the white rose's bud — swelling, anyone can see it, the promise's progress — and holds *next to, always* for tomorrow: the alliance's formation, rehearsed. The eve's renewal will come. The recall will come. The card will be played, and the answering — as decided — will be ready. But tonight the dusk is hers, and the verdict rings, and the town wears the phrase like a gown. Campaign quantities. The town has voted with its shelves and its subscriptions. The *Lantern* is done. The ledger's day is won. Tomorrow: the card — the last card, the recall, the reading she has waited five days to receive standing up, *next to, always*, the formation held through the dusk.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear the verdict — not the court's, the town's. → Remembered: The more final judgment; the town votes with shelves and subscriptions.
> 2. [micro]Try the phrase — "campaign quantities," worn. → Remembered: The town's new gown; the phrase fits, and London wears it.
> 3. [examine]See Thursday's number, uncried — in stacks. → Remembered: The unsold things, lying; the hawkers have stopped crying, the town has stopped buying.
> 4. [stance]Distinguish broken from cracked — the strongbox, opened. → Remembered: The new phase; everyone can see inside now.
> 5. [social]Walk the dusk — the verdict, ringing. → Remembered: How she carries the town's judgment; it hums like a tune, underneath.
> 6. [examine]Know tomorrow — the card, coming. → Remembered: Her certainty; the sleeve holds one thing, and it will be played.
> 7. [choice]Touch the bud — swelling, anyone can see. → Remembered: The promise's progress; vindication is nearly bloom.
> 8. [stance]Hold "next to, always" — for tomorrow. → Remembered: The alliance's formation, rehearsed; the receiving is prepared.

scenes.synopsis: her fear — the last card is hers; the old filth, and what the reading will cost.
scenes.prose:
> *(Lavinia receives her in the scarlet drawing room with the composure of a woman brave all day in public, now allowing herself the luxury of fear in private. "He'll play it tomorrow," she says, without preamble. "The old filth. In his funnier voice. And the jury —" she stops, pours wine with a hand that is almost steady "— the jury laughed today at Larkin's pretty circle. They may laugh tomorrow at mine." Rose takes the wine. "They laughed *with* Larkin," she says. "They will not laugh *at* you. There is a difference, and juries know it." "Juries," Lavinia says, "are men. Men laugh at scarlet women. It is practically a reflex." The private fear, received: the scarlet woman's offstage truth, bravery in public, fear in private — the luxury, allowed.)*
> *(Rose weighs the reflex — mockery as shrinkage, the card's mechanism aimed at the woman — and answers it with the distinction: with, not at. "Then we give them no reflex to have," Rose says. "You read it yourself, yesterday — aloud, in your own voice. What can he add?" "Mockery," Lavinia says. "He will make it *small*, darling — a joke, a footnote. And smallness —" her voice, for the first time all evening, cracks "— smallness is what it was, when it was printed. Small. Mean. Mine." The wound's true words. The filth was small when printed, and she remembers — the crack in the voice, the almost-steady hand, the ally's private arithmetic: a scheduled wound has its own cruelty.)*
> *(Rose sets down her wine and takes the scarlet woman's almost-steady hand, and the alliance — grey and scarlet — holds in the lamplight: not strategy now, but what strategy is for. "Next to," Rose says. "Not behind, not in front. Whatever he reads — next to." Lavinia's hand tightens. "Next to," she agrees. "Always. But Rose — when he plays it: let me answer. Not you. Me. It is mine to receive, and mine to answer." The request, made: Lavinia's claim on her own filth. Rose sits with the fear — the evening's cargo — and understands it will shape tomorrow's answering. The vow, renewed. The formation, held. Tomorrow: the recall.)**
> What can he add?"
> "Mockery," Lavinia says. Small. Mean. Mine." *(Rose sets down her wine and takes the scarlet woman's almost-steady hand, and the alliance — grey and scarlet — holds in the lamplight: not strategy now, but what strategy is for. "Next to," Rose says. "Not behind, not in front. "Next to," she agrees. "Always. Not you. Me. It is mine to receive, and mine to answer.")*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Receive the private fear — the luxury, allowed. → Remembered: The scarlet woman's offstage truth; bravery in public, fear in private.
> 2. [examine]Weigh "men laugh at scarlet women" — the reflex. → Remembered: The card's mechanism; mockery as shrinkage, aimed at the woman.
> 3. [stance]"They laughed *with*" — the difference. → Remembered: Her distinction; juries know with from at, and she trusts them to.
> 4. [micro]Take the almost-steady hand — the alliance, held. → Remembered: The lamplight's geometry; grey and scarlet, not strategy now but its purpose.
> 5. [examine]Hear the crack — "small. Mean. Mine." → Remembered: The wound's true words; the filth was small when printed, and she remembers.
> 6. [choice]"Let me answer. Not you. Me." — the request. → Remembered: Lavinia's claim on her own filth; the answering may be hers by right.
> 7. [social]Vow "next to, always" — again. → Remembered: The formation, renewed; the third decision approaches, and the vow precedes it.
> 8. [stance]Sit with the fear — the evening's cargo. → Remembered: How she bears the ally's dread; it will shape tomorrow's answering.

scenes.synopsis: rises for the last card — the ruling: put it to the witness, or save it for the closing; the card, scheduled for the recall.
scenes.prose:
> *(The fourth day's morning, and Pyke's counsel rises before Quill can call his first witness — rises with the deliberation of a man playing the card held through three days of losing. "My lord," he says, "the defense will now —" and lifts the paper: Lavinia's old filth, the *Lantern's* old numbers about the Cranes, marked and sharpened, the questions arranged like instruments. The courtroom stills. Lavinia goes rigid in the gallery — the spine, aristocratic, already standing up while sitting down. Quill is half out of his seat — the objection, unmade, the restraint of a man who knows the ruling will be lawful. And the judge raises the hand — the carriage-stopping hand, the third time this trial — and says: "Mr. —." The card's new posture: lifted, not read. Lifted is not played, and the difference is the ruling.)**
> *(The pause that follows is the longest of the trial. Counsel stands with the paper raised but not read — the card, lifted but not played — and the whole courtroom does the arithmetic: the ruling's shape. Put it to the witness, or save it for the closing. "The defense," counsel says, slowly, "will recall Lady Lavinia Crane." The paper is lowered, not put away — the lowering, not the putting-away; the card rests, it does not retire. Rose feels Lavinia's hand find hers under the gallery's rail — *next to, always* — and understands with cold clarity: the card will be played *to* her, on the stand, under oath — the old filth, read back at the woman who read it herself three days ago. The cruelty, refined: the stand is worse than the gallery. The last card, unplayed. Scheduled. Certain. Waiting like a second shadow.)*
> *(She holds the second shadow — scheduled, certain — the way she has held everything: with the discipline of a woman who knows the date of the blow. Quill's hand is on his papers. The judge nods. The recall is lawful, and it begins — tomorrow, the fifth day, the stand, the reading. Rose watches counsel sit — the paper lowered — and feels the alliance's grip under the rail: *next to, always*, held before the recall. The town will come to watch. The *Gazette's* pencil will fly. And the answering — as decided — will be ready. The card, scheduled. The waiting, begun.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Watch the paper lifted — raised, not read. → Remembered: The card's new posture; lifted is not played, and the difference is the ruling.
> 2. [stance]Hear the ruling's shape — recalled, or closing. → Remembered: The judge's precision; the card has two doors, and counsel chose the stand.
> 3. [examine]Take "the defense will recall" — slowly. → Remembered: Counsel's choice of door; the filth will be played *to* her, under oath.
> 4. [micro]Feel her hand found — under the rail. → Remembered: The alliance's grip; *next to, always*, held before the recall.
> 5. [social]Watch Quill half-risen — the objection, unmade. → Remembered: Counsel's restraint; the ruling is lawful, and he knows it.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the cold clarity — played *to* her. → Remembered: The card's cruelty, refined; the stand is worse than the gallery.
> 7. [stance]Hold the second shadow — scheduled, certain. → Remembered: How she carries the waiting; the recall has a date, and the date is coming.
> 8. [choice]Watch counsel sit — the paper, lowered. → Remembered: The lowering, not the putting-away; the card rests, it does not retire.

scenes.synopsis: fashion-selection — the evening; the white rose, worn; the recall's eve, dressed.
scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, and the card is scheduled — the recall, the filth to be played *to* her on the stand — and the trial's fourth day is done. In her dressing room Rose dresses for the evening the way one dresses before a battle one cannot fight oneself: not for celebration, but for the statement that the alliance will not be broken by the recall. Tomorrow Lavinia takes the stand again. Tonight's dress is the eve: black-and-white giving way to white, the account closing, the clean name opening — for both of them. The evening's register: statement, not celebration. The recall's eve, dressed.)**
> *(Three evening dresses, and the choice is the recall's eve, testified. **The Ready** — pearl-grey silk with whitework embroidery of white roses — the buds, swelling, Augusta's stricture honored to the letter — at the shoulder, pearl ear-drops, no brooch: the alliance, prepared; the reader will not be diminished. **The Vindication, Early** — white silk, simple and severe, with a single white rose — *in bloom*, at last — pinned at the shoulder, the signet, nothing else: the clean name, stated; worn for the woman who will need it tomorrow. **The Hartwell at Peace** — dove-grey velvet with embroidered wheat-ears in silver thread, the estate's own emblem: the estate, unbroken; the card is scheduled, and the alliance dines. Each choice testifies. Each choice is remembered.)*
> *(She weighs the stricture — honored to the letter, the buds staying buds until the proving lifts them — and notes the rose's destination: tomorrow, to Lavinia. The floriography's gift: the clean name's flower goes to the recalled. She dresses before another's battle — the wardrobe's transition, black-and-white giving way to white — and reads tomorrow's need: the recall, the stand, the dress that must hold through another's trial. The dressing room's counsel — the eve, built. Letitia nods. The white, chosen. The alliance's eve, kept the way eves should be kept: dressed, steady, ready — the white grammar spoken fluently, the statement made before the battle, for Lavinia and the clean name — the dressing room's counsel honored, the eve built the way eves should be built: dressed, steady, ready — and the white, chosen, holding.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [choice]Choose the Ready — the alliance, prepared. → Remembered: Her testimony of readiness; the reader will not be diminished.
> 2. [choice]Choose the Vindication, Early — the bloom, for her. → Remembered: Her testimony of the clean name; worn for the woman who needs it tomorrow.
> 3. [choice]Choose the Hartwell at Peace — the estate, unbroken. → Remembered: Her testimony of calm; the card is scheduled, and the alliance dines.
> 4. [examine]Weigh the stricture, honored — to the letter. → Remembered: Her discipline with the bloom; the buds stay buds until the proving lifts them.
> 5. [micro]Note the rose's destination — tomorrow, to Lavinia. → Remembered: The floriography's gift; the clean name's flower goes to the recalled.
> 6. [stance]Dress before another's battle — statement, not celebration. → Remembered: Her evening's register; the alliance's eve is also a testimony.
> 7. [social]Take the dressing room's counsel — the eve, built. → Remembered: The wardrobe's transition; black-and-white gives way to white.
> 8. [examine]Read tomorrow's need — the recall, the stand. → Remembered: Her anticipation; the dress must hold through another's trial.

scenes.synopsis: texture — the* Lantern's *office, dark again; the gutter weapon, spent; the card, waiting.
scenes.prose:
> *(She walks home by way of Fleet Street — the instructive route, now a habit — and the *Lantern's* office is dark at an hour when, a month ago, it blazed. The press is idle. The shutters are closed. A creditor's notice is pasted to the door — the paper funded by a deep purse dunned for its honest debts, an irony the *Gazette* will savor: the irony, pasted to the door, the funded paper unable to pay its honest bills. The boy is gone from the step. The corners are unswept. The gutter weapon, spent — not with a bang but with a creditor's notice, the most unromantic of endings. The small absences: the machine's servants have left with the machine.)**
> *(She stands across the street in the lamplight and listens to the quiet — the machine wound down, the press's heartbeat stilled, the quiet complete — and thinks of the season's first Thursday, the libel fresh, the town reading her ruin over breakfast — and the town moved on. The hawkers cry other papers. The *Lantern's* ink — bought, funded, operated — has thinned to nothing, and the nothing is the verdict. She does not feel triumph. She feels — and examines the feeling with the auditor's care — something like the end of a long illness: relief, and the strange flatness after. The honest feeling, examined: the end of a long illness deserves its flatness.)*
> *(The card waits for the recall. The alliance waits for the card. The dark office stays dark behind her as she turns for home — the chapter, closed, the instructive route completed. She weighs the waiting card — the recall, tomorrow — against the dark office, done: the courtroom is not done, but Fleet Street is. The town has moved on to other papers, cried by other hawkers. The *Lantern's* office, dark again. The gutter weapon, spent. She walks on, and the lamplight follows, and the recall waits — scheduled, certain — like a second shadow. The dark office stays dark behind her. The courtroom, ahead, is lit — and waiting, the card scheduled, the answering ready — and she walks toward the light the way she has walked all trial: unhurried, unbowed, unafraid.)**
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Read the creditor's notice — in the lamplight. → Remembered: The irony, pasted to the door; the funded paper, dunned for honest debts.
> 2. [micro]Note the boy, gone — the step, unswept. → Remembered: The small absences; the machine's servants have left with the machine.
> 3. [examine]Hear the stilled heartbeat — the quiet, complete. → Remembered: Fleet Street's silence, final; the press will not beat again.
> 4. [stance]Examine the flatness — the auditor's care. → Remembered: Her honest feeling; relief and flatness, the end of a long illness.
> 5. [social]Note the town, moved on — other papers, cried. → Remembered: The gutter's indifference; hawkers cry what sells, and the *Lantern* doesn't.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the waiting card — the recall, tomorrow. → Remembered: The scheduled blow; the dark office is done, the courtroom is not.
> 7. [choice]Turn for home — the chapter, closed. → Remembered: How she leaves Fleet Street; the dark office stays dark, behind her.

scenes.synopsis: Bell's evening line — the unbuyable paper's account of the ledger's day.
scenes.prose:
> *(The *Gazette* arrives with the evening post, and Bell's account of the ledger's day is everything the day was: the quantities, the coin, the one purse, the deep purse that never ran dry — and then, in the paragraph's final sentence, the line the town will quote: "The *Lantern's* ink was bought. The town has now seen the bill." Rose reads it twice — once for the facts, once for the flavor — and the flavor is pure Bell: no gloating, no mercy, just the clinical precision of a paper that judges in the open. The bill. Seen. The town, presented with its own arithmetic — the quote the town will carry, the line the town will quote.)**
> *(But it is the second paragraph that holds her — three lines, dry as dust: "The coin had a master. The master was not in the courtroom. The *Gazette* does not imagine masters." Rose reads the three lines three times, and each reading deepens the respect: Bell has stated the boundary — the purse proved, the face unimagined — in the exact register Quill used in court. The unbuyable paper, judging in the open, has drawn the same line the trial drew: the coin is enough for this courtroom, and the imagination is not evidence. The parallel registers — Bell and Quill, aligned; honesty has one language. The doctrine, stated by Bell: imagination is not evidence, even for the *Gazette*.)*
> *(She folds the edition and lays it on the drawer, and the duelists regard each other — bought and billed, unbought and judging; the drawer's tableau, updated: the *Lantern* thins, the *Gazette* judges. She weighs file or frame — whether the paragraph joins the archive or the wall; some bills deserve the drawer, some the wall — and files it, with the day's other papers. The bill, seen. The nearness — the bloom, to be earned, near enough to touch, not yet held. The clean name's proximity. She goes in to the recall's eve with Bell's lines in her head like a tune: the town has now seen the bill — and the town, having seen it, will never unsee it; the arithmetic, once done, cannot be undone.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Read twice — facts, then flavor. → Remembered: Her double reading; Bell rewards the second pass, as always.
> 2. [stance]Receive "the town has now seen the bill" — the quote. → Remembered: The line the town will carry; bills, seen, are the *Gazette's* verdicts.
> 3. [micro]Read the three lines three times — dry as dust. → Remembered: The boundary, stated by Bell; the master unimagined, the coin enough.
> 4. [examine]Weigh the parallel registers — Bell and Quill, aligned. → Remembered: The paper and the counsel, drawing the same line; honesty has one language.
> 5. [social]Note "does not imagine masters" — the doctrine. → Remembered: The *Gazette's* discipline; imagination is not evidence, even for Bell.
> 6. [stance]Lay the duelists — bought and billed, unbought and judging. → Remembered: The drawer's tableau, updated; the *Lantern* thins, the *Gazette* judges.
> 7. [choice]File or frame — the bill, seen. → Remembered: Whether the paragraph joins the archive; some bills deserve the drawer, some the wall.
> 8. [examine]Feel the nearness — the bloom, to be earned. → Remembered: The clean name's proximity; near enough to touch, not yet held.

scenes.synopsis: Augusta receives the ledger's day — the general's audit; quantities, coin, purse, and the boundary at the face.
scenes.prose:
> *(Augusta receives the ledger's day the way she receives all decisive days — seated, spectacles on, tea at the temperature of judgment — and Rose gives it straight: the quantities, the coin, the one purse, the boundary at the face. The decisive day's register: unembroidered victory, the general's due. The general listens without interruption — applause, of a kind — and when Rose finishes: "Campaign quantities. A deep purse. The coin, traced to its purse, in the open. You drew the boundary well, child. The face demanded and not delivered would have been a doubt. The face unmentioned is a shadow. Shadows wait. That is their office." The seal, over wax: the battle won, the war reserved.)**
> "The masquerade," Rose says. "S4's door. The meeting."
> "In its season," Augusta says. "Not this one. This season's work is the purse — proved, in the open, where the ton can do its sums. The next season's work is the face — met, in the open, where the ton can watch. You have won the battle, child. Do not mistake it for the war. The war has a face, and it is waiting. But it is waiting *for you* — which means you choose the ground. Remember that, when the invitation comes."

scenes.prose:
> *(Letitia is waiting up — she always waits up on ledger days, the habit: twice a habit, thrice a custom — with her sewing and her opinions, both sharp. "A deep purse," she says, threading a needle. "That never ran dry. Two years." The needle flashes. "And the face — offstage. Unnamed. Unshown." She looks up. "Darling, I have lived in London forty years and never seen a purse that deep without a face behind it I was *very* glad not to see. You were right not to chase it. Chasing faces is how girls get ruined in novels, and you —" the needle pauses "— are not in a novel. You are in a trial. Trials end." Forty years' wisdom, threaded: the aunt's genre wisdom, the jurisprudence of the household.)**
> "The masquerade," Rose says. "The meeting. It will come."
> "It will," Letitia agrees, resuming. "And when it does, you will wear —" she considers "— black-and-gold, I suppose. But tonight —" she ties off the thread with a snap "— tonight you will wear the white rose, in bloom, and go to bed. The purse's day is tomorrow, and the auditor needs her rest." She surveys her niece. "The household's verdict, darling: the ledger's day, won. The purse, proved. The face —" a beat "— somebody else's problem, for now. That is the whole of my legal opinion, and I shall bill you for it in breakfasts, as usual."

If let her answer — she takes the questions in her own voice. If answer for her — I call you, and the alliance speaks as one. The decision was made; the choreography is now. Whatever he reads, we receive it standing up. That was never in question." The final briefing: the answering, as decided; the recall's choreography. The choosing's end; what remains is execution.)**
> "The rose," Rose says. "She's wearing it. The bloom."
> "I saw," Quill says. "The jury saw. The* Gazette *saw." The nearest thing to warmth his profession permits crosses his face. "Miss Hartwell — whatever the answering's letter, the flower has already testified. White roses, in bloom, on a scarlet woman in the witness box: the clean name, worn into the recall. She folds her white-gloved hands — the receiving, begun; her body's vow: the recall resumes, and so does she. *Next to, always*. The recall resumes. The answering waits, as decided — in the papers, in the voice, in the formation; the flower already testified, the gloves folded, the ritual's constancy kept — her body's vow, her hands' stillness, the receiving begun — *next to, always*, through whatever comes — the recall, resumed; the answering, ready — *next to, always*.)**

scenes.prose:
> *(The gallery is the trial's true jury for the recall — Rose knows what happens on the stand will be judged twice: once by the box, once by the benches. The double judgment: the recall's two courts; the gallery judges while the jury deliberates. And the benches are full: Fane's lorgnette trained on Lavinia like a small sun; the Directresses leaning, their notes forgotten; the cipher-clerk writing faster than he has all trial; two duchesses who were not here yesterday and are here today, because recalls are the thing one attends. The recall's draw: duchesses attend woundings, it turns out. The ton has come to watch the scarlet woman be read *to* — and Rose understands, with a cold small clarity, that it is not entirely sure it wants her to survive: the town's uncertainty; the story's expectation: scarlet women fall, in the town's tales.)**
> *(But the town is also watching the white — Rose in the front row in vindication's palette, the alliance's uniform — and the watching is doing its own work: the gallery sees two women, grey-white and scarlet, and the pairing is the argument. The gallery's testimony: two women, and the line between them. Lavinia on the stand, the bloom at her shoulder, utterly still; Rose in the front row, white-gloved hands folded, utterly still; and between them the invisible line of *next to, always* — the formation, held. The ton does its sums — alliances, harder to wound; the town's education: the formation is the argument. Fane's lorgnette dips — a fraction, but Rose catches it: respect, or the beginning of it; the ton's respect, beginning; lorgnettes dip for the unbowed.)*
> *(She feels the sums — the town's education, the formation as argument — and knows her own visibility: the front row is also a stage; the gallery's double role: be watched or watch. The recall's audience is not merely watching — it is judging, twice, the box and the benches. The pairing argues. The formation holds. The lorgnette dips. The scarlet woman — supposed to fall, in the town's tales — does not fall: she sits, blooming, utterly still, and the town does its sums. The gallery, watching. The white, watched. *Next to, always* — the argument, worn.)**

scenes.prose:
> *(There is a moment — in the gallery's front row, before the recall resumes — when Rose is alone with the alliance's price. "Broken, darling. Not bought." Lavinia's clause, stated on the dusk walk, written in invisible ink, visible since. The invisible ink, visible: the price stated on the dusk walk, being paid. The trial has given her the breaking: the *Lantern's* credibility broken open, the bought campaign proved, the purse traced to its edge. The breaking — given, in full; the trial's delivery. The *not bought* — the refusal of settlement, of terms, of the merciful end — was her third decision's road not taken. She chose, instead, the harder thing: the witnesses unmade one by one, the ledger read aloud, the card played *to* the ally. The road not taken: terms refused, the harder thing chosen.)**
> *(She touches the white glove's cuff — steady, folded, the auditor's hands; white gloves, the discipline held — and thinks of what the alliance has cost and bought: Lavinia's file, her father's papers, the pattern proved; Lavinia's voice, her own filth read aloud, the courage priced; the rose, blooming, transferred from dressing table to scarlet shoulder. The alliance's ledger: papers, courage, flowers — all entered. The price was never money. The true currency: standing *next to*, in the open, while the card is played. She prices the alliance — never money — and lists the costs: file, voice, rose. The eve, ended. The recall, resumed.)*
> *(She holds the alliance — the eve, ended; how she enters the recall's resumption: the price paid, the formation held — and does not flinch: the decision, embodied; not flinching is the payment. Flinch or not — the price's moment. The recall resumes. Counsel opens his mouth. The filth is about to be read back at the woman who read it first. Rose folds her hands tighter. Broken, not bought. *Next to, always*. The price, paid in full, in the open — the alliance holding, the answering given, the formation unbroken — and the filth, about to be read back at the woman who read it first, already losing — the price paid, the alliance standing, *next to, always* — broken, not bought — the price, paid in full.)**

scenes.synopsis: Bell's verdict on the ledger — the ink was bought, and now, so is its shame; openly Bell's.
scenes.prose:
> *"The ledger, read aloud. Bell's verdict: the Lantern's ink was bought — and now, so is its shame."*
> *(Rose reads it at breakfast — the Gazette comes with the morning post, as it always has — and the sentence lands the way Bell's sentences always land: precisely, and on the exact spot. So is its shame. Not merely the ink was bought — the shame is bought too, purchased along with the paper, itemized in the columns. She thinks of Creech's ledger — the calf binding, the thirty years of hands, the exact month the penny sheet became a weapon — and understands that Bell has done what the ledger did: stated the account. Bought ink. Bought shame. The bill, seen. The town, presented with its arithmetic, and the arithmetic is devastating. She reads the paragraph three times, the way she has read every sting this season: the ledger, read aloud; Bell's verdict, openly Bell's; the ink, bought; the shame, bought with it. Debit, credit, balance. The Gazette, closing the books.)*

scenes.synopsis: the recall — Lavinia on the stand; Pyke's counsel rises for the last card, and plays the old filth back at her.
scenes.prose:
> *(The recall resumes after the midday recess, and the courtroom is so full the clerks have stopped counting. Lavinia sits in the witness box — scarlet, the white rose blooming at her shoulder, utterly still — and Rose sits in the gallery's front row in white, the alliance's uniform, hands folded where the jury can see them. *Next to, always* — as close as the geometry allows. Quill's hand is flat on his papers: the answering, as decided, ready. The judge nods. Pyke's counsel rises — slowly, the way men rise when the card they have held for five days is finally being played — with the marked paper in his hand. The card's final lifting; the held thing is heaviest at the playing. The courtroom holds its breath.)**
> *(He reads. The old filth — the *Lantern's* old numbers about the Cranes, the ruin retold as fraud, the innocent as dupes — in counsel's voice, the funnier voice, the voice meant to shrink it to a joke, a footnote, a thing to be laughed at. Counsel's instrument: mockery is the weapon, smallness the aim. The courtroom listens. Lavinia listens — the spine sufficiently aristocratic, the bloom at her shoulder, the woman who read it first, aloud, in her own voice, three days ago; the receiving, begun: she who read it first hears it again, unbowed. Rose listens — the white gloves folded tighter, the alliance's price being paid in full, in the open; her body's vow: *broken, not bought*, in white gloves. The reading goes on, passage by marked passage, and the town holds its breath.)*
> *(Pyke leans forward — the last brightness; the vanity's final deal: he leans toward his card like a man toward a fire — and the room's suspension holds: the played card hangs like smoke, awaiting the answer. Rose does not look away — whether she hears every passage; the ally is heard, so she hears too: listen, not look away; the reading's demand. The smoke hangs. The filth is read. Lavinia — scarlet, blooming, utterly still — receives it the way she received everything: standing up, while sitting down. And Rose holds the answering — as decided, waiting; the corridor's decision, kept: tomorrow, the alliance answers. The card is played. The answering waits.)**

scenes.synopsis: the morning after the card was played — the alliance answers in the courtroom; law, voice, and name as one.
scenes.prose:
> *(The morning after the card was played, the courtroom is full to the doors — the town has come to hear the answering, and the town has dressed for it: the Directresses in the front row like a jury of fashion, Fane's lorgnette already raised, the cipher-clerk in the back with his pencil sharpened to a needle. Lavinia sits in the witness box — scarlet, the white rose blooming at her shoulder, utterly still — and the stillness is the whole performance: no trembling, no defiance, just the particular composure of a woman who has decided, before entering, exactly what she will give. Counsel's marked paper is lowered. The reading is done. The filth has been played back at her in his funnier voice, and the courtroom has heard it — the old libel, the family's name dragged through the gutter's favorite paragraphs, read aloud by the man who paid to have it printed.)**
> *(And then the answering, as Rose decided: Quill rises with the law — not with rhetoric, with statute — and Lavinia answers with the voice — not the struck-match brightness, the deeper register, the one she uses when the hunger is banked and the mind is working — and with the name: her family's name, spoken plainly, owned completely, the libel's target standing up inside the libel and surviving it. The answering takes eleven minutes. The courtroom does not move for any of them. Rose watches the jury the way she has watched them all trial — the foreman's pencil still, for once — and watches Pyke watch Lavinia answer, and the vanity does the thing vanity does when it meets something it cannot purchase: it goes very quiet, and very still, and calculates.)*
> *(The courtroom receives the answering in the particular hush of history, and the card, played at last, does what Quill knew it would: nothing. Answered by law, by voice, by name, the filth shrinks to what it always was — small, mean, hers, and survived. Lavinia steps down with the bloom at her shoulder, and the gallery does what the town has never done for a scarlet woman: it does not look away. The Directresses nod — once, together, the fashion jury's verdict. Fane lowers the lorgnette. The cipher-clerk writes *answered* and underlines it twice. Rose meets Lavinia's eyes across the courtroom — the struck-match smile, brief, real, tired — and understands the third decision has already begun forming, the way weather forms over warm water: the hunger, loosed or leashed, and the leash in her hand.)**

> 3. [examine]Watch the town not look away — the unprecedented. → Remembered: The gallery's verdict; scarlet, unbowed, and watched with respect.
> 4. [micro]Note the bloom, still at her shoulder — survived. → Remembered: The flower's endurance; the recall did not wilt it.
> 5. [social]Feel the hush — history, twice. → Remembered: The room's double witness; reading and answering, both historic.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the card's nothing — Quill knew. → Remembered: The weapon's emptiness; played at last, it did what was foretold.

scenes.synopsis: the corridor after the answering — the debt between them comes due unnamed; the voice hers, the flower Rose's, the law Quill's.
scenes.prose:
> *(They meet in the corridor with the answering still ringing — the courtroom's hush following them out like a train — Lavinia, descended from the box, the bloom at her shoulder, the spine still sufficiently aristocratic, and Rose, who has been holding her breath for eleven minutes and lets it out now, in the corridor's dimmer light. The debt between them comes due unnamed. "You answered," Rose says. "As decided." "I answered," Lavinia agrees, "as I am." She touches the white rose — the bloom, nodding, absurdly alive against the scarlet. "Yours. The voice was mine, the flower yours, the law Quill's. It took —" she considers, the struck-match mind working "— all three of us to survive eleven minutes of his funnier voice.")**
> "The price," Rose says. "Broken, not bought. The paper is broken. The purse is next."
> "The purse," Lavinia says, "and then —" she stops. The hunger is undisguised now: Pyke, in her sights. Not the paper — the *man*. The vanity, cracked; she wants it shattered. "When this is done, Rose. When the purse is opened and the trial is won. *He* is mine."
> *(Rose looks at the scarlet woman — the bloom, the hunger, the alliance's oldest clause — and understands the third decision is already forming, the way weather forms: Lavinia's hunger, loosed or leashed. "The trial first," Rose says. "The purse, opened. Then —" she meets Lavinia's eyes "— we will discuss what broken means." Lavinia smiles — the struck-match smile, brief and real. "We will," she agrees. "The price was broken, not bought — I have paid it, darling, in the witness box, in scarlet, with your flower at my shoulder. The rest of it —" she glances toward the courtroom doors, toward Pyke's bewildered brightness somewhere inside "— the rest of it is the hunger's hour. But the trial first. The purse, opened. I am" — the smile again — "a woman of my word.")*
> *(They walk the corridor together — scarlet and grey, the bloom between them — and the courtroom's functionaries step aside the way people step aside for weather. The alliance, in the corridor's dim light, is the whole season in miniature: the scarlet woman's hunger, the grey woman's discipline, the white flower's testimony, the law waiting inside. "Eleven minutes," Lavinia says, half to herself. "I have been libeled for years, darling — years of his funnier voice — and it took eleven minutes to answer." "The answering," Rose says, "was always going to be shorter than the libel. Truth is economical." Lavinia laughs — the real laugh, rare as the real smile. "Then let us go and be economical about the purse.")**

scenes.synopsis: Quill's final evidence — the purse, opened; the paid witness, the loud corners, the campaign quantities, laid in order before the jury.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill rises for the plaintiff's final evidence — not a witness, but a reckoning: the purse, opened. He lays it before the jury the way he laid the ledger — in order, the auditor's method, the columns marching: the forty-pound witness, paid from the purse; Larkin's stack, extra for the loud corners, paid from the purse; Creech's campaign quantities, coin that never touched Pyke's office, paid from the purse; the cutout's two years, the deep purse that never ran dry, paid from the purse. The chain, complete, in the open — three hands, one purse, the operation's workings described the way the decision directed: named, on the record, the Network's coin named as coin. The jury follows the columns the way pupils follow a master's hand. The gallery follows the gallery's way — Fane's lorgnette, the Directresses' fans, the cipher-clerk's flying pencil.)**
> *(The courtroom receives the opening in the hush of arithmetic — Fane's lorgnette steady, the foreman's pencil moving in the slow rhythm of a man writing the verdict before the verdict. Rose watches Pyke watch his purse opened in public, and the vanity goes with it: not cracking but coming apart, the bewildered brightness gone, replaced by the flat calculation of a man counting what is left. Which is nothing — the witnesses unmade, the ledger admitted, the chain complete, the purse opened like a ledger on the exhibit table. His counsel sits with his hands folded, the last card played and answered, and does not rise. There is nothing to rise for. The purse is opened. The arithmetic is devastating. The town is doing its sums.)*
> *(Quill sits — the reckoning, delivered — and the courtroom exhales the way courtrooms exhale when the evidence is complete: the long breath of a room that has seen the whole of a thing. Rose feels the season's weight shift — the trial's mechanics closing, the verdict's shape forming in the foreman's moving pencil — and beside her, Lavinia's hand finds hers for one brief pressure: the alliance's signal, *next to, always*. The purse, opened. The paper, broken. The clean name, earned three times over. And beyond the purse's edge — the offstage, the face, the season beyond the trial — waits its own season, in its own time, on ground she will choose.)**

> 4. [micro]Watch Pyke watch — the vanity, coming apart. → Remembered: The proprietor's unmaking; the purse opened, and the vanity with it.
> 5. [social]Count what is left — nothing. → Remembered: The inventory of ruin; paper broken, campaign proved, purse opened.
> 6. [examine]Weigh the fulfilled truth — the open, won. → Remembered: The season's doctrine, completed; the judge unowned, the victory open.

scenes.synopsis: Quill recalls the cutout for one final question — the chain named complete, for the record.
scenes.prose:
> *(Quill recalls the cutout — the clerk's coat, the careful blankness, the man who made a career of being unmemorable — for one final question, and the courtroom understands: the chain is being named, complete, for the record. "You have described the purse," Quill says, the courtroom's quietest voice carrying to the back row. "One purse, through the whole of it, deep, that never ran dry. Now — name what you can name. The purse's keeper: who filled your hand?" The cutout looks at the judge; the judge nods; the cutout looks at his own hands, folded, clerk's hands, and says what he has said all trial: he never asked. Asking was above his station. The purse filled his hand. His hand filled the gutter. The keeper — the keeper he never saw.)*
> *(The courtroom receives the not-answering in the particular silence of a boundary honored — the foreman nods, the honest limit noted for the record: the chain ends at the purse's edge, and the edge is where the trial stops. Rose feels the discipline hold — the season's discipline, the face unchased, the boundary Quill laid in the first week and has never moved. The cutout steps down — unmemorable to the last, the clerk's coat disappearing into the corridor's dimness — and the chain stands complete as chains in courtrooms ever stand: proved to the purse, and the purse's edge the horizon. Beyond it — the meeting, the masquerade, S4's door ajar in the future — waits.)*
> *(Quill does not press — the auditor's restraint, the general's wisdom: complete things left complete — and the judge notes the evidence closed on the purse's opening. The gallery stirs, the arithmetic done, the town's sums filed. Rose watches the empty witness box — the cane-bottomed chair, in the way, exactly where it belongs — and understands the trial has given her everything a trial can give: the purse opened, the paper broken, the name clean. The rest — the face, the meeting, the war's next season — is not the trial's to give. It is hers to choose, on ground she will choose, in the season that is coming.)*
> *(The corridor takes him — the clerk's coat, the careful blankness, unmemorable to the last — and the courtroom turns back to the business of verdicts: the judge's instructions, the jury's retirement, the town's waiting. Rose watches the doors close behind the cutout and feels the chain settle into the record like a stone into a wall: complete, mortared, permanent. The purse's keeper, unnamed. The purse, opened. The trial, having proved what trials can prove, prepares to say so. The rest — the face, the meeting, the masquerade — is not evidence. It is the future, and the future is hers to meet on chosen ground.)**
> "For the record," Quill says, "the chain: the cutout's hand —" his own chest "— the purse's books —" the counting-house "— the Network's coin —" further off. "Three hands. Complete to the purse. The plaintiff does not ask you to imagine further. The purse is proved; the coin is traced; the* Lantern's *ink was bought —" he lets it stand "— and the bill has been read aloud." He sits. The chain, named for the record: the keeper, the books, the coin — everything the trial can honestly hold. Beyond the purse's edge: the offstage, the unnamed, the face that never comes. The record holds it.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Hear the final question — the naming, for the record. → Remembered: The chain's formal completion; named things enter the record permanently.

scenes.synopsis: the trial acknowledges the offstage — Quill states it plainly: the coin had a master; the master is not in this courtroom.
scenes.prose:
> *(It happens in the afternoon — the moment the trial acknowledges the offstage. Quill, in his final address, states it plainly, the courtroom's quietest voice at its plainest: "The coin had a master. The master is not in this courtroom. The plaintiff has proved the purse; the plaintiff does not pretend to have proved the face." The ton does its quick arithmetic, and the London face passes through the trial like a shadow through a room: unnamed, unshown, unimagined — the season's discipline, held to the last line. The jury receives the shadow — the foreman nods: the honest limit, honored. The gallery receives it — Fane's lorgnette dips in something like respect, the cipher-clerk writes *offstage* in his cipher and underlines it three times.)**
> *(The face, never named, never shown, never promoted — the season's discipline, held to the last. And somewhere beyond the courtroom's sightlines, the master sits in his unseen room, and the trial goes on without him — the purse opened, the paper broken, the verdict forming — and the absence is the whole point: the trial is about the coin, not the master; the purse, not the face. Rose feels the boundary like a fence — plain, honest, exactly where Quill laid it — and the relief underneath the discipline: the season beyond the trial is hers to meet on her ground, not the court's to drag into daylight. The second decision waits — demand, wait, or receive — but the trial, here, now, honors the offstage by leaving it offstage.)*
> *(Quill sits — the address, complete — and the courtroom holds the shadow for one full minute before the judge speaks: the minute of the acknowledged offstage, the season's deepest discipline, observed by a room full of people who have spent the season learning it. Rose looks at the empty air where the face is not — the room the face doesn't sit in — and nods, once, to no one: the boundary, kept. The trial will end. The verdict will come. The face will wait — for the meeting, the masquerade, the ground she chooses. The discipline holds.)*
> *(The minute passes — the shadow, acknowledged — and the judge speaks, and the trial resumes its mechanics: the charge, the retirement, the waiting. But the offstage stays offstage, the discipline holding like a fence through the verdict's eve and into the verdict. Rose carries the boundary out of the courtroom like a sealed letter: the coin had a master, the master is not in this courtroom, and the season's deepest wisdom is knowing which truths belong to trials and which belong to meetings. The second decision waits — demand him, wait for the masquerade, or let the Network come — The face will keep. The ground will be chosen. The season will turn.)**

scenes.synopsis: texture — the courtroom doing arithmetic; the ton recalculates the Lantern's two years under the new note of revaluation.
scenes.prose:
> *(There is a moment — after Quill sits, before the judge speaks — when the courtroom is simply a room full of people doing arithmetic. Rose, connoisseur of the ton's sums, listens to the new note underneath: not excitement, not calculation now, but *revaluation*. The Network's coin, in a courtroom: the ton is recalculating everything — the *Lantern's* two years, Pyke's vanity, the libel's price, and — the deepest sum — what it means that money has a master, and masters can be traced. The Directresses' fans move in the slow rhythm of revised opinion. Fane's lorgnette sweeps the room the way it sweeps a sale-room: assessing, pricing, filing.)* herself. "She traced it," the fragments say. "In the open. The purse, opened." The woman who was libeled is now the woman who opened the purse. The ton's arithmetic has a new column, and her name is at the top of it.)*
> *(A coin — an actual coin — has been entered as an exhibit: one of the cutout's, a gold piece, held up by the clerk and laid on the exhibit table where the jury can see it glint. The Network's coin, in a courtroom, glinting under the lamps. The ton stares the way it stares at everything: as a symbol first, a fact second. The symbol: money has a master, and masters can be traced. The fact: this particular gold piece traveled from a deep purse through a clerk's hand to a gutter, and the gutter cried libel. Rose watches the coin glint — the smallest exhibit, the heaviest — and understands the ton is learning the season's lesson at last: the purse is a fact, the master is a shadow, and shadows are not tried in courtrooms.)*
> *(The judge speaks — the arithmetic, interrupted — and the room rearranges itself around the law's voice. But the revaluation continues underneath, the ton's sums running like water under ice: the *Lantern* explained, the vanity priced, the libel filed under *bought*. Rose feels the season turning — the trial's end, the verdict's approach, the town's new gown cut from the purse's opening — and the white rose at Lavinia's shoulder nods in the lamplight, the bloom, the testimony, the flower that went in first and will come out last.)*
> *(The coin glints — the smallest exhibit, the heaviest — and the courtroom's arithmetic runs on: the foreman's pencil, Fane's lorgnette, the Directresses' fans, all doing the new sums. Rose watches the ton revalue in real time — the *Lantern's* two years discounted to nothing, Pyke's vanity written down to zero, the libel's price filed under *paid for* — and understands the trial has done what trials rarely do: it has changed the town's mind about money itself. The Network's coin, in a courtroom: the symbol outlives the verdict. Masters can be traced. Purses can be opened. And the woman in grey, with the auditor's eye, has taught the town to do its sums.)**
> **Turns (7):**
> 1. [examine]Hear the revaluation — the new note. → Remembered: The murmur's final pitch; the ton reprices everything, including her.
> 2. [micro]See the gold piece, glinting — the exhibit. → Remembered: The coin's physical presence; symbols glint, facts merely lie there.

scenes.synopsis: Pyke at his own autopsy — the slyness intact to the end, now a relic; his counsel has nothing left.
scenes.prose:
> *(Pyke sits through the purse's opening with the particular stillness of a man at his own autopsy — present, interested, unable to intervene. The slyness is intact to the end — he never threatened, never blustered, printed and only printed — but it is a relic now, the way a sword is a relic at a trial about poison. His counsel has nothing left: the witnesses unmade, the ledger admitted, the chain complete, the purse opened, the card played and answered. The vanity's last brightness flickers — the bewildered brightness, the man's belief that the town's amusement was the same as the town's love — and goes out, replaced by the flat calculation of a man counting what is left. Which is the office, emptied. The paper, broken. The name, billed.)**
> *(Rose watches him — the proprietor, cornered, sly to the last — and feels the hunger's hour approaching the way weather approaches: Lavinia's hunger, the scarlet woman's reckoning, the price paid and now to be collected. Pyke does not look at Lavinia. He looks at the purse's opening — the columns, the arithmetic, the devastating sums — the way a man looks at the tide coming in: with the particular attention of someone who has just understood the tide does not negotiate. His counsel leans, murmurs; Pyke shakes his head, once. There is nothing to murmur about. The trial is over except the verdict. The verdict is arithmetic.)*
> *(He sits — the autopsy, complete — and the courtroom moves on around him the way water moves around a stone: the judge's voice, the jury's pencils, the gallery's fans, all flowing past the stillness at the defendant's table. The slyness, intact, irrelevant. The vanity, cornered, quiet. The man, whole — walking, still, past Lavinia's window, past her name — and the hunger's hour ticking toward him like a clock. Broken, not bought — the price, paid. The rest of it — Lavinia's — waits.)*
> *(The stillness holds — the man at his own autopsy, present to the last — and Rose feels the season's oldest pity stir and settle: pity for the vanity, not the man. The man printed filth for money and called it slyness; the vanity believed the town's laughter was love. Both are relics now. Lavinia's hunger approaches — the scarlet weather, the hour itself — and Pyke sits unknowing in its path, counting what is left, finding nothing. Broken, not bought — the price, paid in the witness box, in scarlet, with the white rose at her shoulder. The rest of it — the hunger's hour, the reckoning, the watch — is Lavinia's. Rose will decide the leash. The storm will decide the rest.)**
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [examine]Attend the autopsy — present, interested. → Remembered: The proprietor's final posture; unable to intervene, unwilling to leave.
> 2. [stance]Grant the final courtesy — sly to the end. → Remembered: Her last measure; relic-slyness is still slyness, and she notes it.
> 3. [examine]See the flat grey — the sums, not coming right. → Remembered: The vanity's extinction; brightness gone, arithmetic remaining.
> 4. [micro]Catch the second look — the last. → Remembered: The exhaustion, not hatred; spent things are almost decent.
> 5. [social]Not look away — nor triumph. → Remembered: The general's discipline; witnessing without gloating is the final courtesy.
> 6. [examine]Watch Lavinia watch — the cat, the door. → Remembered: The hunger's patience; the gallery holds a predator, blooming.
> 7. [stance]Know the endgame — not the verdict. → Remembered: Her understanding; what comes after is the third decision's country.
> 8. [choice]Pity or finish — the spent, watched. → Remembered: Her final posture; the general finishes, the woman might forgive, neither yet.

scenes.synopsis: the corridor after the purse's opening — Quill does the victory's arithmetic in columns; bought, proved, opened, answered, holding.
scenes.prose:
> *(The corridor after the purse's opening — Quill does the victory the way he does everything: quietly, completely, without spilling a drop. "The purse is opened," he says, the corridor's dim light kind to his tired face. "The chain is complete. The verdict —" he glances toward the courtroom doors "— is arithmetic now." Rose walks beside him — the auditor's walk, the measured pace — and feels the trial's weight lifting the way a siege lifts: slowly, then all at once. "The face," she says. "Offstage. By the discipline." "By the discipline," Quill agrees. "The trial ends where trials end. The rest —" he does not finish. The rest is the second decision: demand, wait, or receive. The rest is hers.)**
> "The purse," Rose says. "What do we do with it — after? Pursue it past the trial, let it lie, or hand it to you?"
> "Ah," Quill says — the nearest thing to delight his profession permits. "The first decision of the endgame. Pursue it — the tracing continues, past the verdict, into the war's next season. Let it lie — complete things should be left complete. Or hand it to me —" he taps his papers "— and I keep the purse's file warm, for whatever comes. The chain, the books, the keeper — evidence, kept long enough."
> *(They walk — the barrister and the auditor, the corridor's flagstones cool underfoot — and the season's proportion settles: enormous, endurable, almost complete. "You chose well," Quill says — the purse, named in court, the record complete, the *Gazette's* amplification carrying it everywhere. "The naming was the boldness. The boldness was the strategy." Rose nods — the decision's weight, the heaviest exhibit, carried well. "The meeting," she says. "The masquerade. S4's door." "In its season," Quill says. "The ground, yours to choose. The surveyor's patience, or the general's reach, or the receiver's openness — but in its season. The trial first. The verdict. The town's sums, filed.")*
> *(The courtroom doors open — the verdict's eve approaching, the town's arithmetic done — and they stand in the corridor's dimness, the victory complete, the war reserved. "The hunger," Quill says, quietly — Lavinia's hunger, the third decision, forming like weather. "The leash is in your hand, Miss Hartwell. Weather is steered, not indulged — but it is also" — the rarest thing: Quill, almost smiling — "never boring." Rose smiles — the auditor's smile, brief, real. "The trial first," she says. "The purse, opened. Then the weather.")*
> *(They stand — the barrister and the auditor, the corridor's dimness holding them — and the season's ledger balances in Rose's head: the purse opened, the paper broken, the name clean, the face offstage, the hunger leashed-or-loosed in her hand. Every account, stated. Every column, added. 'The verdict,' Quill says, 'will be arithmetic. The arithmetic is done.' 'The weather,' Rose says, 'is not.' Quill nods — the rarest concession: the law ends where the hunger begins. They walk toward the courtroom doors — toward the verdict's eve, the town's sums, the white rose's testimony — and the corridor gives them back to the trial, the victory complete, the war reserved, the ground hers to choose.)**

Henry Beaumont sits with the officers, his regard steady; the others — the kind ones, the honorable ones — in their places. The *Gazette* has noted their constancy, Bell's verdict on the season's courtship: honorable men, behaving honorably, in a season of bought ink. The gallery, full to the doors, is the town's final attendance: the Directresses, Fane, the cipher-clerk, the ton in its best black-and-white, come to see the arithmetic conclude.)**
> *(Rose feels their regard — the honorable attention, the season's slow courtship — and the fashion-mechanic underneath: every choice has carried social consequence, and the consequence, today, is this room, this regard, this town. She sits in grey — the auditor's grey, the season's uniform — the white rose nowhere today, its testimony given, its bloom resting. The trial's final days are the season's final examination: the purse opened, the paper broken, the face offstage, the hunger waiting. The suitors watch. The town watches. The jury, retired, decides.)*

Rose looks at the rows — the faces, the fans, the lorgnettes — and understands the season's real trial was never in this room: it was in the town's mind, and the town's mind is made up. The *Lantern's* ink was bought. The purse is opened. The woman in grey is clean. The arithmetic, devastating, complete. The town has voted with its attendance, and the attendance is unanimous.)*
> *(The suitors' constancy — the season's quiet courtship — is the *Gazette's* final note on the season's romance: honorable men, behaving honorably, the routes developing through friendship, the friendship deepening by increments. Rose feels the season's romantic ledger balance: no villain among the suitors, no slyness, only the slow, honorable attention of men who have watched her audit a season and found the auditing admirable. The gallery, full, is the courtship's witness: the town, attending; the suitors, regarding; the woman in grey, clean. The trial ends. The verdict comes. The honorable, remain.)**

> *(Rose walks Fleet Street — the auditor's walk, the measured pace — and the street's arithmetic is the town's: the bought paper, dark; the unbought paper, lit. The *Lantern's* last number lies in the gutter, trodden, its funnier voice silenced. She does not pick it up. The proportion, kept: the paper is broken, the man is whole, the hunger's hour approaches. Pyke's office — the dismantled desks, the silent presses — is the vanity's monument: slyness, intact, irrelevant; brightness, bewildered, extinguished. The town has moved on. The town always moves on.)*

The *Gazette's* stays lit. Rose walks on — the season's lesson, filed: bought ink fades, unbought judgment endures. Mrs. Nance Bell, proprietor, from the first edition: no machinery behind the curtain — just the verdict, written where everyone can read it. The street, the town, the season: the arithmetic, complete.)*

Rose walks past it without stopping — the proportion, kept — and the street's ordinary business flows around her: the hawkers, the coffee-houses, the *Gazette's* lit windows. The campaign's machinery, dismantled in a day, leaves no monument but the dark windows. The town has moved on. The town always moves on. > *(The ton's arithmetic — drawing rooms do their sums on the purse's opening. The Directresses' drawing room, the afternoon: the fans, the tea, the particular murmur of a town revising its opinions. The purse — opened, the counting-house named, the books described — is the season's final sum, and the ton is doing it with the thoroughness of a town that prides itself on never being fooled twice. Fane's verdict, delivered over tea: the *Lantern* was bought, the purse was deep, the woman in grey is clean. The drawing room nods. The sums, filed. The paper, explained.)*
> *(Rose is not there — the auditor, absent from the arithmetic — but the arithmetic is about her, and the ton knows it: the clean name, earned; the white rose, testified; the alliance, holding. The drawing rooms do their sums the way they do everything: thoroughly, publicly, with tea. The verdict's eve approaches, and the ton's verdict precedes the jury's: the town has decided. The *Gazette* will write it. The court will speak it. The drawing rooms have already filed it.)*
> *(The fans slow — the sums, complete — and the drawing room turns to the season's remaining question: the face, offstage; the hunger, waiting; S4's door, ajar. But those are the future's sums, not the afternoon's. The afternoon's sum is the purse: opened, billed, complete. The ton folds its fans, finishes its tea, and the arithmetic is filed with the season's other certainties: the white rose blooms, the auditor adds, the town, having summed, moves on.)*
> *(The drawing room's sums — filed, complete — are the ton's final arithmetic on the season: the purse opened, the paper broken, the woman clean. Rose, absent, is present in every sum: the auditor's grey, the white rose's testimony, the alliance's holding. The ton's verdict precedes the jury's — the town, having summed, awaits the court's speaking of the sum. The fans fold. The tea cools. The season's certainties, filed: the white rose blooms, the auditor adds, the town moves on. Tomorrow: the verdict.  Tonight: the sums, the tea, the drawing room's quiet — and the verdict's eve, the white's choosing, the town's attendance, all filed with the season's certainties.)**
> "And the face?" someone asks — the question the town asks everywhere now, the way it once asked about the libel. "Offstage," Fane says, with the finality of a woman closing a fan. "Unnamed. Unshown. The trial drew the line, and the line holds." *(Rose, listening from the tea table, notes the town's discipline: the face demanded nowhere, the shadow accepted everywhere. The ton fears mysteries and merely bankrupts explanations — and the purse, explained, is bankrupt; the face, unmentioned, is a shadow; and shadows, the town has decided, are not its business. The arithmetic closes. The sums say: the woman won, the paper's broken, the purse is opened — and the rest is the* Gazette's *to write.)*

> *(The verdict's eve — three white dresses; vindication near, worn. Rose's dressing room, the evening: Letitia lays out the whites — the verdict's gown, the vindication's uniform, the clean name's clothing. Three dresses, three whites, three moods: the severe white, the soft white, the triumphant white. The ritual's constancy: even verdicts are received at the right temperature, in the right white. Rose looks at the three — the choice, the season's last dressing decision — and the fashion-mechanic hums: every choice has carried social consequence, and tomorrow's consequence is the town's eyes, the jury's memory, the *Gazette's* paragraph.)**
> *(Letitia's counsel — the duel-grade opinions, weddings and verdicts, the difference known — and the white is chosen: the vindication's white, the clean name's white, the white that says *answered* without speaking. The dressing, unhurried: the gown, the gloves, the hair, the rose — the white rose, blooming still, the testimony's flower, pinned at the shoulder for the verdict's hearing. The mirror's verdict, delivered before the court's: the woman in white, the auditor, the clean name, ready.)*
> *(The lamplight — the white, chosen; the eve, kept — and Rose sits with the verdict's eve the way she has sat with every eve this season: dressed, steady, ready. The three whites hang, the two unchosen waiting their seasons. Tomorrow: the verdict. Tonight: the white, the rose, the lamplight, the proportion.  The season, enormous, endurable, almost complete — the white, chosen; the rose, pinned;  the verdict's eve, kept — dressed, steady, ready, the white rose blooming at the shoulder,  the testimony's flower — the three whites, the chosen and the waiting, the mirror's verdict delivered before the court's — the verdict's eve, kept.)*
> *(The mirror's verdict — the woman in white, ready — is the season's last dressing decision, made: the vindication's white, the clean name's clothing, the *answered* spoken in cloth. Rose looks at the three whites — the chosen, the waiting — and the fashion-mechanic rests: every choice carried consequence, and the consequence, tomorrow, is the town's eyes. The rose, pinned. The gloves, chosen. The hair, dressed. The verdict's eve, kept the way eves should be kept: dressed, steady, ready. The season, enormous, endurable, almost complete.)**

scenes.synopsis: the hunger, named again — scarlet drawing room; Pyke in her sights; the weather, forming.
scenes.prose:
> *(The hunger, named again — scarlet drawing room; Pyke in her window, walking past. Lavinia stands at the window — the bloom at her shoulder, the struck-match gaze — and the hunger is no longer a forecast but the climate: the man, whole, walking; the paper, broken; the price, paid. "He walks," she says — the bright, dangerous voice. "Past my window. Past my name. The trial is over except the verdict, darling, and the verdict is arithmetic. But he —" she watches the street "— he is still walking." The scarlet drawing room holds its breath: the hunger's hour, approaching.)*
> *(Rose looks at the ally — the agenda, the hunger's shape — and the third decision forms, weather-like: rein her in, let her have Pyke, or hold the line, *next to, always*. Lavinia turns from the window — the struck-match smile, bright past bearing. "Broken, not bought — that was the price. I have paid it. Now the rest of it is mine. Unless you say otherwise." The alliance's oldest clause, invoked: the hunger, loosed or leashed, the leash in Rose's hand. The trial first, Rose says. The verdict. Then the weather.)*
> *(The window, the street, the walking man — and the two women, scarlet and grey, the bloom between them. The hunger's climate fills the drawing room like weather fills a sky: particular, patient no longer, the hour itself approaching. Rose meets Lavinia's eyes — the ally with an agenda, the hunger with a history — and understands the season's last decision is the hardest: the storm, steered or released, the formation held or the leash pulled. The verdict first. Then the hunger. The leash, in her hand.)*
> *(The hunger's climate — the scarlet drawing room's weather — fills the season's last days like a sky before storm: particular, patient no longer, the hour approaching. Rose holds the leash — the alliance's oldest clause, the hunger's shape in her hand — and the third decision waits, weather-like: steer the storm, release it, or stand *next to* through it. Lavinia watches the street — the walking man, the whole man, the price's remainder — and the struck-match gaze is the hunger's whole history: years of filth, years of funnier voice, the paper broken but the man walking. The verdict first. Then the hunger. Then the watch.)**
> "He printed filth about my family," Lavinia says. "Years ago. In his funnier voice, or someone's. The paper is broken — but the* man *walks. Walks, darling, past my window, past my name, past everything. Broken, not bought — that was the price, and I have paid it, and now I want the rest of it." *(Rose looks at the scarlet woman — the bloom still at her shoulder, the hunger like weather — and understands the third decision is no longer forming; it has* formed*, the way storms do, and the only question is the lightning's direction. "The verdict first," Rose says. "Then we discuss it." "We will," Lavinia agrees — the struck-match smile. "Oh, darling. We will." The alliance holds: grey and white and scarlet. The hunger waits: patient, particular, entirely Lavinia's.)*
> **Turns (8):**
> 1. [social]Drink to formalities — the verdict's eve. → Remembered: The toast's irony; won things still want ceremony.
> 2. [examine]Hear the glass click — the small hammer. → Remembered: The sound of intent; crystal can be a gavel.
> 3. [stance]Face the undisguised — almost beautiful. → Remembered: The hunger's honesty; unhidden appetites have their own grace.
> 4. [micro]Note the steady hand — the pouring. → Remembered: Her composure's measure; hunger, held elegantly, is still hunger.
> 5. [examine]Hear "the man walks" — past her name. → Remembered: The grievance's geography; windows and names and everythings.
> 6. [social]Name the price paid — broken, not bought. → Remembered: The contract's terms; she paid, and now she collects.
> 7. [choice]Verdict first — the sequencing. → Remembered: Her ordering; lightning waits for the storm's schedule.
> 8. [stance]Hold the alliance — grey, white, scarlet. → Remembered: The formation, maintained; hunger does not break it, yet.

scenes.synopsis: the face, revisited — the boundary at the trial's end; the second decision, shaped.
scenes.prose:
> *(The face, revisited — the boundary at the trial's end; the season's discipline, held. Quill's chambers, the verdict's eve: the second decision, made or waiting — demand him, wait for the meeting, or let the Network come. The face, never named, never shown: the trial ends, and the offstage stays offstage, by the discipline, by the choosing. Rose looks at Quill — the barrister's gravity, the corridor's echo — and the decision's weight is the trial's heaviest exhibit after the purse: the shadow, met or left, the meeting's ground, chosen or received.)**
> *(Quill lays it out — the three postures, no fourth: the court's last grasp, reaching past its grasp, daylight or doubt; the masquerade's season, the ground hers to choose, the surveyor's patience; the invitation, incoming, the draft through the door, receiving as strategy. The face, revisited at the trial's end: the boundary, held. The season's discipline — the purse proved, the face left offstage, the shadow's office intact — is the wisdom the whole season has taught: some things end where trials end. The meeting is not the trial's. It is hers.)*
> *(The chambers' lamplight — the decision, made; the face, offstage — and Rose feels the season's proportion: enormous, endurable, almost complete. The purse, opened. The paper, broken. The name, clean. The face — waiting, in its season, on ground she chooses.  The discipline holds. The trial ends. The meeting waits — the masquerade's season, the ground chosen,  the shadow met where she stands strongest — the surveyor's patience, the general's reach, or the receiver's openness, in its season. The war, reserved.)*
> *(The boundary, held to the last — the trial's end, the face offstage — is the season's deepest discipline, complete: the purse proved, the face unpursued, the shadow's office intact. Rose carries the discipline out of the chambers like a sealed letter: the trial ends where trials end, the meeting waits where meetings wait, the ground is hers to choose. The second decision — demanded, waited, or received — is the season's last strategy, and the strategy's ground is the future: the masquerade, the draft through the door, the master coming to the woman he tried to ruin. The discipline holds. The trial ends. The meeting waits.)**

> 2. [stance]Glance at the empty air — twice, a habit. → Remembered: The trial's tic; offstage places collect glances.

> 4. [social]Recall Augusta's doctrine — the ground, hers. → Remembered: The general's gift; waiting means choosing.
> 5. [examine]Feel the draft — already through. → Remembered: The door's crack; S4's season is leaking in.
> 6. [choice]Reach, wait, or receive — the postures. → Remembered: The three attitudes toward shadows; each is a strategy.

> 8. [examine]Note the bloom — open, hers. → Remembered: The flower's parallel; decisions, like roses, open in season.

scenes.prose:
> *(Evening, Quill's chambers, and the verdict is a day away — the purse opened, the face offstage, the trial's last corridor walked. Quill lays it out with the gravity of a man handling what cannot be handled in court: "The face. Never named, never shown, never in evidence — and the trial is ending. Three postures, Miss Hartwell, and no fourth. Demand him — 'name him' — subpoenas, inquiries, the court's last act reaching past its grasp: the face, dragged toward daylight, or the doubt where he should be. Wait for the meeting — the masquerade, in its season, the ground yours to choose: the shadow, met where you stand strongest. Or let the Network come — make no move at all, and the invitation will find you: the draft is through the door already." Rose weighs the three postures: the court's last grasp, the surveyor's patience, the incoming invitation. The face stays offstage regardless — no choice names him, only the posture toward him.)*
*★ KEY DECISION 2/3 — The offstage face:*
- **Demand him — "name him"** — *Reach+; the court's last grasp.* Subpoenas and inquiries — the face, dragged toward daylight, or the doubt where he should be. *(Quill warns a demanded face undelivered becomes a doubt; Lavinia approves — the hunt is her element.)*
- **Wait for the meeting** — *Ground+; the masquerade, in season.* No move now — the shadow, met later where she stands strongest, the ground hers to choose. *(Quill calls it the surveyor's patience; Augusta approves — wars are won on chosen ground.)*
- **Let the Network come** — *Receive+; the invitation, incoming.* Make no move at all — the draft is through the door, the invitation will find her. *(Quill notes receiving is also a strategy; Bell will write that the master came to the woman he tried to ruin.)*
> *(The game remembers the choice — and the means: the grasp, the patience, the receiving. The destination was never in doubt. The signature is hers.)*

scenes.prose:
> *(The shadow, decision-shaped — what the second decision does to the season's air. The verdict's eve, the town: the face, demanded or waited-for or received — and the season's atmosphere changes with the choosing. If demanded: the court's last grasp, the doubt where he should be, the trial's reach exceeding its grasp. If waited-for: the masquerade's season, the ground chosen, the shadow met where she stands strongest. If received: the draft through the door, the invitation incoming, the master coming to the woman he tried to ruin. The shadow, decision-shaped: the season's air, rearranged.)**

The ton senses it — the drawing rooms' murmur, Fane's lorgnette, the cipher-clerk's pencil: the season is not ending, it is *turning*. The trial ends. The meeting waits. The shadow, decision-shaped, leans toward S4's door, ajar in the future, the draft coming through, wax and winter and black-and-gold.)*
> *(The gaslight, the shadow, the turning season — and Rose understands the second decision was never about the face: it was about the ground. The ground, hers to choose. The meeting, in its season. The discipline — the coin traced, the countenance unpursued — held through the turning. The trial ends. The verdict comes. The shadow waits, decision-shaped, for the season that is coming.)*
> *(The turning season — the trial's end, the meeting's approach — is the year's hinge: the shadow, decision-shaped, leaning toward S4's door. Rose feels the hinge turn — the verdict's eve, the gaslight, the town's murmur — and the season's proportion shifts: the trial, closing; the future, opening; the ground, waiting to be chosen. The second decision's shape is the future's shape: the court's grasp, the masquerade's ground, or the invitation's receiving. The discipline — the purse opened, the face left alone — holds through the turning. The shadow waits. The door stands ajar. The season turns — the trial's hinge, the future's shape,  the ground hers to choose — the masquerade, the draft, the invitation, the meeting that is coming.)**

> *(Texture — the room the face doesn't sit in; the ton's arithmetic about absence. > *(Direction: the verdict's eve is white's, and white's grammar is radiance — vindication, anticipated and then worn. Nothing the Gazette can fault, nothing the jury can misread, nothing the shadow can hide behind. The brief is the clean name, worn into the verdict.)*
> **Occasion brief (published):** "The trial's last eve — the verdict's eve. The dress code: you will sit in the second row through the judge's charge and the verdict, with the town watching, the *Gazette* judging, and Lavinia's hunger waiting in the gallery like weather. The gown must be *white*: vindication, anticipated and then worn — nothing the *Gazette* can fault, nothing the jury can misread, nothing the shadow can hide behind. The white rose, in bloom, at the shoulder — the clean name, rendered in flowers as well as thread. Gloves to the elbow expected; mourning colors forbidden — this is vindication, not grief. **Editorial criterion: radiance.** The brief is the clean name, worn into the verdict."
> **The 3 directions:** *A. The Vindication* (white silk, severe — the clean name, stated) / *B. The Bloom* (ivory with the white rose embroidered at every seam — the floriography, worn as armor) / *C. The Hartwell White* (dove-white velvet with wheat-ears in ivory whitework — the estate, unbroken, worn into the verdict).

> **Turns (21):**
> Direction. [choice]Choose the verdict's eve direction — A. The Vindication, B. The Bloom, or C. The Hartwell White. → Remembered: White's grammar, chosen; the direction governs every pin after.
